molecular.headline: Inherited ring frameworks carry exotic pendant groups; ordinary indole amides and alkylated diones coexist with heteroatom-halogen chains.
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and Parent trajectories were read. Every task has 300 recorded molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals, from seed 0; no task lacks trajectories. The products retain recognizable indole carboxamides, diaryl fused diones, biaryl chromenones, quinoline/piperidine conjugates, arylsulfonyl pyrrolidines and oxygen-rich polyacetals. Ring and branch SMILES rates are 1.0 on every task. Aromatic-bearing SMILES rates range from 0.6448 to 1.0, so abundant aromatic chemistry coexists with a nonaromatic polyacetal upper-score series. These are generally medium-to-large, substantially substituted molecules. Diversity is moderate across the supplied collection but much narrower within its upper-score families; much of the visible novelty is peripheral substitution on frameworks already present initially. Conventional alkyl, ether, amide, amine and carbonyl functionality coexists with terminal diazenes, nitrogen/oxygen chains, direct heteroatom-halogen bonds, persulfides and haloalkynes. The Parent comparison shows changes in these appendages and in the relative prominence of familiar families, without a corresponding general shift toward ordinary medicinal chemistry. Every proposal set has charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Those are absent SMILES annotations, not evidence that the structures lack ionizable groups or stereogenic centres. Synthetic plausibility and liabilities below are structural judgements, not measured stability, route feasibility or biological activity. Recorded scores are rounded for readability. No reference structures or objective-component scores were supplied, so an unseen target pharmacophore cannot be inferred.

per_task.generated_character: The upper-score molecules are medium-sized indole carboxanilides: a fused pyrrolic aromatic system joined through an amide to a phenyl group, usually with aryl fluorine and methoxy or short alkyl substitution. Evaluation 292 adds an aryl terminal diazene; 297 instead has a sulfur substituent directly on the amide nitrogen. The simpler analogue at 240 retains an ordinary amide, methoxy groups, a methyl substituent and aryl fluorine. The wider trajectory also contains biaryl chromenones and densely oxygenated, nonaromatic polyacetals. Mean SMILES length is 51.2, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9138 and halogen_rate is 0.6897. The indole/amide cores are plausible synthetic targets in outline; the complete diazene-, nitrogen-sulfur- and sulfur-fluorine-decorated variants require substantially more chemical justification.
liabilities: The terminal diazene at 292 and direct amide-N-S linkage at 297 make the complete molecules less conventional than their indole carboxamide cores. Other upper examples add direct S-F or N-S-N functionality; a sulfur-fluorine bond here must not be confused with a conventional sulfone.

Oxygen-sulfur appendages recur in the final material. Together with the unassigned geometry of diazene/imine groups elsewhere, they leave chemical identity, compatibility and isolation questions that the scalar score does not answer.
The lower-score polyacetals contain elaborate oxygen-bearing stereogenic frameworks without explicit configurations.
missing_features: The current upper-score excerpt lacks the comparably successful conventional N-alkyl amide chemistry seen in the Parent maximum. An ordinary secondary amide is present at 240, so the gap is sustained coverage of simple amide substitution within the favorable indole arrangement, not absence of amides.

Different fused-ring heteroatom arrangements and alternative connections between aromatic units are not demonstrated by the cited high molecules. Their value remains untested; the observed scores identify a favorable local family, not a specific missing target scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide at 9 scores 0.305105. The less extensively oxygenated indole series reaches 0.352934 at 240, 0.386927 at 297 and 0.394288 at 292. The modified polyacetal at 93 scores only 4.09806e-06, despite its substantial ring and heteroatom content. The observed distinction therefore includes aromatic framework and substituent arrangement, not ring abundance alone. Within the same sulfur-substituted amide series, replacing the indole methyl of 297 with fluorine in 299 changes 0.386927 to 0.204535. The final amino/bis(oxygen-sulfur)-substituted indole at 300 scores 0.127853. More halogen or heteroatom decoration is not uniformly favored. Parent n-edf80f0d6f5e reached 0.395373 with an ordinary N-methyl indole amide. The current maximum occupies a similar recorded neighborhood while carrying a terminal diazene; that substitution is not shown to be chemically necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The trajectory is dominated by large, aromatic diaryl fused dione heterocycles, with a second upper-score family of biaryl chromenones bearing nitriles. The aromatic periphery acquires imines, carbodiimide-type cumulated nitrogen functionality, oxime-like chains, nitrogen-nitrogen links and fluorine bonded directly to nitrogen or oxygen. Evaluation 254 combines a fused dione with imine and fluorinated nitrogen/oxygen appendages; 249 carries similarly decorated aromatic surfaces on the chromenone family. The last molecules also contain oxygen-oxygen chains ending in fluorine. Mean SMILES length is 65.6, aromatic_atom_rate is 1.0, halogen_rate is 0.9621 and cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.631. The underlying ring systems are recognizable, but the dense combinations of heteroatom-halogen and unsaturated nitrogen functionality make the complete products questionable synthetic endpoints.
liabilities: Nitrogen-fluorinated imines/carbodiimides and oxygen-fluorinated oxime-like groups are chemically different from routine aryl fluorination. Their repeated combination raises handling and functional-group compatibility concerns.
The final oxygen-oxygen chains ending in fluorine add peroxide-like connectivity. The acceptable recorded scores do not demonstrate stability or an executable synthesis for these combinations.

Repeated C=N and N=N units introduce geometric possibilities that are unspecified in the cited strings. Cumulated functionality is not automatically implausible in isolation, but these densely heteroatom-substituted combinations are not supported by synthesis evidence.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary realizations of the same aromatic polar substitution patterns are thin in the current high-score excerpt: nitrogen and oxygen are repeatedly supplied through fluorinated unsaturated chains. The missing comparison is a stable, compact functional-group arrangement at those sites, not simply more nitrogen or fluorine.

The upper-score series provides little evidence of new cyclic linkers or changed ring heteroatom patterns. Multiple inherited aromatic families occur, but their pendant-chain elaboration does not establish broad exploration of alternative ring architecture.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dione at 7 scores 0.548381; the elaborated relative at 254 scores 0.589489. The chromenone/nitrile analogue at 249 reaches 0.588545, so the upper region is not restricted to the dione core. The pyrazoline/phenol derivative at 20 scores 0.535497, and the quinoline/phenoxy/piperidine derivative at 18 scores 0.536296. Within the late dione sequence, changing an oxygen-chain endpoint at 298 to the oxygen/nitrogen chain at 299 accompanies 0.580425 versus 0.587001. These observations show local tolerance of elaborate polar aromatic decoration; they do not isolate a requirement for any reactive bond. The Parent maximum was 0.583606 on a diaryl dione decorated with amino, thioether and azo functionality. The current upper-score chemistry shifts toward fluorinated imine/oxime/carbodiimide appendages while retaining a familiar ring family.

per_task.generated_character: These are large, heavily substituted biphenyl/arylsulfonyl-pyrrolidine compounds with flexible secondary or tertiary aliphatic amine linkers. The pyrrolidine nitrogen remains sulfonylated; the visibly available amine centres are elsewhere, including linker nitrogens and aniline groups. The maximum at 286 combines an aniline-bearing biphenyl, a tertiary amine carrying a dibromomethyl group, a chlorinated allylic branch, an aryl thiol and a terminal disulfanyl/persulfide group. The other upper molecules repeatedly carry brominated carbon groups, thiols, persulfides and sometimes oxygen-bromine appendages. Mean SMILES length is 81.5, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9759 and halogen_rate is 0.9517. The core sulfonamide/amine chemistry is familiar, but the cumulative size and unusual peripheral combinations make these questionable complete synthetic targets.
liabilities: Brominated amine substituents, chlorinated allylic branches and extensive aromatic halogenation create a bulky, chemically demanding periphery. Direct O-Br groups in some upper examples are distinct from ordinary carbon-bound bromine.
Aryl thiols, terminal persulfides and mixed sulfur chains add compatibility and oxidation-state concerns. These motifs should not be summarized merely as conventional thioethers or sulfones.

Multiple flexible connections, crowded substituted saturated centres and unspecified stereochemistry complicate molecular identity and synthesis. The recorded task scalar is not a measurement of affinity or selectivity.
missing_features: The dominant family does not independently explore nitrogen electronic state and placement: its cyclic nitrogen stays sulfonylated while added basic centres occupy external linkers. A conventional unsulfonylated cyclic amine in this same geometric setting is not shown; its value cannot be inferred from the low-scoring amine-containing alternative scaffold.

Chemically simple matched alternatives to the dibromomethyl-, persulfide- and oxygen-bromine-bearing periphery are not well represented in the cited upper set. An ordinary secondary amine connector does occur at 214, so the gap is retaining useful amine geometry while independently reducing peripheral liabilities.

The substituted saturated ring and branched linker centres are not stereochemically specified, and explicitly charged alternatives are absent from the proposal strings. Evaluation-side protonation or conformer preparation is not documented here.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial acid/amide-linked arylsulfonyl pyrrolidine at 10 scores 0.0190412. The amine-linked sulfur-rich member at 210 scores 0.187213 and the related compound at 286 reaches 0.284516. Several structural features change together, so neither sulfur addition nor amide/acid removal can be assigned that gain independently. The bromophenyl diaryl dione at 133 scores 0.000747521. The initial quinoline/piperidine at 6 scores 0.000378699 despite containing an ordinary tertiary cyclic amine, showing that amine presence alone does not explain the gradient. The late pair 296 and 297 changes a larger dithiol-containing side branch to a directly attached thiol on the saturated ring, with scores 0.0991265 and 0.192606. Thus additional sulfur-bearing bulk is not uniformly favorable. The Parent maximum of 0.189601 had a chlorinated enamine linker on the same broad arylsulfonyl-pyrrolidine family. The current upper series emphasizes aliphatic amines and sulfur/bromine-rich decoration; no binding pose or specific receptor interaction is established by these records.

per_task.generated_character: The upper-score chemistry is comparatively conventional: alkylated diaryl fused diones bearing ordinary carbonyls, phenols and short hydrocarbon substituents, alongside quinoline/phenoxy conjugates of N-methyl piperidines. Evaluation 92 combines the fused dione with propyl and ethyl substitution, a phenol and an aldehyde. Evaluation 221 has a quinoline ether, an aniline-linked piperidine, a ketone and an aldehyde. The wider proposal set also repeatedly retains the arylsulfonyl pyrrolidine/acid family. These are medium-to-large aromatic molecules; mean SMILES length is 68.3, aromatic_atom_rate is 1.0, halogen_rate is 0.4862 and cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.0. The principal high-score structures look plausible as medicinal-chemistry starting points in outline, although aldehydes and some bulky alkyl elaborations still need scrutiny.
liabilities: Several upper examples carry aldehydes, which leave electrophilicity and chemical-compatibility questions even when the rest of the molecule uses familiar functionality.
Longer alkyl branches add flexible hydrophobic material without a monotonic recorded benefit. The final butyl/pentyl pair makes that limitation visible.
The piperidine-containing examples leave stereochemical configurations unspecified. Earlier N-O-rich variants elsewhere in the trajectory are less ordinary than the principal alkyl/carbonyl series.
missing_features: The high-score quinoline/piperidine entries do not supply a matched set of less reactive alternatives to their aldehydes. The high-scoring dione methyl ester shows that an aldehyde is not universally required in the observed upper range, but transferring that substitution between frameworks remains untested.

Alternative ring arrangements and defined configurations of substituted piperidines are not represented by the cited upper-score molecules. The modest positional and chain-length gradients do not identify a specific absent target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dione at 7 scores 0.167839; the alkyl/aldehyde-substituted member at 92 scores 0.183910. The quinoline/piperidine example at 221 scores 0.181769, and the dione methyl ester at 239 scores 0.181135. The modified biphenyl/pyran carboxamide at 30 scores 0.105623. Ordinary functional groups are therefore compatible with both higher and lower scores; their arrangement on the ring framework matters. The late dione pair 295 and 296 differs in the position of a phenyl methyl substituent and scores 0.175187 versus 0.180579. Extending the peripheral butyl chain of 299 to the pentyl chain of 300 changes 0.177211 to 0.173640. These are direct examples of position and chain length mattering without a general reward for molecular growth. The Parent maximum was 0.175888 in a quinoline/piperidine aldehyde series. The current maximum lies in the diaryl dione family, while ordinary alkyl/ether/carbonyl chemistry remains present in both panels.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest observed molecules are densely oxygenated, nonaromatic polyacetals resembling protected carbohydrate frameworks. Their periphery contains direct S-F groups, alkynes ending in sulfur-fluorine functionality, N-Cl groups and aldehydes. Evaluation 220 has that combination on the polyacetal framework. Aromatic diaryl diones remain common in the trajectory, and evaluation 129 reaches the upper excerpt with fluoroalkynyl and carbonyl substituents. Mean SMILES length is 57.8, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.6448 and halogen_rate is 0.8034: the high polyacetals must not be mistaken for a wholly nonaromatic proposal set. The ring frameworks are recognizable, but their densely substituted heteroatom-halogen and alkynyl periphery is questionable as a stable, isolable synthetic series.
liabilities: Direct sulfur-fluorine and nitrogen-chlorine bonds, fluoroalkynes and alkynyl sulfur-fluorine groups are unusual medicinal substituents whose mutual compatibility is not established by a valid molecular graph.
The crowded polyacetal framework would require stereochemical and synthetic control. The proposal strings provide neither explicit configurations nor evidence of an executable route.

The final aromatic compounds continue to combine sulfur-containing appendages with N-Cl and nitrogen-nitrogen functionality. Their very small scores do not rescue the chemical plausibility of those combinations.
missing_features: The upper polyacetal series lacks demonstrated chemically ordinary replacements that retain its locally favorable heteroatom and unsaturation arrangement without direct S-F/N-Cl or haloalkynyl endpoints. Whether such a replacement preserves any score is unknown.

Configurations of the numerous substituted oxygen-bearing centres are absent. The records therefore do not establish a stereochemically defined series, despite the complexity of the underlying frameworks.

No specific absent pharmacophore follows from these scores: both aromatic and nonaromatic families can enter the upper excerpt, while closely related heteroatom-rich derivatives can score extremely poorly. Missing target chemistry cannot be assigned from the task name.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial polyacetal at 4 scores 2.54690e-05; the substituted relative at 220 scores 0.0317402. The initial aromatic dione at 7 scores 0.00209445, and the fluoroalkynyl dione at 129 scores 0.0158795. The gradient therefore admits more than one ring family. The aryl pyrazoline/thioamide carrying sulfur-fluorine and fluoroalkyl substitution at 184 scores only 3.08411e-39, while the nitrogen-chain-decorated polyacetal at 20 scores 1.16030e-25. Neither sulfur/fluorine presence nor the polyacetal framework alone explains the higher values. In the late polyacetal sequence 295-297, changing the alkyne endpoint gives 0.00159344 for the nitrogen-chlorine variant, 0.00751374 for the sulfur-fluorine variant and 4.65983e-05 for the aldehyde variant. Those matched local examples show a sharp dependence on the particular peripheral group. The Parent maximum was 0.0881235 on a polyacetal decorated with terminal thiocarbonyls, an aldehyde and a trichloromethyl group. The current upper chemistry shifts to S-F/N-Cl/alkynyl decoration and a lower recorded maximum; neither panel supplies evidence of a conventional stable endpoint.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-score examples repeatedly carry direct N-F, O-F, S-F, N-Cl or O-Br bonds, nitrogen/oxygen chains, terminal persulfides and haloalkynes. One proposal set has cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.631 and halogen_rate 0.9621; another has halogen_rate 0.9517. At the same time, a simple indole carboxamide scores 0.352934 and an alkylated diaryl dione scores 0.183910 in their respective trajectories. The molecules demonstrate conventional alternatives, but their polar substituents often become elaborate heteroatom chains rather than independently varied familiar functional groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably express new polar functionality as chemically compatible, conventional local groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs local chemical-environment and compatibility control that keeps ordinary amines, amides, ethers, carbonyls and appropriately stabilized sulfur groups available as alternatives. Separate halogen attached to carbon from halogen attached to a heteroatom, and avoid treating equal atom inventories as chemically interchangeable. Preserve comparable ordinary substitutions for feedback to assess; the observed records do not justify declaring a universal score benefit for any functional-group restriction.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring_closure_rate is 1.0 for every proposal set, yet the cited upper molecules remain recognizable derivatives of initial indoles, fused diones, chromenones, arylsulfonyl pyrrolidines, quinoline/piperidine conjugates or polyacetals. The comparison with the Parent mainly changes pendant groups and the prominence of these same families. Ring abundance therefore does not establish broad coverage of alternative cyclic connectivity or ring heteroatom placement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output demonstrates abundant inherited rings but limited exploration of substantially different cyclic architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broader chemical coverage would require a generator domain that can vary ring connectivity, ring heteroatom arrangement and the links between ring units while preserving feasible chemistry. This is a coverage gap inferred from the products, not evidence that a particular unseen ring system improves an objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre_rate and charged_rate are both 0.0 on every task. The actual products nevertheless include substituted piperidines and pyrrolidines, branched amine linkers and elaborate polyacetals with potential stereogenic centres, as well as ionizable amines and acids. Cited imine and diazene products also leave geometric alternatives unspecified. These observations establish absent submitted-state annotations, not absence of stereochemistry or ionization in solution; evaluation-side preparation is not shown.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated structures leave stereochemical and ionization-state alternatives unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where the candidate contract permits, express chemically justified stereoisomers and ionization states explicitly and preserve those distinctions in candidate identity. Base state handling on generic chemical rules and observed feedback, without assuming that an annotation itself improves a score.

nodes.method_name: Inverse-QSAR: mixed-integer de novo molecular construction
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in inverse-QSAR through coupled linear regression and mixed-integer graph construction. [Zhu et al., Sections 1, 3 and 4](https://www.imrpress.com/journal/FBL/27/6/10.31083/j.fbl2706188) encode both a molecular descriptor function and a learned predictor in a program that constructs a graph satisfying structural specifications. Our benchmark adaptation fits a regularized linear score model only to the current objective's accepted observations, using atom-type, degree and typed-bond counts that can be represented exactly by integer constraints. For each proposal, take a scored molecule, choose a bounded editable peripheral region and retain its connected surrounding context. Represent replacement atom identities, bond orders and attachment choices as discrete variables, with connectivity, valence and descriptor-consistency constraints. Maximize the fitted scalar prediction over these variables instead of solving the paper's fixed target-interval problem. A feasible integer assignment supplies the new molecular graph directly. Validate the actual graph and recompute its descriptors before submission; exclude repeated assignments and retry construction when canonical identity is duplicate or invalid. Vary contexts and editable regions as feedback accumulates, and continue construction until the announced batch is filled. Use bounded subproblems and feasible solver incumbents rather than requiring a proof of global optimality for every proposal. The root needs no generative checkpoint or external labels. It constructs atom and bond combinations, without a corpus molecule pool, stored-fragment retrieval or the paper's subsequent isomer-enumeration stage. Each objective starts with clean scored and fitted state. The hypothesis is that jointly enforcing realizable structure while optimizing a task-local prediction concentrates evaluations on improving molecules and raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Exact descriptor realization cannot compensate for an inaccurate predictor; both predictive usefulness and sufficient construction throughput remain unproven.

approach.method_basis: The reference is DST, the Differentiable Scaffolding Tree of Fu and colleagues, which makes discrete molecular editing differentiable. A molecule is first rewritten as a tree whose nodes are whole substructures, single atoms and intact rings, rather than individual bonds and atoms. The identity of each terminal node, and whether that node exists at all, is then relaxed from a discrete choice into a continuous probability vector, which turns the tree into a smooth object that can be differentiated. A scoring surrogate reads the relaxed tree and its gradient is followed uphill, shifting probability mass toward the substructures the surrogate believes will raise the score. The optimized probabilities are then sampled back down to a discrete tree, and a real molecule is assembled from that tree by choosing attachment atoms and bond orders. The surrogate itself is in two parts: a graph encoder pretrained on unlabeled molecules by predicting masked-out substructures and frozen thereafter, plus a small linear readout refitted on the objective's own scored observations after every batch of feedback.
approach.novelty: Being a root, its commitments are the concrete form it gives that idea. Published versions of this method assume a surrogate trained on a large pool of already-scored molecules, which is unavailable here, so this node splits the surrogate in two: an encoder learned only from unlabeled structure and frozen, and a small ridge readout carrying all the task-specific signal, refitted from as few as ten labels and updated after each batch. It restricts each optimization to at most two terminal substitutions and two expansion sites and holds the interior of the starting molecule fixed, which guarantees a chemically intact product but also bounds how far any single proposal can travel from where it began. Starting molecules are drawn from the scored archive with an exponential preference for high rank rather than greedily. Twenty-two gradient steps are taken per optimization under one frozen surrogate version, so the target does not move underneath the ascent, and the diversity-selection objective of the original published method is deliberately not imported.

nodes.hypothesis: Freeze a corpus-trained masked-substructure graph encoder, fit a regularized linear readout to current-task accepted scores, ascend that fixed surrogate through relaxed leaf identities and leaf/expansion existence variables of observed molecules' scaffolding trees, and stochastically sample and assemble new structures from the optimized variables while preserving their internal scaffold context.

finding_summary.headline: Mid-field at 0.3619: the structural gradients ran cleanly and pointed the wrong way on average
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now knows that this style of surrogate-gradient construction executes faithfully at this budget, and that the surrogate is systematically optimistic. It is fitted in sample to a few hundred points, it is ascended to a strictly higher prediction every single time, and the molecules assembled from that ascent still average worse than the molecules they were built from. The failure is not in the gradient step, which is verified, but in the two lossy translations after it: from relaxed probabilities to a sampled tree, and from a tree to an assembled molecule, where roughly a quarter of attempts fail outright. At 0.3619 against a field spanning 0.2331 to 0.5103, this sits well clear of the undirected search methods and well short of the leader, which suggests that a learned model of structure is worth having but that a point estimate with no uncertainty is the wrong thing to ascend, since ascent drives proposals precisely into the region where the fit extrapolates worst. What stays open is whether calibrating the readout, with a posterior rather than a point prediction or an explicit penalty for distance from the fitted data, would close the optimism gap, and whether the fixed-interior constraint that keeps the chemistry clean is also what caps the score.

molecular.headline: Clean, fully ring-bearing drug-like chemistry that never leaves the scaffolds it was handed
molecular.overall_character: This is the most chemically respectable output of the three nodes examined. Every single proposal on every objective contains a ring closure and essentially all contain aromatic atoms, with a ring closure rate of 1.0 and aromatic rate of 0.986 to 1.0 across the five sets, no cumulated double bonds anywhere, and molecules of ordinary size at mean SMILES lengths of 41 to 80. The recurring pieces are real medicinal chemistry: quinolines, indoles, oxadiazoles, tetrazoles, piperazines, morpholines, pyrimidines and aryl amides. The cost of that cleanliness is visible in the same molecules. Because the interior of the starting structure is held fixed and only terminal units are edited, each objective's whole trajectory orbits the scaffolds present in the ten supplied starting molecules, so the top-scoring sets read as decoration series rather than as searches. Stereocentres are absent throughout, and a recurring set of reagent-grade functional groups shows the substructure alphabet carries no notion of stability.

per_task.generated_character: A single elaborated core: a methylated pyrimidinedione fused to a pyrrole, N-linked to a benzoate ester and carrying an oxadiazolyl ether, decorated with pyridines, pyrimidines and thiophenes. It is a direct elaboration of one of the supplied starting molecules.
liabilities: an anionic phenolate carried as a scoring feature inside the top-scoring entries
formaldehyde-acetal OCO fragments appearing in the low-scoring entries
densely fused biaryl-on-biaryl decoration pushing molecules past 100 SMILES characters
missing_features: a scaffold hop away from the elaborated core, which the fixed-interior rule forbids by construction
saturated linkers that would break the near-planar all-aromatic character of the whole series
defined stereochemistry at the few sp3 centres the series does contain
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The whole top twelve sits in a 0.003 band from 0.5863 to 0.5890616392238477 against a starting best of 0.548381482770623, so the gradient is genuinely being followed but into an extremely flat region. What separates the top from the 0.534 to 0.540 bottom is the oxadiazole ether and the N-aryl substitution; the low entries are the plain methoxy-indole carboxanilide with only small oxygen decorations.

per_task.generated_character: A dichlorophenyl sulfenamide on a proline-like pyrrolidine, joined through an aminal carbon to a morpholine or thiomorpholine and to a biaryl aniline. The halogen rate on this objective is 0.9828, so essentially every molecule carries chlorine or bromine.
liabilities: acid chlorides carried through most of the top twelve, which are reagents rather than compounds
sulfenamide S-N bonds as the load-bearing feature of the entire top-scoring family
aminal carbons bearing two nitrogens, which are hydrolytically unstable
a fluoromethyl ether decoration appearing on the highest-scoring entries
missing_features: a stable connectivity that reproduces whatever the S-N linkage is contributing to the score
an ordinary secondary or tertiary amine of the kind this target class rewards, in place of the aminal
defined stereochemistry, though the pyrrolidine and benzylic centres here are real stereocentres
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The single largest jump in the set comes from adding one thiol to the dichlorophenyl ring, taking 0.38644405836045415 to 0.42602011617052177. Across the top twelve the pattern is aryl halide plus S-N linkage plus a basic saturated amine ring. The lowest entries are the sulfonamide versions of the same molecules, which is telling: replacing the S-N sulfenamide with a proper sulfonamide costs more than an order of magnitude.

per_task.generated_character: A 4,5-dihydropyrazole bearing a furyloxy-phenyl group and an aminomethyl link to a pyridine or pyrimidine. Compact molecules at a mean SMILES length of 41.4, all ring-bearing and all containing aromatic atoms.
liabilities: free thiol and free aryl iodide substituents introduced as terminal decorations
a bare phosphorus substituent on nitrogen in one of the final proposals
an N-Cl bond appearing in another of the final proposals
one top-scoring entry carries a cumulated allene, which is not a stable substituent
missing_features: polar solubilising groups anywhere on the scaffold, absent from the entire series
an aromatic five-membered ring in place of the partially saturated pyrazoline core
defined stereochemistry at the pyrazoline sp3 carbon, which is a genuine stereocentre
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The furan-2-yloxy phenyl on the pyrazoline is fixed across the entire top twelve, so the whole gradient runs through the small amine cap: a pyridyl aminomethyl reaches 0.377 to 0.380 while a piperidine, morpholine or plain phenyl cap on the identical scaffold collapses to 1e-5 or below. That is an unusually sharp cliff for a single-group change, and the search found the right side of it early and then stopped moving.

per_task.generated_character: A tight decoration series on one supplied starting molecule: a methylquinoline benzyl ether linked to the anilide of an N-methylpiperidine carboxamide, with an added imidazolidine ring on the aniline. Every top entry shares that exact skeleton.
liabilities: an aliphatic aldehyde as the highest-scoring terminal group, reactive and metabolically labile
N-hydroxy piperidines appearing in the low-scoring entries
methylthio ether decorations appearing on the late proposals
missing_features: a second scaffold family, which the fixed-interior constraint prevents this generator from reaching
carboxylic acid or other strongly polar termini, absent from the entire series
defined stereochemistry at the two substituted piperidine ring carbons
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top twelve span 0.1749 to 0.18005061593636776, a 0.005 band, and the best is only 0.013 above the best supplied starting molecule at 0.1678386594791329. What moves the score is the small terminal group on the piperidine, aldehyde or acetyl or primary amide, together with the added imidazolidine on the aniline; entries lacking that added ring sit at 0.118.

per_task.generated_character: Methoxy-indole carboxamides derived from a supplied starting molecule, decorated with aziridinyloxy groups, fluorines and small azoles. The score span is extreme, best 0.23408968632790841 against a median of 9e-06, so the overwhelming majority of proposals are effectively zero.
liabilities: a trimethylsilyl group on nitrogen in the single best-scoring molecule, not a medicinal chemistry substituent
N-O aziridine ethers recurring through the top-scoring entries
peroxide linkages present in every one of the final six proposals
aminal carbons replacing the amide throughout the terminal cohort
missing_features: the fluorinated aryl and fused triazole chemistry this class of objective rewards
an amide or other stable connectivity retained through the late proposals instead of an aminal
defined stereochemistry, which this class of objective is built around
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The single best molecule differs from its neighbours mainly by a trimethylsilyl group on the anilide nitrogen, which reads far more like the objective being gamed than like real signal. Below it, entries that keep the indole-2-carboxamide intact score 0.07 to 0.19; once the amide is replaced by an aminal carbon the scores fall to 1e-13 and below, and that is exactly where the whole final cohort ends up.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every optimization holds the interior of a starting molecule fixed and edits at most two terminal units and two expansion sites, and every objective's top-scoring set is a decoration series on one of the ten supplied starting scaffolds, in one case spanning as little as 0.003 in score across twelve entries.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can only decorate the structures it is given; it cannot originate a core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator built this way is bounded by whatever chemistry it was seeded with, and the cleanliness of its output is bought with that bound. It would need an operation that replaces or rebuilds interior substructure, or a route to assemble a molecule from primitives with no starting structure at all, before it could reach a scaffold nobody handed it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 175 structural optimizations ended above their own starting relaxed prediction, yet the mean actual score change relative to the generating molecule was negative on all five objectives, and predicted improvements were realised only 26 to 46 percent of the time.
transferable_gaps.gap: The learned score model is systematically optimistic about its own edits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ascending a point-estimate surrogate fitted to a few hundred labels drives proposals precisely into the region where it extrapolates worst, so the ascent is self-defeating. A generator needs the surrogate to carry uncertainty and to pay a cost for distance from its fitted data, so the ascent stops where the model stops knowing anything.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Of 6268 sampled trees, 1106 failed assembly, 732 of them with no compatible attachment point and 374 failing kekulization, and a further 3712 were duplicates, leaving 1450 usable proposals from all that effort.
transferable_gaps.gap: A quarter of everything the optimizer designs cannot be built into a molecule.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The relaxed representation is not closed under assembly: it can place substructures that the attachment rules then reject. A generator should make attachment compatibility and aromatic ring closure part of the space being optimized, so that gradient effort is never spent on trees that cannot become molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Acid chlorides, sulfenamide S-N bonds, aminal carbons, N-O aziridine ethers, peroxide linkages and a trimethylsilyl group on nitrogen all appear among the highest-scoring molecules, several of them as the load-bearing feature of an entire top-scoring family.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reagent-grade reactive functionality is proposed as if it were finished substituent chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The substructure alphabet was learned from unlabeled corpus statistics and carries no notion of stability or synthetic accessibility, so an unstable primitive that happens to score gets refitted into the readout and then reinforced. A generator needs those primitives filtered, or the assembled molecule screened, before a proposal is allowed to spend an evaluation and enter the archive it is later fitted on.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 across all 1450 proposals on all five objectives, while the emitted molecules routinely contain substituted pyrrolidines, piperidines and pyrazolines whose ring carbons are genuine stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.gap: Configuration is never expressed in any proposal.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The tree representation encodes substructure identity and connectivity but not configuration, so stereochemistry cannot be proposed, optimized or even represented in the relaxation. A generator addressing shape-sensitive properties would need stereo as a variable inside the continuous relaxation, not merely as a tag on the final string.

nodes.method_name: DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in Differentiable Scaffolding Tree: relax molecular substructure identity and existence into continuous variables, ascend a structural surrogate, and sample discrete structures from the optimized variables. [Fu et al., Sections 3.1-3.3](https://wenhao-gao.github.io/assets/publications/2021_DST_ICLR/paper.pdf) describe this proposal mechanism. For our adaptation, derive an atom/ring token alphabet and train a compact graph encoder by masked-substructure reconstruction solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Freeze that encoder and fit a regularized linear scalar readout using only the current objective's accepted observations, updating the readout after feedback. Select scored molecules as local starting structures; hold their internal scaffold context fixed while optimizing relaxed leaf replacement, deletion and expansion variables through the surrogate. Keep surrogate parameters fixed during each structural optimization. Sample edited trees and compatible attachment choices stochastically, assemble new molecules, and repeat generation until the announced batch contains distinct valid structures. The token alphabet supports construction; complete corpus molecules are never retrieved or ranked, and attachment combinations are sampled rather than exhaustively enumerated. Accepted feedback updates both the scored archive and the readout. The hypothesis is that useful structural gradients concentrate new proposals toward real improvements quickly enough to increase the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Reliable gradients from scarce labels and faithful transfer from relaxed to assembled structures are unproven prerequisites.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecule by drawing atom, bond, path and ring edits, normalizing their molecular identities, and directly evaluating the first full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. Both inverse signs from the same selected transition must match to veto a fresh neighbor. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even when its score is worse, and a separate archive retains the best score. The current deletion choices remove one leaf atom or contract one degree-two atom, so removal of a longer pendant substituent requires several separately evaluated transitions. Identity normalization, memory lifetime and accepted-score selection are already established parts of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing deletion menu with a whole pendant-branch choice. When the deletion operator is drawn, it may remove an entire acyclic substituent attached through one single bond to a ring atom, while retaining every ring atom and the connections among retained atoms. Single-leaf choices remain in the same menu, and the operator keeps its existing allocation weight. This adds direct compact neighbors that no existing one-step removal can reach. The earlier sulfur sibling filtered local valence; this experiment changes the size of a permitted deletion and does not inherit or add that filter.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the Parent's existing uniformly sampled leaf-deletion menu with whole multi-atom acyclic branches attached by one non-ring single bond directly to a ring atom, so the same deletion-operator allocation can emit a compact neighbor in one edit while retaining the complete ring framework.

finding_summary.headline: Whole-branch deletion produced compact neighbors, but every score replica regressed.
finding_summary.insights:
A lack of eligible branches was not the bottleneck: the Parent already had branch opportunities in 399 of 435 states, and the extension successfully turned such opportunities into new evaluated neighbors. The added prunings usually lost source score, rarely won their batch and were followed by regrowth whenever selected. Those observations help explain why immediate reductions of several atoms did not produce a lasting shift toward smaller sampled molecules under the unchanged accepted-score walk.

The experiment separates direct access to compact analogues from retaining useful score. Its complete method loses score in every seed, although that loss cannot be assigned solely to the pruned candidates because the changed menu also changes later sampling and trajectories. The molecular assessment remains dominated by sulfur-rich polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds and unresolved ring geometry and stereochemistry. Ring-preserving removal alone does not resolve those chemical limitations.
finding_summary.results:
The expanded menu was available in 391 of 435 actual batch-start states. It selected 83 whole-branch edits, all graph-valid; after seven duplicate exclusions and seven tabu vetoes, 69 prunings reached evaluation. Each removed 2-14 heavy atoms in one step, averaging 3.75 atoms and 2.10 rotatable bonds, while retaining every ring atom and bond. The recorded menus, uniform selection, graph edits and identity joins passed the audit, including exact original behavior in all 55 deletion draws where no added branch was available.

Eight of the 69 evaluated prunings beat their source, and four became the next current state. All four later grew again. Typical emitted size remained essentially unchanged at 33.21 heavy atoms, compared with 33.20 for Parent. All three seeds completed their five 300-evaluation tasks; sampling cost was also similar at 12.14 versus 12.15 attempts per ten-member batch.

Mean macro final Top-1 fell from 0.520918 to 0.456635, a paired mean change of -0.064283. The three seed changes were -0.020009, -0.101316 and -0.071524. Every task mean declined, with the largest losses in DRD2 and sitagliptin. The intended neighborhood expansion and immediate size reduction occurred, while the score-retention hypothesis failed on the supplied panel.

molecular.headline: Sulfur-rich polycycles and reactive heteroatom bonds persist despite some recognizable aromatic amide families
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete corresponding Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 trajectories. Ring-closure and branch presence are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.7322 to 1.0, while charge and stereocentre token presence remain 0.0. These counters indicate SMILES features, not aromatic atom fractions, measured basicity or feasible stereochemistry. The output remains chemically close in broad character to the Parent: compact fused aromatic carbonyl compounds, large decorated nitrogen heterocycles, halogenated aromatic amine assemblies, bridged oxygen/nitrogen carbonyl systems and sulfur-rich cages. Several seeds change detailed scaffolds, giving moderate diversity across the panel, but each late trajectory mainly varies a related family. The more conventional indole or aza-indole amides coexist with multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur, sulfur-carbon triple bonds, N-Cl/N-F/O-F bonds, peroxides and extensive constrained ring closure. Overall synthetic plausibility remains poor and drug-like quality weak; recognizable fragments do not make these complete structures accessible. Score changes differ across seeds and do not consistently accompany a move toward more conventional chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-1 family contains moderately sized fused aza-aromatic amides or thioesters, with ethyl/methyl groups, hydroxymethylthio or bromomethylthio substituents and N-Cl on the fused pyrrolic nitrogen. More conventional indole carboxamide and thioester relatives also score well. Other seeds move into bridged thione/amine systems or unsaturated sulfur-rich frameworks. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9678 and halogen presence is 0.8678. Compared with the Parent's indole, benzofuran N-chloroamide and aryl-ketone families, the current high region preserves compact fused aromatic/carbonyl arrangements while changing ring nitrogen and sulfur linkages. Whole-molecule plausibility is compromised by N-Cl, O-F, N-O and unusual sulfur chemistry.
liabilities: N-Cl, O-F, bromomethylthio and thioester groups create reactivity or stability concerns in otherwise recognizable aromatic scaffolds.
Late multiply bonded sulfur and dense bridged thione/amine structures have unresolved geometry and synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: Stable amide and thioester alternatives preserving the favorable fused aromatic arrangement are underrepresented relative to N-halogen, O-halogen and N-O substitutions.
Accessible alternatives to the late bridged or sulfur-rich ring systems and explicit configurations where stereocentres arise are absent from the shown high/final series.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates direct molecular sampling from a task-local neural flow policy with two rounds of graph crossover and mutation. It learns from the exact token trajectories and real scores of accepted molecules through trajectory balance, a jointly learned normalizer and regularization toward a frozen corpus-trained prior. Accepted graph discoveries re-enter the same replay archive. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior selects which fresh graph offspring receive evaluations while retaining the first fresh-policy handoff. Its reusable prior is chosen along the unchanged unlabeled training trajectory by fixed-noise valid, connected, unique molecular yield, with original holdout loss breaking ties. Online replay currently samples the full accepted archive by global score rank.
approach.novelty: Add a scaffold-balanced mixture to accepted trajectory replay: keep half of each trajectory's original rank probability and allocate the other half equally among available core families, preserving rank preference within each family. This changes which genuine accepted trajectories train the policy, with every accepted label and exact serialization retained. The lineage's other children changed prior preparation or graph posterior selection; none changed replay allocation. Other campaign experiments balanced breeding parents or survivor populations and lost score despite broader core use. This experiment tests a different path, the distribution of neural learning credit over the full accepted archive, and explicitly checks later policy behavior rather than treating extra scaffold counts as success.

nodes.hypothesis: Sample accepted trajectory-balance replay from an equal mixture of inherited score-rank probabilities and uniform scaffold-group mass with the inherited conditional rank probabilities preserved within each group.

finding_summary.headline: Scaffold-balanced replay broadened learning exposure and reached the policy, while completed-seed endpoints worsened
finding_summary.insights: Extra archive coverage did reach neural learning and subsequent sampling, so the result rules out a purely cosmetic entropy increase. It also exposes the allocation tradeoff: on the same accepted histories the mixture cuts expected graph-origin mass from 72.53% to 59.12% and reduces high-score rank emphasis, while giving much more replay to lower-ranked policy and initial records. Some transfer measures and average policy scores improve, yet those changes coexist with fewer novel raw candidates and weaker completed-seed best results. Broad replay therefore does not establish better endpoint search. The chemical assessment reinforces the distinction: plausible cyclic amines coexist with peroxide, N-halogen and constrained unsaturated-ring families, so family breadth does not certify useful functional context. The terminal failure is a separate inherited canonicalization weakness exposed by one emitted molecule; it explains the missing third formal score and does not explain the losses in the two successful seeds. A complete three-seed score-benefit conclusion remains unavailable.
finding_summary.results: The declared replay mixture ran in all 449 executed feedback states. Actual distinct scaffold groups per 32-member update rose from 17.87 to 23.26, with broader exposure in all fifteen task sessions. Graph-origin replay received less probability, but its average sampled trajectory log-probability increase rose slightly from 0.169 to 0.176 nats and more later policy emissions occupied previously trained graph families. Mean accepted policy-origin score increased from 0.205 to 0.238. This did not improve every output measure: raw valid-novel yield fell from 66.59% to 64.74%, duplicates increased, and emitted scaffold coverage narrowed slightly. Both formally successful seed endpoints fell, by 0.02618 and 0.06224. The third seed completed its oracle calls but failed on the final canonical-identity feedback join, leaving its formal macro score unavailable.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich output mixes plausible cyclic amines with peroxides, N-halogen bonds and severely constrained unsaturated rings
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied tasks cover all three seeds, with 900 trajectory rows and 870 optimizer proposals per task. All 4,350 optimizer proposals parse with RDKit, but their chemical plausibility varies substantially. The output is rich in rings and aromatic atoms: digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9782 to 0.9954 and aromatic-token rates from 0.9103 to 0.9759. Median proposal heavy-atom counts are 26, 35, 26, 32 and 25 in the fixed task order, with median ring counts of three, five, four, four and three. Conventional diaryl ethers, thioamides, aryl sulfonamides, heteroaromatic carbonyl systems, cyclic tertiary amines and arylpiperazines coexist with diaryl peroxides, N-chloro or N-fluoro groups, densely fused sulfur/nitrogen frameworks and small rings bearing cumulated carbon double bonds. Each task contains 529-717 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, but many digest leaders are variants within a few families; graph-level diversity does not establish accessible synthetic diversity. Relative to the parent, one leading repertoire becomes enriched in peroxides, another in small-ring allenes and N-halogen bonds, while the strongest cyclic-amine chemistry includes smaller, recognizable benzazepine-like structures. No assigned stereocentres occur among optimizer proposals, despite 273, 179, 562, 373 and 348 proposals containing an unassigned centre in task order. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable overall, with clear plausible subsets; the supplied scores do not establish stability, synthetic access or experimental activity.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains two methyl-substituted phenyl rings connected by an ether or peroxide, with an aryl thioamide attached to a diazine ring. The ether has 24 heavy atoms and the peroxide 25; both have three aromatic six-membered rings. Other leaders are compact fused azaaromatic ketones and a fused aromatic carbonyl/N-N heterocycle. Those carbonyl and thioamide frameworks are recognizable chemistry, but the peroxide, N-chloro amide/thioamide and unusual sulfur double-bond variants make part of the leading family chemically questionable as persistent drug-like molecules. The whole proposal set has median 26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Compared with the parent, O-O single-bond proposals increase from 15 to 89 and N-halogen proposals from five to 27, so the new leading peroxide chemistry reflects a broader change in the sampled output.
liabilities: Diaryl O-O links and N-chloro or N-fluoro nitrogen sites introduce possible bond-cleavage and reactivity concerns; valid SMILES and objective values do not resolve those concerns.

The terminal sulfur-linked N-fluoro example and sulfur oxo/thioxo substitutions are chemically different from ordinary amides or sulfonamides and should not be interpreted as interchangeable polar linkers.
Nine proposals have at most three heavy atoms and four exceed 50, indicating occasional degeneration and overgrowth around an otherwise ring-rich population.
missing_features: The high-score neighborhood lacks demonstrated stable, conventional alternatives that retain the useful diaryl/polar arrangement while replacing its peroxide and N-halogen variants; the high-scoring ether shows such chemistry is already reachable.
Broader coverage of distinct compact aromatic carbonyl arrangements is less visible among the digest leaders than repeated changes around the same diaryl linker and thioamide family.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Replacing the diaryl ether link with an O-O link accompanies a score increase from 0.444319 to 0.455132 in a displayed local pair. Adding N-chlorination to the peroxide thioamide gives 0.439920, and the corresponding N-chloro carbonyl amide gives 0.438748. These observations show that the score tolerates the questionable bonds; they do not establish a benefit from N-chlorination or the chemical stability of a peroxide. Compact fused aromatic carbonyl structures also reach 0.436954 and 0.433013 without those particular bonds. At the low end, oxygen fluoride, methane and trifluoromethylamine score zero, while much larger, heavily elaborated molecules score about 1.05e-68 and 1.11e-62. The gradient therefore favors a structured intermediate-size aromatic/polar arrangement over both tiny fragments and overgrowth, while leaving some local chemical liabilities unpenalized.

per_task.generated_character: This is a large, highly aromatic, halogenated repertoire: median 35 heavy atoms, five rings, four aromatic rings and molecular mass 555.2495; the digest halogen rate is 0.8241. The highest molecule is a comparatively conventional three-ring aminoheteroaryl arylsulfonamide with methyl, fluoromethyl and aryl halogen substituents. Other leaders combine nitrogen/sulfur heteroaromatics with sulfonyl groups, carbonyls and heavily fused, iodine- or bromine-substituted ring systems. One displayed leader has eight rings and seven aromatic rings, and a terminal example contains selenium. The parent also contained large heteroaryl/sulfur frameworks and frequent peroxide or O-halogen connections. Current O-O single-bond proposals fall from 135 to five and O-halogen proposals from 93 to four, but substantial size and fusion remain: 146 current proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
liabilities: Large aromatic surfaces, iodine or bromine substitution and repeated ring fusion produce high molecular masses and little saturated shape in many leaders; no solubility or exposure measurements are supplied.

Some terminal molecules combine unusual nitrogen/oxygen/sulfur bonding or selenium heterocycles with already elaborate fused systems, increasing the uncertainty of interpreting them as ordinary medicinal chemistry.
The proposal distribution reaches 95 heavy atoms and 13 perceived rings; such overgrowth is not justified by the simpler structure at the highest displayed score.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent economical coverage of the productive aminoheteroaryl/sulfonamide arrangement: the highest displayed molecule is much simpler than several heavily fused alternatives.
Synthetic access and stable geometry are not established for the densely fused sulfur/nitrogen leaders; graph ring counts cannot substitute for chemically credible alternative ring systems.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The three-ring aminoheteroaryl sulfonamide scores 0.607553; a six-ring iodine-containing fused system scores 0.604646 and an eight-ring elaboration 0.598471. These examples do not support continually adding rings or heavy halogens as necessary for higher score. The low-scoring examples, around 0.265-0.292, also contain sulfones, carbonyls and sometimes several rings, but distribute them through more saturated or differently connected frameworks. Functional-group presence alone therefore fails to explain the gradient. A terminal small fluorinated diene scores 0.5 despite lacking the elaborate heteroaromatic architecture, so intermediate score itself is weak evidence of molecular completeness.

per_task.generated_character: The leading chemistry is substantially more conventional than the most unusual output elsewhere. The highest displayed molecule is a phenolic benzazepine-like structure: a seven-membered tertiary-amine ring fused to a benzene, with alkyl substituents, only 18 heavy atoms and molecular mass 247.382. A closely related leader has 17 heavy atoms. Another family is an arylpiperazine linked through a long alkyl chain to fluorinated naphthalene or aza-naphthalene rings; these examples have four rings and approximately 29-32 heavy atoms. The full set has median 26 heavy atoms and median sp3-carbon fraction 0.5. Parent leaders also included arylpiperazine chains and fused phenolic amines, but some were much more bridged or polycyclic; current median heavy-atom count falls from 30 to 26.
liabilities: Long alkyl chains in the arylpiperazine family increase conformational freedom, and extra halogenation increases mass, while the compact phenolic amine shows that neither feature is universally needed.
Some terminal structures add strained or partially dearomatized rings and duplicated arylpiperazine appendages; these are less straightforward chemical proposals than the leading conventional amines.
Thirty proposals contain an N-halogen bond, but the displayed highest-scoring conventional amines do not require that liability.
missing_features: No additional mandatory pharmacophoric group can be inferred from near-ceiling scores; the supported missing chemistry is configurationally specified coverage of the successful cyclic amines.

The compact leading phenolic amines have an unassigned stereogenic carbon. Across proposals, 562 molecules contain an unassigned centre and none has an assigned centre, leaving geometry-dependent interpretation unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Both the compact phenolic cyclic amine and the long-linker arylpiperazines reach scores above 0.999999. Their shared association is accessible tertiary-amine functionality presented with aromatic regions; extensive halogenation, multiple aromatic rings or one exact linker length is not required by all leading examples. An acetylated bis-sulfonamide aniline scores about 3.80e-05 and an aromatic carbamate about 9.56e-05, despite their heteroatoms and rings. The terminal shorter fluoroalkyl diazepane scores 0.036190, whereas related extended arylpiperazine architectures remain around 0.975-0.996. These observations indicate contextual amine/aromatic placement rather than generic nitrogen enrichment, and do not establish experimental receptor activity.

per_task.generated_character: The leading repertoire is dominated by fused azaaromatic systems with N-methylated cyclic amide carbonyls, supplemented by a bicyclic amine/ketone family carrying an N-ethoxy connection and an aromatic ether arm. The highest molecule has 30 heavy atoms, five rings and four aromatic rings; closely related N-alkyl variants occupy much of the digest. Several carbonyl-bearing rings are seven- or eight-membered within multiply fused frameworks, and another leader has a perceived nine-membered ring. These are complex rather than sparse ring systems. Full proposals have median 32 heavy atoms and four rings, with 668 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds. Parent leaders also included N-methyl cyclic carbonyl systems and aromatic assemblies, with additional sulfonylpiperazine chemistry; the current digest is more visibly concentrated in fused carbonyl/N-alkyl variants.
liabilities: Complex fused and bridged carbonyl frameworks may impose synthetic and conformational constraints that their accepted SMILES do not capture.
N-O bonds in the N-ethoxy family and unusual N/N/O ring arrangements deserve separate chemical scrutiny; their presence is not interchangeable with a conventional ether or amine.
Sixty proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and 373 contain an unassigned stereocentre, so size and geometry remain unresolved even though rings and carbonyls are plentiful.
missing_features: The leading set lacks broad chemically distinct alternatives that preserve the observed aromatic and cyclic-carbonyl arrangement; much of the visible variation changes N-alkyl groups or local ring closure.
No supplied evidence establishes stable conformations or accessible syntheses for the unusual fusion patterns, and the N-ethoxy bicyclic leader leaves a stereocentre unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused N-aryl carbonyl framework reaches 0.202215, the N-ethoxy bicyclic amine/ketone example 0.200010, and several nearby fused N-alkyl variants approximately 0.197-0.199. These small differences do not identify a unique missing substituent. The low end includes oxygen bonded to fluorine and chlorine at zero, bromopropane at 0.018950, ethyl acetate at 0.030544 and a small amino heterocycle at 0.041345. Those lack the combined aromatic/cyclic-carbonyl architecture of the leaders. A long-chain sulfur-rich cyclic molecule also scores only 0.031469, demonstrating that molecular size and heteroatom abundance alone are insufficient. Late, related N/O-rich fused carbonyl structures remain around 0.16-0.18 rather than establishing a different high-score chemotype.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family combines a fused nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl heterocycle, N-methyl and N-fluoro substituents, a hydroxylated azaaryl ring and a four-membered carbon ring. In the two highest displayed molecules that small ring contains a cumulated C=C=C unit; another leader contains a four-membered conjugated diene. These are severe ring-geometry liabilities, despite all SMILES parsing. Other leading families contain an N-acetyl arylsulfonamide with a sulfinamide substituent and unsaturated fluorinated five-membered rings, or hydrazone/polyene chains ending in a charged nitrogen/oxygen/sulfur group. Median proposal size is 25 heavy atoms and three rings. Compared with the parent, N-halogen proposals rise from five to 157, carbon-allene proposals from one to 113, and proposals with a carbon allene contained in a perceived ring of at most five atoms from zero to 93. The current chemistry is therefore not simply a conventional heteroaromatic analogue series.
liabilities: There are 93 proposals with a carbon allene in a perceived ring of at most five atoms, and 62 with a four-membered ring containing at least two double bonds. Their constrained unsaturation is a chemical-realizability concern that ordinary valence parsing does not test.

N-halogen bonds occur in 157 proposals, and the digest charged rate is 0.2471; the leading N-F and unusual charged sulfur/nitrogen forms require stronger chemical qualification than neutral carbonyl heterocycles.
Twenty-five proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, while repeated small-ring or heterocycle duplication can produce vanishing scores without removing the original local liabilities.
missing_features: The leading neighborhood lacks demonstrated ordinary, geometrically credible ring alternatives preserving the useful carbonyl/azaaryl arrangement without a four-membered allene or diene.

Stable nitrogen substitution and sulfur/nitrogen electronic structures are not established for the N-fluoro and charged terminal-group families; the observed scores do not establish that these unusual bonds are required.
Configurationally explicit proposals are absent despite 348 molecules having an unassigned centre; the highest small-ring-allene examples also leave a stereogenic centre unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-fluoro dicarbonyl structures with a four-membered cyclic allene score 0.419765; the related four-membered diene scores 0.401915. A fluorinated five-membered diene sulfonamide scores 0.369632 and its cyclic-allene counterpart 0.366311. These values associate compact polar heterocycles and unsaturated substituent arrangements with higher score, but cannot establish stable realizable chemistry or a general benefit from cumulated bonds. The digest median is 0.001873, while eleven full-trajectory rows are exactly zero. Very large linked structures and long-chain polyamines populate that zero-score tail; duplicating the unusual N-halogen dicarbonyl framework in a terminal molecule gives approximately 1.63e-26. Compactness helps explain part of the visible gradient, while serious local bonding liabilities remain in the leaders.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A diaryl peroxide scores 0.455132 while the corresponding ether scores 0.444319, and N-chlorinated derivatives remain nearby. Another session has 157 N-halogen proposals, 113 carbon-allene proposals and 93 with an allene inside a perceived ring of at most five atoms; its highest structures carry both N-F and four-membered cumulated unsaturation. All proposals parse with RDKit, so these liabilities survive ordinary molecular-graph acceptance. Conventional aromatic carbonyl and cyclic-amine leaders elsewhere show that unusual bonds are not universally needed for appreciable reward.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve ordinary bond chemistry and feasible ring geometry within productive structural neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is reliable access to stable, geometrically credible alternatives that retain a useful arrangement of rings and polar groups. Chemical plausibility needs to distinguish ethers from peroxides, ordinary N-substitution from N-halogen bonds, and accessible unsaturated rings from extremely constrained cumulenes, independently of objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Median heavy-atom counts are 26, 35, 26, 32 and 25, but 4, 146, 7, 60 and 25 proposals respectively exceed 50 heavy atoms. Tiny fragments such as oxygen-halogen species or simple esters also occur at the low end. In one session the highest displayed aminoheteroaryl sulfonamide has three rings, whereas six- and eight-ring alternatives have slightly lower scores. In another, a phenolic tertiary amine with 18 heavy atoms reaches near-ceiling score alongside much larger arylpiperazines. Duplicating a polar heterocycle can coincide with a score around 1.63e-26.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has inconsistent control of molecular size and topology around otherwise useful chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Useful chemical coverage requires economical alternatives with controlled ring fusion, linker length and appendage size, while retaining demonstrated compact and extended chemotypes. A fixed preference for either very small molecules or maximal ring growth would miss the contextual structural relationships visible in the supplied feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4,350 optimizer proposals there are no assigned stereocentres. The five supplied sessions contain 273, 179, 562, 373 and 348 proposals with an unassigned centre. Digest leaders include a compact phenolic cyclic amine, an N-ethoxy bicyclic amine/ketone and fluorinated unsaturated rings with unspecified configurations. Ring richness therefore does not imply defined three-dimensional molecular proposals.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits stereogenic structures without specifying their configurations or resolving relevant bond geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The chemical representation needs to support explicit, internally consistent stereoisomers and bond geometries wherever those degrees of freedom exist. Their usefulness must remain determined by observed feedback, without assuming an unobserved preferred configuration or requiring stereochemistry in naturally achiral chemotypes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each session contains 529-717 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, yet the displayed leaders repeatedly vary diaryl thioamide linkers, fused sulfonyl heterocycles, arylpiperazine chains, N-alkyl cyclic-carbonyl systems or N-fluoro dicarbonyl cores. Several nearby variants have identical or very similar scores. The leaders also demonstrate that nitrogen environments are not interchangeable: conventional tertiary amines, acylated nitrogens, sulfonamide nitrogens and N-halogen forms occupy very different chemical contexts.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many graph scaffolds do not translate into broad coverage of chemically distinct productive core arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs chemically meaningful alternatives in core connectivity and polar-group placement, beyond peripheral halogen changes, N-alkyl substitutions and new ring closures. Preserve the ability to explore different stable architectures that realize an observed useful arrangement, while distinguishing functional-group electronic context and avoiding any prescribed objective-specific scaffold.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.
