approach.method_basis: The Parent runs short molecular editing episodes from molecules that already have real scores. Several persistent lanes each propose one action per batch. At a decision, it generates a fresh neighborhood of valid single graph edits and usually selects the edit preferred by one neural estimate of future episode improvement, with occasional uniform random choices. Every accepted molecule becomes the lane's next state, including molecules that score worse. Rewards measure only increases in that episode's best score. A replay buffer of real accepted transitions trains the value network through double-Q backups: the current network chooses a continuation and a delayed copy evaluates that same continuation. This machinery was confirmed in the Parent, including learning that affected later actions, but its best molecules concentrated around one core per objective. All lanes use the same learned value function, and their explicit random exploration is sampled separately at each decision.
approach.novelty: Add episode-consistent exploration through bootstrapped value functions. Five independently initialized value networks learn from different persistent random subsets of the same accepted transitions, each with its own delayed target copy. Each lane samples one network when an episode begins and uses that network for the episode's exploitation decisions, including decisions after a temporary score loss. Keeping the network identity through a sequence gives different lanes different learned reasons to pursue edits over several steps; feedback can still update that network between batches. The proposed change is new within this lineage, whose supplied sibling history contains only the single-network Parent. It tests the exploration direction deferred by that Parent. The activation claim is that persistent, differently trained heads make different actual exploitation choices on the same available edits; broader search and better final scores are possible consequences to measure, not assumptions.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the Parent's single acting Q-function with five independently initialized Q-functions trained on persistent Bernoulli bootstrap masks of accepted replay, each with its own lagged double-Q target, and select one head uniformly at episode start to control all exploitation decisions in that episode while retaining the Parent's epsilon branch.

finding_summary.headline: Learned episode heads diversify real choices and molecular distances, but lower the aggregate score
finding_summary.insights: Scarce feedback was sufficient to produce distinct learned head policies that changed real multistep search. The receipts rule out unused network copies, numerical value offsets alone, mask regeneration and broken feedback handling as explanations for this run. The exploration effect also appeared in average fingerprint distances, yet the large docking-score loss outweighed gains on three tasks. Greater policy and state diversity therefore did not deliver a higher aggregate score in this test. The molecular assessment still finds concentrated high-scoring families, reactive heteroatom motifs and demanding short bridges. The docking decline accompanies a different nitrogen, bridge and sulfur arrangement, which is an observed association rather than an identified causal structural defect. Broader fingerprint movement has not yet established broader coverage of useful, practical scaffold families. Further evidence is needed to separate the contributions of independent initialization, masked learning and persistent head identity, and to estimate score reliability across seeds. These results come from one paired screening seed; they do not establish a general score penalty or calibrated uncertainty.
finding_summary.results: The heads learned from different persistent transition subsets and kept their assigned identities through all 250 molecular editing episodes. Of 1070 exploitation decisions after learning, 710 strictly preferred an edit outside head zero’s maximizing choices; every episode offered multiple exploitation decisions under its persistent head. All 7250 head updates had nonzero parameter changes, and paired average learning residuals decreased for every task and head. Mean molecular fingerprint distance from episode starts rose from 0.443448 to 0.489426, and distance between contemporaneous lane states rose from 0.681615 to 0.733227. Later episode-best gains following losses increased from 123 to 145 events, although their mean positive increment fell from 0.015693 to 0.010788. The single-seed evaluator macro Top-1 score fell from 0.406693 to 0.350704, a change of -0.055989. Task Top-1 scores changed as follows: zaleplon_mpo 0.332184 to 0.438122 (+0.105938); deco_hop 0.614535 to 0.621204 (+0.006669); drd2_docking 0.753647 to 0.301684 (-0.451962); median_2 0.195125 to 0.184354 (-0.010772); sitagliptin_mpo 0.137973 to 0.208154 (+0.070181). All five tasks completed their 300-evaluation budgets with no invalid or duplicate proposals.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, heteroaryl lactones and dense bridged scaffolds coexist with peroxide chains and unusual sulfur chemistry
molecular.overall_character: The supplied seed-0 trajectories cover all five tasks, with 300 observed molecules and 290 optimizer proposals per task; there are no tasks without trajectories. These are mostly substantial, ring-rich organic graphs carrying aryl or heteroaryl groups, carbonyls, ethers, amines and halogens. The digest ring-closure rates are 0.9966 to 1.0 and aromatic-token presence is 0.9379 to 1.0. These are proportions of proposal strings containing the feature, not ring counts, aromatic atom fractions or evidence that the molecules are planar. Nonaromatic rings, bridges and saturated carbon centers are visibly present. Mean SMILES lengths range from 47.9 to 69.8 characters, a text-size indicator rather than molecular weight. The higher-scoring sets remain concentrated in a few related structural families, despite considerable peripheral and ring-connectivity variation. Ordinary medicinal chemistry is clearest in the hydroxyindole acetamide series. Elsewhere familiar lactones, diones and amines coexist with oxygen chains, oxygen-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur valence contexts, and very short bridges between separated positions on aromatic rings. Synthetic plausibility is therefore uneven and often questionable; a readable molecular graph does not establish an accessible synthesis or feasible geometry. All five charged-marker and stereocentre-marker rates are 0.0. Neutral drawings still contain ionizable groups, and several cited structures have unspecified stereogenic centers. The Parent trajectories show changes in the actual chemical families accompanying changes in observed scores, but these single-seed comparisons do not identify causal molecular features. The missing features below are inferred from the observed high/low contrasts; these data do not reveal an exact absent motif required by an objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Higher-scoring coumarin/azaaryl products contain successive oxygen-oxygen bonds, oxygen-chlorine termini and unusual sulfur-nitrogen triple bonds. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically ordinary functional-group contexts.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use chemical context when proposing changes to ethers, carbonyl groups and sulfur centers, with coherent alternatives in recognized bonding and oxidation-state contexts. Treat valence validity separately from stability and preparative plausibility. Any context restrictions should remain independent of objective identity and should not reject all heteroatom-heteroatom bonds indiscriminately.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading multiaryl acid and fused-dione families contain very short carbon or ether bridges across separated aromatic positions. Other higher-scoring products contain aziridines, unsaturated small lactams or densely crosslinked nitrogen/oxygen cages. Ring-closure presence is already 0.9966 to 1.0, and actual saturated rings are present; the deficiency is practical topology, not absence of rings or saturated atoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: Abundant ring formation is not accompanied by reliable control of feasible ring and bridge geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer ring and bridge changes with chemically feasible geometries, using contextual ring templates or task-independent geometric feasibility checks. Preserve access to ordinary saturated heterocycles and manageable ring-size alternatives while distinguishing them from severe short-bridge or crosslink strain. A higher ring count should not stand in for useful three-dimensional chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five digest stereocentre-marker rates are 0.0. Cited products include benzylic amino/acid centers, substituted saturated heterocycles, acetal-bearing bridge carbons and potentially stereogenic sulfur environments, all without specified configuration. This does not imply that every molecule is chiral; the conventional leading hydroxyindole amide is a counterexample.
transferable_gaps.gap: New stereogenic connectivity is emitted without explicit configurational alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: When an edit creates or modifies a genuine stereogenic element, preserve valid existing stereochemistry and make chemically meaningful configurations accessible as explicit alternatives. Let observed task-local feedback determine their utility. The present trajectories do not establish a stereochemical score ceiling or a preferred unseen stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The higher-scoring excerpts recur around hydroxyindole acetamides, amino-azaaryl coumarins, halogenated multiaryl amine/acids and substituted fused diones. Many nearby products alter oxygen chains, single substituents or ring crosslinks; practical alternative core/linker arrangements retaining the useful functional roles are less evident. Different cores and saturated rings do occur, so the evidence supports concentrated high-end coverage rather than an absolute inability to leave a scaffold.
transferable_gaps.gap: Higher-scoring polar and aromatic arrangements are explored through a limited set of related scaffold families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coherent scaffold and linker alternatives that retain useful carbonyl, donor, acceptor and aromatic roles while changing their arrangement in manageable ways. Maintain chemically distinct alternatives using the observed scalar feedback, without prescribing a benchmark scaffold or assuming that any new core will score better.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest charged-marker rate is 0.0, yet the molecules include secondary and cyclic amines, azaaromatics, phenols and carboxylic acids. Several high products combine an acid with an amine in one molecule. This is a limitation of the emitted representations, not evidence that these compounds remain neutral in solution or that downstream processing ignores protonation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ionizable structures are represented without explicit charge-state alternatives in the observed output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where the molecular interface permits distinct microstates, make chemically reasonable protonation and tautomer representations consistent with the generated functional groups. Avoid treating neutral SMILES as evidence of nonionizability. Any microstate exploration should be task-agnostic and evaluated rather than assumed beneficial.

nodes.method_name: MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in MolDQN's value-based control of molecular edits: learn future action returns from scored transitions and choose subsequent graph modifications with a deep Q-network. [Zhou et al., Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/1810.08678v3) describe finite molecular edit episodes, fingerprint features and double Q-learning. Our adaptation starts short episodes from task-local scored molecules and samples fresh valence-aware atom and bond edits at each state. A compact Q-network takes current and successor fingerprints, remaining episode depth and the episode's best observed score. Use a single Q-function with epsilon-greedy action selection in the root. Evaluate only selected new whole molecules; values assigned to unselected successors are predictions. Advance each trajectory after its matched feedback, even when the new molecule scores worse. For Top-1 alignment, use reward max(previous_episode_best, new_score) minus previous_episode_best and undiscounted finite-horizon backups: accumulated reward equals improvement in that episode's best score. This reward adaptation is our inference, not the paper's original reward. Train immediately from accepted transition replay using double-Q target selection and a lagged target network, with zero continuation value at episode termination. Retain all accepted intermediate molecules in the task incumbent archive. Interleave episodes according to announced batches, and generate further edits to replace invalid or duplicate proposals. Each decision samples an evolving neighborhood; no corpus pool, complete-molecule retrieval or fixed candidate enumeration is involved. No pretrained generator or external labels are required, and every objective starts with clean learning state. The hypothesis is that learned lookahead identifies useful edit sequences, including temporary score losses, quickly enough to raise the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Learning useful continuation values from scarce transitions is unproven; the paper's much larger training regime does not establish this transfer.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a molecular sequence flow from unlabeled structures, then adapts that flow to high-scoring observations within each independent objective. After every adaptation it re-encodes all accepted molecules and fits a Gaussian process to their scores. It proposes continuous changes around scored molecules by perturbing whole token blocks selected using estimated sequence-level pointwise mutual information. Correlated Thompson samples rank those continuous points before inverse decoding, canonicalization and novelty filtering produce a full batch. The inherited precision repair runs the online flow in double precision and preserves strict reconstruction of every observed token, including termination and padding.
approach.novelty: Add canonical decode-and-reencode projection before acquisition: first determine the fresh molecular identities produced by the existing proposals, then query the existing Gaussian process at the current flow encoding of each canonical molecule. This makes a candidate use the same representation convention used when an accepted molecule trains the surrogate. The hypothesis is that predictions tied to the actual decoded molecule will change which novel identities receive evaluations and may reduce optimistic errors. The original implementation and its precision-repair Child both queried the raw continuous perturbation; neither tested this projection. This experiment keeps the learned flow, proposal rule and Gaussian-process model, and changes the candidate coordinates used for acquisition.

nodes.hypothesis: Project each representable fresh decoded canonical molecule through the current sequence-flow encoder before applying the unchanged latent-GP joint Thompson acquisition, so acquisition uses the molecular representation on which accepted-score training is defined.

finding_summary.headline: Canonical projection reproduced across seeds, while a DRD2 miss exposed large score variation.
finding_summary.insights:
The coordinate correction has a reproducible local effect: it changes allocation beyond duplicate and representability filtering, and improves predictions for the molecules actually evaluated. The low-scoring DRD2 replica makes the remaining limitation concrete. It still changed the selected molecules in 23 of 28 groups with surplus candidates and achieved projected prediction error of 0.00416 with 95.2% coverage, yet never reached the high-scoring family found in the other two runs. Accurate predictions within a weak region can coexist with poor discovery. The molecular assessment supports this distinction: the successful DRD2 run finds a recognizable aromatic saturated-amine core, while the weak run stays among less useful arrangements. Which aspect of preparation or subsequent search determines access to that family remains open; the replicas use different pretrained checkpoints and vocabularies as well as different search seeds.

Proposal support remains narrow. Of 184,080 raw decodes in the added replicas, 174,820 returned their generating center; filling the batches required 477 refill groups. The representability gates excluded 675 candidates for unknown tokens, 46 for excessive length and 18 for failed lossless encoding. The shared-pool diagnostic separates the immediate projection effect from those gates, but their separate effects on a complete search have not been measured. Coverage also remains uneven, falling to 83.4% and 78.6% on sitagliptin despite wider intervals. The assessed chemistry retains radical, unusual-charge and chain-growth liabilities around recurring cores. Projection therefore establishes representation agreement and a more useful local predictive model; reliable access to useful scaffolds, uncertainty calibration and chemically plausible alternatives remain distinct problems.
finding_summary.results:
Both added replicas used canonical projected coordinates for all 2,900 evaluated proposals, with exact token and molecular-identity reconstruction. Every evaluated proposal moved from its raw continuous coordinate; the mean distance in normalized GP features was 0.95846. Holding the eligible molecules, fitted GP and random draw fixed, projection changed the selected identity set in 218 of 272 groups with more eligible molecules than available positions, replacing 469 selections. Every objective completed 300 evaluations in full batches of ten valid, novel molecules.

On the same accepted outcomes, projected predictions reduced mean absolute error from 0.07795 to 0.04938. Nominal 95% coverage increased from 1,656/2,900 (57.1%) to 2,653/2,900 (91.5%), and mean signed standardized residual moved from -1.83106 to +0.03189. Mean interval width increased from 0.16169 to 0.21524. Lower error and higher coverage occurred in every objective in both added replicas; the original screening replica showed the same direction of change.

The added replicas scored 0.4858806 and 0.2958706 in macro final Top-1, compared with 0.4804828 in the screening replica. The complete three-seed mean is 0.4207447, with population standard deviation 0.0883268. DRD2 accounts for most of this variation: final scores were 0.9043966, 0.9089320 and 0.0688042. Three-seed mean final scores are 0.3918935 for zaleplon, 0.5768938 for decoration hopping, 0.6273776 for DRD2, 0.1694639 for median_2 and 0.3380946 for sitagliptin. The original unprojected Parent has only its screening result at 0.4197516, so a paired three-seed score benefit remains unresolved.

molecular.headline: Recognizable cores are repeatedly reshaped into radicals, unusual charged species and cumulated chains, with weak medicinal plausibility.
molecular.overall_character: The seed-1 and seed-2 digest covers every listed objective, with 600 evaluated molecules and 580 optimizer proposals per task. Ring chemistry is present: ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.6034 to 0.9603. Aromatic_atom_rate varies much more, from 0.1224 to 0.6621, and several leading families retain recognizable indole, aryl cyclic-amine or fused dicarbonyl heterocycle cores while other families become nonaromatic or acyclic. The striking shared feature is unconventional electronic structure. Charged_rate ranges from 0.4241 to 0.7569, and cumulated_double_bond_rate from 0.0552 to 0.3638. These are text-based presence rates, not molecular charge, radical counts or perceived bond statistics. Inspection of the supplied leading SMILES also shows radical-bearing neutral nitrogen and under-coordinated charged boron, carbon and nitrogen; these are chemically different from ordinary protonated amines or conventional boron-containing functional groups. Mean SMILES lengths range from 39.8 to 57.2, but the maximum reaches 304 and the low tail includes very long hydrocarbon or repeating phosphorus chains. Conventional amides, ethers, aromatic rings and tertiary amines coexist with unusual multiply bonded phosphorus/sulfur fragments, poorly stabilized ions, ring opening and irregular cyclization. The set therefore has weak drug-likeness and is often implausible as isolable medicinal compounds, although individual conventional cores and neutral examples remain. Structural variety exists, but useful, chemically ordinary core families are much narrower than the variety of graph edits suggests. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0. The supplied parent_trajectories belong to seed 0 of this same node, n-119906c93e5d; comparisons below concern different runs of the same algorithm. Missing-chemistry statements describe output limitations, and do not establish that any unobserved replacement would improve an objective.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules preserve an indole carboxanilide with a para-fluorophenyl group, methoxy or methyl decoration and a vinyl substituent. However, the methyl-substituted bracketed nitrogen is radical-bearing rather than an ordinary methylamino group. Seed 1 favours extensively rearranged indole-related amide ring systems bearing under-coordinated anionic boron or carbon; a leading derivative even incorporates phosphorus into an aromatic ring. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9207, aromatic_atom_rate 0.6207, charged_rate 0.7466 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1724. Thus the output retains many rings but frequently changes their aromaticity and electronic structure. Typical proposal length is moderate, while the long tail includes huge hydrocarbon appendages, repeating charged phosphorus and polyunsaturated macrocycles. The prior seed-0 leader scored 0.36633919598396925 and already contained boron/cumulene chemistry around an aryl amide. The new best restores a more recognizable indole core but still carries an electronic-structure liability.
liabilities: The leading indoles encode a neutral nitrogen radical. Other leading structures contain poorly coordinated anionic boron or carbon, rather than ordinary medicinal boron groups or a defined protonation state.
Aromatic phosphorus, cumulated unsaturation and irregular large ring closures make some high-scoring analogues difficult to regard as routine synthesis targets.
The low tail includes repeated charged phosphorus atoms and very long carbon chains; the final macrocyclic material loses the recognizable high-score pharmacophoric arrangement.
missing_features: Ordinary closed-shell substitutions around the useful indole/aryl-amide arrangement are poorly represented in the supplied high tail. The initial molecule demonstrates that a conventional version of this core exists.

Controlled ring and linker changes that preserve aromaticity, amide connectivity and reasonable size are missing from many later proposals. Simply retaining a ring-closure marker does not preserve the useful core.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial conventional methoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. A related nitrogen-radical derivative scores 0.3726558544705772, and the vinyl-substituted indole leader reaches 0.41184841281151274; replacing its methoxy substituent with methyl gives 0.40196779766986834. The anionic-boron ring-rearranged amide reaches 0.3974929831413733, while an anionic-carbon/cumulated-chain pyrrole carboxamide reaches 0.3960446945907104. These higher observations retain the heterocyclic amide and aromatic anilide relationship despite substantial liabilities. A late nonaromatic sulfur-containing analogue that keeps an anilide scores 0.23800702843013238, while the final long polyunsaturated ring lacking that aromatic amide arrangement scores 1.7672523900312278e-13. Repeated phosphorus-chain expansion, an extremely long hydrocarbon appendage and a tiny sulfur-containing unsaturated fragment all appear at 0.0. The visible gradient favours retaining a bounded heterocyclic/aryl amide arrangement; it does not demonstrate that radicals or unusual ions are chemically necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecules fall into methoxyaryl families with either flexible imine/amidine-like and nitrogen-oxygen linkages, or a bridged diaryl arrangement containing a hydroxylated aminal carbon. Fluorinated and amino-substituted aromatic relatives occur. These leaders are moderate-sized and include neutral, closed-shell examples, making them more chemically recognizable than the more extreme charged tails. Nevertheless, the flexible imine and nitrogen-oxygen chains and the hydroxylated aminal bridge introduce stability and configurational questions. The digest reports ring_closure_rate 0.8931, aromatic_atom_rate 0.6241, charged_rate 0.4241 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1121. Other proposals contain broken aromatic systems, boron cumulenes or under-coordinated sulfur/phosphorus substituents. Prior seed 0 reached 0.5923028785982478 with a related methoxyaryl, hydroxylated nitrogen-linked assembly carrying an unusual charged nitrogen terminus.
liabilities: Multiple imine/amidine-like sites and nitrogen-oxygen bonds create possible hydrolytic, tautomeric or configurational liabilities; the trajectories provide no stability evidence.
Some near-leading variants replace ordinary peripheral groups with under-coordinated sulfur or anionic phosphorus.
Lower and late proposals repeatedly lose aromatic organization or acquire unusual charged substituents without moving beyond the leading score range.
missing_features: Robust alternatives to the imine, nitrogen-oxygen and hydroxylated-aminal connections are not established among the leading families. The molecules suggest useful polar connectivity but do not identify a uniquely required replacement.
Useful independent heterocyclic cores are sparsely represented in the leading examples compared with repeated decoration, ring expansion and opening of the methoxyaryl families.
The fluorinated saturated centres and imine-rich connections lack sufficient stereochemical or geometric specification to define the proposed molecular shapes.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluoro-substituted flexible methoxyaryl nitrogen/oxygen chain scores 0.5732613823172039 and its nonfluorinated counterpart scores 0.5717183425094176. The bridged fluoro diaryl aminal scores 0.5710412519733681, and its aminoaryl relative scores 0.5709544518196383. Different ring and linkage arrangements therefore reach very similar values. A terminal phosphorus-substituted analogue scores 0.565608397874928, below the ordinary ethyl-substituted leader. A thiol-bearing imine-chain molecule and its unusual sulfur-triple-bond extension both score 0.5655272375890807, illustrating a chemically consequential change with no observed score distinction. Butene and a boron/cumulene-containing nonaromatic polycycle both score 0.5. Late charged-chain variants score 0.5413086582947786 and 0.5617317822651449. The observed preference is for retaining methoxyaryl and polar nitrogen/oxygen relationships rather than hydrocarbon or boron-rich unsaturation alone. The new leaders remain below the prior seed-0 best, and the local score differences do not establish improved chemical stability.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high tail is dominated by an N-propyl tetrahydroisoquinoline-like core bearing an additional phenyl group and a variable side chain. This supplies an accessible saturated tertiary amine and substantial aromatic surface, but many side chains include unusual boron bonding, anionic carbon, selenium, or reactive aldehyde/imine ends. A neutral aldehyde-containing analogue retains a recognizable conventional core. Seed 2 instead stays largely among amido-acid, sulfur-containing and partially dearomatized structures and reaches only 0.06880419326700524 in its supplied trajectory. The digest's ring_closure_rate is 0.9069, but aromatic_atom_rate is 0.4776; charged_rate 0.5362 includes chemically unusual ions as well as ordinary ammonium groups. These are medium-to-large substituted ring systems and extended chains rather than uniformly small ligands. Prior seed 0 reached 0.904396584492305 with a tertiary-amine/biphenyl arrangement containing unusual phosphorus and an aryl triple bond. The new high core is more recognizable, while problematic side-chain chemistry persists.
liabilities: Under-coordinated anionic boron and cationic boron appear in the leading structures, sometimes with radical character. These are not conventional boronic acids or ordinary charge-state alternatives.
Anionic carbon, selenol functionality and unusually multiply bonded boron occur alongside reactive aldehyde and alkyl bromide substituents.

Extended unsaturation, altered aromaticity and irregular linkers frequently accompany low-scoring late structures, while the high family remains chemically concentrated around a single recognizable amine core.
missing_features: Stable, ordinarily bonded side-chain variants around the useful aryl saturated-amine core are underrepresented in the high tail. The neutral aldehyde example shows that exotic boron is not necessary to access that score neighbourhood.

The useful amine/aromatic relationship is not consistently maintained across runs or during subsequent changes; amines placed in unrelated acid/amide/polyene arrangements do not reproduce the high-scoring family.
Configurationally specified variants of the substituted saturated core and side chains are absent. The data do not establish which, if any, configuration would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The boron-linked aminoalkyl/bromo side-chain derivative scores 0.908931975508402, as does a relative with an additional cationic boron terminus. A boron-triple-bond side-chain analogue scores 0.9082735141610837. The ordinary aldehyde-side-chain molecule already scores 0.901222096572042, and the related terminal imine scores 0.8928968873484273. The observed high-score relationship is therefore present without exotic boron connectivity. A small protonated amino ether scores 0.0014478418038224013, the nitrogen-acylated amido-acid structure scores 0.0013483218327874778, and the pyrazoline/thioamide with a phosphorus-containing unsaturated substituent scores 0.0009365365935512206. Seed-2 terminal ammonium-containing structures still score only 0.018985024896303125 and 0.0226174773238248. These comparisons support the combination of an accessible saturated amine with an appropriate aromatic core and local connectivity, not positive charge or nitrogen presence alone. The pooled median is 0.026155 despite the much higher seed-1 family.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules retain the initial diaryl fused nitrogen heterocycle with carbonyl groups and N-methyl substitution, while modifying the attached aryl group into lactone-bridged or partially saturated ring systems. These are moderately large, multiring molecules with amide-like carbonyls, esters and ethers. Some leaders are neutral and closed-shell, but other near-leading examples replace a phenolic group with a bare cationic nitrogen or introduce under-coordinated silicon or sulfur. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9603 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.6621, so ring and aromatic chemistry are well represented. Charged_rate 0.5052 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.2655 describe a broader proposal set with much less ordinary connectivity than the leading neutral examples alone imply. The previous seed-0 best, 0.16817499303650435, used a related fused carbonyl heterocycle heavily modified with phosphorus and sulfur. The new leading examples are more conventional electronically, but remain close relatives of the initial carbonyl-rich core.
liabilities: A bare cationic nitrogen replacing a phenol is under-coordinated and radical-bearing, rather than a conventional ammonium substituent.
Silicon and sulfur substitutions, charged carbon/boron termini and repeated cumulated bonds undermine the medicinal plausibility of much of the broader output.
Lactone bridges and additional ring closures increase synthetic and geometric demands, while the best scores remain close to the initial scaffold.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary, independently different high-scoring cores are missing from the supplied leading set, which repeatedly edits the same diaryl carbonyl heterocycle.

Controlled changes of ring fusion, saturation and polar-group placement are incomplete: the generator frequently substitutes unusual valence states or opens the core into polyenes instead of producing coherent alternatives.
The new bridged and partially saturated structures lack explicit stereochemical specification where configurational alternatives are possible.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. The lactone-bridged derivative reaches 0.17089498068254003, a further bridged relative scores 0.17004430934016446, and a partially nonaromatic substituted-ring variant scores 0.16932164980768666. These retain much of the starting carbonyl/aryl arrangement and provide only limited separation from its score. The phenol-to-bare-cationic-nitrogen derivative also scores 0.1678386594791329, exactly matching the initial value despite a substantial change in electronic plausibility. A silicon-containing acyl derivative scores 0.1613052191741566. At the low end, the open hydrocarbon polyene/alkyne scores 0.009653840941344688, the charged carbamate/heteroatom chain scores 0.014242471194266176 and the cumulated amino-polyene chain scores 0.014379295573510231. The final boron/carbon-cation-bearing aryl carbonyl structure scores 0.14553656463999998. The visible gradient rewards preserving the heterocyclic carbonyl and aromatic arrangement; neither more charge nor ring rearrangement supplies a clearly different high-scoring chemical solution.

per_task.generated_character: The supplied leading set is acyclic and nonaromatic. Seed 1 produces branched conjugated chains containing an amide, enol-ether-like groups, fluorinated unsaturation and cumulated double bonds ending in a carbonyl. These chains repeatedly carry anionic carbon or nitrogen, unusual phosphorus multiple bonding, phosphonium-like centres or radical-bearing phosphorus. Seed 2 more often emits partially unsaturated oxygen-containing rings attached to boron/nitrogen, silicon and oxonium-containing chains. The digest confirms sparse aromatic character, aromatic_atom_rate 0.1224, with ring_closure_rate 0.6034, charged_rate 0.7569 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.3638. Ring-bearing proposals exist, but none of the digest's leading structures has a ring. Mean_smiles_length is 39.8; the ordinary-looking length conceals chemically unusual valence and reactive unsaturation. Prior seed 0 reached 0.3712004138157673 with a boron/cumulene and phosphorus/sulfur-containing cyclic structure. The new upper chain family changes topology without restoring ordinary medicinal chemistry.
liabilities: Cumulated unsaturation ending in carbonyl groups, anionic amine/carbon centres and unusual phosphorus triple/double-bond combinations make the leading structures questionable as isolable medicinal compounds.
Other examples encode under-coordinated silicon, boron-imine bonds, and oxonium-containing multiple bonds; the presence of nitrogen and oxygen does not turn these into ordinary amines or ethers.
The low tail includes runaway hydrocarbon growth and repeated phosphorus/sulfur multiple-bond chains, while chain and ring geometry remain incompletely specified.
missing_features: A stable, ordinarily bonded implementation of the leading amide and nitrogen/oxygen arrangement is missing from the supplied high tail; the observed leaders depend on unusual anions, cumulenes or phosphorus chemistry.

Conventional aromatic and saturated heterocyclic alternatives to the leading acyclic arrangement are poorly represented at high score. This is a coverage gap, not evidence that the objective requires rings.
Defined geometry around the unsaturated chains and consistent preservation of the useful polar-group arrangement are absent from many rearranged or extended variants.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The anionic-nitrogen, multiply bonded phosphorus chain reaches 0.38696599108397595. The anionic-carbon enol-ether/amide chain scores 0.3743960351343562, and its phosphorus-containing connection variant scores 0.34361125950464805. A related phosphorus-free but still anionic-carbon chain scores 0.32514654079522326. These observations associate the higher scores with a compact, specific amide/nitrogen/oxygen/fluorinated-unsaturation arrangement, rather than proving that phosphorus itself is essential. Extending the 0.34361125950464805 structure with a repeating sulfur/phosphorus multiple-bond chain yields 4.4347495233539386e-39. A very long hydrocarbon/phosphorus conjugate scores 0.0, while a short boron-containing cumulene ring scores 7.711774876445608e-25. A late seed-2 boron/silicon/oxonium oxygen-ring structure scores 0.1438849867348233, and its final related structure scores 0.0009012715453817541. The pooled median is 0.00614. The trajectory shows a narrow useful arrangement with severe sensitivity to elaboration; it does not show that adding an aromatic ring would be rewarded.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited leading indole contains a neutral nitrogen radical, a leading aryl saturated-amine derivative contains under-coordinated anionic boron, and a bare cationic nitrogen substitution matches its conventional phenolic precursor at 0.1678386594791329. Charged_rate spans 0.4241 to 0.7569 across the supplied proposal sets. These markers include unusual carbon, boron, phosphorus and nitrogen states, so they cannot be interpreted as a useful population of protonated amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish ordinary closed-shell medicinal structures from radical or poorly coordinated charged species.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent hydrogen count, valence, radical state and chemically credible ionization together when constructing or replacing functional groups. Preserve useful cores while enabling ordinary amines, ethers, amides and other stable local alternatives; accepted score alone is not evidence that an arbitrary bracketed atom is a plausible substitution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading chains include cumulated double bonds ending in carbonyl groups, anionic nitrogen or carbon, and unusual phosphorus multiple bonding. Other cited molecules use under-coordinated boron, silicon, selenium or sulfur. Cumulated_double_bond_rate ranges from 0.0552 to 0.3638. A conventional aldehyde-side-chain aryl amine already scores 0.901222096572042 near its exotic boron relatives, and a phosphorus-free chain remains in another high-score neighbourhood at 0.32514654079522326.
transferable_gaps.gap: Element and bond changes repeatedly create reactive cumulenes and unusual organoelement fragments instead of coherent functional-group alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make element substitutions and bond-order changes as chemically complete functional-group transformations, with the surrounding coordination environment preserved. Provide stable alternatives to cumulenes and exotic element linkages while retaining the polar-group and aromatic relationships already supported by accepted molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited low tail contains very long carbon appendages, a repeated charged-phosphorus chain in a set whose max_smiles_length is 304, and a sulfur/phosphorus multiple-bond extension that changes a 0.34361125950464805 chain into a 4.4347495233539386e-39 molecule. Conversely, tiny disconnected-from-the-useful-core fragments also occupy low tails. The problem is loss of useful molecular organization during both growth and contraction.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular growth lacks consistent termination at a chemically coherent size and can repeat the same atoms or unsaturation excessively.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded core-preserving growth, contraction and termination, with explicit handling of repeated chain units. Let accepted molecular feedback determine useful size locally while maintaining complete functional groups and preventing unbounded repetition from replacing meaningful chemical exploration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The high-score molecules repeatedly retain an indole carboxamide, a methoxyaryl polar-linker family, an aryl fused saturated-amine core, or a diaryl carbonyl heterocycle. Lower and final examples often become nonaromatic polyenes or irregular ring systems. Ring_closure_rate remains substantial at 0.6034 to 0.9603, while aromatic_atom_rate varies from 0.1224 to 0.6621. Distinct seeds can remain in chemically different score neighbourhoods even when both contain nitrogen and rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring editing and apparent graph diversity do not consistently preserve useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements or reach independent credible cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer core replacements and ring transformations that preserve useful donor/acceptor, amine and aromatic relationships while accessing separate chemically credible families. Track retained chemical organization and core diversity rather than treating a new ring closure, altered atom symbol or new string as sufficient exploration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Cited fluoro-substituted polar chains, substituted saturated amine cores, hydroxylated aminal bridges and rearranged lactone-containing ring systems admit configurational alternatives. Imine-rich and polyunsaturated families also introduce geometric choices that are not defined in their cited structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted chemistry lacks explicit stereochemical control over saturated centres and adequate specification of many unsaturated or bridged geometries.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stereochemical and geometric alternatives explicit when changing a saturated centre, imine, alkene or ring junction, while preserving chemically credible connectivity. The evidence establishes missing representation; accepted feedback must determine whether particular configurations are useful.

nodes.method_name: NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals
nodes.method_thesis: Use NF-BO's SeqFlow mapping, exact left-inverse decoding, and token-adaptive trust-region search. Train a compact SELFIES flow on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Within each fresh objective session, adapt it using highly scored task-local sequences, re-encode all observations after updates, and fit a latent-space GP. Generate new latent proposals around scored observations by perturbing token blocks according to their estimated pointwise mutual information with the decoded sequence. Thompson sampling selects proposals for inverse-flow decoding. These mechanisms follow [NF-BO, Sections 4 and 5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.14889v1). Regenerate as needed to fill the evaluator-announced batch with distinct canonical molecules; no corpus molecules are ranked or retrieved. The hypothesis is that score-directed local search around exactly reconstructable observations finds improving structures efficiently enough to raise the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Exact reconstruction alone is not the objective. Useful flow training and surrogate prediction under the permitted preparation and feedback remain empirical prerequisites.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus, then starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that prior. The prior stays frozen. After each scored batch, the policy trains on the best-scoring half: its log probability for each elite's actual sampled SMILES is fitted toward the frozen prior's log probability plus sixty times the observed reward. Each update takes at most twelve clipped-gradient steps. The updated policy writes complete new SMILES token by token; chemical validation and canonical duplicate filtering retain a full batch of novel molecules. Training uses each scored batch once, and its sequence records are then discarded. Earlier high-reward examples consequently have no direct role in later updates.
approach.novelty: Add bounded historical elite replay. Keep the thirty-two highest-scoring previously selected elites, preserving their original SMILES and accepted scores. Each later update draws up to as many historical elites as current elites and trains on both groups with the Parent's existing likelihood target. This gives rare favorable examples repeated influence when subsequent batches have much weaker rewards. The lineage has tested only its current-batch root, so repeated training on historical elites is new here. Each replay uses the original serialization, making reuse of earlier feedback the single mechanism under test. The expected intermediate change is a measurable historical contribution to the policy gradient and improved fitting of those older examples' fixed targets.

nodes.hypothesis: Add a task-local, score-ranked memory of at most 32 previously selected elites and uniformly replay up to one historical elite per current elite, using each molecule's original accepted SMILES serialization and score in the unchanged Augmented Hill-Climb loss alongside the current batch elites.

finding_summary.headline: Elite replay changed learning in both replicas; historical target error fell in 278 of 280 updates
finding_summary.insights: The repeated result establishes that accepted historical information changes learning and is fitted again across seeds; the original activation was not peculiar to the screening run. It does not establish forgetting in the current-only algorithm or a reliable score advantage over it, because the supplied baseline is the same replay implementation on seed 0 and each replica used a separately prepared prior. Historical reward was stronger than current-elite reward in 150 of 280 new updates, including 42 of 56 median-similarity updates and 35 of 56 sitagliptin updates. Its pooled reward mean was nevertheless lower than that of current elites. Older elites therefore add stronger reward information in particular sessions, rather than being uniformly better training examples. Fitting these targets requires both likelihood directions: the historical sequence log likelihood rose by 2.530 on average when its target was above the starting value, and fell by 1.253 when the target was below it. Of the 1,400 exposures, 328 had positive log-probability targets, which cannot be attained. This inherited limitation remains even when replay works. Lower duplicate concentration did not recover the strongest zaleplon result. The molecular assessment points to different amide connectivity and substituent arrangements there, while finding continued narrow productive families, uncontrolled growth and unspecified stereochemistry elsewhere. Replay preserves accepted reward information but does not by itself preserve favorable chemical relationships during exploration. Matched current-only replicas would be needed to assess score benefit separately from prior and search variation.

molecular.headline: Conventional aromatic and cyclic-amine families, with missing stereochemistry and uneven control of size, connectivity and reactive substituents
molecular.overall_character: The supplied evidence covers seeds 1 and 2, using seed 0 of the same Algorithm Node as the baseline. All five tasks have trajectories, each containing 600 evaluated records including 580 optimizer proposals. The predominant chemistry is recognizable medicinal-chemistry material: indole carboxamides, anilino pyrimidines, aryl sulfonamides, piperazines and piperidines, fused carbonyl heterocycles and hydrazones. Related high-scoring series sit within a more diverse background. Structural diversity is moderate overall, with substantial scaffold variety on some tasks and concentration within a few favorable families on others. Ring-closure indicators span 0.9828–0.9983 and aromatic-atom indicators 0.9483–0.9966. These are fractions of SMILES containing those features, not aromatic atom fractions or measurements of three-dimensional shape. Mean SMILES lengths span 39.9–48.3, although the trajectories include much larger alkyl, peptide-like and densely fused structures. Most ordinary cores support plausible apparent makeability, but reactive variants and extreme size or polarity make overall drug-likeness moderate. Every stereocentre indicator is 0.0. This leaves configurations unspecified in substituted saturated rings, aminoaryl side chains and complex polycycles, despite those structures being represented. The output is not missing aromatic rings or basic amines as classes. Its gaps concern preserving favorable relationships between those features, controlling growth and polar-group additions, and producing defined, chemically tractable variants.

per_task.generated_character: The high group contains medium-sized ethyl/ethoxy indole carboxanilides, benzimidazole carboxamides with N-acyl saturated nitrogen rings, indole enone/sulfonamide compounds and diarylamine-linked aryl sulfonamides. These have conventional aromatic scaffolds and amide, sulfonamide, ether or trifluoromethyl substituents, with comparatively few strongly basic aliphatic centres. Mean SMILES length is 40.8, ring_closure_rate 0.9966 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9862. The familiar building blocks make most upper examples plausible synthetic targets, while large fused or duplicated scaffolds and very long chains appear at the low end.
liabilities: The indole enone family contains a conjugated ketone electrophile with unspecified double-bond geometry. A favorable score does not establish its stability or selectivity.
Long hydrophobic chains, duplicated aromatic cores and densely fused, multiply functionalized structures create substantial size or synthetic complexity without preserving favorable scores.
missing_features: The current high group does not reproduce the favorable amide N-alkylation and aryl-linker arrangement observed in the baseline; comparable changes around the same core would be more informative than the score-tied halogen series.
Controlled addition of carbonyl or other polar groups without disrupting size and attachment patterns remains uneven, as the low-scoring dimethylcarboxamide-containing final example illustrates.
Configurations of substituted saturated nitrogen rings are unspecified, although these files do not establish stereochemical sensitivity of the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The ethyl indole carboxanilide scores 0.4067656765249372 and its ethoxy relative 0.4064265251651748. The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 best at 0.5280588545286916 retained the indole carboxamide but used an N-methyl benzyl-nitrile substituent instead of the current direct N-aryl attachment. This points to amide connectivity and substituent arrangement as an unresolved chemical difference; the comparison does not isolate a requirement for the nitrile. A second family of indole enone/sulfonamides has exactly the same score, 0.3949199041196016, for terminal Cl, Br or F. In the diarylamine/sulfonamide family, the compact example scores 0.3900700429110833, while adding a dimethylcarboxamide substituent in the last proposal gives 0.016846474583107045. Larger highly connected or long-chain examples fall to 6.104593358645627e-24 and 6.925504833777315e-22, but the small dichloroaminopyridine is also low at 1.496608667066175e-13. The median is 0.106506. These observations favor a bounded scaffold and polar-group arrangement rather than maximum aromaticity, minimum size or a particular terminal halogen.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high family is dominated by anilino pyrimidines bearing aryl and trifluoromethyl or benzylamino substituents, attached to benzofuran, naphthalene or substituted phenyl systems. These are aromatic, nitrogen-containing screening-like frameworks with familiar amino and ether links. Seed 2 also explores aminoaryl esters, sulfonamides and more complex cyclic acetals. Mean SMILES length is 48.3, ring_closure_rate 0.9983, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9966 and halogen_rate 0.8483. The primary heteroaryl chemistry appears makeable, though extensive fluorination and linked aromatic rings give a large hydrophobic surface.
liabilities: The upper series can combine many aromatic rings and fluorinated substituents; solubility, conformational preferences and synthetic tractability are not given by the score.
A high acylhydrazone leaves hydrolytic stability and C=N geometry unresolved, and late N,O-acetal-like connections require chemical-form assessment.
Elemental fluorine is a reactive non-medicinal outlier despite its nonzero score.
missing_features: The connected anilino-azaaryl donor/acceptor arrangement is not consistently preserved when the output moves to aminoaryl esters, acetals or sulfone-containing alternatives.

Chemically comparable core and linker changes are needed to distinguish the favorable heteroaryl geometry from a general preference for highly fluorinated aromatic molecules; no unique required decoration is established.
The stereogenic aminoaryl side chains and cyclic acetals seen in the second trajectory lack configuration specification.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated benzofuran/anilino-pyrimidine scores 0.61192894944948, and the methoxynaphthyl analogue scores 0.6067590497737556. Benzylamino-substituted relatives remain near this upper group. The seed-0 best at 0.5913471190523991 was an amino-linked quinoline-like system with a nitroaryl acylhydrazone, so the replication uses a different linker/core arrangement while retaining connected azaaryl and amino features. The initial fused-dione ester scores 0.548381482770623 and the median is 0.545366. Low examples include aromatic carbon-bonded sulfones at 0.2707003622563395 and 0.2713068181818182, plus a morpholine/imine/sulfone compound at 0.2801857585139319. Thus aromaticity, fluorination or a nitrogen ring alone does not explain the favorable anilino-azaaryl arrangement. A late sulfonamide-containing aminoaryl structure scores 0.5616122965172838, so sulfur oxidation itself is not sufficient to explain the low carbon-bonded sulfones. The isolated proposal FF scores 0.5; this is elemental fluorine, not a medicinal organic scaffold, and demonstrates that a middling numerical value cannot be read as chemical quality.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high group is a coherent family of N-arylpiperazines connected by alkyl spacers to brominated indoles. Alkyl or alkoxy substitutions on the N-aryl ring and changes in spacer length occur repeatedly. These expose an aliphatic basic piperazine nitrogen in an aromatic environment. Seed 2 instead generates densely fused indole/aryl systems with tertiary cyclic or appended amines, sometimes including a ketone. Mean SMILES length is 44.0, ring_closure_rate 0.9879 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9672. The flexible piperazine family is generally synthetically recognizable; the complex fused family entails substantially more stereochemical and synthetic complexity.
liabilities: The high-scoring bromomethyl-substituted member contains a benzyl bromide, an electrophilic alkylating handle, yet scores 0.9999999997416186. This is a concrete example of chemical reactivity not being ruled out by the objective.

Several upper examples retain long flexible chains between aromatic and amine regions, while the second trajectory creates densely fused polycycles. Both require conformational or stereochemical characterization.
Heavy aromatic bromination and extensive hydrophobic surface remain physicochemical questions, rather than established benefits of the near-ceiling score.
missing_features: The favorable exposed-amine/aromatic arrangement is already present. What is missing in the fused series is explicit stereochemical definition of its multiple saturated ring junctions and substituted carbons.

The near-ceiling family does not demonstrate which spacer or peripheral substituent gives a materially distinct chemical advantage; tractable alternatives need assessment beyond numerical closeness to the score ceiling.
No additional obligatory target interaction can be inferred from the shown molecules and scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The propyl-substituted arylpiperazine linked to a bromoindole scores 0.9999999999666845. Multiple linker, aromatic-substitution and bromine-position variants also have scores extremely close to 1. The baseline best at 0.9999917871646155 paired an indoline/aryl region with an ethyl-linked piperidine, retaining exposed aliphatic amines in a different framework. Both sets therefore support the same broad amine-plus-aromatic arrangement. By contrast, a nitroaryl acid/amide heterocycle scores 1.8588450134335675e-05, an aromatic ester/amide scores 2.8794410596630625e-05, and an acylated/sulfonylated nitrogen structure scores 3.8021829379963674e-05. A tertiary aniline-containing example is also low at 6.624810470904373e-05, showing that nitrogen presence alone is insufficient. The median is 0.707754, and late seed-2 fused amine structures remain high, including 0.9899704115532137. The chemical association is strong, but these near-ceiling scores do not determine an exact spacer length, halogen pattern, conformation or experimental affinity.

per_task.generated_character: The high group spans an indole-containing fused/bridged lactam-sulfonamide, a very simple N-methyl-N-sulfonyl piperazine, aryl sulfonamides bearing benzylpiperazines, cyclic diones and carbamate-containing heteroarenes. This is a substantial range of size and ring complexity rather than a single scaffold. Mean SMILES length is 39.9, ring_closure_rate 0.9879 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9759. Most motifs are conventional, but the bridged high scorer and unusual sulfur or small reactive low-end fragments need more chemical scrutiny.
liabilities: The best fused/bridged scaffold requires stereochemical and synthetic-route definition, even though its component functional groups are familiar.
The low output includes a small organic azide, a highly halogenated electrophilic carbonyl fragment and an unusual nitrogen-oxide head group on a long chain.
A late piperazine carries a hydrogen-bearing sulfur oxide/hydroxy group whose chemical form is less straightforward than an ordinary sulfonamide.
missing_features: Consistent favorable placement of aromatic, carbonyl/sulfonyl and cyclic nitrogen groups remains unresolved across the many scaffolds; a simple piperazine already approaches the more elaborate upper structure.
The bridged lactam/sulfonamide high scorer has an unspecified stereogenic carbon. Configuration-sensitive alternatives are absent from the shown comparison.
The available scores do not identify a unique missing target-like ring system or justify adding rings indiscriminately.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The indole/lactam/cyclic-sulfonamide scores 0.21944544104637362, but the much simpler N-methyl-N-phenylsulfonyl piperazine already scores 0.20718664161756667. A larger aryl sulfonamide with benzylpiperazine scores 0.20289642340591482. Greater ring complexity is therefore not a general requirement. The seed-0 best at 0.20090425134085538 was an aryl/benzodioxole-substituted nitrogen heterocycle with a carbonyl, while the initial fused-dione ester scores 0.1678386594791329. The recurring favorable chemistry is an aromatic framework with a particular cyclic polar or sulfonamide/amine arrangement, not a single shared scaffold. At the low end, allyl azide scores 0.0, an N-hydroxy/trichloromethyl formamide scores 0.007693218186208301 and a small highly chlorinated enone scores 0.010594028769395466. A long fatty-acid-like nitrogen-oxide structure also scores only 0.019641313778463534. The median is 0.125545. Late charged heteroarenes and unusual sulfur-containing piperazines remain below the upper examples, showing that generic heteroatom, charge or nitrogen-ring addition is insufficient.

per_task.generated_character: The favorable structures include a compact N-rich fused bicyclic dicarbonyl heterocycle with an exocyclic imine, phenyl and benzyl groups, and dimethylaminoacetamide/furan-carboxamide-substituted anilines. Other upper examples use thiazole-fused diones, acylhydrazones and phenolic or methoxy aromatic groups. Mean SMILES length is 39.9, ring_closure_rate 0.9828 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9483. These are mostly recognizable small-molecule functional-group combinations, but the full population also contains very large peptide-like, polyether, polyol and heavily decorated structures.
liabilities: The best imino/dione structure has tautomeric-form questions, and the hydrazones introduce hydrolytic-stability and C=N-geometry questions.

Peptide-like boronic acids, long polyethers and highly oxygenated chains depart sharply from the compact favorable molecules. These extremes add substantial polarity, flexibility or synthetic complexity.
Very large amide/aryl assemblies can retain chemically familiar fragments while losing nearly all score, so ordinary fragment identity is not evidence of a well-balanced whole molecule.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently retain a favorable balance of size, polar-group density and attachment pattern when extending the compact high-scoring cores.
Chemically defined tautomeric and double-bond forms of the imino/dione and hydrazone structures are not established by their SMILES scores.
A particular missing basic amine, fluorinated fragment or target-like connection cannot be specified from these diverse high scorers; the output already supplies multiple relevant functional classes.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused imino/dicarbonyl compound scores 0.3108657757276207 at the final evaluation. The para dimethylaminoacetamide/furan-carboxamide aniline scores 0.28770317918999355 and its meta positional isomer 0.28307300457324674. These close relatives show that linkage placement can be varied within a favorable compact polar/aromatic neighborhood. The seed-0 best at 0.2932061327730367 used an N-acyl sulfonamide attached to a fused azaarene, another different arrangement of moderate size and polar groups. The current best lacks an exposed aliphatic basic amine, while the dimethylamino series has one; neither basicity nor a particular fluorinated group is a universal visible requirement. At the low end, a peptide-like boronic acid scores 5.3426487496943955e-90, a large amidine/amide/aryl assembly scores 6.4760197316862265e-80, and a relatively small polyhydroxy acid scores 1.059041359266943e-68. Size alone therefore does not explain the gradient; polar-group density and topology matter as well. The reported median is 0.000002, and late hydrazone extensions remain extremely low before the final compact high scorer. A familiar ring or amide by itself is not enough.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 across 580 optimizer proposals. Digest examples include a bridged indole/lactam/sulfonamide, aminoaryl side chains, cyclic acetals and densely fused tertiary-amine polycycles with stereogenic carbons. The simpler flexible arylpiperazine high family is largely achiral, so the omission should be tied to eligible structures rather than attributed to every high scorer.
transferable_gaps.gap: Configurationally complex saturated scaffolds are emitted without explicit stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable and preserve configurationally specified variants where stereocentres exist and evaluate them through current task-local observations. The files establish the omission but not its implementation cause or any objective-specific stereochemical sensitivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Mean SMILES lengths range from 39.9 to 48.3, while task maxima range from 84 to 107. Digest low examples include long hydrophobic chains, duplicated aromatic assemblies, a peptide-like boronic acid, an extended polyether and a polyhydroxy acid. A compact aryl sulfonamide scores 0.3900700429110833 while its dimethylcarboxamide-containing relative scores 0.016846474583107045; a small polyhydroxy acid also scores extremely poorly, showing that size reduction alone is insufficient.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently control appended size and polar-group density while retaining an otherwise favorable core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded changes to linker length, appendage size and polar-group count around observed useful molecules. Let local feedback select the appropriate balance; do not impose a universal preference for the smallest, least polar or least flexible compound, because favorable longer-spacer amine families are also present.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An indole enone/sulfonamide series has the same score, 0.3949199041196016, for Cl, Br and F. In contrast, the baseline indole N-methylbenzyl-nitrile amide at 0.5280588545286916 differs in attachment pattern from the current secondary arylamide family near 0.4068. Elsewhere, a simple N-methyl-N-sulfonyl piperazine at 0.20718664161756667 approaches a much more complex bridged structure at 0.21944544104637362. These examples do not support ring or heteroatom count alone as a useful chemical control.
transferable_gaps.gap: Peripheral analogue coverage is stronger than the demonstrated control of core attachment and nitrogen functional state across scaffold changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make controlled changes to amide N-substitution, aryl versus benzyl connection, cyclic nitrogen attachment and nearby carbonyl/sulfonyl placement available while retaining the surrounding core. Compare these chemical relationships using task-local observations rather than prescribing a particular amine state, terminal group or scaffold for all objectives.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An arylpiperazine/indole molecule containing a benzyl bromide scores 0.9999999997416186. The digest also includes elemental fluorine at 0.5, high-scoring conjugated enones or acylhydrazones, and late unusual sulfur oxide forms. These show that ordinary scaffold chemistry and a favorable numerical value can coexist with reactive or non-medicinal fragments.
transferable_gaps.gap: Numerically favorable refinement is not consistently accompanied by chemically conservative substituents and molecular forms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer tractable alternatives to reactive handles and preserve coherent hydrogen, valence and charge states within related scaffold families. Treat chemical-form plausibility separately from the scalar score, while avoiding blanket removal of all electrophilic, sulfur-containing or ionizable groups.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent prior on the original unlabeled molecular strings, samples training rows uniformly within length buckets, and keeps the checkpoint with the lowest ordinary heldout token loss. Each objective starts an adaptable copy while the prior stays fixed. Neural batches refresh a scored graph population; the first following graph batch protects a descendant of a fresh neural parent. A fingerprint posterior fit to accepted scores selects other offspring from temporary pools, and accepted graph trajectories feed trajectory-balance policy learning. This existing reciprocal search, including its posterior selection, receives the changed prior but is otherwise preserved.
approach.novelty: Give original training molecules carrying less frequent token contexts a bounded increase in sampling probability while retaining a uniform component for every row. Rarity is learned only from the unlabeled training split and is capped so isolated unusual contexts cannot dominate allocation. Unlike the earlier siblings, this intervention neither creates alternative strings nor selects checkpoints with a generative probe. It tests whether allocating more learning opportunities to underrepresented original contexts broadens usable prior support without changing online search.

nodes.hypothesis: Reallocate unlabeled prior-training rows within each inherited length bucket using an equal mixture of uniform sampling and capped inverse-document-frequency context-rarity weighting, while retaining original strings and the ordinary holdout checkpoint rule.

finding_summary.headline: Rare-context learning improved, but later validity fell and one replica ended early.
finding_summary.insights:
This establishes that extra exposure to existing rare token contexts can improve their heldout likelihood without improving average likelihood or adapted generation validity. The conditional result concerns only 306 rare-context targets across the three holdouts, about 0.052% of all heldout targets; there are no heldout contexts absent from training. It therefore supports learning of underrepresented existing syntax, while broad chemical support and unseen-context generalization remain open. Common contexts slightly deteriorated in every seed, and all update caps were reached, ruling out fewer training updates as the explanation for that tradeoff.

The molecular evidence further limits what the higher completed-replica scores mean. Conventional aromatic/amine and carbonyl families coexist with high-scoring peroxide/O–halogen variants, hydroxyallenes and strained closures; favorable scores do not show that those liabilities are necessary, since more conventional alternatives also score highly. The changed training distribution did not supply missing stereochemical examples. The early termination exposes a separate fragility in inherited graph canonicalization, whose source was unchanged; it does not invalidate the verified training allocation, but it prevents a complete reliability claim. A useful next question is how to retain the observed rare-context learning while preserving common-context performance and chemically credible generation, with the identity failure addressed as a separate online mechanism.
finding_summary.results:
Training consumed the intended redistribution in every seed: all 89,226 minibatches changed row membership, and mean capped rarity rose from 2.25875 under the paired uniform reference to 2.38357, a 5.53% increase. Rarity rose in all seven length buckets in every seed. Exposures to contexts below the training-frequency median increased about 1.86-fold. Independent evaluation of the selected checkpoints on identical holdout rows found lower rare-context token loss in all three seeds: pooled Parent loss 2.25659 fell to 1.85778. Common-context loss increased from 0.56370 to 0.56435; the recorded ordinary mean holdout loss increased slightly from 0.56458 to 0.56501. All preparations completed 29,742 steps, with mean preparation time rising from 259.5 to 368.4 seconds. Original strings, ordinary checkpoint selection and online search interfaces remained intact.

The generation outcome was less favorable. Across matched complete tasks, raw policy validity fell from 70.04% to 62.77%, although candidate-side duplicate rejection also fell. First-batch validity was 91.17% in the Parent and 89.67% in the child; later batches were substantially less valid and already reflected task feedback. The two fully completed replicas increased mean final Top-1 from 0.522200 to 0.576765, with paired gains of 0.035148 and 0.073981. Gains centered on sitagliptin and one deco-hop replica, while other task comparisons were mixed. The third zaleplon task stopped after 120 of 300 evaluations when repeated canonicalization of a ring-closure offspring alternated aromatic representations and tripped the inherited trajectory-identity check. Fourteen of fifteen tasks completed, so no complete three-seed child macro result is available.
