molecular.headline: Rich ring chemistry includes hydroxyallenes, bridged amines, thionoesters, and high-scoring peroxide/O–F and strained ring variants.
molecular.overall_character: All available trajectories were read: 4,320 child rows, including 4,170 optimizer proposals, and 4,500 Parent rows, including 4,350 proposals. Coverage is incomplete for zaleplon_mpo: child seeds 0 and 1 have 300 rows each, while seed 2 ends at evaluation 120 and its supplied summary is buggy. Its molecular description therefore covers 720 rows and 690 optimizer proposals, compared with 900 and 870 in the Parent; nothing is inferred about the missing 180 evaluations. The other four tasks each supply all 900 rows and 870 proposals. Every observed child optimizer SMILES parses in the supplied RDKit environment. The repertoire is ring-rich, with aromatic and partly saturated heterocycles, aryl amines, carbonyl groups, bridged amines and sulfur-containing groups. Digest ring-closure rates are 0.9812–0.9908 and aromatic-marker rates 0.8333–0.9805; these are string-presence counters rather than atom fractions or guarantees of credible ring geometry. Read-only RDKit median heavy-atom counts are 24.5, 38, 30, 32 and 25 in the supplied task order. Conventional motifs coexist with hydroxyallenes, O–F bonds, peroxide/peroxyhalogen groups, short closures across aromatic frameworks and highly elaborated linked molecules. All digest stereocentre rates are 0.0; unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 196 of 690 first-task proposals and 180, 608, 501 and 441 of the 870 proposals in the remaining tasks, with assigned centres in none. These output observations support mixed chemical plausibility and uneven useful-core coverage; they do not establish the cause of the incomplete execution or whether any algorithmic mechanism activated.

per_task.generated_character: This assessment covers the 720 observed rows, including only 120 rows from seed 2. Seed 0 favors a benzofuran-like aromatic core attached to pyridyl and saturated diaza-ring groups, with a hydroxyallene side chain in the leader. That molecule has 24 heavy atoms and four rings, three perceived as aromatic. Other high neighbors contain an aminocyclopentyl substituent and a carboxylic acid on a fused or rearranged ring framework. The observed seed-2 family is more conventional acetyl/dimethyl indole carboxamide chemistry with a fluorophenyl or chlorophenyl amide. Thus aromatic nitrogen, amines, carbonyls and ring diversity are present. Parent leaders included biaryl pyrazole/acetanilide and quinoline/urea structures, with an indole-amide branch as well. The child median is 24.5 heavy atoms and three rings, but its raw scaffold and feature counts cannot be treated as complete three-seed coverage because the Parent supplied more observations.
liabilities: The leader contains a hydroxyallene, and its neighbors include sulfur- or fluorine-substituted cumulenes. The digest cumulated-double-bond marker rate is 0.0594; actual persistence and reactivity of these proposed forms are unmeasured.
Some favorable acid/amine structures use a contracted four-membered ring or other rearranged fused connectivity. Parseability does not establish low strain or a practical synthesis.
The low tail includes a small cyclic peroxide and very large polyene or polar assemblies; these depart substantially from the moderate-sized high families.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary alternatives that retain the favorable aryl/amine/oxygen-ring arrangement while varying the hydroxyallene or rearranged ring geometry are not established as a coherent high-level series. The conventional indole-amide examples show that unusual cumulene chemistry is not the only productive observed family.
Explicit configurations are absent from substituted saturated-ring and fused-ring variants. No preferred stereoisomer is identified by the available rows.
Complete chemical coverage of the third replica is unavailable. Any conclusion about absent core families or final chemistry must remain limited to its first 120 evaluations.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The hydroxyallene/benzofuran-like leader scores 0.4412371986661207, a sulfur-substituted hydroxyallene relative 0.4300843748877827, and a fluorinated pyridyl relative 0.427264458706691. An aminocyclopentyl/carboxylic-acid structure scores 0.43351949803907636 and a related oxygen-ring structure 0.432935295928208. The acetyl indole carboxamide reaches 0.4156220505432479 with either fluorine or chlorine on the amide-linked phenyl ring. A late thionocarbonyl replacement gives 0.3953519239480604, while adding a fluorobenzyl appendage in another late relative gives only 0.01212896246612932. These observations support particular connected aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements rather than indiscriminate elaboration. Small fragments, a cyclic peroxide and a long peroxide-bearing polyene appear at 0.0, and a large polar assembly scores 2.640871328396657e-59. The observed digest median is 0.138412; the missing seed-2 tail is not assumed to share that distribution.

per_task.generated_character: The pooled leaders are seed-1 aminoquinazoline-like structures bearing an oxygen-fluorine substituent and peroxide, peroxyhalogen or oxygen/sulfur attachments. Their aryl partner contains an extra short closure across the nominal aromatic framework; RDKit identifies two four-membered rings in the leading 23-heavy-atom molecule, alongside the two six-membered aza-aromatic rings. This is not an ordinary phenyl-substituted quinazoline despite the familiar-looking aromatic SMILES. A separate high example has a more conventional substituted aminoquinazoline/aryl-ether framework with a thiophene-linked oxime ether. Other seeds explore larger nitro-containing heteroaromatic assemblies. The child median is 38 heavy atoms and five rings, compared with 36 and four in the Parent, and 177 of 870 proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms versus 128 Parent proposals. Parent high families also combined aminoheteroaromatics and carbonyl/imine linkers, but the new leading neighborhood prominently exhibits peroxide/O–F and short-ring chemistry.
liabilities: O–O single bonds occur in 66 of 870 child proposals versus five Parent proposals; O–halogen bonds occur in 54 versus seven. Leading cited molecules directly contain O–F and O–O–halogen connections.

The high family with two four-membered rings formed by a short aromatic-framework closure has major geometric and synthetic questions. Ring-closure markers alone do not establish conventional aromatic ring systems.

The full set includes very large linked molecules, reaching 114 heavy atoms. Their extensive aromatic/heteroaromatic assembly and charged groups leave physical-property balance and synthesis unestablished.
missing_features: Matched, synthetically credible alternatives preserving the useful aza-aromatic/donor/aryl arrangement are not established for the leading peroxide/short-ring family. A different conventional high example shows that the upper score region is not restricted to that problematic connectivity.
Controlled independent changes to linker geometry, ring size and peripheral oxygen functionality are underrepresented among the near-identical leaders.

The output does not demonstrate a uniquely missing target functional group. Its visible limitation is chemically credible realization of useful arrangements, rather than a general shortage of heteroaromatics.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The O–F/peroxide leader and several peroxy-chlorine, O–S and alkyl variants all score 0.8796240145542753. The corresponding methoxy/O–F relative scores 0.8710847975553858, and the distinct, more conventionally connected oxime-ether/aryl-ether example scores 0.8713274281080406. The narrow upper spread does not establish that a peroxide, peroxyhalogen bond or the unusually short closure is necessary for a favorable score. In contrast, the aryl sulfone/chloroketone low example scores 0.2609581835714912 and a much larger polar heterocycle 0.30152798326615987. A late nitro/heteroaromatic assembly scores 0.6170311056359716, while an extremely elaborated linked/fused assembly scores 0.5932862873991009. The digest median is 0.581171. The gradient favors particular connected aminoaza-aromatic arrangements and tolerates chemically concerning replacements; it is not evidence of those replacements being practical chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The high seed-2 family combines a bridged saturated tertiary-amine core fused to a pyrrole with a phenethyl aryl substituent. Alkyl chains on nitrogen, aromatic fluorine/chlorine and linker length vary around that arrangement. The leader has 24 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, with two unassigned tetrahedral centres. Seed 1 also produces arylpiperazines with aminoalkyl substituents and fused aza-aromatic partners, while seed 0 contains linked saturated nitrogen rings and halogenated aromatics. These preserve the broad aromatic/basic-amine chemistry already seen in the Parent, but change its leading shapes and linkers. The child median is 30 heavy atoms and four rings versus 28 and four in the Parent. Its low charged-marker rate, 0.0264, does not indicate a shortage of potentially basic amines: many are written in their neutral form.
liabilities: Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 608 of 870 proposals, including two in the leading molecule. This limits interpretation of the bridged-core geometry.
Longer nitrogen substituents, repeated aromatic groups and new heteroatom ring connections may change basicity, flexibility or reactivity; the molecular score does not measure those properties.
Several related structures are recognizable amine architectures, but the more elaborate bridges and short closures lack supplied synthetic or conformational evidence.
missing_features: No additional required group can be identified from scores already near the upper limit; saturated basic centres and aromatic surfaces are present.
Configurationally specified bridged-amine variants are absent, even in the leading family. The data do not establish a preferred configuration.
Linker, ring and heteroatom edits do not consistently preserve the useful amine geometry and electronic environment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-butyl bridged amine scores 0.9999989512281267; N-propyl and fluorophenyl relatives each score 0.9999987410495211. A longer aryl linker gives 0.9999981580921362. These tiny near-limit differences do not establish a required alkyl length or halogen. Parent aryl/amine structures already reached 0.9999986918258995. The aminoalkyl arylpiperazine family reaches 0.9999825001153204, supporting another whole-molecule realization of accessible amines and aromatic surfaces. A late ring-expanded N–O-connected relative scores 0.321880221646489, and a sulfur-ring/fluoromethyl relative scores 0.7295970738860437; several features differ, so these are not isolated oxygen or sulfur effects. The sulfone/chloroketone low example scores 8.483379224649191e-05 and a carbonyl-rich nitro hydrazide 0.00014488129305738882. The observed gradient concerns the complete amine/aryl/geometry arrangement rather than nitrogen count alone.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains a diaryl fused nitrogen/carbonyl framework whose dicarbonyl-ring nitrogen is connected through an N–N bond to N-methylpiperazine. Methoxy, isopropyl, aldehyde and extra ring-fusion variants decorate the aromatic portion. The leader has 37 heavy atoms and five rings, including a seven-membered carbonyl-containing ring. A separate near-high example is a smaller carbonyl aza-heteroaromatic/piperazine structure with a compact sulfur/oxygen ring system. Other seeds generate contracted unsaturated nitrogen rings and large bridged amine/carbonyl assemblies. The child median is 32 heavy atoms and five rings, compared with 36 and five in the Parent, whose leaders likewise combined elaborate carbonyl heterocycles with saturated nitrogen rings. Familiar amine/carbonyl ingredients are abundant, but their attachment chemistry and fused geometry are frequently complicated.
liabilities: The leading dicarbonyl-imide-like N–N attachment, aldehyde-bearing variants and extra small ring closures merit individual chemical assessment rather than being treated as ordinary peripheral decoration.
O–halogen bonds occur in 134 of 870 child proposals versus 63 Parent proposals. Several late cited assemblies carry O–F directly on an aromatic oxygen substituent.
Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 501 proposals. The leading isopropyl example itself has no detected tetrahedral centre, but many aldehyde-substituted, fused or bridged neighbors do.
missing_features: Compact, chemically coherent alternatives that retain useful aromatic/carbonyl/amine relationships are not consistently developed; near-equal smaller examples show that extensive fusion is not the only observed route to the high neighborhood.
The electronic and geometric consequences of attaching piperazine through an N–N bond versus ordinary aryl or carbon links are not established as a controlled chemical series.
Stereochemically specified saturated junctions and constrained-ring variants are absent from the output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxy/isopropyl diaryl dicarbonyl/piperazine leader scores 0.20299778547953037; an aldehyde-bearing relative scores 0.2019128097982617, and replacing methoxy by methyl gives 0.20101797606311947. Another fused-ring variant scores 0.20088496007425613. A smaller sulfur/oxygen heterocycle-bearing carbonyl/piperazine structure scores 0.19897566548044113, close to those more elaborate relatives. The upper tail therefore does not establish a need for maximal size, aldehyde addition or extra ring fusion. Late highly elaborated O–F-containing assemblies score 0.14137309073805335 and 0.1855727066064119. Tiny fragments including methane and dihalogen/peroxide molecules score 0.0; fluoromethane and methylamine score 0.008773280079294957. The digest median is 0.15629. Connected aromatic, carbonyl and nitrogen environments are supported, while the precise missing feature behind the modest observed upper values is not identifiable.

per_task.generated_character: Two quite different families occupy the upper digest. Seed 1 produces an N-methylaminomethyl-substituted azetidine attached through its nitrogen to a fluorinated, partly saturated fused oxygen/nitrogen heterocyclic network; the leader has 25 heavy atoms, five perceived rings and three unassigned tetrahedral centres. Ring expansion to a sulfur-containing ring or pyrrolidine gives related examples. Seed 0 instead favors a fluorinated, partly unsaturated nitrogen/carbon bicyclic system carrying thionoester groups and an amide-linked side chain. The leading example in that family has 29 heavy atoms and two rings, with no perceived aromatic ring. C=S functionality occurs in 209 of 870 child proposals versus 32 Parent proposals for this task. The Parent high chemistry included amino/hydrazino triazolyl azetidines and nitroso/carbonyl nitrogen rings. The new output changes both core geometry and sulfur/carbonyl chemistry, while retaining substantial chemical liabilities. The child median is 25 heavy atoms and four rings versus 24 and three in the Parent.
liabilities: The fused fluorinated heterocyclic network and substituted azetidine combine geometric complexity with unspecified configuration; a parsed graph does not establish an accessible synthesis.
Multiple thionoesters or other C=S groups, sometimes adjacent to carbonyl groups and fluorinated oxygen-linked substituents, raise reactivity and stability questions that the score does not resolve.
The wider set includes peroxide substitutions and occasional very large polar or aromatic assemblies. Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 441 of 870 proposals and assigned centres in none.
missing_features: Configurationally defined versions of the aminomethyl azetidine and its fluorinated polycyclic attachment are absent. Their observed scores cannot identify which of the possible configurations is appropriate.

Chemically stable, well-characterized alternatives preserving the thionoester-family polar arrangement are not established by the trajectory; a separate amine/polyheterocycle family shows that extensive C=S chemistry is not the only favorable observed chemistry.
Core and substituent changes do not consistently retain the compact useful arrangement, and the observed families do not identify a unique missing target heterocycle or amine placement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact azetidine/amine/polyheterocycle leader scores 0.5273514746694421. A sulfur-ring-expanded relative scores 0.5196824227182583, another changed ring system 0.5081965087232951, and a pyrrolidine relative 0.48440434571016927. These whole-molecule comparisons suggest a specific compact amine/heterocycle arrangement without proving an isolated preferred ring size. The thionoester-rich nitrogen-ring family reaches 0.5066662778005617, with related fluoromethyl thionoester and thionocarbonyl variants at 0.49357812339608453 and 0.4834063542846959. Their scores do not establish that C=S is a necessary or chemically robust replacement for C=O. A large polar peptide-like assembly scores 0.0, and large polyaryl or polyfunctional structures give 1.0871796166883121e-73 and 1.0290786123867312e-65. A late different fused nitrogen-ring/ether system scores 0.31955621409660756, while a peroxide-bearing relative in that late family scores 0.22752393925311112. The digest median is 0.015275. The visible preference is for specific compact functional-group arrangements, not arbitrary nitrogen, fluorine or sulfur enrichment.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited structures near 0.8796240145542753 combine O–F, peroxide or peroxyhalogen functionality with a useful aminoaza-aromatic framework; a more conventional oxime-ether/aryl-ether example reaches 0.8713274281080406. Elsewhere, high families include hydroxyallenes, dicarbonyl N–N attachments and multiple thionoesters. C=S functionality occurs in 209 of 870 proposals in one set versus 32 Parent proposals. Favorable observations thus coexist with chemically sensitive alternatives, without establishing those alternatives as necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically credible functional-group bonding within favorable molecular neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent functional-group alternatives that preserve useful surrounding aryl, donor, acceptor and amine relationships. Distinguish carbonyl from thionocarbonyl, ordinary ether from peroxide or O–halogen, and carbon-linked amines from N–N or N–O attachments. Use current-session accepted feedback to compare actual alternatives rather than equating parser validity or a high score with chemical persistence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited aminoaza-aromatic leader contains two four-membered rings produced by a short closure across its aryl partner. Other high examples include an azetidine with a fluorinated polyheterocyclic attachment, a bridged pyrrole/tertiary-amine core and rearranged carbonyl-ring systems. Every digest gives stereocentre_rate 0.0; unassigned centres occur in 196 of 690 observed first-task proposals and 180, 608, 501 and 441 of 870 proposals in the remaining sets, with assigned centres in none.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring topology and stereochemical representation do not provide adequate control of the geometry of complex output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support credible ring closure, expansion and contraction together with explicit configurations for existing stereogenic centres. Keep geometry, saturation and connectivity changes distinguishable so accepted feedback can evaluate defined chemical alternatives. The current absence of specification does not establish a benefit for any chosen configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited low tails include methane, dihalogen/peroxide fragments, a cyclic peroxide and long polyene or polar assemblies. One complete set has 177 of 870 proposals above 50 heavy atoms versus 128 Parent proposals and reaches 114 heavy atoms. Yet smaller carbonyl/piperazine examples can sit near much larger relatives in another upper tail, and some larger heteroaromatics are favorable. The evidence therefore supports context-dependent useful size rather than a universal small-molecule rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Some size-changing proposals fragment away or overbuild useful connected molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable growth, contraction and linker changes that preserve a coherent accepted core and its useful local polar-group arrangement. Avoid relying on tiny fragments or repeated assembly of whole motifs, and let accepted observations determine the appropriate complexity for the current session.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest repeatedly revisits hydroxyallene/heteroaryl amines, aminoaza-aromatic peroxide/short-ring variants, bridged aryl amines, dicarbonyl/piperazine assemblies and aminomethyl or thionoester-rich heterocycles. Different seeds access different families, but much of each upper neighborhood changes peripheral atoms or ring closures. Nonchiral Murcko counts in the four fully covered child sets are 713, 523, 702 and 545; such graph counts include local edits and highly elaborated assemblies, and the partially observed first set cannot be treated as full-panel coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful core diversity remains uneven within the leading neighborhoods despite a varied overall ring repertoire.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to multiple accepted chemical families and enable core replacements that retain useful spatial and electronic relationships among aromatic groups, amines, donors and acceptors. Assess core and functional-group diversity directly rather than relying on a new string, peripheral decoration or an additional ring closure as evidence of a useful new family.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a SELFIES variational autoencoder on the permitted unlabeled corpus and freezes it. A complete Gaussian state contains both the semantic latent and the variables that determine categorical decoding, so each state produces one reproducible molecule. During an objective, a Gaussian process learns from the fingerprints and scores of that session's accepted molecules. Parallel pCN chains sample the Gaussian prior weighted by the GP probability of beating the best observed score. The Parent randomly takes a novel batch from retained chain states and submits the exact molecules used for prediction.
approach.novelty: Add empirical elite-threshold conditioning: after each feedback message, use the 90th percentile of accepted scores as the probability threshold. This asks whether a molecule can enter the observed upper score region even when an isolated record lies far above the decoder's predicted scores. The proposed causal change is a less extreme threshold that changes which pCN transitions are accepted. This lineage has only its root so far; its incumbent threshold is the direct comparator, and no sibling has tried an elite-percentile threshold.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the observed-maximum threshold in the Parent's GP-probability pCN target with the linearly interpolated empirical 90th percentile of unique accepted current-session scores, so the same prior-preserving sampler conditions on entering an observed elite score region instead of exceeding an isolated incumbent.

finding_summary.headline: Elite conditioning changed sampling but lowered the single-seed mean score to 0.391
finding_summary.insights:
An extreme incumbent tail can be relaxed enough to materially redirect sampling without improving record discovery. The paired receipts rule out an inactive cutoff, unaccepted labels or prediction/submission mismatch as explanations for this score result. Lowering the cutoff changed relative preferences: it accepted 5,401 moves the incumbent rule would reject, and rejected 1,103 moves that rule would accept. The effect therefore includes which molecular transitions are preferred, as well as the overall acceptance rate.

On the two sessions that motivated the intervention, the elite target became permissive: mean retained-minus-prior log elite probability was only 0.087 for drd2_docking and 0.021 for sitagliptin_mpo. Their scores moved in opposite directions. This narrows the next question to how much record-seeking pressure is useful, and whether the GP can distinguish useful molecular arrangements within the decoder's reachable space. The molecular assessment finds abundant rings and familiar medicinal fragments, but inconsistent whole-molecule assembly and control of functional-group placement in both runs; threshold relaxation leaves those generator limitations open. These chemistry observations suggest further hypotheses, not a proven cause of the score loss. One seed establishes the logged behavioral effect but cannot establish the reliability of the score tradeoff, GP calibration or equilibrium mixing.
finding_summary.results:
The intended threshold and sampling effects occurred. All 145 fitted cutoffs exactly matched the accepted-score 90th percentile and lay below the incumbent. On 4,640 identical prior probes, the mean standardized threshold deficit fell from 5.193 to 1.057, and the fraction more than three posterior standard deviations below the cutoff fell from 66.49% to 0.43%. Retained states showed the same direction in every round. Replaying both rules with the same proposals and random draws changed 6,504 of 36,800 accept/reject decisions (17.67%); every actual update followed the elite rule. All 1,450 submitted molecules retained exact prediction identity and filled the budget.

The seed-0 mean final-best score fell from 0.433167 to 0.390832, a decrease of 0.042335. The largest change was drd2_docking, which fell from 0.867722 to 0.572905. median_2 fell from 0.171784 to 0.167839. Gains on zaleplon_mpo (0.340635 to 0.375713), deco_hop (0.573265 to 0.574331) and sitagliptin_mpo (0.212429 to 0.263373) did not offset those losses. This is confirmed mechanism activation with a negative score result on the one available seed.

molecular.headline: Abundant rings and medicinal fragments coexist with awkward connectivity and no defined stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers every supplied objective for seed 0: each digest contains 300 evaluated structures, including 290 optimizer proposals. The output is structurally broad, spanning ordinary aryl heterocycles, saturated amine rings, fused and bridged systems, lactams, ethers and esters, alongside long polyenes and unusually connected nitrogen, sulfur and phosphorus groups. Most molecules have a substantial medicinal-chemistry-sized skeleton, but very small fragments and much larger, highly decorated structures also occur. Ring chemistry is abundant: the per-task ring_closure_rate spans 0.9828 to 0.9966, and aromatic_atom_rate spans 0.7793 to 0.8897. These are SMILES presence rates, not perceived ring counts or fractions of atoms that are aromatic. Mean SMILES lengths span 44.6 to 46.4; text length is not molecular weight. Every stereocentre_rate is 0.0 despite structures containing potentially stereogenic tetrahedral centres. The lack of stereochemical specification does not imply that all structures are planar. The parent trajectories show the same broad mixture of recognizable fragments and awkward assemblies. There are chemically interpretable individual proposals, but broad structural diversity and accepted SMILES do not establish a feasible synthesis, an ordinary closed-shell state, or stability. Score-gradient readings below are associations within these trajectories; they do not identify hidden target structures or prove that any particular functional group caused a score.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring proposals are mostly moderately sized ring assemblies with aromatic carbon, ring nitrogen or oxygen, and limited peripheral substitution. Evaluation 149, score 0.37571328785207686, joins a fused N-methyl N/O aromatic system to an alcohol-bearing side chain and a fluorinated unsaturated aza ring with an amino substituent. Evaluation 185, score 0.33690534619560325, is a much more conventional methylimidazole bearing benzyl and chlorobenzyl-thioether substituents. The initial trimethoxyindole carboxamide at evaluation 9 already scores 0.3051048083696145. The low end includes an extensively benzylated, peptide-like amide assembly with unusual sulfur at evaluation 11 and a large polyunsaturated ring assembly at evaluation 179. The late set still mixes exotic phosphorus/sulfur structures with the aryl-thiophene thioamide and unsaturated lactone at evaluation 299. Synthetic plausibility is therefore mixed rather than uniformly poor.
liabilities: The high-scoring fused imine structure at evaluation 110 includes a small, densely connected nitrogen ring; several other high structures also have unusual unsaturated ring closures that complicate a plausible synthesis.

Evaluations 223 and 268 carry conjugated aldehyde substituents. Evaluation 299 combines an aldehyde, thioamide and unsaturated lactone, so a useful score does not remove potential chemical reactivity.
The late phosphorus species at evaluation 295 and bracketed hydrogen-bearing sulfur at evaluation 296 are unusual valence environments for an ordinary medicinal series.
missing_features: The set lacks consistent elaboration of the compact, chemically conventional heteroaromatic arrangements already represented by the imidazole and initial indole carboxamide; many alternatives change ring topology and appendage size at the same time.

No uniquely required absent functional group can be inferred. The evident gap is reproducible control of scaffold size and substituent polarity, rather than absence of rings, nitrogen, carbonyls or halogens.
Configurations are unspecified at the alcohol-bearing and other tetrahedral centres; the trajectory provides no stereochemical comparison from which to infer a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best score is 0.37571328785207686 and the digest median is 0.011458. The larger, flexible amide-rich structure at evaluation 11 scores 4.062031856671369e-45, while evaluation 179 scores 9.963756221572277e-36. Together with the high aromatic examples, this supports a preference for a bounded scaffold size and a coherent aromatic/heteroatom arrangement over indiscriminate molecular growth. Smallness alone is insufficient: the initial alkyl bromide scores 8.305895500294491e-10. Carbonyls are not an established requirement because the best proposal lacks one. The fluoro/chloro matched pair at evaluations 223 and 268 has the identical score 0.3365357296869613, so halogen identity is not a differentiating signal in that pair. Parent n-a08278654dda reaches 0.340634631669846 with an aryl-substituted diazacycle bearing a small N/O ring; the child maximum has a more fused aromatic core, while the parent and child share the 0.33966649739182625 sulfur-containing heterocycle at evaluation 111. The higher maximum does not coincide with removal of questionable ring connectivity.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end is rich in aromatic and heteroaromatic rings with multiple nitrogen functions, usually on moderately sized to larger scaffolds. Evaluation 247, score 0.5743310208126858, contains linked and fused aza-aromatic systems joined through an extended unsaturated N-N-containing segment. Evaluation 253, score 0.5664592760180995, has a recognizable aryl amide and indole, but its intervening carbon also bears a nitroso group. Evaluation 191 combines a biphenyl amide with imine/hydrazone chemistry, while evaluation 218 combines an aryl amide, a saturated diazacycle, a thiourea and a fused N/O heteroaromatic ring. Familiar synthetic fragments are present, but the output does not define a consistently straightforward series. The low examples include unsaturated sulfone-linked rings, a saturated cyclic sulfone with a fused N/O ring system, and the morpholine-containing sulfone at evaluation 299.
liabilities: Nitroso substitution at evaluation 253, extended imine/hydrazone connectivity at evaluations 247 and 191, and the allyl thioether/thiourea combination at evaluation 218 warrant chemical scrutiny before treating these as ordinary stable analogues.

The final evaluation-296 structure has a very elaborate polycyclic assembly containing bracketed hydrogen-bearing sulfur, ester/amide groups and a carboxylic acid; a recognizable morpholine appendage does not make the full assembly straightforward to synthesize.
missing_features: The upper structures suggest value in specific aromatic nitrogen and donor/acceptor arrangements, but systematic chemically stable versions of those arrangements are missing from the bounded high-scoring set.

The evidence cannot identify a missing target decoration or a required scaffold replacement: broad structural classes already overlap in score, and the apparent sulfone association has a strong parent counterexample.
Defined stereochemistry is absent even in substituted indole side chains and saturated fused systems.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest median is 0.520459. Aromatic nitrogen-containing assemblies at evaluations 247, 191 and 158 sit above the nonaromatic or less aromatic sulfone-rich structures at evaluations 50, 170 and 299, whose scores are 0.25758568374594853, 0.26375771547557075 and 0.26539368531376917. Yet the tiny propionitrile at evaluation 41 still scores 0.5, and the extended polyene/amide structure at evaluation 99 scores 0.5609057782404998. Thus the narrow upper score differences do not establish a general size penalty, and the low sulfone examples do not establish that sulfones themselves are disfavored. In fact, parent n-a08278654dda's maximum, 0.5732649174777824 at evaluation 218, is an aryl sulfone attached to a nitrogen-rich heterocyclic assembly. The child maximum replaces that chemistry with a more extensively conjugated aza-ring assembly, without a clear improvement in apparent synthetic plausibility. The shared evaluation-158 structure scores 0.5644679320458192 in both trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: The useful upper examples combine aromatic surfaces with nitrogen-containing linkers or saturated nitrogen rings. Evaluation 87, score 0.572904722089471, is an arylpiperazine connected to an N-hydroxy, unsaturated amino fragment and a phosphine-substituted phenyl group. Evaluation 29, score 0.31273900914359654, carries a dimethylaminopropylamino chain on a methoxybenzene fused to an unsaturated four-membered carbocycle; the small ring is chemically consequential. Evaluation 18 contains a tetrahydroisoquinoline-like tertiary amine, and evaluation 135 combines a secondary amino linker, an aryl ether, a pyridine and an oxime. The low end contains aryl imines, amides, conjugated nitrogen systems and thioethers without an equivalent exposed saturated amine arrangement. The overall output still spans small fragments, ordinary medium-sized scaffolds and much larger polyunsaturated assemblies.
liabilities: The best proposal contains an arylphosphine and an N-hydroxy unsaturated amino unit. Their possible chemical liabilities are separate from the supplied score.

Evaluation 29 has an unusual fused unsaturated four-membered ring; evaluation 255 adds a pyridinium group and an amino carbon attached to pyrrolidine, giving a different charge and aminal environment from a simple tertiary amine.
Hydrazone-like connectivity, nitro groups and extended unsaturation remain in late proposals; the broad output does not establish a stable or synthetically coherent amine series.
missing_features: Reliable construction of accessible aliphatic amine centres at controlled positions relative to aromatic surfaces is underdeveloped. Such centres are present, so this is a problem of their arrangement and recurrence, not absolute absence.

Chemically uncomplicated versions of the useful aryl/amine arrangements are not consistently represented among the strongest child examples: phosphine, N-O, oxime and unusual small-ring features accompany them.

The observed cationic or nitrogen-rich structures do not by themselves specify a useful protonation state; amide, imine, aromatic and saturated amine nitrogen must remain chemically distinct in this reading.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best score is 0.572904722089471, but the digest median is 0.007702. The amine-bearing structures at evaluations 29, 18 and 135 score 0.31273900914359654, 0.2586499693063822 and 0.21811628298646404, whereas the aryl imine at evaluation 212 scores 0.00011879516001877162 and the simple phenoxypropyl amide at evaluation 55 scores 0.00033303319833196673. This supports an association with the chemical state and placement of nitrogen near aromatic groups, rather than nitrogen count alone. It is not sufficient: the final N-N-linked diazacycle at evaluation 299 scores only 0.0014980745212506842. per_task.generated_character: The stronger proposals combine multiple rings with carbonyl-containing or ether-containing motifs: lactams, esters, cyclic amide/urea-like units, aryl ethers and oxygenated aromatic rings. Evaluation 257, score 0.16273417606729546, is an elaborate polycyclic amine/imine and lactone assembly with a dihydroxybenzene element. The late evaluation-295 structure, score 0.16095095675340096, is a more compact N-methyl pyrrole fused to a lactam ring, with a phenyl substituent and an oxazoline ring. Evaluation 242 is a benzene-fused medium-ring lactam bearing a methyl ester and benzyl substituent; evaluation 151 is an oxygen-linked aromatic cyclic ketone assembly. The fixed initial structure at evaluation 7 contains a fused nitrogen heterocycle with carbonyls, phenyl substitution and a hydroxybenzoate ester, and remains the highest-scoring structure in the child trajectory. At the other extreme are formaldehyde and a long acyclic brominated polyene containing multiple nitrogen linkages.
liabilities: Evaluation 257 obtains an upper-set score with a complicated bridged ring system and an imine; this is less straightforward medicinal chemistry than its recognizable amine, phenol and ester fragments imply.
The acyclic evaluation-116 structure combines extensive unsaturation, bromination and N-N linkages. Evaluation 80 has adjacent positively charged nitrogen atoms in an unusual ring system.

The final evaluation-296 polycycle remains large and densely connected, with several imine-containing rings; late output is not uniformly represented by the more conventional lactam at evaluation 295.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent preservation and controlled variation of the organized aromatic/heterocyclic and carbonyl/ether arrangements already visible in the initial and stronger generated molecules.
Ring and oxygen atoms are plentiful; the unresolved feature is their specific connectivity and spacing, which the score comparisons cannot reduce to a single required heterocycle or carbonyl count.
Potentially stereogenic benzylic and ring-junction centres, including that in evaluation 295, remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial evaluation-7 score is 0.1678386594791329; no child proposal exceeds it. The best generated score is 0.16273417606729546 and the digest median is 0.109215. The low formaldehyde score of 0.008773280079294957 and acyclic polyene score of 0.015539494866471998 contrast with the ring-rich, oxygenated upper structures. The latter low example is not merely too small, supporting an association with organized ring and functional-group topology. Carbonyls are common in the upper set but not obligatory: the aryl-ether/imidazole structure at evaluation 248 scores 0.1566926618156574. Parent n-a08278654dda reaches 0.1717839775079566 with an aromatic, oxygenated polycycle containing several amide carbonyls. The child reproduces the parent's evaluation-260 polycycle at its evaluation 257 with the same 0.16273417606729546 score. This looks like broad coverage of the same oxygenated ring chemistry, with additional unrelated structures rather than evidence for a new missing functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest proposals are moderately sized but chemically varied: an N/O polycyclic amidine connected to an aldehyde-bearing cyclic enol ether at evaluation 182; a vinylpyridine with an oxime ether and thiol/hydrazone segment at evaluation 256; a polyenynyl cationic aza ring attached to an aminopyrazole at evaluation 123; and unsaturated imide/lactone or imide/ether ring systems at evaluations 17 and 77. They are not a coherent conventional amine-amide series. The bottom end includes both heavily decorated large ring assemblies and sprawling chains with multiple phenyl groups, boron or phosphorus, many unsaturated bonds and several polar functions. Familiar functional groups are available, but their combined architectures often look difficult to make and chemically delicate.
liabilities: Evaluation 182 combines an aldehyde, cyclic enol ether and amidine-containing polycycle; evaluation 256 adds oxime-ether, thiol/hydrazone and enol functionality. Their scores do not demonstrate stability or a practical route.

The shared parent/child cationic structure at evaluation 123 contains an undercoordinated bracketed positive nitrogen; direct graph inspection identifies radical character, so it should not be interpreted as an ordinary protonated amine.
The bromomethyl group and multiply unsaturated medium/large rings in evaluation 17, and the very elaborate ring connectivity at evaluation 52, create additional chemical and synthetic concerns.
missing_features: The set lacks a repeatedly expressed, chemically uncomplicated combination of modest scaffold size and organized polar ring/linker functionality; high values are attached to structurally disparate and often delicate assemblies.

No specific absent pharmacophore is supported by these molecules alone. Nitrogen, carbonyls, ethers and halogens all occur among very low structures as well as some higher ones, so their presence cannot identify the missing arrangement.
Defined stereochemistry is absent from the polycyclic and substituted ring structures, but the available scores cannot establish a stereochemical preference.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 182 scores 0.26337307291649803 and evaluation 256 scores 0.22480871596011054. They exceed parent n-a08278654dda's maximum, 0.21242900824222632, which belongs to the same cationic polyenynyl/aminopyrazole structure found at child evaluation 123. The higher child maximum therefore has a more oxygenated cyclic amidine/enol-ether arrangement, but still carries an aldehyde and unusual ring connectivity. The very large structures at evaluations 52 and 167 score exactly 0.0, while the benzyl-rich nitrogen-containing structure at evaluation 172 scores 1.5436686042133222e-64. Modest size and an integrated polar arrangement appear more compatible with the upper region than extensive hydrophobic or polyfunctional growth; this is not a clean matched-pair inference. Halogens alone are uninformative: the best proposal is unhalogenated, whereas the multiply fluorinated late evaluation-297 structure scores 2.151807787068372e-13. The digest median is reported as 0.0, but the trajectory includes many tiny nonzero scores, so that rounded median is not an exact-zero count. transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring and aromatic token presence are high, yet upper examples include ONC(=CCc1ccccc1P)N1CCN(c2ccccc2F)CC1 with phosphine and N-O chemistry, and Cc1cc(OC(F)F)ccc1C(=O)NC(Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)N=O with a nitroso group. More conventional chemistry is demonstrably available in Cc1ncc(SCc2cccc(Cl)c2)n1Cc1ccccc1. The deficit is therefore the reliability of whole-molecule assembly, not absence of useful fragments. Unusual groups occur at both high and low scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably assemble familiar medicinal fragments into chemically uncomplicated, interpretable whole molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs stronger control of functional-group compatibility, ordinary valence/electronic states and ring connectivity while retaining its broad de novo scaffold coverage. It should be able to vary an existing useful arrangement without incidentally adding reactive or exotic groups. This chemical plausibility gap does not justify assuming that every such group universally lowers the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: COc1cccc2c1C=C2NCCCN(C)C scores 0.31273900914359654, and Cc1ccc(F)cc1OCCNCC(CC=NO)Cc1ccccn1 scores 0.21811628298646404 in their supplied session, whereas CCCC(=O)NCCCOc1ccccc1 scores 0.00033303319833196673 in that same session. The latter still contains nitrogen and an aromatic ether, but its nitrogen is an amide. The corresponding parent's strongest structures also carry saturated aliphatic amines. The child clearly can emit such centres; the missing capability is repeatable control of their attachment and environment, not simple nitrogen enrichment.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve the chemical state and placement of amine nitrogen relative to aromatic surfaces.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator should be able to retain or vary an aliphatic amine centre, its substitution and its spacing from a ring independently of wholesale scaffold changes. Distinguish that chemistry from amides, conjugated imines, aromatic nitrogen and unusual formal charges. Which nitrogen environment to retain must come from current-session observations, without an objective-specific motif rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Compact organized examples such as Cn1cc(C2=NCCO2)c2c1NC(=O)CC2c1ccccc1 score well relative to the acyclic C=COC(=CC=CC#CCC)NC=NC=C(Br)C=NNN=NC(Br)=CC=O in their shared trajectory. Elsewhere large decorated structures reach tiny scores. However, C=CC=C(C(=O)C=CCNCC=C(CC=C)NC(=O)c1cc(C(C)NCc2cnc(C)[nH]2)ccc1O)c1cccnc1C(C)=NON has recorded scores 0.5609057782404998 and 2.241116085184792e-33 in different sessions. Thus a universal small-molecule or ring-count preference would contradict the evidence. A fluoro/chloro matched pair is present, but most cited upper structures differ by much more than a controlled substituent change.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks reliable independent control of scaffold topology, molecular extent and polar-group placement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support de novo variations that change a substituent or ring connection while preserving the rest of a chemically meaningful size and donor/acceptor arrangement. Molecular growth, contraction and polarity changes should be controllable dimensions whose value is learned from the local scores. Broad ring coverage already exists; simply increasing ring or heteroatom occurrence does not fill this gap.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied proposal-set stereocentre_rate is 0.0. Cn1c2ccccc2c2oc(C(O)CC3=NC=CC(N)C=C3F)cc21 contains an unspecified alcohol-bearing centre, and Cn1cc(C2=NCCO2)c2c1NC(=O)CC2c1ccccc1 contains an unspecified substituted tetrahedral ring carbon. Both appear among the higher-scoring proposals. This is absent stereochemical specification, not proof of absent three-dimensional shape or proof that a particular enantiomer would score better.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces potentially stereogenic structures without representing defined tetrahedral configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs the capacity to retain and deliberately vary valid explicit stereochemical assignments when its scaffolds create stereogenic centres. No preferred configuration can be prescribed from these trajectories; any utility would have to be established from permitted current-session feedback.

nodes.method_name: COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact SELFIES VAE from the permitted unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze its decoder. Within each independent objective session, fit a Tanimoto-kernel GP directly to the observed molecular fingerprints and scores. Generate new molecules through preconditioned Crank-Nicolson MCMC targeting the Gaussian latent prior multiplied by the GP probability that the deterministically decoded molecule exceeds the observed incumbent. The molecule assessed by the surrogate must be the molecule submitted. Fill the protocol-announced batch with distinct generated structures and update the GP after feedback. The corpus supplies a generative prior, never a ranked molecule library. This follows the decoupled mechanism in [COWBOYS](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/moss25a.html). Our hypothesis is that structure-level prediction and immediate Bayesian conditioning can direct scarce labels toward a higher final observed maximum without fitting a reward-dependent neural generator. Success is measured by the benchmark's mean of independent final Top-1 scores.

approach.method_basis: The Parent keeps every accepted score in a task-local archive for a fingerprint Gaussian process, but allows only the sixty-four highest-scoring accepted molecules to remain in its breeding population. It samples parents from three preferred score bands, generates a fresh pool through graph crossover and mutation, and selects evaluations using correlated posterior draws. Accepted offspring immediately compete for survival and can breed in later batches. This gives a functioning learning loop, while chemically distinct lower-scoring parents can disappear from the breeding population before their descendants are explored.
approach.novelty: Allocate survivor places in rounds across molecular cores: the best member of each core competes in the first round, the second-best members in the next, and so on until the existing population is full. Within a round, higher real scores win; the final survivors return to score order for the existing parent sampler. This protects several accepted core families while retaining the incumbent. The recorded lineage has tested posterior selection of generated offspring; this experiment changes the accepted molecules available for future breeding, with the inherited parent-draw rule intact.

nodes.hypothesis: Retain accepted breeding molecules by successive score-ordered rounds across Murcko cores, prioritizing each core's best member before any core's next member, then restore global score order for the unchanged parent sampler.

finding_summary.headline: Core-round survival broadened breeding, but protected records never bred and all three score replicas fell.
finding_summary.insights:
Preserving a low-ranked core and exploring it are separate events under the unchanged sampler. Of the 542 protected offspring, 116 survived into a later breeding state, but all remained below the sampled score bands. Six were still retained when the experiment ended and had first received protection in the terminal batch. The broader breeding came through changes to stronger analogues and the ranks of other survivors, rather than descendants of the directly protected records. A local support-promotion trace confirms that this indirect route can produce a parent-beating child, but such participation did not offset the overall loss in productive evaluations.

The actual trajectory also changes the apparent opportunity: on the already diversified Child states, only two incoming molecules were rescued from immediate greedy rejection, while 1,058 newcomers that local greedy selection would accept were excluded. Both rescued newcomers stayed outside breeding support. This narrows the result to a strong redistribution of survivor competition, with little evidence for the hoped-for exploration of protected weak parents. Mean generating-parent strength and mean offspring score both fell, so the smaller average parent deficit is not evidence of better candidates. The molecular assessment still finds repeated oversized heterocycle assemblies, tiny fragments, reactive bonds and constrained ring systems. Core coverage increased without resolving those chemical limitations. The passive greedy lists use existing labels only; they provide no alternate descendants or scores for an independently executed search.
finding_summary.results:
All 4,365 retention calls matched the declared core-round rule, preserved the incumbent and respected the 64-member capacity. Among 3,540 capacity-limited contests, 1,606 changed the local greedy survivor set and added one represented core; 1,266 also changed the immediate breeding support. Mean cores actually used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 24.20, and all fifteen final populations contained 64 distinct cores. There were 12,012 actual parent uses outside greedy breeding support reconstructed from the same accepted history. Those uses contributed to 326 evaluated offspring, including 35 best-parent beats and two incumbent gains.

The direct protection route remained unused: none of the 602 records retained against local greedy eviction, including 542 evaluated offspring, subsequently entered the breeding bands. Overall strict best-parent beats fell from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 526/4,350 (12.09%), and incumbent gains fell from 218 to 175. Mean final-best score fell from 0.544374 to 0.514684, a paired change of -0.029690. All three seed deltas were negative, as were all five task means. The retention mechanism and changed breeding support are confirmed; the intended score improvement was not observed.

molecular.headline: Large repeated aromatic assemblies coexist with compact but reactive carbonyl, amine and fluorinated ring families
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete paired Parent n-fc2c108a5253 trajectories. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9138 to 0.9862 and ring-closure presence from 0.9644 to 0.9908. Charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These counters report SMILES features, not aromatic atom fractions, actual ionization or feasible stereochemistry. The output spans compact aza-lactams and aryl carbonyl compounds, large aromatic heterocycle assemblies, polyamines attached to constrained rings, expanded cyclic dicarbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/carbonyl polycycles. Tiny fragments coexist with extensive repeated-module growth. This is especially visible in deco_hop, with mean SMILES length 105.0 and maximum 242; high and final molecules contain many linked aromatic or nitrogen-dione units. Compared with the Parent, broad chemical themes persist while ring topology and substituents change. N-F, peroxides, cumulene imines, unusual sulfur bonding and unspecified ring junctions remain material limitations. Overall synthesis is questionable and drug-like quality weak, although some conventional carbonyl and amine subseries are much more plausible than the extreme products. Diversity across seeds is moderate, with related families dominating late output.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecule is a moderately sized aryl-substituted aza-lactam with alkyl groups and an O-linked cumulated imine side chain. Other high members are fused oxygen/nitrogen heterocycles carrying aryl thioester, ketone or amide groups. Seed 2 retains indole-carboxamide and fused lactam relatives. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9793 and halogen presence is 0.8184. The core carbonyl/heteroaromatic chemistry is recognizable, but N-O bridges, cumulene imines and unusual fused-ring arrangements complicate complete synthesis. Compared with the Parent ketone/amide and sulfur-containing ring families, the successful region still centres on bounded aromatic carbonyl structures.
liabilities: Cumulated imine, N-F and thioester functionality introduces reactivity or stability concerns despite familiar carbonyl fragments.
Constrained oxygen/nitrogen ring fusion, occasional peroxide-containing relatives and tiny fragmented products limit chemical coherence.
missing_features: Stable alternatives to the cumulated imine and N-O-containing fused linkages are underrepresented around the favorable aryl/carbonyl arrangement.
Configurations of stereogenic lactam or fused-ring centres and geometric isomers are unspecified; a unique required target fragment cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best aryl aza-lactam/cumulated-imine molecule scores 0.4470018114651393 versus the Parent seed-1 maximum of 0.4126819838532174. Fluorinating its terminal imine nitrogen gives 0.41930905650182426. Other current seeds have lower maxima than their paired Parents, although fused aryl thioester and ketone members reach 0.4238198477630873 and 0.4207408531749377. Tiny fluorosulfur, hydrocarbon and fluoroalkene fragments score 0.0. The evidence favors the complete aromatic/carbonyl arrangement over fragment-sized products and does not show a general need for reactive nitrogen fluorination.

per_task.generated_character: The highest seed-1 structures are large multiaryl aza-heterocycles containing cyclic carbonyl or imino groups, ether links, fluorinated aromatic partners and a fused cyclic sulfide. Closely scoring variants add more aromatic rings, aryl peroxide connections or hypochlorite O-Cl. Seeds 0 and 2 generate repeated nitrogen-dione/aza-aromatic assemblies with carbonyl, N-N, ester or thioester links, including N-Cl/N-F variants. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9862 and halogen presence is 0.7586. The Parent also generated expanded heterocyclic assemblies; the current high region remains heavily aromatic and often much larger than conventional small-molecule frameworks. Whole-molecule synthesis is doubtful despite recognizable individual rings.
liabilities: Large repeated aromatic assemblies create severe size, solubility, flexibility and synthetic-complexity liabilities.
Peroxide, O-Cl, N-halogen, thioester and constrained unsaturation variants add chemical instability or reactivity.
missing_features: Compact accessible versions of the favorable heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement are poorly represented among the very large late products.
Stable replacements for aryl peroxide, N-halogen and labile multicarbonyl/thioester linkages are not systematically demonstrated at comparable attachment geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best seed-1 assembly scores 0.6112877583465819 versus the paired Parent maximum of 0.6324703199409752; all current paired maxima are lower. Contracting its cyclic sulfide ring gives the same 0.6112877583465819. Larger peroxide/polyaryl variants score 0.6104792370120253 or 0.6100296233601354, so their added complexity is not consistently rewarded. Related ordinary versus cumulated unsaturation variants tie at 0.6087949743003997. Tiny hypochlorite, fluorinated and nitrogen fragments score 0.5. The recurring heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement matters, but these plateau-like differences do not establish a need for repeated module growth or reactive linking groups.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest seed-0 family combines fluorinated/chlorinated aromatic rings, a branched polyamine side chain and a tightly fused nitrogen/sulfur ring system. Its exocyclic carbon-sulfur double bond is attached to a sulfur atom that also has ring bonds, rather than being an ordinary terminal thione. A carbon analogue and less fused nitrogen-ring relatives also score well. Seed 1 contains aminoalcohol/cyclobutane compounds with aryl peroxide, while seed 2 favors bulky halogenated aryl amines and cyclic aminals. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9747 and halogen presence is 0.9908. The Parent already reached high scores with aromatic amines; the current strongest family adds more unusual sulfur and constrained geometry.

Aryl peroxides, heavy halogenation, excessive aromatic/amine growth and unspecified stereochemistry remain liabilities across the seeds.
missing_features: Stable conventionally bonded ring systems preserving the successful aromatic/polyamine spacing are underrepresented despite the favorable matched carbon analogue.
Defined ring-junction and side-chain configurations, together with relevant amine protonation alternatives, are absent from the displayed comparisons.

It contains several N-methyl groups, an exocyclic amino/enamine region and, in relatives, a saturated version of that region. Other seeds retain fused aromatic lactam/dione frameworks. A shorter linker gives 0.21350507156602996, and a saturated relative gives 0.20678693060961814. The current maxima for the other seeds are below their Parents. per_task.generated_character: The best seed-1 molecules are moderately sized fluorinated imino/carbonyl nitrogen heterocycles attached to a densely bridged, unsaturated carbon framework with an exocyclic imine. Leaders often contain N-F as well as carbon-bound fluorine; methylated and N-Cl relatives are also present. Other seeds produce acyclic urea/formamide/enamine arrangements or fused phenolic nitrogen-carbonyl systems. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9138 and halogen presence is 0.6092. Large doubled aromatic/dione assemblies occupy the very low-scoring tail. Compared with the Parent fluorinated carbonyl/nitrogen families, the strongest current seed has a more constrained imino-containing ring geometry with unresolved stereochemistry and reactive N-F.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest extremes include small hydrocarbon/halogen fragments and repeated multiaryl or nitrogen-dione products. One set has mean SMILES length 105.0 and maximum 242; large coupled products elsewhere reach scores as low as 1.6758614448245604e-53.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator continues to span tiny fragments and oversized repeated assemblies rather than consistently preserving useful molecular scale.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide compact recombination, linker shortening and removal of duplicated modules while preserving useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine attachment patterns. Repeated growth should not dominate the alternatives to an intact favorable scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leaders and close relatives contain cumulated imines, N-F/N-Cl, aryl peroxides and multiply substituted sulfur with a carbon-sulfur double bond. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand stable matched nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur and carbon linkages, and represent chemical compatibility independently of scalar feedback. Different local score preferences make general stable-alternative generation more useful than assuming every high-scoring reactive group is necessary.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre-token presence is 0.0 throughout despite aryl-substituted lactams, branched polyamines, saturated amino-bearing rings and fluorinated bridged imines. Dense fusion and constrained unsaturation occur repeatedly among leaders.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces constrained and stereogenic ring systems without resolving their configurations or accessible geometry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cyclic-sulfide ring variants share 0.6112877583465819; ordinary versus cumulated unsaturation variants share 0.6087949743003997. A shorter-linker cyclic dicarbonyl at 0.21350507156602996 is close to its longer-linker counterpart at 0.21523191119058618.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The reference is Genetic GFN, published by Kim and colleagues, a two-phase generator that keeps handing work between a learned sampler and ordinary graph editing. A sequence model that writes molecules one token at a time is first trained on a large unlabeled corpus of drug-like structures, then adapted separately for each objective so that the chance of it finishing any particular molecule rises with the score that molecule actually received. Molecules it samples are dropped into a small scored population, which is then improved by ordinary genetic operations on the molecular graph: crossover between two parents, and single atom, bond and ring edits. The scored offspring are turned back into training targets for the sequence model, drawn preferentially from the high-scoring end of the archive, so the network proposes globally, the graph operators refine locally, and the refined results reshape what the network proposes next. A learned scaling term lets the model fit that reward-proportional target without knowing the total reward in advance, and a pull back toward the frozen corpus-trained model keeps it from collapsing onto whatever it found first.
approach.novelty: This is a root, so everything concrete here is a choice the implementation makes rather than something inherited from a parent. It fixes the alternation as one neural batch followed by two graph batches of ten molecules each, so roughly two thirds of the evaluation budget goes to graph refinement rather than to the network. It forces neural output into the breeding population at every cycle boundary instead of letting the population close over itself. It caps the scored population at sixty-four members. It sets the training reward as an exponential in the raw score, so a small score difference becomes a large difference in training weight. It draws replay targets with a probability that falls off as one over rank, so top molecules are revisited without the rest of the archive being starved. And it trains the corpus model only on unlabeled data, keeping every reward-bearing update local to one objective, so nothing learned from one objective can leak into another.

nodes.hypothesis: Alternate de novo sampling from a task-local GFlowNet SMILES policy with graph crossover and mutation of its refreshed scored population, then distill accepted graph descendants back into the policy through rank-weighted off-policy trajectory-balance replay with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen corpus-trained prior.

finding_summary.headline: Best of the thirteen Discovery roots at 0.5103, but the lead rests on one near-saturated objective
finding_summary.insights: The reciprocal loop demonstrably ran, and the node running it leads a field of thirteen roots whose scores span 0.2331 to 0.5103. What the run does not show is that the coupling produced the lead. Most graph offspring still fell below their generating parent, which is exactly the limitation this lineage was framed to address, so the advantage may come from the corpus-trained prior supplying realistic starting chemistry rather than from the feedback cycle itself. The per-objective spread is the sharper message: the same optimizer that nearly saturates one objective returns roughly 0.20 on another, so the campaign's current ranking is driven mostly by how well a method's proposal distribution happens to overlap each objective's answer, not by uniform competence, and a macro mean over five objectives will reward a method that wins one of them outright. With one seed and no parent this is not a reliability claim. What stays open is whether the lead survives more seeds, and whether being selective about which descendants get evaluated would convert the four-fifths of offspring that currently degrade their parent into usable gains.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean 0.510250764298028 on the single screening seed, the highest of the thirteen roots. Per objective the run returned 0.989650581855642 on the docking objective, 0.6290937996820349 on the decoration objective, then 0.46331566856387824, 0.27137962936984883 and 0.19781414201873615 on the remaining three, so one near-saturated result plus one strong result carry most of the lead while three objectives sit low. Every pre-registered observable activated and the falsifier did not trigger. The corpus-only prior cut held-out token loss from 4.560865074576297 to 0.5625432162352548 over 29742 steps on 1268755 sequences, and 150 later integrity checks found zero changes to it. Five hundred policy-generated molecules were admitted across 50 population refreshes, and 2958 complete graph-to-policy-to-sample-to-breeding chains were reconstructed through 106 distinct policy bridges. All 76800 replay draws came from accepted observations, with realized top-rank enrichment 0.2551173919195906 above the 0.5 uniform reference. Trajectory-balance residual fell from 27.86439877950252 to 22.643096844616046 across 2400 updates, 2381 of which reduced it, and all 2240 graph-bearing updates produced nonzero graph-derived gradients over 54110 draws. Of 1450 unique proposals, 500 came from the policy and 950 from graph operators, but only 173 descendants (18.2 percent) strictly beat their best generating parent, and the mean child-minus-best-parent change was -0.09497708681416797.
