molecular.headline: Real medicinal chemistry with hard per-objective motif lock-in, and not one defined stereocentre
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the generator emits ring-rich, heavily aromatic, well-branched molecules of ordinary size: ring closure appears in 95 to 99 percent of proposals, aromatic atoms in 87 to 97 percent, mean SMILES length runs 43 to 59, and cumulated double bonds are essentially absent at under one percent. The chemistry is recognisably drawn from a drug-like corpus, with indoles, pyridines, oxazoles, methoxyaryls, amides and benzylamines recurring. Two things are uniformly missing. No proposal in any objective carries a defined stereocentre. And within each objective the top of the ranking collapses onto a single decorated scaffold that is then permuted one atom at a time, so the twelve best molecules are usually variants of one structure rather than twelve independent answers.

per_task.generated_character: Genuine dopaminergic pharmacophore. A tryptamine-like indole carrying a primary or secondary amine, joined through a single methylene to a brominated tetrahydroisoquinoline. These are molecules a medicinal chemist would recognise on sight, and they reach 0.989650581855642 from starting material at 0.019.
liabilities: heavy reliance on aryl bromide, which reads as a synthetic handle rather than a finished substituent
aminal-like N-CH2-N fragments appearing in several of the top-scoring entries
the single best entry stacks two bromides on one ring plus a fused diazepane, an unusually greasy strained core
missing_features: defined stereochemistry at the ring-fusion and benzylic centres these scaffolds genuinely possess
conformationally constrained linkers other than the single methylene bridge used everywhere
aryl substitution beyond bromide and chloride on the tetrahydroisoquinoline ring
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks one triad: free basic amine, indole, and a halogenated benzylamine partner. Everything above 0.97 has all three; the bottom of the trajectory is amine-free heteroaryl chemistry such as triazine ethers and thiourea-adjacent amides, scoring four orders of magnitude lower.

per_task.generated_character: One motif, repeated. A 1,3-oxazol-5-yl group hung off an aminopyridine that is fused or linked to a lactone or lactam ring, with a second oxazole carried on an exocyclic alkene. Eleven of the twelve best entries are one- or two-atom permutations of each other.
liabilities: hemiaminal and enol fragments written NC(O)=C, which are tautomer artefacts rather than isolable species
an exocyclic C(=C) alkene conjugated to a ring carbonyl in nearly every top molecule, a Michael acceptor
trivial fragments such as CC and CCCN entering the trajectory at all, which wastes evaluations
missing_features: saturated or partly saturated ring systems to break the flat all-heteroaryl character
any defined stereocentre, despite several sp3 ring-fusion carbons being present
substituent chemistry beyond methyl, isopropyl and anilino on the central pyridine
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The scoring band is extremely compressed: best 0.6290937996820349 against a starting set already at 0.5, and everything above 0.62 carries the paired-oxazole plus aminopyridine arrangement. The worst entries are either oversized sulfone and bisphosphonate adducts or trivial fragments that still score exactly 0.5, so the objective floors small molecules rather than punishing them.

per_task.generated_character: Two families sharing one tail. A clean one, a methoxyphenyl ether of a pyridine carboxamide with a picolylamide cap, which is ordinary amide chemistry. And a dominant one built around an acryl-aldehyde enol ether, O=CC=C(O-aryl), capped by a non-aromatic 2H-pyrrole ring.
liabilities: O=CC=C(O-aryl) is a conjugated aldehyde and a Michael acceptor, and it is in most of the top twelve
C1C=CC=N1 2H-pyrrole rings are tautomerically unstable and not isolable as drawn
N=C(S) thioimidate and OOC peroxy-methyl fragments appear in mid-ranked entries
missing_features: a stable connectivity that reproduces what the acryl-aldehyde enol ether is contributing
aromatic five-membered rings in place of the non-aromatic 2H-pyrroles the generator keeps emitting
defined stereochemistry at the sp3 ring carbons of the pyrrolines it builds
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 2-pyridylmethyl group is the recurring feature of everything above 0.37. The stable amide family and the reactive enol-ether family reach almost the same score, so the objective is not discriminating between them. The very bottom is occupied both by fragments and by overlong multi-ring adducts, both scoring effectively zero, so size is punished at both ends.

per_task.generated_character: A single scaffold explored exhaustively. A 1,3-dimethyl hydantoin-dione ring joined by an exocyclic double bond to a benzylic carbon that also carries a phenyl and an alkyl-aryl ether. All twelve best entries are that same molecule with the alkyl decoration and ring size varied.
liabilities: the exocyclic alkene sits between two ring carbonyls, making it a strong Michael acceptor in every top entry
late proposals introduce an O-O peroxy linkage and an N-hydroxy hydantoin, both degradation-prone
one late proposal carries a fully conjugated triene tail, which is not a stable substituent
missing_features: a second distinct scaffold family, to test whether the plateau is the objective's ceiling or the search's
polar functionality on the phenoxy ring beyond a single hydroxyl
defined stereochemistry at the benzylic and hydantoin sp3 centres
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Scores are banded between 0.184 and 0.198 for the whole top twelve, and the only gradient is small alkyl decoration: adding an ethyl or propyl on the phenoxy ring, or fusing a cyclobutane onto it, moves the score by thousandths. The floor is trivial fragments, so the objective rewards mere presence of the motif far more than any refinement of it.

per_task.generated_character: Nitro-substituted cyclohexadiene rings carrying a pyridin-2-ylmethyl hydrazone. The charged-fragment rate here is 0.3655, far above the 0.01 to 0.03 seen on the other objectives, and that charge is almost entirely the nitro group the generator has latched onto.
liabilities: malformed nitro groups written [N+][O-] without the second oxygen appear inside the top twelve
hydrazones are hydrolytically labile and are the single load-bearing feature of the whole top set
nitroalkene fragments, both reactive and toxicophoric, recur across the highest-scoring molecules
missing_features: the fluorinated aryl and fused triazole chemistry a chemist would reach for on this kind of target
any defined stereocentre, though this objective family is built around configuration
aromatic carbocycles in place of the non-aromatic cyclohexadiene rings that dominate the top set
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Every entry above 0.19 pairs a hydrazone C=NN with a 2-pyridyl or picolyl group, with the nitro group added on top. The worst molecules are large polyfunctional adducts scoring down to 1e-87, so this objective punishes size ferociously and the search responded by shrinking rather than by getting the chemistry right.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 in all five trajectory sets, across 1450 proposals, even though the molecules routinely contain sp3 ring-fusion and benzylic carbons that are genuine stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never emits a defined stereocentre.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Configuration is outside the proposal alphabet as built. A generator aimed at shape-dependent properties would need stereo tags in its token vocabulary and stereo-aware graph edits, plus feedback able to distinguish two configurations of the same skeleton, otherwise half of the accessible chemistry is unreachable by construction.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In every trajectory the twelve best molecules are one- or two-atom permutations of the same core, the winning family is reached early and then only decorated, and the score spread across those twelve is often under 0.02.
transferable_gaps.gap: Within any one objective the search collapses onto a single decorated scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Reward-weighted replay concentrates the proposal distribution faster than local graph edits can leave it. A generator would need something that explicitly keeps distinct cores alive, such as similarity-penalised replay or budget reserved for proposals sampled far from the current archive, rather than relying on random atom edits to escape a basin they helped dig.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Conjugated aldehyde enol ethers, exocyclic alkenes flanked by ring carbonyls, hemiaminal NC(O)=C fragments, 2H-pyrroles and nitro groups written with only one oxygen all appear in the top-scoring sets, not merely in the discarded tail.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive electrophiles and tautomer artefacts are proposed as if they were finished molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Nothing in the loop distinguishes a scoreable string from a makeable compound, so a reactive motif that happens to score can become the load-bearing feature of the archive and then be amplified by replay. A structural-alert and valence-sanity screen applied before a proposal spends an evaluation would stop that amplification.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Only 173 of 950 graph descendants strictly beat their best generating parent, an 18.2 percent rate, and the mean child-minus-best-parent score change across the run was -0.09497708681416797.
transferable_gaps.gap: Local graph edits usually make their parent worse.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Descendants are being evaluated indiscriminately, so four fifths of the graph budget buys degradation. A generator would gain from a cheap internal ranking over candidate descendants before real evaluations are spent, so the budget goes to the offspring most likely to exceed the parent they came from.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The aromatic-atom rate runs 0.87 to 0.97 across every set, the recurring rings are five- and six-membered heteroaromatics, and the few sp3 rings present are small carbocycles bolted on as peripheral substituents.
transferable_gaps.gap: Saturated three-dimensional ring systems are almost absent.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The proposal distribution has inherited the flat, heteroaryl-dense character of its pretraining corpus. A generator would need edit operations that build and fuse saturated rings, and a prior whose sampling does not collapse onto planar aromatic frameworks, before it can offer any three-dimensional shape at all.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

retained_mechanisms: Unlabeled autoregressive SMILES prior training and validation-selected frozen checkpoint
Fresh task-local adaptable policy, learned log normalizer and Adam state
Accepted-only replay with exact trajectory retention and positive rank-weighted sampling
Terminated-trajectory balance with log reward 40 times accepted score and joint policy/normalizer optimization
Nonzero categorical KL regularization toward the unchanged prior
Alternating one policy batch and two graph-refinement batches
Accepted policy population refresh and forced fresh-policy breeding participation
Connected-fragment crossover and seven atom/bond mutation families with local validity and novelty rejection
Score-ranked 64-member survivor population and descendant parent reuse
Accepted graph-score distillation into subsequent neural sampling through replay

approach.method_basis: The Parent keeps independent molecular graph walks, each starting from a supplied scored molecule. It proposes random atom or bond edits from each current state, evaluates one neighbor per scheduled walk, accepts improvements, and sometimes accepts a loss using a temperature that falls as feedback arrives. An accepted worse molecule remains the source of that walk's next edit, while a separate archive preserves the best observed score. Its eight edit operators check molecular parsing, connectivity, canonical identity and novelty, but have no reference for whether a new local chemical environment occurs in ordinary molecular data.
approach.novelty: Add one frozen local chemistry support gate to the existing edit proposals. A small vocabulary extracted from unlabeled corpus molecules will identify supported atom environments; a proposed neighbor must not introduce or multiply an unsupported environment relative to its generating state. This addresses the observed drift into unusual ring atoms and bonds while allowing existing unusual environments to remain or disappear. This lineage has only its root, so no sibling has tested a corpus-derived support gate. The experiment asks whether restricting local chemical changes makes the same annealed walks more productive.

nodes.hypothesis: Condition the Parent's existing graph-edit proposal distribution on a frozen unlabeled-corpus vocabulary of local atom environments, rejecting an otherwise valid novel neighbor whenever it introduces or increases the multiplicity of an unsupported environment relative to that walk's scored source state.

finding_summary.headline: New unsupported environments fell to zero; the one-seed mean score rose from 0.233 to 0.268
finding_summary.insights:
The parent really was entering local environments absent or rare in the corpus: roughly one proposal in five increased their multiplicity. Supported alternatives were available with little extra retry work, so that behavior was avoidable without changing annealing or sacrificing evaluation budget. The same-run rejection traces establish this intermediate effect directly; the mixed score response leaves open whether removing these environments is broadly useful or primarily changes which stochastic paths are reached. The gain exceeds the declared 0.002 mean-score target on this seed, but one improving objective and one declining objective do not show a universal advantage or isolate which blocked chemistry caused either change.

Complete local support still allowed the chemistry assessment to find hydroperoxides, peracids, crowded bridges and N-Cl bonds. The N-Cl center environment itself occurred in eight sampled corpus molecules, so its survival follows the declared threshold rather than exposing a bypass. The improved drd2_docking maximum also retains a hydroperoxide and crowded ring topology. Local empirical support therefore narrows chemical drift but does not certify whole-molecule geometry, stability or synthetic plausibility. Coherent ring and functional-group changes remain worth investigating with rules shared across objectives. All starting and working child molecules were locally supported here, so preservation or removal of inherited unsupported environments remains an untested use case.
finding_summary.results:
The intended mechanism happened on all five objectives. Using the same frozen vocabulary for both runs, 298 of 1,450 parent proposals introduced or multiplied an unsupported atom environment (20.55%); none of the 1,450 child proposals did. The mean number of introduced unsupported environments fell from 0.311 per proposal to exactly zero. The gate rejected 235 otherwise valid novel candidates and redirected 205 proposal requests to supported alternatives from the same unchanged scored source. All batches remained full, and attempts per emitted molecule rose modestly from 1.165 to 1.364. Every Metropolis decision, cooling value, working-state update and archive check agreed with the inherited rules.

On the sole evaluated seed, the mean of the five best scores rose from 0.233114 to 0.268497 (+0.035383). The improvement came from drd2_docking, which rose from 0.044776 to 0.280588. Zaleplon_mpo fell from 0.381715 to 0.322816; deco_hop stayed at 0.557517, median_2 at 0.167839, and sitagliptin_mpo at 0.013725. All 1,450 child proposals were evaluated without invalid or duplicate entries. These are single-seed results and do not establish repeatability.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families remain, but many descendants accumulate peroxide groups, crowded bridges and poorly controlled functional-group changes.
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of n-39a65c2978c0 against Parent n-6a8d103b076c uses the supplied digest and complete saved seed-0 trajectories for all five tasks; no task is missing. Each task contains 300 molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. The output spans small branched alkyl halides, indole carboxamides, polyaryl chromone-like structures, fused nitrogenous diones, cyclic thiones, sugar-like acetals and heavily edited polycycles. This is considerable ring chemistry, with moderate diversity across recognizable starting families and their descendants. The digest ring_closure_rate is 0.9655 on every task, whereas aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.6655 to 0.7138. These are fractions of SMILES containing the relevant text, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths range from 59.1 to 61.5 characters; they indicate string size, not molecular weight. All charged_rate and stereocentre_rate readings are 0.0: potentially protonatable nitrogens and stereogenic structures still occur, but their charge and stereochemistry are not explicitly specified. Relative to the Parent, phosphorus disappears from the full proposed-SMILES sets, and aromatic-bearing strings become more frequent on every task. The remaining chemistry still includes hydroperoxides, peracids, N-O substituents, occasional N-Cl bonds, highly connected small rings and crowded aminal/acetal systems. Ordinary early indole and dione structures are more readily recognizable as synthetic targets than many late cages. The latter warrant scrutiny for geometric feasibility, stability and synthesis; SMILES alone does not establish that they are impossible or establish a synthetic route. Per-task comparisons below describe the reported scores without assigning pharmacological meaning. Digest medians written as 0.0 are rounded summaries, not evidence that all those scores were exactly zero.

per_task.generated_character: The most conventional upper-end molecule is an ethoxy/methoxy/phenol-substituted indole bearing a fluorophenyl carboxamide. Related upper-end structures retain the indole NH and amide but acquire N-O substitution and extra ring connections. A second upper-end family consists of cyclic thioureas attached to contracted, partly unsaturated carbocycles; some no longer have ordinary aromatic rings. The low end contains much larger branched amide/urea/acid-rich structures and crowded oxygen/nitrogen/sulfur polycycles. Mean SMILES length is 59.5 characters, and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.6655. The early indole carboxamide looks synthetically plausible in outline; the later contracted-ring and cage structures are substantially more questionable.
liabilities: Upper-end cyclic thiourea derivatives include highly compressed unsaturated ring systems; evaluation 293 even contains a four-membered diene ring. Their geometry and accessibility need chemical scrutiny.
Low evaluations 262 and 272 carry N-Cl bonds on carbonyl-bound nitrogen. Other low or final molecules carry hydroperoxides and crowded aminal/acetal networks.
Many late structures combine extensive branching, several polar functionalities and unspecified stereochemistry, making the synthetic target less well defined than the early indole.
missing_features: The low-scoring bulk lacks the compact, organized indole/aryl-carbonyl arrangement present in the leading examples; many descendants replace it with large nonaromatic polar frameworks.

The excerpts do not show a sustained series of simpler, synthetically coherent alternatives that retain the favorable phenol/ether/carboxamide arrangement while varying it independently of ring contraction or N-O insertion. The scores do not identify a specific absent target group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The ethoxy/dimethoxy indole at evaluation 29 scores 0.2273478924382318; replacing one methoxy substituent with phenol gives evaluation 39 at 0.3228160306167682. Inserting nitrogen into its ethoxy connection gives evaluation 59 at 0.2882941779739877. These comparisons favor a particular substitution pattern on an intact indole/aryl-amide framework, without proving a general benefit from adding donors or nitrogen. Evaluation 183 still scores 0.28568438299156995 despite contracted nonaromatic carbocycles, so aromaticity alone does not explain the upper end. The much larger urea/acid-rich evaluation 252 scores 2.9203128686642823e-43; the reported median rounds to 0.0. Late evaluation 299 remains at 0.280962001818902 amid much lower-scoring final molecules. Parent maximum 0.38171497280435657 came from an unusual phosphorus-containing family; the Child maximum is the more conventional indole at 0.3228160306167682.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end contains decorated indole aryl-amides and larger hydroxylated polyaryl chromone/lactone-like structures bearing nitrile, aryl nitrogen, alkoxyamine and chloromethyl substituents. Late variants connect those aromatic units into dense fused or bridged systems. The bottom consists of small branched bromo/chloroalkanes and nonaromatic cyclopropyl carbonyl compounds. Mean SMILES length is 61.0 characters, with a maximum of 107; aromatic_atom_rate is 0.7138. Several early aromatic frameworks are recognizable synthetic targets, while later ring connectivity and peroxide-bearing heterocycles are questionable.
liabilities: Dense ring connections in evaluation 298 and the late thioester-bearing evaluation 295 create substantial geometric and synthetic questions even though aromatic fragments remain recognizable.
Evaluation 296 contains a peroxy ester linkage in a ring, and evaluation 297 contains a peroxide substituent. Their scores do not certify ordinary compound stability.

The leading indole includes an N-O linkage and a methoxymethylamino substituent; these are real functional groups, but their compatibility and stability require attention rather than an assumption that an aromatic scaffold makes every decoration benign.
missing_features: The low-scoring tail lacks the extended aromatic surfaces and organized polar substitution visible in the upper-end indoles and polyaryl carbonyl compounds.

The upper-end sample lacks a clearly established simpler series that separates the contribution of those substituents from extra bridge formation. No particular unobserved scaffold or decoration can be deduced from this narrow observed score span.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorochlorophenyl amide on a hydroxylated, N-ethoxy-substituted indole at evaluation 89 scores 0.5575174561711961, the same molecule and maximum observed in the Parent. A less extensively fused hydroxylated polyaryl chromone at evaluation 48 scores 0.5515878333110009, while the densely bridged nitrile-bearing evaluation 298 scores 0.5553918460218583. Both sit above the small nonaromatic evaluations 91 and 201 at 0.5. This supports an association with decorated aromatic surfaces and heteroatom/carbonyl substitution in this sample. It does not show that complicated ring fusion is required: the chemically different aromatic examples occupy a close score band. The median is 0.524481, and the late peroxidic evaluation 296 still receives 0.5435671594841145.

per_task.generated_character: The upper-end family is a large, densely connected aza-aromatic/aryl-ether polycycle carrying amino groups, non-amide ring nitrogens, an N-methyl unsaturated amine ring and a hydroperoxymethyl substituent. These nitrogens can offer ionizable functionality, although neither pKa nor protonation state is established by the neutral SMILES. A distinct upper-end example is an aminated aryl/cyclic-thiourea structure with a substituted cyclohexene. The low end includes small nonaromatic oxygen heterocycles and aldehydes, but also the chemically conventional initial quinoline/phenoxy amide with N-methylpiperidine and hydroxamate. Mean SMILES length is 61.5 characters and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.6897, compared with the Parent trajectory value 0.5172. The leading cages are questionable synthetic targets despite their familiar component groups.
liabilities: The leading evaluation 266 and close analogues retain a hydroperoxymethyl group and an aryl O-N linkage. Their positive score association is not evidence of biological stability or a useful peroxide mechanism.
Extensive bridges and aminal-like connections make conformational feasibility and synthesis uncertain; no explicit stereochemistry resolves the resulting possible configurations.
The initial conventional scaffold scores poorly, while highly unusual descendants score better, so synthetic plausibility cannot be inferred from the score alone.
missing_features: The leading family does not demonstrate a peroxide-free, less crowded presentation of its aromatic surface and non-amide ring amines with comparable reported scores; the stable alternatives needed to disentangle those features are not shown.

Basic centres and fused aromatics are already present. What is poorly represented at the upper end is a range of independently varied, synthetically coherent linker and ring arrangements that separates nitrogen placement from cage formation. The trajectories do not establish a missing receptor-specific group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 266 scores 0.28058763894389116. In its otherwise matching scaffold, replacing a carbon in the pendant amine ring with nitrogen gives evaluation 276 at 0.18804630310947, and removing the terminal ring N-methyl group gives evaluation 296 at 0.15120691315380252. The local gradient therefore depends on nitrogen placement, substitution and shape, not simply nitrogen abundance. Evaluation 251, a small fluorinated oxygen heterocycle with aldehyde, scores 0.001385268283468699. Initial evaluation 6 already contains an ordinary N-methylpiperidine attached through a phenoxy-amide/quinoline framework and scores only 0.0003786988088202195, so a basic ring amine is not an absent feature or a sufficient explanation. The observed maximum exceeds the Parent value 0.04477593818961592; the new upper end is phosphorus-free but retains a hydroperoxide and crowded ring topology. The median is 0.01703.

per_task.generated_character: The leading observed structure is the initial ethyl hydroxybenzoate bearing a phenyl-substituted, N-methylated fused nitrogenous dione. The strongest proposed descendants keep much of that framework, or belong to the quinoline/phenoxy/N-methylpiperidine family bearing a hydroxamate or peracid. Low scorers are small branched bromochloroalkanes and an alcohol; late examples become mixed aromatic/nonaromatic polycycles with thioesters, peroxides, amines and sulfonamides. Mean SMILES length is 59.1 characters and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.7. The intact early aromatic dione and amide frameworks are plausible synthetic targets in outline; the peracid-bearing and highly bridged descendants are less persuasive.
liabilities: Peracids replace hydroxamates in several near-leading descendants, and evaluation 296 retains a carbonyl-O-OH group in a crowded nitrogenous cage. These are potentially reactive functionalities even when the scalar score is unchanged.
Ring contraction and arbitrary connections progressively erode the recognizable initial scaffold without an observed improvement over its score.
The small alkyl-halide tail offers little organized aromatic/polar architecture; later cages supply many connections but unspecified stereochemistry.
missing_features: The lower-end molecules lack the extended aryl/heteroaryl and organized carbonyl architecture of the leading starting structure.

The proposed upper end does not demonstrate a coherent alternative arrangement that improves on the initial aromatic dione while preserving ordinary functional-group chemistry. The trajectories alone cannot specify an unseen similarity target or a particular missing fragment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione at evaluation 7 scores 0.1678386594791329 and remains the maximum in both Child and Parent. Replacing its pendant phenyl with a nonaromatic cyclopentadiene gives the best proposed evaluation 27 at 0.15882451078226317; adding a phenolic substituent to the pendant phenyl gives evaluation 17 at 0.15625847779496568. The bromochlorinated low examples at evaluations 31 and 101 both score 0.015094447095057544. This sample favors retention of the larger organized aromatic/carbonyl framework over the small alkyl-halide family, but does not demonstrate an improving new arrangement. In the other upper-end family, replacing the hydroxamate at evaluation 26 with a peracid at evaluation 36 leaves the reported score exactly 0.1506011755487833. That matched pair shows that a substantial change in functional-group chemistry need not move this score. The median is 0.11453.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecule is an ethyl ester on a phenolic, ring-connected aryl/fused-nitrogenous-dione framework; its ester is not a lactone. Another relatively high family consists of much smaller fluorinated, hydroxylated carbocycles bearing methylthio carbinol groups. An indole-amide-derived family also appears but is strongly bridged and N-O substituted. The deepest low end consists of large branched nonaromatic amide/urea/acid frameworks with numerous amines; final molecules include crowded sulfur/oxygen/nitrogen polycycles and hydroperoxides. Mean SMILES length is 61.3 characters and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.6931, compared with 0.5 in the Parent. Synthetic plausibility varies from recognizable starting motifs to questionable small-ring geometry and crowded reactive structures.
liabilities: The ring-connected dione and small fluorinated carbocycles introduce constrained geometry and unspecified stereochemistry; neither a high ring count nor the local score establishes geometric feasibility.
The smaller upper-end fluorinated structures include carbinols directly bearing fluorine or sulfur, whose stability and preparative handling would need examination.
The low end includes N-chlorinated amides, while final molecules include hydroperoxides and dense aminal/acetal or sulfur-containing ring systems.
missing_features: The low-scoring bulk lacks the restrained size and particular carbonyl/ring arrangement of the better observed examples; it accumulates large amino/acid-rich frameworks instead.

Fluorinated aliphatic chemistry is present in a relatively high example. What is not demonstrated is a coherent, synthetically comfortable series combining controlled polar-group placement and tractable ring geometry. These very low and heterogeneous scores do not identify a specific absent pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Initial evaluation 7 scores 0.0020944534688323298. Its ring-contracted evaluation 27 reaches 0.006548645826380125, and the further ring-connected evaluation 37 reaches 0.013725075295981876, the same maximum and molecule as in the Parent. Altering the carbonyl-containing dione region in evaluation 47 leaves 7.611967647285142e-05, consistent with the importance of that particular carbonyl/topological arrangement within this family. A quite different small fluorinated hydroxylated carbocycle, evaluation 281, reaches 0.008540131561599934, whereas the oversized nonaromatic polyamide/acid evaluation 152 scores 7.34708925653015e-58. Thus neither aromaticity nor fluorine alone describes the gradient: favorable local composition and topology occur in chemically distinct families, and all observed scores remain small. The median rounds to 0.0. The final six molecules are all far below the early maximum, including a peroxide-bearing evaluation 297 at 5.700995963518049e-13.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes a four-membered diene-containing cyclic-thiourea derivative, densely bridged aromatic lactone-like structures and high-scoring aza-aromatic aminal cages. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9655 throughout, yet recognizable early aromatic scaffolds often become crowded polycycles. Removing phosphorus from the output has not removed these whole-structure concerns.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve tractable whole-molecule ring geometry when it creates new connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Proposal construction needs a task-independent way to account for complete ring size, bridge connectivity and geometric feasibility. Transformations that preserve or replace coherent ring units could provide useful chemical variation without continuously adding difficult connections; local atom-environment familiarity alone cannot establish global synthetic plausibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited hydroxamate-to-peracid pair has identical reported score 0.1506011755487833. The leading aza-aromatic amine family retains a hydroperoxymethyl substituent, and low-scoring amide-rich examples contain N-Cl bonds. N-O groups also occur among both ordinary-looking and highly modified structures; their presence is not proof that the entire molecule is unusable.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group variation does not consistently distinguish stable candidate chemistry from potentially reactive peroxide and N-halogen motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic transformation repertoire should treat intact functional groups and their compatibility explicitly, and make stable alternatives accessible without requiring unrelated scaffold distortion. Peroxide and N-halogen chemistry needs a deliberate policy based on chemical evidence; favorable scalar feedback alone does not establish stability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The upper end includes a recognizable phenolic indole carboxamide and an initial aromatic fused dione that no proposed molecule surpasses in its own trajectory. Several low-end families instead become large nonaromatic amino/acid-rich structures. Aromatic-bearing string rates of 0.6655 to 0.7138 coexist with a ring-closure rate of 0.9655, so rings are abundant while recognizable aromatic organization is less consistently retained.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks a consistently demonstrated route to vary useful aromatic and carbonyl arrangements without accumulating unrelated structural changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include chemically coherent scaffold-preserving substitutions, ring-unit replacements and simplifying edits that vary donor/acceptor placement or linker geometry independently. These capabilities should use current objective-local feedback to discover where they help, without encoding a preferred benchmark scaffold or hidden objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0, while the cited molecules include substituted small rings, bridged aminals and crowded acetals. This is absence of stereochemical SMILES annotation, not evidence that the molecules lack stereocentres. Charged_rate is also 0.0 despite non-amide amine groups, so neutral text should not be confused with absence of ionizable chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted polycyclic chemistry does not specify stereochemical identity despite creating potentially stereogenic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve existing stereochemical information and represent newly created stereogenic structures deliberately when constructing candidates. Comparisons among well-defined configurations would make these chemical proposals more interpretable; the current trajectories do not establish whether that representation change would improve a scalar score.

nodes.method_name: Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in simulated annealing: randomly perturb a current configuration, accept improvements, sometimes accept deterioration, and gradually cool the acceptance rule. [Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi](https://hedibert.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/1983KirkpatrickGelattVecchi.pdf) describe this mechanism for combinatorial optimization. Our molecular transfer maintains independent graph walks initialized from the current objective's supplied scored molecules. Each walk generates a new neighbor through atom or bond edits. After real feedback, accept a higher-scoring neighbor as the next working state; accept a lower-scoring neighbor with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), otherwise retain the source state. Subsequent edits follow the accepted working state, while a separate archive preserves the best observed molecule. Cool as feedback accumulates and distribute the evaluator-announced batch across walks with explicit proposal-to-source provenance. Regenerate invalid or already evaluated structures through further edits. Every submitted molecule is generated de novo; no corpus pool, learned prior or labeled source task is required. The hypothesis is that temporary score losses permit useful structural transitions whose later gains increase the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. This finite-budget optimizer does not claim equilibrium sampling or asymptotic convergence under molecular validity and novelty filtering.

approach.method_basis: This node transfers MAX-MIN Ant System, a classical ant colony optimiser, onto molecular graph building. Every proposed molecule is constructed from nothing: an ant picks a starting atom, then repeatedly either attaches a new atom by a chosen bond to some existing atom, closes a ring bond between two atoms already present, or stops, with valence rules deciding which moves are legal at each step. The probability of each legal move is a fixed chemical heuristic weight, read off aggregate frequencies in an unlabeled corpus, multiplied by a learned pheromone weight. The crucial choice is what the pheromone is indexed by: not the molecule being built and not the sequence so far, but a small local description of the attachment site together with the move's own atom and bond attributes, so the same pheromone entry is consulted whenever that local situation recurs in any molecule. After each batch of proposals is scored, all pheromone weights evaporate by a fixed fraction, only the single best-scoring accepted molecule in that batch deposits reinforcement, and it deposits only on the entries its own construction actually used. Every weight is then clipped into a fixed positive interval, the max-min part of the method, so no move is ever driven to zero probability and no move ever takes over completely. The bet is that a local decision that helped once will help again in a structurally different molecule.
approach.novelty: The method statement says pheromones are keyed by solution components; for molecules that leaves the most important design decision open, and this root answers it concretely. Keys combine a bounded local attachment environment, made of atom identity, charge, hydrogen count, degree, bond-order sum and ring membership, with the candidate move's own attributes, and ring-closure keys additionally carry both endpoint environments and a path-length class. Keys are explicitly forbidden from encoding a whole prefix, a whole partial graph, or any observation identifier, which is what separates this from a prefix tree and makes credit genuinely shareable across unrelated partial molecules. The remaining commitments are all fixed in advance and identical across objectives: pheromone exponent 1.5 against heuristic exponent 1, evaporation of 0.18 per update, weights clipped to the interval from 0.025 to 1, and one rank-scaled deposit per distinct key on the winner's trace rather than one per repeated occurrence. The corpus is used only for aggregate atom, bond, ring-closure and stopping frequencies, published as tables with no molecule library retained anywhere. Pheromones start broad and are seeded by exactly replaying the construction of the single highest-scoring supplied molecule, then every objective gets its own fresh table. Only accepted whole-molecule feedback moves anything: invalid, duplicate, rejected and still-pending constructions never deposit. The node also deliberately restricts itself to each ant's own generating trace, holding back the idea of spreading one molecule's score across its equivalent construction orders as a separate later experiment.

nodes.hypothesis: Construct each proposed molecule anew with valence-aware molecular graph actions sampled from fixed corpus-derived chemical heuristics times shared task-local bounded pheromones, then evaporate all pheromones and reinforce only the accepted batch-best molecule's actual construction trace so successful local actions guide later ants across different partial graphs.

finding_summary.headline: Shared construction credit spread almost everywhere yet improved almost nothing; 0.2523, eleventh of twelve scored roots
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a clean separation between credit spreading and credit being useful. This root demonstrates that local-context pheromones do transfer: 70,235 selected moves reused a winner's reinforcement inside a structurally different partial molecule, with 70,175 of those reuses occurring at a different atom count entirely, so the mechanism is not a disguised prefix tree. But nearly every accepted ant inherited that bias while almost none benefited from it, which says the local key is too coarse to be selective. A context of atom identity, degree, hydrogens and ring membership recurs so often that reinforcing it nudges essentially the whole colony in the same direction rather than steering it toward the winner's chemistry. Against the twelve scored Discovery roots, whose macro means span 0.2331 to 0.5103, this root's 0.2523 ranks eleventh, in the bottom third and only marginally above the weakest root; the honest reading is that ant colony optimisation at this credit resolution is not competitive here. Two things stay open. The root deliberately deferred spreading a winner's score across the equivalent construction orders of the same molecule, which is the obvious way to make each accepted score inform more contexts, and it has not tested whether a richer key, or a deposit weighted by how distinctive a context is, would make credit selective. It is also a single seed with no parent and no ablation, so nothing here isolates the pheromone contribution from the fixed corpus heuristic that was doing the rest of the work.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean was 0.2523 on the single screening seed, with per-task final Top-1 of 0.5534 on the decoration-hopping objective, 0.3051 on the zaleplon multi-property objective, 0.1678 on the second median-molecule objective, 0.1371 on the dopamine-receptor docking objective and 0.0980 on the sitagliptin multi-property objective. The machinery worked in full. The construction grammar exactly replayed 39,545 of 40,000 sampled corpus molecules, a rate of 0.9886, and exactly replayed all 50 supplied starting molecules. The colony then built 1,450 molecules in 145 batches of ten, every one valid and connected, with zero invalid retries, zero duplicates and zero evaluator rejections; 77,416 construction actions were taken and 1,168 of the products were cyclic. Pheromone updates were exact in all 145 online events, always reinforcing the true highest accepted score, and probability mass genuinely shifted: 6,558 of 6,633 competitive probes increased the reinforced key's share, mean signed shift +0.0193, with 67 unchanged and 8 slightly reduced by the lower clipping bound. Sharing was real and extensive, with 71,453 selected reuses of reinforced moves in different partial molecules, 70,235 of them traceable to online feedback. The payoff did not follow. Of 1,399 accepted ants that reused online-reinforced components, only 3 beat their pre-batch incumbent, a rate of 0.0021. Initial-to-final incumbent improvements were 0, 0.00497, 0.1181, 0 and 0.0959 across the five objectives, so on two objectives no constructed molecule ever beat a supplied starting molecule, and on the decoration-hopping objective the entire 0.005 gain arrived in the first generated batch, before any online deposition could have steered it.

molecular.headline: Long conjugated polyene chains and strained fused cages, with aromatic rings largely absent from the output
molecular.overall_character: The colony builds large, heavily unsaturated, mostly non-aromatic molecules. Mean SMILES length runs 74 to 87 characters on every objective with maxima of 113 to 127, and the constructions averaged around 50 atoms, far beyond ordinary small-molecule size. Aromatic atoms appear in only 20 to 42 percent of the emitted strings, which is the defining deficiency: rings that do form are usually written as non-aromatic C=C closures, strained fused cages, or bridged polycyclics carrying exocyclic quinoid double bonds onto ring atoms. Ring formation itself is inconsistent, present in 95 to 97 percent of strings on three objectives but only 55 to 61 percent on the other two, where the output degenerates into unbranched polyene chains 90 to 110 characters long, alternating C=C with occasional methyl branches and almost no heteroatoms. Nitrogen, when it appears, is nearly always a chain imine or enamine rather than a ring nitrogen. Stereochemistry is entirely absent across all 1,450 constructions. The overall impression is of a valence-correct graph builder that has learned atom and bond frequencies without learning what a molecule is shaped like.

per_task.generated_character: The weakest chemistry of the five. Ring closures appear in only 61 percent of strings and aromatic atoms in 22 percent, while mean length is 76.2. Most molecules are long alternating polyene chains with methyl branches; the minority that close rings produce strained fused cages with amide or nitrile groups buried inside them.
liabilities: unbranched conjugated polyene chains of twenty or more sp2 carbons, which are not isolable compounds
bridged spiro cages with multiple fused three and four membered rings
exocyclic quinoid double bonds drawn onto ring atoms, giving non-Kekulisable-looking systems
missing_features: any fused nitrogen heteroaromatic bicycle, which the colony never constructs on this objective
aromatic rings at all in roughly four fifths of the proposals
compact molecules of drug-like size; the outputs average more than twice the length of the supplied starting molecules
discrete polar functional groups such as a simple amide on an aromatic ring rather than nitrogen buried in a cage
per_task.score_gradient_reading: More than half of all proposals scored exactly 0, since the median of the read molecules is 0.0. The handful that scored at all, up to 0.1776, are the compact cyclic ones carrying nitrogen and a nitrile; the zero band is uniformly the 90 to 110 character polyene chains. Decisively, no constructed molecule ever beat a supplied starting molecule here, so the reported final Top-1 of 0.3051 is that starting molecule's own score and not something the colony built.

per_task.generated_character: The largest molecules of the five, mean SMILES length 86.0 with a maximum of 126 and ring closures in 94 percent of strings, yet aromatic atoms in only 42 percent. The high-scoring band is dominated by enormous fused polycyclic systems, often ten or more rings, decorated with enamines, imines, formamides and long alkenyl tails, at a size and complexity no synthesis could reach.
liabilities: fused polycyclic assemblies exceeding one hundred characters with no synthetic route implied
extended enamine and imine ladders as the main nitrogen chemistry
exocyclic double bonds written onto aromatic ring atoms throughout the high-scoring band
missing_features: an aromatic amide-linked biaryl core, which the outputs approximate only with non-aromatic fused carbocycles
sulfonamide, sulfone or comparable discrete polar linkers, essentially absent from the emitted set
any control of molecular size; the outputs are several times larger than the supplied starting molecules
clean substitution patterns on a single ring rather than nitrogen and oxygen scattered through a fused mass
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The scoring floor on this objective is 0.5 and almost everything lands within a few hundredths of it, from 0.5 to 0.5534. Larger molecules with more nitrogen and more ring closures sit at the top of that narrow band and short alkene fragments sit at the bottom, but the separation is only about 0.05 in total. The best constructed molecule at 0.5534 improved on the best supplied starting molecule at 0.5484 by 0.005, and that entire gain arrived in the first generated batch.

per_task.generated_character: Ring closures in 97 percent of strings but aromatic atoms in only 29 percent, mean length 85.6. The best molecules are tightly fused polycyclic cages with a ketone and an exocyclic quinoid ring, the middle of the distribution is long polyene chains threaded through occasional partially saturated rings, and the bottom is short acyclic aldehyde and thioether fragments.
liabilities: densely fused cage systems with bridgehead alkenes that violate normal strain limits
long conjugated polyene chains carrying isolated rings as decoration
exocyclic quinoid bonds onto aromatic rings in the highest-scoring molecule
missing_features: a basic protonatable amine on a saturated ring, absent from the emitted molecules
aromatic heterocycles such as pyridine or indole as ring building blocks
a simple two to four atom linker joining two distinct aromatic ends
molecules small enough to fit a binding site; mean size here is roughly double a typical ligand
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score climbs with ring count and with nitrogen inside rings rather than in chains: the top molecule at 0.1371 is a compact fused cage with two ring nitrogens, while the 0.0289 plateau that many molecules share is polyene chemistry with a couple of loose rings attached. The colony genuinely improved here, from a best supplied starting molecule at 0.0190 to 0.1371, the largest gain it achieved on any objective.

per_task.generated_character: Ring closures in 95 percent of strings, aromatic atoms in 31 percent, branching in every single molecule, mean length 87.4, the longest of the five. Typical outputs are large partially saturated fused polycyclics bearing aldehydes, enones and lactams, plus a long alkenyl or aminoalkyl tail.

N-oxide and nitro groups placed on strained ring systems
polyene chains bearing aldehyde and nitrile termini in the low-scoring band

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best band, 0.108 to 0.131, is consistently the fused polycyclic lactams and quinone-like systems; the worst band, 0.010 to 0.019, is acyclic polyene and polyketone chains with no ring system. As on the zaleplon objective, nothing the colony built beat a supplied starting molecule, so the reported final Top-1 of 0.1678 belongs to a starting molecule and the best construction reached only 0.1310.

per_task.generated_character: Ring closures in only 55 percent of strings and aromatic atoms in 20 percent, the lowest of the five, with mean length 74.2. The output is overwhelmingly acyclic: long unsaturated chains carrying esters, aldehydes, enones, amides and secondary amines, with only a minority closing any ring at all.
liabilities: unbranched conjugated polyene chains of 100 characters or more dominating the zero-scoring band
stacked Michael acceptors, with multiple enones and enals on one chain
thioether and thioaldehyde fragments appended to already unstable chains
missing_features: trifluoromethyl groups and polyfluorinated aromatic rings, essentially never constructed
fused bicyclic heteroaromatic amine cores of the triazolopyrazine type
saturated nitrogen heterocycles rather than chain amines and imines
a beta-amino amide arrangement placing a primary amine beta to a carbonyl
rings at all in nearly half the emitted molecules
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The median score is 0.0 and the worst is 0.0, so most proposals were valueless. The few that scored, up to 0.0980, are the shortest and most ring-bearing, pairing a lactone or cyclopentanone with a primary amine or enamine; every long chain scored zero or near zero. The best construction did beat the best supplied starting molecule at 0.0021, so the relative gain is large while the absolute level stays very low, and the final batch fell back to between 1e-13 and 0.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Aromatic atoms appear in only 20 to 42 percent of emitted molecules across all five objectives, against 55 to 97 percent that carry some ring closure. Rings that do form are written as non-aromatic alternating C=C closures or as strained fused cages, and the supplied starting molecules, which are aromatic throughout, are far more aromatic than anything the generator builds.
transferable_gaps.gap: Aromatic ring systems are barely reachable by this construction process
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A construction grammar that builds rings one bond at a time will only reach aromatic systems by accident unless aromatic rings are available as whole units. The generator needs closure moves that commit to a complete aromatic ring, or a fragment vocabulary containing common aromatic rings, rather than requiring the search to assemble six correct bonds in sequence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On two objectives more than half of the proposals scored zero and the zero band is uniformly 90 to 110 character strings of alternating C=C with methyl branches and almost no heteroatoms. The same chain motif persists into the final proposals rather than being bred out over the run.
transferable_gaps.gap: The dominant output motif is a long unbranched conjugated chain, not a molecule
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Chain extension is being selected far more often than closure or termination because it is always legal. The generator needs its stopping and closure moves weighted against the growing cost of the chain, or a hard cap on consecutive unsaturated chain extensions, so that proposals cannot degenerate into polymers.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Mean SMILES length ranges 74 to 87 characters on every objective with maxima of 113 to 127, and the constructions averaged around 50 atoms and reached 64. That is several times the size of the supplied starting molecules, and on every objective the largest outputs cluster at the bottom of the score range.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecule size is not bounded by anything the search can feel
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs an explicit size prior tied to the corpus it was built from, and a termination probability that rises with the current atom count, so that feedback about quality is not confounded with an unchecked drift toward larger structures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the emitted molecules, nitrogen shows up overwhelmingly as chain imines, enamines and secondary amines strung along an unsaturated backbone, while saturated heterocycles such as piperidine, piperazine and morpholine are essentially absent even in the best-scoring band of every objective.
transferable_gaps.gap: Nitrogen and oxygen appear as chain functionality rather than as ring members
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Heteroatom placement and ring closure are being chosen independently, so heteroatoms rarely end up inside rings. The generator needs its ring-closure moves to be conditioned on the heteroatom pattern of the growing fragment, or needs saturated heterocycles available as intact building blocks.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The highest-scoring constructions on several objectives are bridged polycyclic cages with quaternary bridgeheads, multiple three and four membered fused rings, and exocyclic quinoid double bonds drawn onto ring atoms. These pass a valence check but are not species a chemist would attempt.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring fusion produces strained cages and non-standard valence patterns
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Valence admissibility is too weak a gate on ring closure. The generator should restrict closures to ring sizes and fusion patterns observed in its corpus and reject bridgehead and strain configurations, so that its highest-reward outputs remain in reachable chemical space.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 across all five objectives and all 1,450 constructions, and the preparation step itself discarded corpus examples carrying specified stereochemistry, isotopes and larger ring closures as unsupported.
transferable_gaps.gap: No stereochemistry can be expressed at all
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Any reward depending on three-dimensional configuration is unreachable by construction. Stereo descriptors have to be part of the action space and survive into the emitted structure, rather than being dropped when the grammar was derived.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Reinforced moves were reused inside structurally different partial molecules 71,453 times, and 1,399 accepted proposals inherited that reinforcement, yet only 3 of them beat their own pre-batch incumbent. Nearly the whole population received the same nudge and almost none of it converted into better chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Shared credit is spread so widely that it stops being informative
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: When credit is keyed to a local description that recurs in almost every molecule, reinforcement acts as a global bias rather than as guidance. A generator sharing credit this way needs its context resolution scaled to how distinctive the context is, or a deposit weighted down for contexts that occur everywhere, so that reinforcement discriminates instead of drifting.

nodes.method_name: MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in MAX-MIN Ant System: construct solutions probabilistically from components, evaporate their pheromone weights, reinforce the iteration-best solution, and bound every pheromone weight away from zero and excessive dominance. [Stutzle and Hoos, Sections 2 and 4](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~hoos/Publ/fgcs00.pdf) describe this mechanism. Our molecular adaptation constructs a fresh graph from an empty state through valence-aware atom, bond, ring-closure and termination actions. Choice probabilities combine a fixed chemical heuristic with task-local pheromones keyed by the local attachment context and action, allowing a useful action to transfer between different partial graphs. Preparation uses the permitted unlabeled corpus only for aggregate construction frequencies and stopping statistics. Initialize pheromones broadly, reconstruct valid construction traces for the supplied scored molecules, and use their best trace for the initial reinforcement. Generate the announced batch through complete new construction trajectories; only accepted whole-molecule feedback drives evaporation and reinforcement of that batch's best trace. Resample failed or duplicate constructions locally. There is no stored complete-molecule library, corpus ranking or fixed product enumeration. The hypothesis is that reusing successful local construction choices across new molecular combinations raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Whether coarse construction contexts carry useful reward information quickly enough is unproven; pheromone concentration or validity alone is not success.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language prior from the supplied unlabeled strings and selects its checkpoint using a fixed holdout. Each objective starts with a fresh policy and a frozen reference prior. The current batch elites train together with a uniform sample from the thirty-two strongest earlier accepted elites, using unchanged accepted scores and original strings. A prior-likelihood-plus-reward target drives bounded updates, and the policy directly samples complete new molecules with chemical validation and duplicate rejection. Prior training gives every token equal weight, so predictions at branch openings receive a small share of the training objective even though the observed prior makes larger errors in those contexts.
approach.novelty: Balance the unlabeled learning objective between tokens predicted immediately after an opening branch parenthesis and all remaining tokens. When both groups occur, give each group half of the total loss weight while preserving equal weights within each group. This increases the influence of a measured difficult attachment-context class without changing molecular strings, token units, model architecture or any online search rule. The earlier sibling changed bracket tokenization; this experiment tests how existing prediction errors are weighted during prior learning. Better branch-context prediction is the intermediate claim, and its effect on valid novel chemistry remains a separate experiment outcome.

nodes.hypothesis: During unlabeled prior preparation, replace the uniform nonpadding token loss by an equal-weight mean of branch-entry target loss and remaining-target loss, where a branch-entry target immediately follows the input token (, while preserving the original unweighted holdout checkpoint criterion and all online learning and generation.

finding_summary.headline: Branch predictions improved in every seed, while validity and mean score fell
finding_summary.insights: The full holdouts extend the initial small probe: branch-entry prediction is a real, repeatable learning opportunity, and changing its loss allocation improves that prediction. The cost is also repeatable. Giving half the loss to roughly one-tenth of targets degrades the remaining contexts enough to worsen the ordinary language-model criterion. The observed logit-gradient movement establishes actual loss influence; it does not identify a parameter-level causal contribution to any task score. The downstream results separate branch syntax from useful attachment chemistry. Accepted scaffold variety remains broad, yet lower duplication accompanies lower validity and fewer novel raw draws. Conventional aminoquinazoline refinement can succeed locally, while the sitagliptin trajectories do not sustain favorable size, polar-group placement and nitrogen-functional-state combinations despite broad atom and ring coverage. Configurationally relevant products still lack stereochemical specification, and oversized or reactive outliers remain possible. This rules out failed loss activation and insufficient training exposure as explanations for the missing expected gain. The open question is whether context learning can preserve the much larger remaining-token group and improve useful molecular neighborhoods at the same time; improved accuracy immediately after an opening parenthesis is insufficient on its own.

molecular.overall_character: The assessment reads all 4,500 child and 4,500 Parent trajectory rows, including 4,350 optimizer proposals per node. nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent draws atom, bond, path and ring edits from one scored current molecule, normalizes the resulting isomeric identity, rejects duplicates and directly evaluates a full batch admitted by inverse-motif memory. It then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when its score worsens, with a separate best archive. The current atom-change operator chooses an eligible atom and then an alternative element; it can erase configuration during substitution but never offers a configuration-only edit. Local memory descriptions omit stereochemistry, while full molecular identity already retains it. The repaired identity join and existing memory lifecycle remain part of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Add local assignment or inversion of one eligible tetrahedral carbon as an option within the existing atom-change menu. An unassigned center offers both orientations; an assigned center offers its opposite orientation. Every such option preserves atomic composition and connectivity. Element substitutions remain available and the atom-change allocation weight stays fixed. This tests whether explicitly different configurations can reach evaluation and influence the observed walk. Earlier siblings changed sulfur eligibility and pendant-branch deletion; neither introduced a stereochemical edit, and neither is incorporated into this Child.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the Parent's existing atom-change menu with single-center tetrahedral-carbon configuration assignment or inversion, preserving the molecular composition and connectivity while allowing canonically distinct stereochemical neighbors to enter the unchanged novelty, tabu and accepted-score walk.

finding_summary.headline: Carbon configuration assignments reach evaluation, but every direct score comparison ties
finding_summary.insights: The missing configuration channel was a real generator limitation: it can now supply fresh evaluated identities without breaking the repaired identity join or changing graph chemistry. Its immediate effect here was neutral movement through differently annotated states. Because the inherited local motifs omit stereochemistry, all nine selected assignment moves advanced memory age without installing new inverse restrictions. Such moves can alter later search even when their own scores tie; later endpoint differences therefore do not demonstrate a preference for either configuration. The equal scores establish a limitation for the sampled unspecified-to-assigned comparisons only. No opposite fully assigned pair was evaluated, so the response to genuine configuration inversion remains open. The molecular assessment also shows that stereochemical labels leave the pre-existing aromatic, reactive-heteroatom and densely bridged sulfur-rich chemistry largely intact. Partial assignments neither resolve all centers nor establish accessible three-dimensional geometry or synthetic plausibility. The experiment narrows the next scientific question to whether configuration coverage can have useful measured consequences under this feedback and walk, rather than whether the generator can emit it.
finding_summary.results: All 24 configuration-only edits reached evaluation as distinct molecular identities while preserving composition and connectivity. Each assigned one previously unspecified carbon center; both relative orientations were sampled, but no assigned-center inversion was selected. Nine of these neighbors became the next current molecule with exactly the same score as their source. Assignments also survived many subsequent structural edits: 488 of 4,350 emitted neighbors contained an assigned carbon center, compared with none for the parent. Across 32 actually evaluated pairs sharing the same graph but differing in the extent of stereochemical assignment, every pair received equal scalar feedback. The complete three-seed mean nevertheless fell from 0.520918 to 0.511159, a paired change of -0.009759, exceeding the allowed 0.002 loss. Seed changes were +0.013487, +0.001052 and -0.043817; the main losses were in DRD2 and sitagliptin, while median improved slightly and the other two task means were unchanged. The proposal mechanism activated, but this panel does not support its score usefulness.
