The emitted aminocyclopentyl structure NC1CCC(c2c[nH]c3ccc(-n4cnnc4)cc23)C1 and substituted cyclopentene OCC1CC(n2cncn2)=C(c2cc(Br)cc(O)c2Br)C1c1ccccc1 contain saturated substitution patterns whose stereochemical alternatives are not specified. This establishes an output representation gap, not a measured score gain from stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not emit explicit stereochemical identities for its saturated and potentially stereogenic structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stereochemical specification available in de novo generation and preserve it through identity handling. Let accepted observations from the current session determine whether particular configurations are useful; do not assume every objective distinguishes them.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The structure c1ccc2c(c1)CCCN2CCCN1CCC(c2noc3ccccc23)CC1 scores 0.999998249672007, while the later amine-containing c1ccc(N2CCN(C(Cn3cccn3)c3ccncc3)CC2)cc1 scores 0.19802005266210823. In another supplied trajectory, O=S(=O)(Nc1ccc(-n2ccnc2)cc1)c1cccc2cnccc12 scores 0.5732259891576988 but O=S(=O)(CCNCCOc1ccc(Br)cc1)c1ccc(F)cc1 scores 0.2715410107705054. Both comparisons retain broad functional-group categories while changing connectivity and environment; they are observational contrasts, not matched molecular pairs. The output already contains cyclic amines and sulfur chemistry, so adding those categories alone would not address the gap.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not demonstrate controlled variation of linker geometry and nitrogen environment while preserving a promising ring arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support de novo conditional variations that can retain a locally promising ring framework while changing linker length, attachment position or a nitrogen functional state separately. Derive any retained arrangement only from accepted observations within the current session, without a task-specific motif library.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Task mean SMILES lengths stay between 37.6 and 39.8 characters, but long and elaborate tails remain. The long-chain phosphorus-acid structure O=P(O)(O)OP(=O)(O)c1cncc(CCCC#CCCCCCCC(O)CSCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCO)c1 scores 0.0, as do the bulky oxime-ether ester and glycoside cited above. A large polar guanidine/sulfonamide assembly and a large hydrophobic polyaryl amine score 2.1621778663534096e-63 and 4.5515839886258796e-63 in the same trajectory, while its compact heterocyclic examples reach 0.19736413136179395 and 0.18901307662677713. Conversely, a tiny nitrotriazole in another trajectory also scores poorly, so indiscriminate shortening is unsupported.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably control whole-molecule size and polar appendage growth around useful chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Allow de novo generation to adjust scaffold extent, branch growth and polar substitution separately, preserving enough context to learn which combinations the current accepted observations favor. Use adaptive chemical size control rather than treating SMILES length as molecular weight or imposing a universal small-molecule cutoff.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The emitted chlorinated peroxyester C=C(Cl)C(Cl)C(Cl)CCOOC(C)=O scores 0.02101192765437668 and the activated nitroalkene/sulfone C=C([N+](=O)[O-])S(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1 scores 9.203194082858293e-05. In contrast, some common amide, ether and cyclic-amine combinations score well. The high-scoring imino heterocycle also shows why an unfamiliar functional group cannot be discarded solely because it looks unusual.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a valid molecular graph from a chemically ordinary, plausibly preparable arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemical-stability, tautomer and synthetic-complexity context during generation or candidate review, so accepted feedback can distinguish useful diversity from awkward assemblies. Prefer coherent chemistry learned from the permitted unlabeled corpus; avoid blanket bans on heteroatoms, formal charge or all uncommon groups.

nodes.method_name: ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in [ChemTS](https://arxiv.org/html/1710.00616v1): train a compact autoregressive SMILES model solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze it. For each independent objective, maintain a fresh prefix tree whose nodes hold visit counts and observed returns. Initialize its statistics from the supplied observations. Select prefixes through upper-confidence tree search, expand them using the frozen model's next-token distribution, and generate complete molecules by stochastic continuation. Backpropagate accepted oracle scores through the corresponding paths after feedback. Generate further continuations until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. This is an expanding generative tree, with no corpus ranking or fixed molecular candidate set. The hypothesis is that sharing each scarce reward across its visited prefixes directs subsequent continuations toward promising molecular families quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. The root adapts tree statistics; it does not update neural parameters with rewards. The paper supports this search mechanism, but its larger, time-limited experiments do not establish performance under this benchmark's scarce feedback. Learning a useful rollout prior within permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.

approach.method_basis: A genetic algorithm run directly on molecular graphs. It keeps a population of molecules that have already been scored by the objective, samples breeding parents from the high-scoring end of that population, and builds new candidates by cutting two parents apart and recombining connected fragments, and by making small local edits to atoms and bonds. Everything generated is sanitised, canonicalised and sent straight to the oracle; whatever comes back with a good score is merged into the population and the weakest members are dropped. There is no surrogate model, no pretrained network, no library of catalogue molecules to rank, and no cross-task memory: the only thing that steers the search is the scores of the molecules this run has itself already paid for.
approach.novelty: The method statement leaves the selection pressure, the population bookkeeping and the failure handling open, and this implementation fixes all three. Parents are drawn from three declared high-ranked score bands rather than from a single elite cut, so breeding stays broad while still being score-directed. Survival is greedy on a bounded population of sixty-four, seeded only from the ten scored molecules supplied at the start, with accepted offspring merged the moment their scores arrive so the very next batch already breeds from them. Proposals that come back invalid or already-seen are replaced by generating more molecules from the same operators, never by falling back to a fixed reserve list. Seven distinct atom and bond mutation operators sit alongside fragment crossover, and every breeding event logs its parent ranks, operator provenance and parent-beating outcome so the selection pressure can be checked after the fact rather than assumed.

nodes.hypothesis: Evolve a task-local population of scored molecular graphs by sampling breeding parents across high-ranked score quantiles, generating de novo offspring with graph crossover and atom/bond mutation, and greedily retaining the highest-scoring observed survivors after each feedback batch.

finding_summary.headline: Plain graph evolution with no learned model ranks third of thirteen Discovery roots, and every intended behaviour activated
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a strong, cheap baseline. Against the thirteen Discovery roots on this seed, which span 0.2331 to 0.5103, this root sits third at 0.4917, within 0.019 of the best method in the round, and it did that with no pretraining, no corpus-trained generator, no surrogate and no learned policy. That reframes what the more elaborate lineages have to justify: any learned component now has to earn its place against direct selection on task-local scores, not against a naive baseline. The interesting tension is that activation was clean while efficiency was not. Roughly six in seven oracle calls went to molecules that did not beat the parent that made them, and the mean offspring was worse than its parent, so the strong result comes from occasionally getting lucky at scale rather than from reliably climbing. That is precisely the bottleneck a proposal-filtering mechanism would attack, and it is the most concrete Development target this root produces. What is still open: one seed only, so no reliability claim and no anchor decision; no paired comparison against any other algorithm; and the retry machinery was never stressed, since the longest rejection streak was two, so behaviour on an exhausted or hostile neighbourhood is untested.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean 0.4917 on the single screening seed, with per-task finals of 0.5989 on deco_hop, 0.9051 on drd2_docking, 0.2083 on median_2, 0.3315 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.4145 on zaleplon_mpo. All four pre-registered observables moved in the intended direction and the falsifier was not triggered. Parent selection was strongly score-directed: across 2225 breeding selections the mean topness percentile was 0.883 against a uniform baseline of 0.5, an enrichment of +0.383, and all three declared quantile bands were used on every task. Both operator families produced offspring on every task, with crossover behind 0.439 and atom/bond mutation behind 0.743 of the 1450 emitted molecules; 74 outer retries were needed for 1524 attempts. Feedback demonstrably changed the search: 1025 offspring were admitted to the population immediately, 432 distinct admitted offspring were later chosen as parents 2084 times, and reuse began in batch 2 on every task. Final population best rose above initialization everywhere, most sharply on drd2_docking (0.0190 to 0.9051) and sitagliptin_mpo (0.0021 to 0.3315). The one weak number is local improvement: only 201 of 1450 offspring, or 13.9 percent, strictly beat their best breeding parent, and the mean child-minus-best-parent difference was -0.084.

The campaign now has a strong, cheap baseline. Against the thirteen Discovery roots on this seed, which span 0.2331 to 0.5103, this root sits third at 0.4917, within 0.019 of the best method in the round, and it did that with no pretraining, no corpus-trained generator, no surrogate and no learned policy. molecular.headline: Ring-rich, aromatic, entirely achiral molecules that converge hard onto one inherited scaffold per run, with an unstable-motif tail
molecular.overall_character: Across all five runs the generator emits ring-heavy, strongly aromatic molecules: ring-closure rate 0.92 to 0.99 and aromatic-atom rate 0.89 to 0.96 in every run, with essentially no cumulated double bonds (0.000 to 0.007). Mean SMILES length varies widely by run, from 38.8 to 70.2, which shows the graph operators do grow and shrink molecules in response to feedback. What each run converges on is recognisably a decorated descendant of one of the ten molecules it started with: the top twelve structures in a run typically share a complete skeleton and differ only in single-atom substituent swaps. Two systematic absences stand out. Stereocentre rate is exactly 0.000 in all five runs, so the generator never writes a stereochemical assignment even when it builds tetrahedral ring-fusion carbons. Charged-atom rate is also exactly 0.000 everywhere, so no ionised or zwitterionic forms are ever proposed. Alongside the plausible majority there is a persistent tail of chemistry a bench chemist would reject outright: peroxide and trioxide chains, N-hypofluorite groups, S-O-N linkages, and degenerate one- and two-atom fragments that still consume oracle calls.

per_task.generated_character: Almost every proposal is a 6-5 fused bicyclic heteroaromatic carrying an aryl carboxamide. The entire top of the run is one indole or azaindole 2-carboxamide anilide skeleton rewritten with methyl, ethyl, methoxy, fluoromethyl and halogen swaps, and that skeleton is visibly a decorated version of the best molecule the run was handed at the start.
liabilities: Peroxide O-O linkages introduced by crossover between two aromatic cores
Bare one- and two-atom fragments such as elemental halides submitted as candidates
Thioamide substitution of the amide carbonyl, giving a metabolically unstable analogue
missing_features: No ring systems beyond the inherited bicycle - no bridged, spiro or tricyclic cores are ever built
No stereodefined sp3 centres anywhere in the run
No basic or ionizable side chain to balance the neutral amide core
No ring-size variation, since every new ring closed is five- or six-membered
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks how completely the inherited skeleton survives. The three structures tied at 0.4145 all keep the fused bicycle, the ring NH, the exocyclic amide and the 4-fluoroanilide intact and differ only at one substituent. The zero tail is either a one- or two-atom fragment or an oversized crossover product that fused two whole copies of the scaffold together, so the objective gives no partial credit for half a scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The run settles on the xanthine, or purine-2,6-dione, core carried in from the starting set. It is N-aminated with a halogenated aminopyridine and decorated with a second aryl or heteroaryl ring, and most of the top structures also hang a conjugated polyene or enamine tail off the core. Mean SMILES length reaches 56.6, so molecules here grow substantially larger than their parents.
liabilities: N-hypofluorite groups written on the imide nitrogen, which is not a real functional group
Long conjugated polyene tails built by repeated mutation at the same site
Peroxide and N-N-O chains formed by blind heteroatom substitution
missing_features: No saturated or partially saturated linker to place the decoration out of the core plane
No stereochemistry on the sp3 centres it does create
No ring systems beyond fused five- and six-membered rings and simple biaryl links
No acidic or basic ionizable group anywhere in the run
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The objective barely separates anything: the whole run lies between 0.500 and 0.599, and the starting molecules already scored 0.500 to 0.548, so the entire 29-batch search bought about 0.05. Everything sitting exactly at the 0.500 floor is a one- to three-heavy-atom fragment, which means the score behaves mostly as a has-any-structure indicator with a small decoration bonus on top.

per_task.generated_character: This is the one run whose winners look like a real receptor-ligand series. The strongest structures pair a 2-aryl-pyridine with an N-alkyl pyrrolidine or piperidine basic amine, several carrying a free carboxylic acid on the connecting carbon. Molecules are the largest of the five runs at mean length 70.2, and the ring-closure rate is the highest at 0.986.
liabilities: Aryl thiol substituents on the biaryl tail, which would oxidise readily
S-O-N chains produced by heteroatom substitution on the aromatic ring
Free aldehyde groups retained on high-scoring structures
missing_features: No stereochemistry, despite genuine tetrahedral centres in the winning series
No explicit protonated ammonium form of the basic amines
No conformationally constrained bicyclic amine head groups
No aromatic ring systems larger than a single biaryl pair
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises steeply with the presence of a protonatable N-alkyl saturated amine attached to a biaryl tail. The 0.905 and 0.884 structures both carry exactly that pair, whereas the 0.0004 to 0.002 tail retains the aromatic halves and has lost the basic nitrogen entirely. Adding halogen and thiol decoration to the tail while keeping the amine moves the score only within the 0.72 to 0.91 band, so the amine is the discontinuity and the decoration is fine-tuning.

per_task.generated_character: One fused polycyclic aminal-plus-cyclic-urea cage bearing an ethoxy-substituted aryl arm dominates the entire top of the run. The twelve best differ only in whether individual ring carbonyls are C=O or C=N, whether the aryl arm is propyl or butanoyl, and whether an extra amino group is present. Halogen rate is 0.145, the lowest of the five runs, so the generator essentially stopped using halogens here.
liabilities: Aminal N-CH2-N motifs at the heart of every top structure, which would hydrolyse readily
Cumulated allene-type double bonds appearing in a small fraction of proposals
Enamine C=C linkages conjugated into the ring carbonyls
missing_features: No aromatic variation beyond an unsubstituted or amino-substituted phenyl ring
No halogen substitution anywhere on the winning series
No stereochemistry on the several sp3 ring-fusion atoms in the cage
No alternative cage topology - the same fused system is reused for the whole run
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The band is extremely narrow, 0.2008 to 0.2083 across the whole top twelve, while the losing tail is trivially small - a single carbon, acetonitrile, ethanol, isopropyl chloride. So the gradient rewards keeping the complete cage plus arm assembled and is almost flat once that assembly exists, which is why the search plateaued at 0.2038 for batches 14 through 21.

per_task.generated_character: Compact, heavily oxygenated fused polycyclics: a methoxylated benzene fused to an imidazole and to a dioxole or dioxane ring, usually with one fluorine sitting on a ketal-like carbon. Mean SMILES length is 38.8, the shortest of the five runs, and the aromatic rate drops to 0.886, so this run built more saturated ring content than the others.
liabilities: Peroxide and trioxide chains such as O-O-O-C appearing in the zero-scoring tail
Orthoester and ketal carbons carrying both a fluorine and two alkoxy groups
One- and two-atom fragments submitted as candidates and consuming oracle calls
missing_features: No trifluoromethyl or polyfluorinated aliphatic groups
No primary aliphatic amine or amide nitrogen chain
No stereochemistry, although the chemistry this objective rewards is stereodefined
No open-chain flexible backbone - almost everything proposed is caged
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 0.331 winner and its 0.271, 0.250 and 0.238 followers are the same tetracyclic ketal-imidazole with the fluorine and methoxy positions permuted, so the run is a single-scaffold decoration search. Everything at zero is either a single atom, a diatomic, or an oversized dimer built by crossover, and the median score of 0.031 against a best of 0.331 shows how sharply the objective drops away from that one cage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.000 in all five independent runs, across 1450 proposed molecules, even though the winning series in several runs contain genuine tetrahedral carbons - a substituted pyrrolidine attached to a biaryl, ring-fusion carbons in a fused aminal cage - where configuration would change the chemistry entirely.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no concept of stereochemistry at all
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator set writes only flat connectivity. A generator that can address three-dimensional chemistry needs mutation operators that set, invert and permute tetrahedral and double-bond configuration as first-class edits, and a novelty check that treats two configurations of the same skeleton as distinct molecules rather than as a duplicate to reject.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In every run the entire top twelve share a complete ring skeleton that is visibly present in one of the ten molecules the run was handed at the start, and successive improvements only swap single substituents on it. Where a new ring does appear it comes from fusing two copies of an existing core together, which produced oversized dimers that scored zero.
transferable_gaps.gap: Rings are inherited and decorated, never invented
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Fragment recombination plus atom and bond edits can decorate a skeleton but cannot construct an unseen ring system, so the reachable chemistry is bounded by whatever ring systems the starting molecules happen to contain. A generator would need ring-construction and ring-breaking operators, or a fragment source outside the current population, to reach scaffolds not present at initialization.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Bare one- and two-atom species - a chlorine atom, a diatomic interhalogen, a single carbon, acetonitrile, ethanol - were emitted as candidates and consumed oracle evaluations, scoring zero every time. At the other extreme, crossover produced dimers well over 140 characters that also scored zero. Both extremes appear in the worst-scoring set of multiple runs.
transferable_gaps.gap: No control over what counts as a submittable molecule
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Validity is being checked only as chemical sanitisation, which a lone halogen passes. A generator spending a fixed evaluation budget needs a size and complexity floor and ceiling on emitted structures, so that operator accidents are rejected and regenerated locally instead of being paid for at the oracle.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Peroxide and trioxide chains linking two aromatic rings, N-hypofluorite groups written onto an imide nitrogen, and S-O-N chains on an aromatic ring all appear among the proposed molecules, in some cases inside otherwise reasonable structures. These are products of substituting one heteroatom for another without any check on the resulting local environment.
transferable_gaps.gap: Blind heteroatom substitution creates motifs that cannot exist as stable compounds
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation alphabet treats all heteroatom swaps as equivalent. A generator would need a substructure-level plausibility screen applied after each edit, rejecting known-unstable local environments before the molecule is proposed, which costs nothing at the oracle and removes a systematic slice of wasted budget.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Within each run the twelve best molecules differ from one another by single-atom substituent swaps, and the population best plateaus for long stretches - fifteen consecutive batches with no improvement in one run, eight in another - while the population mean keeps creeping up. The search is refining a single basin rather than testing alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Selection collapses onto one skeleton and cannot recover breadth
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Greedy score-ranked survival on a bounded population removes structural variety faster than the operators can regenerate it, so the population converges to near-duplicates and breeding produces near-duplicates in turn. A generator needs an explicit diversity term in survival, a similarity cap on the retained population, or a restart mechanism, so that budget spent after a plateau is spent somewhere new.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The charged-atom rate is exactly 0.000 in all five runs. Carboxylic acids and basic amines do appear, but always drawn in their neutral forms, and no quaternary, zwitterionic or explicitly ionised species is generated anywhere in 1450 molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: No ionizable or charged chemistry is ever proposed
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operators never place a formal charge, so a whole region of chemistry - permanently charged head groups, zwitterions, salt forms - is unreachable regardless of how the objective scores. A generator intended to cover ordinary medicinal chemistry needs charge-setting edits and a canonicalisation policy that preserves them.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The failed NF-BO Parent searches around already scored molecules using an injective SELFIES sequence flow. It learns the flow density from unlabeled molecules, adapts the same flow to high-scoring observations within each independent objective, and re-encodes every observation before fitting its latent Gaussian process. It generates fresh trust-region proposals by perturbing whole token blocks according to estimated sequence-level pointwise mutual information, ranks them with correlated Thompson samples, and decodes through the explicit inverse flow. Canonical validity and novelty checks refill each announced batch. This recovery retains that algorithm and every bound mechanism.
approach.novelty: This is a numerical recovery of the failed Parent, not a new research mechanism. Execute the loaded task-local flow, recurrent states, and its continuous latent path in double precision so that rounding drift is less likely to cross a token-decoding boundary after adaptation. Preserve the strict equality check for every token, including termination and padding, and retain every adaptation step. The proposed precision repair is not yet verified; success requires the original reconstruction checks and complete task execution.

nodes.hypothesis: Recover the recorded post-adaptation left-inverse crash by promoting the loaded task-local sequence flow and its continuous recurrent forward/inverse latent calculations from float32 to float64, with dtype-compatible probe assignment and unchanged strict token reconstruction checks.

finding_summary.headline: Double precision restores exact reconstruction and completes all five tasks; recorded best scores stay unchanged.
finding_summary.insights: The result supports finite-precision recurrent inverse drift as a recoverable implementation bottleneck: strict equality survives without omitting padding, dropping observations, or skipping adaptation. It does not identify the original mismatched token positions, so a padding-only explanation remains unproven. Numerical recovery also leaves the main search-quality questions intact. Nominal 95% GP intervals cover only 466 of 1,450 outcomes (32.1%); coverage on the 1,240 shared predictions is unchanged at 444 outcomes, and only 22 of the 210 added predictions are covered. In addition, 97.6% of examined decodes reproduce their generating center. The molecular assessment finds the same narrow high-scoring families and recurring unusual charged heteroatoms and chain growth, with weak chemical plausibility. These findings make surrogate calibration and useful, chemically credible local variation worth probing independently. Recovery is demonstrated for this seed and checkpoint under the existing budget; continuous inverse error still reaches 0.004864 in one successful check, so exact reconstruction here does not establish stability for arbitrary future histories.
finding_summary.results: On the screening seed, all five objectives complete 300 evaluations. The two sessions that previously stopped at 150 and 240 evaluations now finish, bringing the total from 1,290 to 1,500. All 300 reconstruction checks preserve the full padded token sequence and canonical molecule: 46,500 of 46,500 observation-check instances match exactly. At the former failure points, maximum continuous inverse error falls from 0.405526 to 0.000005301 on drd2_docking and from 0.404005 to 0.00000001510 on median_2. Preparation produces the identical checkpoint. All 150 online adaptations execute their original 24 steps, every GP fit uses freshly encoded observations, PMI still favors informative token blocks, and posterior uncertainty still affects selection. Every emitted batch contains ten valid novel molecules. The completed macro score is 0.419751565. All 1,290 shared trajectory records match the parent exactly, and the additional 210 evaluations produce no new task best. Because the parent lacks a complete macro score, these results establish numerical recovery without establishing a paired macro-score gain.

molecular.headline: Recognizable aryl and nitrogen heterocycles persist among the high scorers, amid unusual charged heteroatoms and unsaturated chains.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-50bccbe8104b produces recognizable aryl amides, diaryl nitrogen linkers, pyrrolidines and carbonyl-rich heterocycles, together with extensive ring opening, unusual heteroatom substitutions and chain growth. The seed-0 digest covers 300 records per task, including 290 optimizer proposals and 10 supplied initial molecules. Rings are frequent: the per-task ring-closure rates range from 0.631 to 0.9828, while aromatic-marker rates range from 0.3103 to 0.6517. These are fractions of SMILES containing text markers, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. The output is therefore neither ring-free nor uniformly aromatic. Its most recognizable higher-scoring series remain concentrated around a few aryl and nitrogen-containing frameworks, despite 300 unique recorded molecules per task. The collection has weak medicinal-chemistry plausibility because ordinary fragments are repeatedly connected through undercoordinated charged atoms, unusual multiply bonded boron, phosphorus or sulfur, labile-looking nitrogen/oxygen linkages, or long unsaturated tails. The synthetic-plausibility judgment concerns these specific combinations; it does not assert that all organoboron, organophosphorus, charged molecules or cumulenes are impossible. No synthesis or stability evidence is supplied, and no measured binding interpretation is inferred from a scalar score. Compared with Parent n-77c41c9bc036, every shared trajectory record is identical in molecule, score and evaluation order. Three full trajectories are unchanged; the other two extend identical prefixes from 150 and 240 records to 300. Every task retains the same recorded best score. nodes.method_name: NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals
nodes.method_thesis: Use NF-BO's SeqFlow mapping, exact left-inverse decoding, and token-adaptive trust-region search. Train a compact SELFIES flow on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Within each fresh objective session, adapt it using highly scored task-local sequences, re-encode all observations after updates, and fit a latent-space GP. Generate new latent proposals around scored observations by perturbing token blocks according to their estimated pointwise mutual information with the decoded sequence. Thompson sampling selects proposals for inverse-flow decoding. These mechanisms follow [NF-BO, Sections 4 and 5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.14889v1). Regenerate as needed to fill the evaluator-announced batch with distinct canonical molecules; no corpus molecules are ranked or retrieved. The hypothesis is that score-directed local search around exactly reconstructable observations finds improving structures efficiently enough to raise the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Exact reconstruction alone is not the objective. Useful flow training and surrogate prediction under the permitted preparation and feedback remain empirical prerequisites.

approach.method_basis: The reference is MolDQN, published by Zhou and colleagues, which applies value-based reinforcement learning directly to molecular graphs, with no generative model in between. It starts from a molecule that already has a real score and then runs a short episode of single edits: add or remove an atom, add or remove a bond, change a bond order, always within what valence allows. At each step it draws a bounded set of legal successor molecules and asks a small neural network which one is worth taking, where the network is given fingerprints of the current molecule and the candidate, how many edits are left in the episode, and the best score the episode has seen so far. Selection is epsilon-greedy, so most of the time it takes the network's favourite and occasionally it takes a random legal edit. The reward is not the new molecule's score but the amount by which that score raises the episode's running best, so an edit that makes things worse earns nothing and is still taken as the next state to build from. That is the point of the method: a molecule can be walked downhill deliberately if the network expects a payoff a few edits later. Because there is no discounting and rewards are increments of a running maximum, an episode's total return is exactly the improvement it achieved. The network learns by double Q-learning from a replay buffer of edits that actually received oracle scores: an online network picks the best continuation from the successor state, a lagged copy of that network supplies its value, and the difference between that target and the online prediction drives the update.
approach.novelty: The commitments this root makes go well beyond the method statement. The reward definition is the largest: rewarding the increment to the episode's running best, undiscounted, is an adaptation chosen so that the quantity the agent maximises telescopes into exactly the best-score improvement the benchmark cares about, rather than the original formulation's terminal-property reward. Episodes are deliberately short, six edits, with ten independent lanes interleaved so that each ten-proposal batch contains exactly one pending action per lane and no lane ever influences another mid-batch. Candidate actions are drawn fresh every time, forty at each decision and eight for each replay continuation, and crucially the continuations used to form learning targets are re-sampled at training time rather than stored, so the action set is never allowed to harden into a fixed candidate library. Value predictions for candidates that were not selected stay predictions: only edits the oracle actually scored enter replay, and a rejected action leaves the lane's state and remaining depth untouched. The root uses one Q-head with a declared epsilon schedule falling from 0.4 toward roughly 0.16, explicitly no ensemble and no episode-fixed randomised value function, so that any exploration benefit later observed can be attributed. Each objective restarts weights, target copy, optimizer, replay and archive from nothing, and preparation stores no learned artifact and no molecule pool at all.

nodes.hypothesis: Select fresh molecular graph edits with a single epsilon-greedy continuation-value network, advance persistent finite-horizon episodes through every matched accepted successor, and learn from accepted transitions using undiscounted episode-best improvement rewards and double-Q Bellman backups through a lagged target network.

finding_summary.headline: Graph-edit Q-learning activated in full but scored 0.4067, eighth of thirteen Discovery roots
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a clean answer to a question it could not previously separate: correct temporal-credit machinery is not by itself worth a score. Every part of the Bellman construction was audited and held, including the exact double-Q target, the detached lagged network, reward telescoping, and the use of updated weights in subsequent decisions, and the result still lands in the lower half of the roots and below the frozen-latent swarm root that carries no learning at all. Two mechanisms explain that. The learning signal is thin, because four fifths of transitions carry zero reward under a running-best definition, so most gradient comes from the zero mass and the mean continuation term of 0.014 sits at the same scale as the residual error the network still has, which is also why nearly three thousand continuation values came out negative when the true quantity cannot be. And the search collapses: the molecules produced show that exploitation, once it finds a good core, spends its remaining budget swapping single atoms on that core, which is precisely the behaviour a value function would need a long-horizon reason to escape. For method choice this argues that direct graph editing is the right way to stay in makeable chemistry, but that pairing it with a value-learning controller adds machinery whose payoff is not visible at this feedback scale; the effort is better spent on the exploration and diversity side than on the credit-assignment side. Still open: this is a single seed with no parent and no paired comparison, so the ranking is indicative; the 216 recovered-loss links and 123 later episode-best gains after temporary losses are descriptive and do not isolate learned lookahead from ordinary hill-climbing; and whether episode-consistent randomised exploration would change the picture was deliberately left untested here.
finding_summary.results: One screening seed, macro mean 0.406692671573943, eighth among the campaign's thirteen Discovery roots on a spread running 0.2331 to 0.5103. Per objective the means were 0.7536466193285815 on the docking task, 0.6145349727054742 on the decoration-hop task, 0.33218372414937963 on the zaleplon task, 0.19512536527753646 on the median task and 0.13797267640874414 on the sitagliptin task. Every registered observable moved as intended. The graph sampler filled all 1450 acting neighbourhoods with 40 valid novel candidates each and all 20215 replay continuation neighbourhoods with eight, emitting exactly 29 batches of ten unique molecules per objective with zero invalid, duplicate or rejected proposals; an independent re-execution of 17026 distinct edit receipts reproduced every one. The temporal machinery worked: 250 episode starts, 1200 multistep continuations, and 800 accepted transitions that strictly lowered the score yet still advanced their lane, of which 666 went on to be the source of a later edit. Reward telescoping held to a maximum residual of 5.551115123125783e-17 with gamma exactly one. Of 22900 replay targets, 2685 were horizon terminals equal to reward and all 20215 nonterminal continuation terms were nonzero, mean 0.013847408184662015, so the targets genuinely differed from reward-only regression. Learning registered: mean paired Huber loss fell from 6.10635587187527e-05 to 5.3964929417511364e-05 and mean absolute temporal-difference error from 0.004401601105964189 to 0.004148056249060887, decreasing on every objective, with 1242 of 1450 individual steps improving. The learned values then drove behaviour: 1095 exploitation choices against 355 random ones, every neighbourhood showing nonconstant values, and a fixed sixteen-candidate diagnostic probe changing its preferred molecule 30 times over training. The counterweight is the sparsity of signal: 1179 of 1450 accepted transitions carried zero reward, only 271 were positive, and 2880 of the sampled continuations were predicted negative even though a true remaining episode-best gain can never be below zero.

molecular.headline: Drug-like fused aromatic scaffolds inherited from the seeds, decorated with impossible bonds and collapsed onto one core per objective
molecular.overall_character: Because every molecule is one legal edit away from a molecule that was already there, this node's output looks far more like real medicinal chemistry than a decoder's would. Ring closures appear in 99 to 100 percent of emitted molecules and aromatic atoms in 94 to 100 percent; the sets are full of genuine fused heterocycles, indoles, coumarins, xanthines, benzodioxoles and aminopyridines, carrying amides, sulfonamides and basic amines at sensible positions. The two problems are structural rather than cosmetic. First, the edit operators are constrained only by valence and connectivity, so they cheerfully form bonds that no chemist would draw: oxygen-fluorine, oxygen-chlorine and oxygen-bromine hypohalites, nitrogen-sulfur and nitrogen-chlorine bonds on imide nitrogens, NON(O)O chains, peroxides, hemiaminals, and three-membered oxygen rings fused straight onto an arene. Second, the search converges hard: within any objective the twelve highest-scoring molecules are one- and two-atom variants of a single core, several sharing scores to four decimal places, so what reads as optimisation is largely relabelling. Stereochemistry is absent everywhere and no molecule carries a formal charge.

per_task.generated_character: Two families only. One is a methoxy- or ethoxy-substituted fused indole bearing a carbinolamine and an N-linked fluorinated bicycle, repeated with single-atom substitutions across almost the entire best list. The other is the supplied dimethoxyindole carboxamide with one atom changed. Ring closure and aromatic rates are both at or near 1.0, and the halogen rate of 0.86 comes almost entirely from a single inherited aryl fluoride.
liabilities: carbinolamine and aminal centres of the C(O)N type, which are hydrolytically unstable
sulfur attached directly to an amide or ring nitrogen as a bare SH
a bridged bicyclic alkene written across ring-closure pairs that would be anti-Bredt
a cumulated allene fragment surviving in the low-scoring set
missing_features: no pyrazolopyrimidine or comparable fused bicyclic nitrogen core is ever constructed
no nitrile group appears despite it being a common feature of this chemotype
no N,N-dialkyl acetamide is built onto the aryl ring
no stereochemistry on the sp3 carbinolamine centre the scaffold creates
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top eleven molecules occupy a band from 0.317 to 0.332 and differ from each other by a methyl versus ethyl, a hydroxyl versus methoxy, or the position of one substituent, so score is essentially flat across the whole exploited core. The zero-scoring tail is composed entirely of the supplied starting molecules and their immediate first edits, which means the improvement came in one jump and was then elaborated rather than extended.

per_task.generated_character: A single scaffold, elaborated exhaustively: a methoxy-substituted coumarin or benzoxazinone fused to a three-membered oxygen ring, bearing an aminopyridine that in turn carries a second heteroaryl with sulfur and oxygen substituents. Aromatic atoms appear in 100 percent of molecules and rings in 100 percent, and the mean length of 56 characters is stable across the run, which is what a converged edit search looks like.
liabilities: sulfenic acid substituents written as SO and OS directly on an aromatic ring
a three-membered oxygen ring fused across two adjacent aromatic carbons, an arene oxide
an NON(O)O chain built onto a fused heteroaromatic
an O-bromo substituent on a lactone carbon, which is a hypobromite
missing_features: no sulfonamide is ever formed, only lower sulfur oxidation states
no saturated ring is added anywhere on the periphery
no basic amine or other solubilising handle is introduced
no stereochemistry, even where the fused three-membered ring creates defined faces
per_task.score_gradient_reading: All twelve best molecules fall between 0.594 and 0.615, separated only by whether a given position carries SO, OS, O, S, Br or SC, and by whether the fused ring is a five- or six-membered lactone. The worst molecules, at 0.52 to 0.53, are the supplied starting molecules with a single atom changed. The objective evidently rewards the scaffold much more than the decoration, and the search extracted that in the first few batches and then plateaued.

per_task.generated_character: The most convincing output of the run and the longest, averaging 72 SMILES characters. Almost every high scorer is a dichlorophenyl sulfur group on a methylated diazepane or piperazine, connected through a benzylic tertiary amine to a pyridine bearing a fluorophenol and an acetic acid arm. These are recognisable ligand-shaped molecules assembled by editing the supplied sulfonamide reference, with a halogen rate of 0.92.
liabilities: a sulfilimine-oxide written as C=S(=O)(N), which is not a preparable functional group
an aryl hypofluorite O-F substituent standing in for a fluorine
an S-chloro substituent on an aromatic ring
an aminal nitrogen placed alpha to a ring nitrogen in the diamine
missing_features: the inherited sulfonamide is never rebuilt at full oxidation state once degraded
no stereochemistry on either the benzylic or the ring sp3 centre, both of which a real ligand would define
no alternative aromatic core is ever explored beyond the one inherited from the seed
no amide linker is offered as a replacement for the sulfur-nitrogen hinge
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks how much of that assembled pharmacophore survives. The 0.65 to 0.75 band keeps all four pieces, the dichloroaryl sulfur, the cyclic diamine, the basic benzylic amine and the fluorophenol-pyridine; the 0.23 to 0.46 band loses one, usually by swapping a hydroxyl onto the dichloroaryl or replacing fluorine with an O-F. The near-zero tail is small aziridine and bromoalkane fragments produced early before the core was found.

per_task.generated_character: One core and nothing else: an N,N-dimethyl xanthine fused to a benzofuran, carrying an alkoxyphenyl on the ring-fusion nitrogen. Every one of the twelve best molecules is that scaffold with one substituent moved or relabelled, and the aromatic and ring rates are both exactly 1.0. It is inherited almost intact from the strongest supplied starting molecule.
liabilities: an N-chloro imide nitrogen, which is an oxidising and unstable group
a peroxide written into an alkoxy substituent as CCOOC
an ynol ether, an alkyne bonded directly to an aromatic oxygen
an epoxide appended by atom insertion onto a heteroaromatic ring
missing_features: no scaffold departure at all from the inherited xanthine-benzofuran system
no aliphatic or saturated ring is ever introduced into the molecule
no ionisable acid or base handle is added anywhere
no stereochemistry, though several edits create sp3 ring carbons
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best band spans 0.189 to 0.195, a range of six thousandths across twelve molecules, and the two top entries share the same score to six decimal places while differing by an ether position. The worst molecules at 0.106 to 0.117 are edits of the other supplied starting molecules that never reached this core. So the entire gain over the supplied incumbent of 0.168 is a small decoration effect on a scaffold the search was handed rather than found.

per_task.generated_character: The node's weakest objective. Output is a single purinone or pyrazolo-fused bicyclic core carrying two aryl rings, a fluorine on one of them, a hydroxymethyl on the imide nitrogen and a bare sulfur on the ring nitrogen, repeated with tiny variations. Aromatic atoms are present in 94 percent of molecules and rings in 100 percent, so this is a flat, fully unsaturated set.
liabilities: a bare SH substituent on an imide nitrogen, which is a sulfenamide with no stability
N-hydroxymethyl hemiaminal groups on both imide nitrogens
a benzylic hypofluorite written as COF on an aromatic ring
a thiocarboxylic acid formed by substituting sulfur into a carboxyl
missing_features: no trifluoromethyl group is ever assembled, only single fluorine substituents
no saturated fused ring or piperazine-like system is constructed
no primary aliphatic amine beta to a carbonyl
no defined stereochemistry, which for a target defined by one configuration caps the score outright
no polyfluorinated aromatic ring
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Scores are compressed between 0.110 and 0.138, with five of the twelve best sharing 0.115357 exactly while differing only in where the fluorine and hydroxymethyl sit on their respective rings. The zero tail is edits of the supplied starting molecules. There is no readable gradient here at all: the search found one core early, and moving substituents around it changes almost nothing.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Emitted molecules carry oxygen-fluorine, oxygen-chlorine and oxygen-bromine bonds (OF, OCl, OBr substituents), nitrogen-sulfur and nitrogen-chlorine bonds on imide nitrogens, NON(O)O chains, and a sulfilimine-oxide written C=S(=O)(N). Every one of these passed sanitisation, reparsing and an independent structural re-execution.
transferable_gaps.gap: Edit operators form element pairings that valence permits but chemistry forbids
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Legality checks on valence and connectivity are not sufficient to keep a graph editor inside makeable chemistry. The proposal step needs an element-pair and functional-group context filter, so that a heteroatom-heteroatom bond is only formed where such a bond is actually known, applied before a molecule consumes an oracle call.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In every objective the twelve highest-scoring molecules are one- or two-atom variants of a single fused scaffold, with score bands as narrow as six thousandths across all twelve, and five molecules in one set sharing an identical score to six decimal places. Late-run output is indistinguishable from mid-run output apart from substituent position.
transferable_gaps.gap: The search collapses onto one core and then relabels single atoms
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Sampling a local neighbourhood and taking its best member cannot leave a basin once it is in one, no matter how good the value estimate is, because every legal move is one atom wide. A generator needs a scaffold-level move, an explicit novelty or diversity pressure across lanes, or forced restarts from unrelated regions, or it will spend the majority of its budget confirming a structure it already has.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Sulfonamides present in the starting molecules are degraded to sulfinamides and then to sulfilimine-oxide forms, and sulfur substituents appear across the range from thioether to sulfenic acid within a single best list, purely as the by-product of adding and deleting oxygen atoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group oxidation state is edited as if it were a free variable
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Treating a functional group as an arbitrary collection of atoms lets the editor wander through oxidation states that are not isolable. Groups should be manipulated as units with a declared set of allowed states, so that an oxygen deletion either produces a real lower oxidation state or is not offered at all.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring-closure rates of 0.99 to 1.00 sit alongside aromatic-atom rates of 0.94 to 1.00, and no emitted molecule introduces a new aliphatic ring: rings that appear are either inherited flat heteroaromatics or accidental three-membered oxygen rings fused onto an arene.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator builds no saturated or three-dimensional structure
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Atom and bond edits on an aromatic template can decorate but cannot saturate, so the whole sp3-rich half of drug-like space is unreachable. Ring-forming operators that close aliphatic rings, and operators that reduce aromatic systems, are needed for a generator to explore three-dimensional shape.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 across every emitted molecule, including the many products bearing sp3 ring carbons with four distinct substituents and the benzylic amine centres the operators construct.
transferable_gaps.gap: No stereochemistry is set even where the edits create defined centres
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: An edit vocabulary that changes atoms and bonds but never sets configuration cannot address any property that depends on it, and worse, it silently produces racemic answers to questions whose answer is a single enantiomer. Stereo-setting operators and stereo-aware features are a prerequisite, not a refinement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Inserting a single oxygen produced peroxides such as the CCOOC ether chain, inserting oxygen next to nitrogen produced carbinolamine and hemiaminal centres of the C(O)N type, and inserting carbon next to an aromatic oxygen produced an ynol ether. None of these were rejected.
transferable_gaps.gap: Atom insertion creates unstable linkages as an unnoticed by-product
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Single-atom insertion is the operator most likely to build a group nobody intended, because the atom lands between two existing heteroatoms. A proposal-time substructure blocklist covering peroxides, hemiaminals, strained fused small rings and heteroatom-heteroatom chains would remove most of this class at no cost to reach.

nodes.method_name: MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in MolDQN's value-based control of molecular edits: learn future action returns from scored transitions and choose subsequent graph modifications with a deep Q-network. [Zhou et al., Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/1810.08678v3) describe finite molecular edit episodes, fingerprint features and double Q-learning. Our adaptation starts short episodes from task-local scored molecules and samples fresh valence-aware atom and bond edits at each state. A compact Q-network takes current and successor fingerprints, remaining episode depth and the episode's best observed score. Use a single Q-function with epsilon-greedy action selection in the root. Evaluate only selected new whole molecules; values assigned to unselected successors are predictions. Advance each trajectory after its matched feedback, even when the new molecule scores worse. For Top-1 alignment, use reward max(previous_episode_best, new_score) minus previous_episode_best and undiscounted finite-horizon backups: accumulated reward equals improvement in that episode's best score. This reward adaptation is our inference, not the paper's original reward. Train immediately from accepted transition replay using double-Q target selection and a lagged target network, with zero continuation value at episode termination. Retain all accepted intermediate molecules in the task incumbent archive. Interleave episodes according to announced batches, and generate further edits to replace invalid or duplicate proposals. Each decision samples an evolving neighborhood; no corpus pool, complete-molecule retrieval or fixed candidate enumeration is involved. No pretrained generator or external labels are required, and every objective starts with clean learning state. The hypothesis is that learned lookahead identifies useful edit sequences, including temporary score losses, quickly enough to raise the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Learning useful continuation values from scarce transitions is unproven; the paper's much larger training regime does not establish this transfer.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a population of at most sixty-four accepted molecules, kept in descending score order. It chooses a high-ranking score band and then a molecule uniformly within that band, produces a fresh surplus of crossover and mutation offspring, and uses correlated draws from a fingerprint Gaussian process to choose which offspring to evaluate. Every accepted score trains the posterior, even if its molecule leaves the breeding population. This loop reliably learns and selects, but most evaluated offspring do not improve on their generating parents, and successful molecular cores accumulate many close relatives.
approach.novelty: Give each represented molecular core equal breeding probability within the already selected score band. A core with many surviving analogues will share its probability among those analogues, while a less represented accepted core gains an opportunity to breed. The existing preference for high-scoring bands remains intact. The lineage's earlier child changed how generated offspring are selected for evaluation; this child changes only which accepted parents produce those offspring. Neither recorded sibling nor a supplied mechanism cluster has tested this conditional correction for core multiplicity.

nodes.hypothesis: Within each inherited score quantile, sample accepted breeding parents with probability inversely proportional to the number of eligible survivors sharing their Murcko core, so every represented core has equal conditional mass.

finding_summary.headline: Core-balanced breeding broadened core use and raised parent-beating yield, but lowered final scores.
finding_summary.insights:
Equalizing core probability can reduce repeated use of abundant families without improving the best molecules found. The clearest coverage expansions were in decoration hopping and DRD2, yet their parent-beating counts and final-score means fell. Zaleplon breeding became more concentrated despite correct balancing within each selected band, showing that changing the conditional draw does not guarantee broader realized coverage once the evolving survivor population is considered.

The modest parent-beating gain also uses a weaker reference: mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.419645 to 0.395720, while mean evaluated-offspring score fell from 0.319152 to 0.301731. This relative yield gain therefore does not establish stronger offspring production. The number of admitted offspring later reused for breeding stayed almost unchanged, at 2,163 versus 2,167, and incumbent gains did not increase. The evidence narrows the problem to allocating toward productive surviving families rather than simply reducing their multiplicity imbalance; discarded or ineligible cores still receive no opportunity. The molecular assessment also shows that broader structural coverage continues to include repeated heterocycle growth, tiny fragments, reactive nitrogen-halogen/peroxide groups and strained fused rings. Murcko-core coverage alone does not resolve those quality limitations. Passive comparisons supply probabilities and parent identities, with no scores for alternate offspring or an alternate search trajectory.
finding_summary.results:
The allocation change executed correctly in all three replicas. Of 111,246 parent draws, 86,634 had unequal core multiplicities; every logged probability vector and inverse-CDF choice matched the intended rule. On the same eligible states and logged uniform variates, 36,398 selected parent ranks and 29,554 selected cores differed from the passive uniform comparator. Mean represented cores used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 14.60, and mean concentration of breeding uses fell from 0.299 to 0.189, measured as the sum of squared core-use shares. Coverage rose in 10 of 15 task/seed sessions; the effect was not universal. All accepted-state, survivor and pending-provenance checks passed, and both panels completed all 4,500 oracle evaluations.

Strict best-parent beats increased from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 600/4,350 (13.79%), and mean child-minus-best-parent score improved from -0.100493 to -0.093989. Incumbent improvements were nearly unchanged, at 216 versus 218. Mean final-best score across tasks and seeds fell from 0.544374 to 0.524118, a paired change of -0.020256. Seed changes were -0.052822, -0.023812 and +0.015865; all five task means declined. Thus the intended allocation mechanism is confirmed, while the intended score increase was not observed.

molecular.headline: Repeated heterocycle growth and tiny fragments coexist with reactive, highly fused leading molecules
molecular.overall_character: The current panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete three-seed Parent n-fc2c108a5253 trajectories. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9425 to 0.9931 and ring-closure presence from 0.977 to 0.9931; charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These are string-presence measurements, not aromatic atom fractions, ionization measurements or evidence of feasible stereochemistry. The output is ring-rich and often extensively aromatic: fused nitrogen carbonyl systems, aromatic amine/aminal frameworks and halogenated unsaturated heterocycles dominate the leaders. Chemical scale varies from tiny fragments to large assemblies of repeated heterocycles. This is particularly pronounced in deco_hop, whose mean SMILES length is 115.4 and maximum is 235; its seed-2 final molecules visibly repeat nitrogen-dione units. The Parent also produced reactive and extensively connected structures. Current leaders retain N-halogen bonds, peroxide or hypohalite motifs, tight ring fusion and unspecified configurations. Overall synthetic plausibility is questionable, with strongly implausible individual small-ring or growth outliers, and drug-like quality remains weak. Across-seed diversity is moderate; many late streams mainly elaborate a common core.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 molecules are moderately sized fused unsaturated nitrogen heterocycles bearing fluoroaryl carboxamides, alkyl/alkoxy substituents and hydroxymethyl or aminomethyl groups. Amide N-Br/N-Cl/N-F and fused-ring N-F are frequent in the leaders. Seed 0 reaches pyrazole thioamides with phenolic, cyclopentadienyl and cyclobutenyl groups; seed 1 reaches an aryl ketone with N-O/N-N functionality. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9782 and halogen presence is 0.7149. Relative to the Parent aromatic ketone, amide and thioheterocyclic families, the compact aromatic/carbonyl theme persists, with reactive nitrogen substitution and unusual ring geometry.
liabilities: N-Br, N-Cl and N-F bonds add reactivity to amide and ring nitrogens; N-O/N-N variants add compatibility concerns.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: Simulated annealing keeps one current configuration, perturbs it randomly, and always accepts an improvement while accepting a deterioration with a probability that falls as a temperature parameter cools. Early on the walk can move downhill and escape a local optimum; late on it behaves almost greedily. Applied to molecules, the configuration is a graph, the perturbation is an atom or bond edit, and the acceptance test uses the observed score returned by the oracle.
approach.novelty: This root runs many independent walks in parallel rather than one, with at most one outstanding proposal per walk, so the oracle batch is filled by different points in the space instead of by one trajectory. It ties the cooling schedule to accumulated feedback rather than wall time, seeds the initial temperature from the spread of the initial scores, and keeps a separate best-observed archive so that accepting a downhill move never loses the incumbent.

nodes.hypothesis: Maintain independent task-local molecular graph walks, generate de novo atom or bond edits from each current working state, accept nondecreasing observed scores and accept decreases with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), and cool T as accepted feedback accumulates while preserving a separate best-observed archive.

finding_summary.headline: The annealing machinery was exact in every respect and produced the round's lowest score, 0.233
finding_summary.insights: This node isolates the round's most important lesson. The search algorithm is provably correct and the search still failed, so what separates the field is not the optimizer but the proposal distribution it draws from. Aromatic content here is 50 to 67 percent against 87 to 100 percent for every root above 0.4, and the graph edits repeatedly produce aromatic phosphorus rings and hypervalent centres that are not real chemistry. Any future work on this lineage belongs in the edit operator set, not in the acceptance rule or the cooling schedule. One seed only, and its deco_hop result shows the walk does work where the initial molecules are already close.
finding_summary.results: This is the weakest of the thirteen roots at 0.233. It reached 0.558 on deco_hop and 0.382 on zaleplon_mpo but collapsed to 0.045 on drd2_docking and 0.014 on sitagliptin_mpo, where the median score across all 290 proposals was zero. Every mechanism check was exact: the recomputed cooling schedule agreed with all 145 proposal temperatures and all 1,450 stored proposal temperatures, the Metropolis decision reproduced 1,450 times out of 1,450 including the logged uniform variates, 557 downhill moves were accepted and 546 of them were genuinely reused as the source of a later proposal, and the best archive matched an independent cumulative maximum at all 1,600 checkpoints.

nodes.method_name: Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in simulated annealing: randomly perturb a current configuration, accept improvements, sometimes accept deterioration, and gradually cool the acceptance rule. [Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi](https://hedibert.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/1983KirkpatrickGelattVecchi.pdf) describe this mechanism for combinatorial optimization. Our molecular transfer maintains independent graph walks initialized from the current objective's supplied scored molecules. Each walk generates a new neighbor through atom or bond edits. After real feedback, accept a higher-scoring neighbor as the next working state; accept a lower-scoring neighbor with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), otherwise retain the source state. Subsequent edits follow the accepted working state, while a separate archive preserves the best observed molecule. Cool as feedback accumulates and distribute the evaluator-announced batch across walks with explicit proposal-to-source provenance. Regenerate invalid or already evaluated structures through further edits. Every submitted molecule is generated de novo; no corpus pool, learned prior or labeled source task is required. The hypothesis is that temporary score losses permit useful structural transitions whose later gains increase the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. This finite-budget optimizer does not claim equilibrium sampling or asymptotic convergence under molecular validity and novelty filtering.

approach.method_basis: NF-BO does Bayesian optimization in a latent space that is exactly invertible. A normalizing flow maps molecular sequences to continuous latents and back with no reconstruction error, so a point chosen in latent space decodes to a definite molecule rather than an approximation. A Gaussian process is fitted over the scored latents, Thompson sampling picks promising directions, and proposals are made by perturbing selected token blocks within a trust region before decoding back through the inverse flow.
approach.novelty: This root commits to choosing which token blocks to perturb by an estimated sequence-level pointwise mutual information rather than uniformly, so the perturbation concentrates on positions the flow considers informative. It also adapts the flow to high-scoring task-local sequences mid-session and re-encodes every observation after each adaptation, which keeps the latent geometry aligned with the current objective instead of frozen at corpus statistics.

nodes.hypothesis: Search around scored task-local molecules in an injective SELFIES SeqFlow latent space, adapt the flow to high-scoring observations, and use a latent GP with Thompson sampling to select fresh trust-region proposals whose perturbed token blocks are chosen from estimated sequence-level PMI before exact inverse-flow decoding.

finding_summary.headline: The only root to fail: the flow adaptation aborted mid-run and two objectives never finished
finding_summary.insights: The failure is not in the idea but in adapting the flow while a session is live. Re-encoding every observation after each adaptation is what makes the latent geometry stay useful, and it is also what puts a failure-prone training step inside the oracle loop, where an abort costs the remaining budget on that objective. The partial results that did land are suggestive, with 0.652 on drd2_docking from only 140 calls, so the approach is not obviously weak. The molecules also show a distinct problem: perturbing token blocks in a SELFIES-based latent produces boron, phosphorus and cumulated-double-bond structures at very high rates. A repair should move adaptation to a batch boundary with a guarded fallback before this lineage is judged on score.
finding_summary.results: The node is recorded buggy with no macro score, and its mechanism is refuted. Three objectives completed their full 290 proposals, but drd2_docking stopped at 140 accepted molecules and median_2 at 230, in both cases when a flow adaptation aborted. Of 129 adaptation attempts only 127 completed. The components that did run checked out: corpus pretraining moved held-out token loss from 15.283 to -3.877, exact left-inverse decoding held with a maximum error of 7.7e-07 at the selected checkpoint, all 840 pointwise mutual information estimates were nondegenerate, and every one of the 124 completed batches emitted exactly the announced ten valid novel molecules.

Of 129 adaptation attempts only 127 completed. The components that did run checked out: corpus pretraining moved held-out token loss from 15.283 to -3.877, exact left-inverse decoding held with a maximum error of 7.7e-07 at the selected checkpoint, all 840 pointwise mutual information estimates were nondegenerate, and every one of the 124 completed batches emitted exactly the announced ten valid novel molecules.

The failure is not in the idea but in adapting the flow while a session is live. Re-encoding every observation after each adaptation is what makes the latent geometry stay useful, and it is also what puts a failure-prone training step inside the oracle loop, where an abort costs the remaining budget on that objective. The partial results that did land are suggestive, with 0.652 on drd2_docking from only 140 calls, so the approach is not obviously weak. The molecules also show a distinct problem: perturbing token blocks in a SELFIES-based latent produces boron, phosphorus and cumulated-double-bond structures at very high rates. A repair should move adaptation to a batch boundary with a guarded fallback before this lineage is judged on score.

molecular.headline: Boron, phosphorus and cumulated double bonds: latent perturbation decodes to chemistry that does not exist
molecular.overall_character: This is the most chemically implausible output in the round. Cumulated double bonds, essentially absent from every other root, appear in 42 percent of proposals on one objective and 95 percent on another. Boron appears as a terminal double-bonded atom, phosphorus appears as cationic chains, and charged species reach 88 percent on one objective. Aromatic content runs 31 to 66 percent, and one proposal reaches 239 characters. The exact-inverse property the method depends on is working correctly; the problem is that the latent neighbourhood being searched decodes to sequences that are valid SELFIES and impossible molecules.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The token vocabulary treats successive double bonds as an ordinary continuation, so a small move in latent space can insert one anywhere. Penalising or removing those tokens from the perturbable set would cost nothing the search actually needs.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Two objectives terminated early, one at 140 of 300 accepted molecules and one at 230, when a flow adaptation aborted; 127 of 129 adaptation attempts completed and the two failures ended those sessions.

nodes.method_name: NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals
nodes.method_thesis: Use NF-BO's SeqFlow mapping, exact left-inverse decoding, and token-adaptive trust-region search. Train a compact SELFIES flow on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Within each fresh objective session, adapt it using highly scored task-local sequences, re-encode all observations after updates, and fit a latent-space GP. Generate new latent proposals around scored observations by perturbing token blocks according to their estimated pointwise mutual information with the decoded sequence. Thompson sampling selects proposals for inverse-flow decoding. These mechanisms follow [NF-BO, Sections 4 and 5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.14889v1). Regenerate as needed to fill the evaluator-announced batch with distinct canonical molecules; no corpus molecules are ranked or retrieved. The hypothesis is that score-directed local search around exactly reconstructable observations finds improving structures efficiently enough to raise the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Exact reconstruction alone is not the objective. Useful flow training and surrogate prediction under the permitted preparation and feedback remain empirical prerequisites.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds from score-ranked accepted molecules and recombines a fragment from each of two selected parents. For the first parent it usually keeps the larger side of a random bridge cut, then joins that piece to a donor fragment and may apply a local mutation. A Gaussian process trained on all accepted observations selects a batch from the resulting fresh pool. The random cut can separate ring systems or discard part of a strong first parent's core before the selector sees the product.
approach.novelty: Preserve the first parent's complete ring core during fragment crossover. Choose only pendant cuts whose retained side contains every source ring atom and the paths connecting them, then attach the donor fragment through the existing crossover. This changes the physical fragment retained, whereas earlier siblings changed parent allocation, survival or similarity-based pairing. It also differs from the separate whole-branch pruning experiment: donor replacement and learned pool selection already belong to this Parent, so the new question is whether preserving its core improves recombination.

nodes.hypothesis: When forming a crossover's first-parent fragment, sample only pendant single-bond cuts and retain the side containing every source ring atom and its connecting linkers.

finding_summary.headline: First-parent ring cores survived crossover, but final scores fell on all three seeds
finding_summary.insights: Physical inheritance of the first parent’s complete ring system worked and reached evaluation, but the full-core restriction did not improve the complete method. The crossover cohort produced more parent-beating descendants while the complete search ended at lower scores, so that local diagnostic is insufficient to establish improved optimization. It rules out failed cutting or lack of exposure to the selector as the explanation for the negative utility result. Keeping every ring can also keep a large or unproductive framework, while the donor adds more structure and useful peripheral functional relationships can still be removed. Optional mutation can then undo the protected structure. The supplied chemistry is consistent with this limit: conventional arylamide and sulfinamide leaders coexist with duplicated frameworks, dense bridges, reactive substituents and unspecified stereochemistry. The next useful distinction is which core and attachment relationships deserve preservation, and when replacement or simplification is beneficial; this result does not establish that all rings should always survive. The observed crossover subgroups differ in parents and later edits, and the changed random-call schedule alters subsequent search history. Neither the subgroup score difference nor molecular size identifies an individual protected cut’s causal value, and unused candidates have no oracle counterfactual labels.
finding_summary.results: Across 34,564 informative first-parent fragment calls, the inherited rule would retain the complete source ring/linker core with mean probability 55.968%; the applied pendant-cut rule made that probability one. All 33,626 sanitized protected crossovers preserved the original core atoms and bonds before canonicalization. Protected crossovers reached 28,875 novel pool descendants and 1,714 actual evaluated descendants; 1,587 of those emissions followed an immediate crossover that changed the first parent’s identity. Of 600 evaluated crossover descendants with a later mutation, 224 no longer contained the original typed ring/linker core. One additional unselected immediate-only pool product changed aromatic representation during the inherited canonicalization step. Mean emitted size rose from 33.39 to 40.90 heavy atoms, and 938 attempted products exceeded the unchanged 120-atom limit. The protected crossover cohort had 210/1,714 strict best-parent beats and mean child-minus-best-parent score -0.112347, compared with 172/1,679 and -0.156871 in the Parent’s crossover cohort. All fifteen Child task/seed runs completed. Mean final score fell from 0.544374 to 0.529067, a paired change of -0.015307; all three paired seeds declined (-0.014873, -0.022309, -0.008738). The mean DRD2 change was -0.090254, despite gains on three other tasks.
