molecular.headline: Compact arylamide and sulfinamide leaders coexist with repeated large frameworks, dense bridges, and reactive substituents
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied current and parent trajectory was read; all tasks and seeds are covered. Each current task contains 900 observations and 870 optimizer proposals. The current proposals are consistently substantial molecules: ring-closure and branch presence are 1.0 throughout, and aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9931 to 1.0. These text counters indicate whether a SMILES contains the relevant token, not aromatic atom fractions or feasible three-dimensional rings. Small fragments are not the visible limiting chemistry. Instead, the low-scoring excerpts repeatedly join complete arylamide or dione systems, and one population has mean SMILES length 130.8. More compact leaders include ordinary N-methyl arylamides and a recognizable tertiary-amine/cyclobutane/sulfinamide series. Other families use densely bridged nitrogen/carbonyl rings or N-fluorinated enol/thiol-containing structures. Drug-like functional groups are therefore present, but synthetic plausibility and stability are uneven. Explicit tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero throughout; formal charge tokens are rare, appearing at rate 0.0034 in the arylamide population and zero elsewhere. Neutral drawings can still contain basic amines. Several seed families provide moderate structural diversity, while much nominal variety comes from decoration, repeated units, or additional bridges. Relative to the parent, some leading chemistry becomes more conventional, but size, topology, and reactive bond liabilities remain.

per_task.generated_character: The best current family consists of compact fused/bridged heteroaromatics carrying an ordinary N-methyl phenylamide, methoxy or methylamino substitution, small alkyl groups, and a carbon-bound fluorine on a ring bridge. Nearby leaders replace phenyl with pyridyl or use sulfur/nitrogen ring connections. The leading molecule avoids the direct amide N-F bond seen in the parent's seed-2 leader, although other current seeds still produce N-fluorinated or N-chlorinated heteroaromatic amides. Ring presence is 1.0, aromatic presence 0.9989, and mean SMILES length 47.2. The compact leading architecture and standard amide are recognizable, but ring-bridge geometry and stereochemical identity still require assessment. The low excerpt instead contains duplicated, often heavily decorated arylamide systems connected through N/O/S or carbon linkages.
liabilities: Fluorinated bridge connectivity and dense fusion make accessible geometry and stereoisomer identity uncertain.
Bromomethyl and chloromethoxy variants add potential reactivity without establishing a general score advantage.
Other seed families retain direct N-F/N-Cl or additional N-N connections.
Joining complete arylamide systems sharply enlarges the molecules and appears repeatedly among the lowest supplied scores.
missing_features: Matched simpler bridge connections retaining the leading N-methyl arylamide and substituent relationships are insufficiently represented.
The substituted fluorinated bridge has no explicit stereochemical identity.
Stable compact alternatives are still incompletely represented across seeds, where direct N-halogen bonds and duplicated arylamides remain.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxy/methyl/fluorinated-bridge N-methyl phenylamide reaches 0.459794. Replacing phenyl with pyridyl lowers the score to 0.442564; replacing the aryl methyl with fluoromethyl gives 0.441920. In that fluoromethyl series, replacing methoxy with methylamino gives 0.458807, and fluoromethyl-to-bromomethyl exchange ties at 0.458807. Extending methylamino to ethylamino then lowers a closely related final structure to 0.299139. These local changes reveal specific substituent preferences, not a general benefit from adding fluorine, nitrogen, or size. Repeated arylamide assemblies score as low as 3.62e-22 despite retaining the apparent core functionality. The current seed-2 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.416350 while replacing an N-fluoroamide with N-methyl amide chemistry and a different bridged core. The parent's overall maximum was 0.446352 in another bridged N/O-carbonyl family. This is evidence of a different productive molecular arrangement, not proof that any individual bridge or fluorine position is required.

per_task.generated_character: This population is dominated by large, extensively linked aromatic structures. The leading family contains a benzopyranone-like carbonyl core, biaryl connections, a terminal ethynyl group, and repeated pyridyl/diazine-type rings linked through ethers. Carbon-bound fluorine, chlorine, methyl, and methoxy substituents decorate the extended framework. Its ring sizes and bond types are more recognizable than the unusual heteroatom-halogen chemistry in some parent leaders, but the overall assembly is very large and rich in aromatic acceptors with little donor functionality. Other seeds make still larger mixtures of repeated carbonyl heterocycles, imine/enol-ether connections, and unsaturated chains. Mean SMILES length is 130.8 and maximum 232, with aromatic and ring presence both 1.0. Synthetic assembly and physical properties are major unresolved issues even where individual substructures are ordinary.

Repeated azaaryl-ether units add considerable molecular size without a monotonic supplied-score gain.

Replacing that small group with an additional heteroaryloxy appendage gives 0.608641; much longer unsaturated appendages score 0.608404-0.610960. The smaller peripheral arrangement therefore does at least as well within the supplied family. Several different changes tie at 0.608641, including chlorine/methyl exchange on a remote ring, ether-to-thioether substitution, and carbonyl-to-thiocarbonyl substitution in related molecules. These ties provide no evidence that extra remote size or sulfur is needed. per_task.score_gradient_reading: The pyrrolyl/fluorinated-cyclobutenol-thiol leader scores 0.576998; its analogue replacing the saturated ring fluorine with thiol gives 0.555217. The fluoropyridyl/cyclopentenol family reaches 0.571115, versus 0.526837 without that aromatic fluorine and 0.531910 after replacing its saturated ring fluorine with thiol. Within a methyl-substituted cyclobutenol series, replacing the vinylic thiol with hydroxyl causes a particularly large change, from 0.532883 to 0.032767. This is a specific observed functional-group preference, not evidence that all sulfur or fluorine additions help. An open-chain enol/thiol analogue still reaches 0.530545, so a strained small ring is not established as essential. A late doubled molecule scores 1.66e-21, and a large early hybrid scores 2.88e-57. The current seed-2 maximum exceeds its parent's 0.407140 but remains below the parent's overall 0.584558 aryl dione/aminomethyl/fluoromethyl maximum, which had different and more conventional peripheral chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Low-scoring excerpts repeatedly duplicate arylamides or diones, with supplied scores as small as 3.62e-22 and 1.66e-21. One proposal population has mean SMILES length 130.8. Within its leading family, replacing a remote heteroaryloxy appendage with methoxy raises the supplied score from 0.608641 to 0.611490.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator too often joins complete molecular systems instead of preserving a compact productive core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide controlled removal of repeated units and simplification of remote appendages while preserving the informative core and key group relationships. Use accepted local comparisons to determine useful size instead of assuming that retaining two complete parent-like architectures is beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited molecules include fluorinated aromatic bridges, densely overlapping nitrogen/carbonyl cages, constrained oxygen/azaaromatic closures, and unsaturated small rings. Ring-closure presence is already 1.0 throughout, while simpler sulfinamide/cyclobutane chemistry and an open-chain enol/thiol analogue also achieve high local scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Geometric and synthetic feasibility remain unresolved as ring systems acquire additional bridges.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make bridge opening, alternative connection points, ring expansion, and saturation changes accessible while preserving useful functional-group spacing. Treat valence-valid closure as incomplete evidence of accessible geometry or a credible synthesis.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several families retain direct N-F or N-Cl bonds, N-N connections, enol/thiol groups, or labile unsaturated appendages. Ordinary N-methyl arylamide and sulfinamide leaders demonstrate access to more conventional bonding. A thiol-to-hydroxyl change can sharply reduce a supplied score, so simple blanket removal of every reactive group would also discard locally useful chemical distinctions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable functional-group alternatives are not explored systematically around reactive high-scoring structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer matched stable substitutions that preserve the surrounding scaffold, polarity pattern, and approximate size, then let current score feedback evaluate them. Distinguish the chemical role of a group from its incidental reactivity instead of copying it uncritically or removing an entire functional class.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest population has zero explicit tetrahedral stereolabel presence. The leading sulfinamide has stereogenic sulfur and substituted carbon connections, while bridged amides and fluorinated enol/thiol rings introduce additional stereochemical distinctions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical identity is left unspecified even in families with clear carbon and sulfur stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve stereochemical information through structural changes and make valid local stereoisomers available when new centres arise. Combine this with credible ring geometry and current scoring feedback so that one unspecified connectivity is not treated as a fully defined accessible molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Chlorine/fluorine exchange in a sulfinamide series ties at 0.981641, several remote ether/thioether or carbonyl/thiocarbonyl changes tie at 0.608641, and methylamino-to-ethylamino extension lowers another local score from 0.458807 to 0.299139. Elsewhere, multiple simultaneous ring and connecting-group changes obscure which chemical feature matters.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically local alternatives are too sparse to separate useful functionality from incidental growth and topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand matched changes to substituent position, carbonyl connection, heteroatom identity, amine spacing, and bridge geometry while keeping the remaining structure fixed. Include independently connected, synthetically credible alternatives rather than relying mainly on large rearrangements or repeated units.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored graph population with score-ranked parent sampling from three high-ranked quantiles
Connected-fragment graph crossover with inherited donor cut/side selection and single-bond attachment
First-parent pendant cut selection that retains every original ring atom and its connecting linkers, with deterministic component metadata caching
Local atom/bond mutation, bounded inner retries, occasional multistep graph walks and optional post-crossover mutation
Sanitization, canonical/isomeric identity checks, temporary-pool uniqueness and bounded fresh-pool generation; saturation-dependent retry branches retained
Bounded greedy score-ranked survivor retention and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring

approach.method_basis: The Parent is an ant colony optimizer that builds each molecular graph from an empty state. At each step it chooses a starting atom, attaches an atom to an existing site, closes a ring bond, or stops. Fixed aggregate frequencies from an unlabeled molecular corpus supply chemical preferences, including attachment, ring-closure and stopping weights. A separate table of task-local pheromones multiplies those preferences. The Parent identifies a reusable attachment component by the central atom's identity, charge, explicit hydrogens, degree, used bond order and ring membership, together with the proposed bond and new atom. Ring-closure components use both endpoint descriptions and their path length. Initial reinforcement comes from an exact reconstruction of the best supported starting observation. After feedback, all pheromones evaporate and only the highest-scoring accepted molecule in that batch deposits credit on its actual construction trace, once per distinct key. Positive lower and upper bounds preserve exploration. Later ants share the credited local components even when they occur inside different partial molecules.
approach.novelty: I add neighborhood-resolved pheromone credit: an attachment site also carries a sorted description of its directly bonded neighbors, and a ring closure carries this description at both endpoints. A move that was rewarded beside one arrangement of atoms and bonds will therefore share that reward only with the same bounded neighborhood. For example, the same central carbon description can acquire different credit when its neighboring atom is oxygen instead of carbon. This tests the Parent's observed loss of selectivity, where almost every accepted ant reused reinforcement but very few improved the incumbent. The lineage currently contains only the original ant colony root, so no sibling has tested a finer pheromone key. The corpus-derived heuristic still uses its original contexts; the new distinction acts specifically through which construction decisions share accepted winner credit.

nodes.hypothesis: Refine only the Parent's attachment and ring-closure pheromone keys with fixed, permutation-invariant one-bond neighborhood descriptors so accepted winner reinforcement transfers between matching local neighborhoods instead of all sites sharing the Parent's coarser endpoint description.

finding_summary.headline: Neighborhood credit localized and lifted the screening mean, but successful molecules remained rare
finding_summary.insights: This experiment separates local credit discrimination from productive molecular search. Different neighborhoods really were being collapsed by the old keys, and the new keys distinguish them without changing the legal chemistry or fixed heuristic weights. Matching neighborhoods also recur often enough to transfer credit across different partial molecules, so the refinement did not eliminate transfer through excessive sparsity. Yet most ants still inherit some online credit, and only 5.84% of the observed split-menu groups carried unequal refined pheromones. More precise keys therefore changed specific decisions without making successful whole molecules common. The chemistry explains why the modest mean gain should not be read as a broadly improved generator. The molecular assessment found a compact acyclic urea behind the strongest score increase, but long unsaturated chains and unconventional ring assemblies still dominate. Mean atom count fell slightly, while ring-closure actions fell sharply and terminations at the 64-atom ceiling became more frequent. In every task the late molecules were larger than the early molecules. Local credit refinement alone did not produce sustained access to compact, organized, functionalized chemistry. The result supports the implementation and shows a descriptive gain on this seed; it does not establish a reliable oracle-score benefit of selective credit. Larger changes in different objectives nearly cancel, some counted gains are near numerical ties, and the same-menu probability comparisons do not score unsubmitted alternatives. Whether broader molecular constraints or a better size and termination prior can make the now-demonstrated local discrimination useful remains open, as does its reliability across seeds.
finding_summary.results: The intended credit localization happened. Across the five task-specific tables, 3,027 attachment keys and 6,522 ring-closure keys separated previously shared neighborhoods. All 145 online winner updates withheld deposits from other neighborhoods when opportunities existed, totaling 75,964 alternative/update pairs. Every one of 10,719 mixed-neighborhood update probes increased the winner neighborhoods' conditional probability mass. Later construction contained 18,485 selected moves whose conditional probabilities changed and whose exact neighborhoods traced to earlier accepted online winners. The optimization gain was much smaller than the amount of activity. Among accepted ants that reused online credit, 7 of 1,396 beat their pre-batch incumbent, compared with 3 of 1,399 for the Parent; reuse still reached about 96% of accepted ants. All strict incumbent beaters increased from 8 to 12, but three of the new online-reusing docking beaters were steps of at most 0.00000044 along a low score plateau. The single screening seed's mean final Top-1 rose from 0.2523 to 0.2579. The sitagliptin multi-property score rose from 0.0980 to 0.2392, while dopamine-receptor docking fell from 0.1371 to 0.0289 and decoration hopping fell from 0.5534 to 0.5484. The zaleplon and median-molecule scores stayed at 0.3051 and 0.1678. No generated molecule beat the supplied starting incumbent on three of the five objectives. All 1,450 submitted molecules were accepted; one additional local construction repeated a molecule and was replaced before submission.

molecular.headline: Long polyene chains dominate; occasional polar cages and a compact urea score better, but conventional scaffold chemistry remains sparse.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied task trajectories and their Parent counterparts were read for seed 0. Each contains 290 optimizer proposals plus 10 initial observations. The generated population consists mainly of long, repeatedly unsaturated carbon chains, interrupted by amines, enamines, occasional imines, ethers and carbonyls. Rings are substantial in amount but often unconventional in arrangement: partially unsaturated carbocycles and dense fused or bridged assemblies occur alongside isolated aryl segments. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.3966 to 0.8966, while aromatic-text rates range from 0.1241 to 0.5690; these are fractions of strings carrying a feature, not aromatic atom fractions or assessments of ring quality. Mean SMILES lengths range from 60.1 to 76.5. Direct atom counts from the trajectories show that shorter strings than the Parent frequently reflect fewer closures and branches rather than a substantial size reduction. The emitted structures have no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry, and inspection also found no specified alkene geometry. All supplied generated SMILES parsed with RDKit, which establishes readable molecular graphs, not stability or synthetic accessibility. The quality labels describe substantial ring occurrence, sparse aromatic organization, questionable preparative chemistry, weak resemblance to ordinary medicinal chemistry and recurrent polyene motifs despite distinct molecular identities. Atom and functional-group counts below are direct structural readings of the supplied SMILES; all scores are the recorded evaluator values. Digest medians displayed as 0.0 are rounded and must not be interpreted as a majority of exactly zero observations.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 73.6; direct heavy-atom counts average 47.46 and reach 64. Ring-closure and aromatic-text rates are 0.8966 and 0.5690. Much of this ring content is a carbocycle or aryl segment embedded in a long polyene, rather than a compact aromatic scaffold. Evaluation 11, the best generated structure, is a compact, densely bridged nitrogen-containing polycycle bearing a nitrile, chlorine and cyclic ketones. Other higher examples include a partially unsaturated N/O polycycle and a nitrogen-free aryl-containing enone/aldehyde chain. Late structures are predominantly long hydrocarbon-rich polyenes, sometimes with ketones, aldehydes or a nitrile. Conventional fragments are recognizable, but their extended unsaturation and crowded ring combinations make synthesis and isolation questionable.
liabilities: Long polyenes and conjugated carbonyl chains create numerous unspecified alkene geometries and potential chemical-stability burdens.
Dense bridged rings with extensive unsaturation and unassigned stereochemistry need geometric and synthetic scrutiny; successful SMILES parsing does not resolve those concerns.
missing_features: Repeated production of compact, conventionally substituted aromatic NH heterocycles with an attached amide, as seen in the best supplied initial molecule; generated aromatic content is frequently carried on long unsaturated extensions.

Sustained access to the compact polar arrangements found among the higher generated examples. The final proposals mostly lose their concentrated nitrogen/carbonyl organization; the data do not identify one mandatory heteroatom motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 24-heavy-atom bridged nitrile at evaluation 11 scores 0.19324099086270913; the 21-heavy-atom N/O polycycle at evaluation 65 scores 0.17464941125558517. The nitrogen-free, shorter carbonyl-containing structure at evaluation 176 still scores 0.13915472870419515, so nitrogen alone cannot explain the gradient. Long final polyenes score zero or near zero; evaluation 300 has 64 heavy atoms and score 0.0. Exactly 130 of the 290 generated proposals score zero. The clearest association is with compactness and functional-group arrangement, not simply having a ring: many zero-scoring chains also contain rings. The supplied indole carboxamide at evaluation 9 remains best overall at 0.3051048083696145. Compared with Parent n-3ab6a944e3dd, ring-closure/aromatic-text rates rise from 0.6103/0.2172 to 0.8966/0.5690 and the generated maximum moves from 0.1775836262122333 to 0.19324099086270913, while that initial overall best remains unchanged.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 75.3 and direct heavy-atom count averages 50.05. Ring-closure rate is 0.8345, but aromatic-text rate is only 0.2655. The best generated molecule at evaluation 223 combines aryl-containing fused ring units, amide groups and nitrogen-containing linkers with a very long alkenyl appendage. Evaluation 26 is smaller and contains a fused N/O ring assembly, an amino substituent and an imine/N-N-containing chain. Other proposals distribute amines, enamines, imines, ethers and amides through long unsaturated backbones. The late molecules retain scattered rings and polar groups but look like extended polyene constructs; their synthesis is considerably less straightforward than the supplied conventionally substituted aromatic starting molecules.
liabilities: Extended polyenes with repeated amine/enamine and occasional imine or hydrazone-like functionality impose stability and stereochemical complexity.
Some highly fused N/O assemblies and densely unsaturated ring junctions have questionable preparative accessibility despite acceptable formal valence.
missing_features: Reliable production of clearly substituted aryl and carbonyl-bearing nitrogen heterocycle arrangements like those present in the stronger initial observations; such organization is diluted by unsaturated tails in much of the generated set.

Compact variants that preserve a polar ring system while varying its substituents. The two leading generated examples show that both compact and large structures can reach the upper observed band, but no clean analogue series identifies the decisive arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The generated maximum is 0.5468883205456095 at evaluation 223, versus the observed floor of 0.5 for hydrocarbon-rich chains and sparsely functionalized carbocycles. An aromatic/N/O-rich 29-heavy-atom molecule at evaluation 26 scores 0.5441609421000981, close to the 64-heavy-atom generated maximum. Thus ring-associated polar functionality and aromatic organization distinguish the higher band more consistently than size alone; neither a universal growth benefit nor a universal small-molecule preference follows. The final cited proposals range from 0.500866325911808 to 0.5162088883649651. The best supplied initial molecule scores 0.548381482770623 and remains best overall. The Parent generated maximum was 0.5533540672422114; its ring-closure/aromatic-text rates were 0.9448/0.4241. The current products have less ring and aromatic occurrence while retaining almost the same mean atom count.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 76.5 and direct heavy-atom count averages 51.10. Ring-closure and aromatic-text rates are 0.5345 and 0.1241. The upper observed score band is dominated by very long, mostly nonaromatic polyenes with chain amines or enamines and occasional partially unsaturated carbocycles or N-containing rings. Acyclic and cyclic structures occur at the identical maximum. Smaller low-scoring examples include propene, aldehyde/imine-containing structures, an acyl chloride and an unusual three-membered cyclic dicarbonyl graph. The extended chains and unusual reactive or constrained outliers support questionable synthetic plausibility; the score plateau is not evidence that these are convincing receptor ligands.
liabilities: Long chains with many unassigned double-bond geometries provide poorly specified three-dimensional structures and substantial hydrophobic bulk.
Low-scoring proposals include an acyl chloride, unusual sulfur bonding and a very small cyclic dicarbonyl; these raise direct reactivity or strain concerns.
missing_features: Compact scaffold coverage comparable to the Parent structures that received scores above the present plateau. The current high band mainly samples long unsaturated chains rather than demonstrating an improved compact binding arrangement.

Conventional aromatic and saturated nitrogen-ring arrangements are underrepresented, not absent. Their independent benefit and any receptor-specific missing pharmacophore cannot be established from these tied scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Exactly 111 generated molecules share the maximum 0.02885837683273086. Evaluation 96 has 60 heavy atoms and an N-containing ring, while evaluation 123 is an acyclic 53-heavy-atom amine/polyene at that same score. Propene scores 0.004764078329913475 and the three-membered cyclic dicarbonyl scores 0.003770354034741671. The observed progression toward larger chains ends in a repeated plateau, which cannot distinguish a favored ring system, amine placement or binding geometry. The best initial observation is 0.01904115112334333; another initial molecule already contains an N-methyl saturated amine ring yet scores only 0.0003786988088202195, so simply adding such an amine is unsupported guidance. The Parent had a compact fused, nitrogen-substituted polycyclic outlier at 0.13712669868003655, above this plateau. Its ring-closure/aromatic-text rates were 0.9724/0.2897, versus the current 0.5345/0.1241. Those differences describe a loss of ring-rich output, without establishing why the docking scores differ.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 73.1 and direct heavy-atom count averages 50.47. Ring-closure rate is 0.8552 and aromatic-text rate is 0.4310. The best generated molecule at evaluation 62 is a large, partly aromatic N-rich fused assembly with carbonyl functionality, a fluoro-substituted unsaturated linker, an aryl amine connection, a tertiary amide and an amino-ether tail. Other higher examples are densely bridged nitrogen cages with nitriles and ketones, or complex heteroaromatic/carbonyl-containing systems. The lower band contains acyclic amino-polyenes of both small and very large size. The ring-rich structures have more differentiated functionality, but their congested topology and long tails leave synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: Congested fused and bridged unsaturated rings, together with unspecified stereochemistry, complicate three-dimensional feasibility and route planning.
Long amino-polyene and aldehyde-containing tails add unsaturation and reactive functionality without consistently retaining the organized polar scaffold of the better examples.
missing_features: Routine access to conventionally linked aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl heterocyclic units like those in the stronger supplied starting molecules, without converting the whole structure into a bridged cage or a long polyene.

Controlled substitution around a retained compact ring system, which would help separate the observed contributions of ring identity, carbonyl placement and heteroatom arrangement; the present examples change several of these together.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The generated maximum is 0.12097167578182677 at evaluation 62; the bridged nitrile/ketone cage at evaluation 11 scores 0.1000061734111242. The short amino-polyene at evaluation 32 scores 0.0, and the 64-heavy-atom acyclic nitrogen-containing chain at evaluation 226 scores 0.006228601608634516. Thus the distinction is not simply small versus large: organized rings and associated functionality separate the higher band from chain-only structures. The best supplied initial aromatic, carbonyl-rich heterocycle remains best overall at 0.1678386594791329. The Parent generated maximum was 0.13095077916237702. Aromatic-text occurrence increases from 0.3069 to 0.4310, while ring-closure occurrence falls from 0.9517 to 0.8552 and the overall best remains the same initial molecule. More aromatic text alone therefore does not establish better scaffold organization.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 60.1 and direct heavy-atom count averages 39.66. Ring-closure and aromatic-text rates are 0.3966 and 0.1379, so most generated structures are acyclic and nonaromatic. The best generated molecule at evaluation 62 is a 19-heavy-atom substituted urea with unsaturated arms ending in an aldehyde and an imine. Other higher examples include a complex N/O fused carbonyl-containing structure, an acyclic imine/vinyl-ether-rich molecule and a short amino-polyenone. Later proposals are predominantly hydrocarbon polyenes with occasional amines or terminal aldehydes. The urea itself is a conventional linkage, but its unsaturated imine/aldehyde substituents and the broader polyene population raise stability and synthesis concerns.
liabilities: The best-scoring molecule still combines multiple unsaturated bonds with terminal imine and aldehyde functionality; its score does not establish stability or a practical route.
The dominant late polyenes have extensive unspecified alkene geometry, low polar-group density and frequent terminal carbonyl reactivity.
missing_features: Consistent regeneration of compact molecules with concentrated carbonyl and nitrogen functionality. The best urea is an isolated example, while late products mostly return to extended unsaturated chains.

Chemically stable variants of the compact polar arrangements already receiving higher scores, with less reliance on imines, enamines and aldehydes. Improved stability is a chemical need here, not an independently demonstrated scoring requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact acyclic urea scores 0.23921423452807236. The N/O fused structure at evaluation 20 scores 0.0814995806289838 and the acyclic heteroatom-rich structure at evaluation 43 scores 0.04838092252183626. The long final aldehyde/polyene at evaluation 299 has 64 heavy atoms and score 0.0; exactly 108 of the 290 optimizer proposals score zero. The higher examples favor compactness and concentrated polar functionality relative to long hydrocarbon-rich chains, but they do not establish that a ring, fluorination or a particular named heterocycle is required: the best example has none of those features. The initial maximum was 0.0020944534688323298. The Parent maximum was 0.09799523162987753 for a cyclic amino-polycarbonyl/lactone structure; the present best instead uses an acyclic urea arrangement. Ring-closure/aromatic-text occurrence falls from the Parent values 0.5483/0.1966 to 0.3966/0.1379. The higher best score therefore does not correspond to more aromatic or cyclic chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Mean heavy-atom counts from the generated trajectories range from 39.66 to 51.10, against 28.40 for the shared initial set. In each trajectory the final 50 proposals have a higher mean atom count than the first 50. The compact 19-heavy-atom urea at score 0.23921423452807236 and the 24-heavy-atom nitrile cage at 0.19324099086270913 contrast with long final polyenes scoring zero. A different upper-band example has 64 heavy atoms, so the evidence does not justify a universal preference for the smallest possible molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Compact functionalized molecules are reached occasionally but are not sustained as a substantial output regime.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide a corpus-grounded size and termination prior that keeps compact functionalized structures readily reachable while retaining multiple size classes. Measure size with atom counts and unsaturated-chain extent; shorter SMILES alone can reflect lost ring structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest ring-closure rates span 0.3966 to 0.8966, while aromatic-text rates span 0.1241 to 0.5690. The examples include isolated rings embedded in long chains, highly bridged unsaturated cages and an unusual three-membered cyclic dicarbonyl. Direct ring inspection finds only 6 to 10 proposals per 290 with a saturated nitrogen-containing ring, including rings inside cages; this is a deficit of conventional scaffold coverage, not an inability to close any ring.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring closure is common, but conventional aromatic and saturated heterocyclic organization is poorly represented.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make common aromatic rings, saturated heterocycles and supported fusion patterns reliably available with controlled substitution and attachment geometry. Corpus-derived ring-environment support or coherent ring motifs could supply this capability without identifying the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The generated examples contain amines, enamines, imines, ethers and carbonyls, so heteroatoms are not absent. Higher examples include a compact urea, nitrile/carbonyl ring assemblies and aromatic amide-containing initial molecules, but many later proposals consist mainly of carbon chains with scattered nitrogen or terminal aldehydes. Direct inspection finds only 4 to 10 generated molecules per trajectory carrying an aromatic nitrogen atom.
transferable_gaps.gap: Polar groups are often dispersed through unsaturated chains instead of organized into compact, chemically distinct environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve the bond-order and neighboring-group context that distinguishes an amine, enamine, imine, amide, urea or heteroaromatic nitrogen. Enable compact variants of observed polar arrangements and controlled changes around those arrangements so scalar feedback can compare related chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All supplied optimizer SMILES parse, yet the cited structures include dense unsaturated bridges, a very small cyclic dicarbonyl, acyl chloride functionality and repeated enal/enone or imine-containing chains. Some of these motifs appear in higher-scoring examples, so recorded reward alone does not establish an isolable or readily synthesizable product.
transferable_gaps.gap: Readable valence-consistent graphs still include chemically questionable ring and reactive-group combinations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use corpus support for complete ring/fusion environments and reactive-group co-occurrences when weighting or validating constructions. Track geometric and functional-group compatibility separately from formal valence, while retaining supported polyene and polycyclic chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre rate is 0.0 on every trajectory, and the full generated strings contain no explicit alkene-geometry markers. Long polyenes and multiply bridged ring systems therefore reach evaluation without their potential stereochemical alternatives being explicitly distinguished. These observations establish missing output specification, not that any particular objective necessarily rewards one isomer.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemistry even when its unsaturation and ring topology create isomeric choices.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Allow feasible tetrahedral and alkene stereochemistry to be assigned, retained through canonicalization and explored as part of molecular identity. Constrain assignments using the actual ring geometry and local bonding rather than an objective-specific stereochemical template.

nodes.method_name: MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in MAX-MIN Ant System: construct solutions probabilistically from components, evaporate their pheromone weights, reinforce the iteration-best solution, and bound every pheromone weight away from zero and excessive dominance. [Stutzle and Hoos, Sections 2 and 4](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~hoos/Publ/fgcs00.pdf) describe this mechanism. Our molecular adaptation constructs a fresh graph from an empty state through valence-aware atom, bond, ring-closure and termination actions. Choice probabilities combine a fixed chemical heuristic with task-local pheromones keyed by the local attachment context and action, allowing a useful action to transfer between different partial graphs. Preparation uses the permitted unlabeled corpus only for aggregate construction frequencies and stopping statistics. Initialize pheromones broadly, reconstruct valid construction traces for the supplied scored molecules, and use their best trace for the initial reinforcement. Generate the announced batch through complete new construction trajectories; only accepted whole-molecule feedback drives evaporation and reinforcement of that batch's best trace. Resample failed or duplicate constructions locally. There is no stored complete-molecule library, corpus ranking or fixed product enumeration. The hypothesis is that reusing successful local construction choices across new molecular combinations raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Whether coarse construction contexts carry useful reward information quickly enough is unproven; pheromone concentration or validity alone is not success.

approach.method_basis: The Parent first trains a recurrent SMILES prior on unlabeled molecules. Each objective starts a fresh adaptable copy and alternates one neural proposal batch with two graph-breeding batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh a scored breeding population, with a real fresh neural parent protected at the first graph handoff. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior trained only on that objective's accepted scores samples functions over fresh offspring pools to choose the remaining graph evaluations. Accepted graph trajectories then train the neural policy through trajectory balance, a learned normalizer and regularization toward the unchanged prior. The reusable prior still learns only the supplied molecular strings, even though the online neural sampler must compose new strings.
approach.novelty: Expose the unlabeled prior to two identity-equivalent traversals of a molecule: retain its original string and sometimes train on one checked atom-order alternative. This broadens the local sequence contexts in which the same molecular structure is learned without changing the molecule allocation or adding scored data. Neither sibling has changed prior serialization support; their difference was graph-offspring selection. The online learning, graph edits and posterior selector remain exactly as in the current Parent, so this experiment asks whether a less serialization-specific starting distribution supplies better material to the existing reciprocal search.

nodes.hypothesis: Train the reusable unlabeled recurrent prior on a half-original, half identity-checked alternative-SMILES serialization mixture for the same selected training rows, preserving the original holdout checkpoint rule and all online components.

finding_summary.headline: Alternative-traversal support and scores improve, while raw neural validity worsens
finding_summary.insights: This establishes broader support for equivalent molecular traversals, with a measurable cost in fitting the original strings. That support does not automatically make adapted neural generation more chemically valid or improve every task. The higher overall score coexists with more invalid draws and with chemically questionable high-scoring structures: the Molecular assessment identifies an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur family in the largest-gain task, selenium-containing aromatic amines elsewhere, poor size control and absent stereochemical specification. The gain therefore cannot be interpreted as a general chemical-quality improvement, nor as evidence that selenium or the atypical sulfur connectivity is necessary. The experiment isolates the changed preparation mechanism in source, but its downstream effects pass through the inherited reciprocal graph search and posterior selection; the logged first neural batches already follow initial-observation adaptation and are not a pure-prior test. The useful new distinction is between learning more traversal syntax, sampling valid molecules, and obtaining favorable scalar scores. All three must remain visible.
finding_summary.results: The intended preparation mechanism activated in every seed. About 3.786 million changed-alternative exposures entered gradient minibatches per completed preparation, and more than 99.5% of the distinct consumed alternative rows added adjacent-token contexts absent from their own original strings. The original molecular row schedule and holdout split were preserved, with identity and encoding checks backed by independently reconstructed logged pairs and the full holdout. Learned support broadened: on the same held-out alternative traversals, token NLL falls from the Parent’s 1.76–1.78 to about 0.765, and the alternative-versus-original gap shrinks from about 1.19–1.22 to 0.157–0.159. Original-string fit worsens, from about 0.563–0.566 to 0.607, despite both nodes completing the same 29,742 training steps. Preparation takes about 1,056–1,071 seconds versus 218–281 seconds for the Parent. All online code and prior-freezing checks remain intact. All required evaluations finish, and all three seed macro scores improve: the mean rises from 0.520669 to 0.546307, a paired gain of 0.025638, with individual gains of 0.010517, 0.025244 and 0.041153. The benefit is uneven across tasks: the sitagliptin mean rises by 0.163551, while three other task means decline. Raw neural validity also falls from 70.34% to 61.88%; invalid and unterminated strings rise even though every announced batch is filled.

Each prior.pt was loaded with weights_only=True on CPU and every tensor hash recomputed. The independent likelihood audit used only forward passes of these existing selected checkpoints on exactly the original/alternative heldout pairs; it made no oracle calls, optimizer updates, new sampling runs or checkpoint choices. Token denominators and total sequence NLL are preserved separately for original and alternative strings. CPU FP32 and original CUDA mixed-precision values are labeled separately. Full preparation evidence, all 61 validation points for each of the six preparations, selected-checkpoint counters, diagnostics, pair/row-schedule hashes and read-only paired likelihoods are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0008-03-improve-L07.analysis-prior-audit.json. Preparation source and log points establish that only unweighted original holdout loss selected the state, and that all three runs reached 29,742 steps within the unchanged deadline. The seed-0 preparation reused from smoke is identified by its formal prepared-artifact hash; its smoke score is never used as research evidence. Every Parent and Child seed-N/logs/TASK.log was scanned for initialization, flow_replay_complete, genetic_flow_feedback, genetic_flow_observation, policy_trajectory_generated and genetic_flow_batch evidence. These join to all 9,000 accepted trajectory records across the two nodes with exact canonical identities and observed scores. All 30 objective initializations and 900 replay-complete receipts preserve the respective prior. Per-seed and first-versus-later neural counters, event line references, task scores and trusted paired aggregation are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0008-03-improve-L07.analysis-log-audit.json. molecular.headline: Rich aromatic and nitrogen-ring chemistry, with new selenium and unusual sulfur families, uneven size control and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The supplied trajectories contain 4,500 evaluated molecules, including 4,350 optimizer proposals, across all three supplied replicas and all five tasks; the same 4,500 parent rows were read for comparison. The repertoire includes fused nitrogen heterocycles, phenols, carbonyl-containing rings, diarylamines, saturated amine rings, aryl alkynes and selenium heteroaromatics. All 4,350 emitted child SMILES parsed with the supplied RDKit environment, but graph validity is distinct from synthetic plausibility. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9839 to 0.9908 and aromatic-marker rates from 0.9609 to 0.9793; these are string-level presence counters, not aromatic atom fractions. Read-only RDKit measurements on optimizer rows give median heavy-atom counts of 26, 43, 29, 34 and 26 in the brief task order. Useful-looking medium-sized medicinal chemistry coexists with very small fragments, oversized linked assemblies, unusual heteroatom connectivity and strained-looking ring edits. Several seed-specific leading families differ substantially from the Parent, while many leading neighbors within each family remain close relatives. The structural-diversity judgment is therefore moderate despite numerous distinct molecular graphs. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit detects unassigned tetrahedral centres in 290, 215, 433, 511 and 298 optimizer rows respectively, and assigned tetrahedral centres in none. The observations describe output chemistry; they do not establish the cause of its change, a synthetic route, or measured stability.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest digest examples are medium-sized fused aryl/nitrogen systems: a phenyl-substituted indazole-like N-carbamoyl core fused to a gem-dimethyl oxygen ring, followed by phenolic diaryl pyrazoline-like compounds. The leading structure has 24 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, three aromatic. Seed 0 also explores aryl ureas and sulfur-linked carbamoyl groups attached to a four-membered unsaturated nitrogen ring bearing an aldehyde. Across optimizer rows the median is 26 heavy atoms and three rings, with 624 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds; the Parent had medians of 25 heavy atoms and three rings and 529 such scaffolds. These counts include small ring edits and do not demonstrate an equivalent number of synthetically useful core families. The Parent high tail instead included biaryl pyrazole/acetanilide and quinoline/urea arrangements. Thus the new output changes the core families while retaining extensive aromatic, donor/acceptor and carbonyl chemistry.
liabilities: Aldehyde-bearing four-membered unsaturated nitrogen rings and sulfur-linked variants need chemical scrutiny; their accepted graphs and scores do not establish accessible or stable compounds.

Both tiny heteroatom fragments and much larger flexible assemblies consume part of the observed proposal set. Sixty-five of the 870 optimizer rows contain a bond from N, O or S directly to a halogen, compared with 34 Parent rows under the same bond-based count.
Repeated phenol, heteroatom and ring-closure edits can change reactivity or geometry even when much of the favorable aromatic framework remains.
missing_features: Reliable exploration of compact alternative cores that preserves the useful aryl, nitrogen and carbonyl arrangement remains incomplete; many surrounding edits lose the favorable combination rather than cleanly substitute another core.
The pyrazoline-like saturated centres and other substituted ring junctions lack explicit stereochemical specification. No preferred configuration can be inferred from these observations.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused N-carbamoyl leader scores 0.4811252243246881, its extra-phenol analogue 0.4588069837338257, and its ring-oxygen-deleted relative 0.458386638264238. Replacing the N-carbamoyl group by methyl in a late relative gives 0.387244764147529; extending one geminal methyl substituent to ethyl gives 0.34636729936804345. These local observations favor a particular compact ring/substituent arrangement, not indiscriminate heteroatom addition. A phenolic pyrazoline-like molecule scores 0.4201182934804424, while the aldehyde/aryl-urea family reaches 0.40910891241125485. In contrast, Cl, OO and OF each score 0.0, and a very large flexible polyamine/polyaryl molecule scores 1.8344487388079707e-40. The pooled median is 0.129972. Whole-molecule size and functional-group placement both matter in the observed gradient; these data do not identify a uniquely missing target scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The digest high tail is concentrated in compact, mostly planar triazole-substituted aminopyridine pairs decorated with fluorine and chlorine. The leader has 23 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings, with a diarylamine bridge and several ring nitrogens. Its close relatives change small alkyl groups, halogen positions or fusion to the triazole. These look more conventional as synthetic targets than many of the large late seed-2 carbonyl/thione/sulfur-rich fused assemblies, although no routes are supplied. The full proposal distribution is much larger than its leading family: the child median is 43 heavy atoms and five rings, versus 36 and four in the Parent; 347 of 870 child proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, versus 128 in the Parent. The digest mean SMILES length is 85.5, maximum 197, and charged-marker rate 0.1724. Parent leading families included heteroaryl amino and acylhydrazone/imine connections; the new compact triazole/aminopyridine family changes their linkage chemistry without eliminating the large-assembly tail.
liabilities: The larger population contains extensive polyaromatic fusion, sulfur/carbonyl linkages, conjugated exocyclic unsaturation and multiple charges or ionizable groups. Their combined synthesis and physical-property balance are unestablished.
Halogen-rich heteroaromatic leaders are plausible motifs, but their observed scores do not demonstrate favorable solubility, stability or the utility of additional halogenation.
New short ring closures and fused arrangements can change geometry sharply. Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 215 of the 870 child proposals, with no assigned centres.
missing_features: Compact alternatives that change the core or bridge while retaining the useful heteroaromatic arrangement are not well represented among the leading examples; most quoted leaders decorate the same aminopyridine/triazole family.

Controlled variation between compact and elaborated structures is uneven. The many large assemblies do not establish a missing objective-specific group, and their size is not required by the compact leading examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methyl-, ethyl- and differently halogenated triazole/aminopyridine examples all score 0.6220806794055203. A less halogenated close relative scores 0.6203208556149733, and an additional heteroaromatic ring gives 0.6203675187352428. The narrow spread suggests that local decoration changes do little once that ring/linker arrangement is present. A much larger late carbonyl-rich fused heterocycle still scores 0.6048855296308467, so large size is not uniformly rejected. Nevertheless, the bulky sulfone/amide/cyclic-amine low example scores 0.2889922015596881, and a very heavily brominated polyaromatic assembly scores 0.29217856536262243. The pooled median is 0.574287. These comparisons support useful heteroaromatic connectivity rather than a simple rule to maximize rings, halogens or size.

per_task.generated_character: The pooled high tail is an arylpiperazine/alkylamine family attached to chlorinated benzoselenophene-like rings. Many examples combine an aryl- or pyridyl-substituted piperazine with an additional tertiary amine and a flexible carbon linker. The leading example has 31 heavy atoms and four rings; a simpler high-scoring relative has 25 heavy atoms, a propyl linker and one arylpiperazine. Read-only atom counts find selenium in 174 of 870 child proposals, versus none of the 870 Parent proposals for this task. Other child seeds reach oxygen/carbonyl aromatic systems linked to saturated amines and sulfur/nitrogen heteroaromatics with substituted piperidines. The broader class of accessible saturated amines plus aromatic surfaces was already present in the Parent, whose leaders included diaryl aminoalkyl piperidines and linked saturated amine rings. The child median is 29 heavy atoms and four rings; the aromatic-marker rate is 0.9609. Its low charged-marker rate, 0.0149, does not mean basic centres are absent, because the molecules are written as neutral amines.
liabilities: The selenium heterocycle is unusual within the supplied Parent repertoire and adds an element-specific chemical liability that has not been assessed for stability or synthesis. It should not be called infeasible solely because it contains selenium.
Multiple basic centres, long flexible linkers and repeated aromatic units may complicate physical-property balance. The score alone does not establish those properties.
Some relatives add strained-looking short closures across aromatic frameworks, N–N connections or N–Cl bonds. The leading branched structures also leave tetrahedral configuration unspecified.
missing_features: No further required functional group can be inferred from a high tail already close to the score limit. Saturated basic centres, heteroaromatics and aromatic surfaces are represented.

Defined configurations and systematic linker geometry are not demonstrated for the branched amine family. The present data show missing stereochemical representation, without identifying a rewarded configuration.

Chemically matched conventional alternatives to the selenium-containing family are not established as a controlled comparison. Their absence prevents attributing the favorable whole-molecule score to the unusual element.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The extended pyridylpiperazine/tertiary-amine/selenium structure scores 0.9999994775753148, while the simpler propyl-linked arylpiperazine scores 0.9999993561334308. Removing the extra tertiary-amine branch still permits 0.9999980741980992 in a close family. Conversely, duplication into a much larger polyamine/selenium assembly gives only 0.03431111746034991, and the N-chlorinated nitrogen-ring example scores 0.00036530897832142426. The nitrofuran ester low example scores 6.212341904497256e-05 and an amide-rich heterocycle scores 7.81343751377966e-05. The visible association is with the whole aryl/saturated-amine/linker arrangement, rather than nitrogen count or maximal elaboration. Parent molecules without selenium already reach 0.9999986918258995, so the trajectory does not establish a selenium requirement or a chemically meaningful benefit from tiny differences near the upper score limit.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family combines an ethoxy-substituted fused conjugated carbonyl core with N-methylpiperazine, fluorine and an aryl or five-membered N–N/carbonyl appendage. Ring perception identifies a seven-membered conjugated carbonyl ring fused to a six-membered ring in the two strongest cited examples. The leader has 37 heavy atoms and five rings, including an N-phenyl-substituted saturated N–N/carbonyl ring; a near-equal example has 34 heavy atoms, a bromophenyl group and a propionyl substituent instead. Other seeds explore densely fused carbonyl heterocycles and sulfonylated saturated nitrogen rings. These retain the Parent broad pattern of aromatic, carbonyl and saturated nitrogen-ring chemistry, but with different fused cores. The child median is 34 heavy atoms and five rings, compared with 36 and five for the Parent. The digest mean SMILES length is 63.8 and maximum 152. Common medicinal-chemistry substituents are present, while the complete leading frameworks remain elaborate and configurationally unresolved.
liabilities: Large fused conjugated carbonyl systems, multiple appended rings and rearranged short closures can make synthesis and geometry difficult to interpret; no route or conformational assessment is present.

The late high-scoring oxygen-fluorine analogue scores 0.21440741901011376 despite its unusual O–F bond. A favorable observation is therefore compatible with chemically concerning functional-group connectivity.
Duplication of substantial core fragments increases bulk without preserving the leading score in the cited late example. Several important saturated positions remain stereochemically unspecified.
missing_features: Less encumbered alternative cores that retain the favorable carbonyl/aryl/amine relationships have not been explored consistently in the leading neighborhood; near-equal simpler appendage choices show that additional ring complexity is not automatically helpful.

Configurationally specified variants of the substituted saturated N–N/carbonyl rings are missing. RDKit identifies two unassigned tetrahedral centres in the leading molecule and at least one unassigned centre in 511 of 870 child proposals.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-phenyl N–N/carbonyl appendage scores 0.22243686751733371 and the bromophenyl/propionyl alternative scores 0.22234616366476415. A benzyl-substituted N–N/carbonyl analogue scores 0.22082458431832067; the simpler bromophenyl/methyl relative scores 0.22050990442479085. These small differences do not establish that the extra saturated nitrogen ring or maximum carbonyl count is essential. The supplied Parent leading values include 0.2124137877466535 for a different fused carbonyl/amine architecture. A heavily duplicated late aromatic/carbonyl assembly scores 0.15308748742436262, while a one-carbon-linked close analogue retains 0.21606790785072147. Methane, OF and difluoromethanol each score 0.0, and a small acyclic fluorinated carbonate-containing molecule scores 0.018771276394456953. The observed preference is for connected aromatic, carbonyl and nitrogen environments; the data do not reveal a specific absent target fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest seed-1 family consists of fluorinated pyridyl–aryl alkynes bearing an oxygen-linked fluoromethyl group and an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur centre. In the leading SMILES that sulfur has an oxo bond, two nitrogen bonds, one carbon substituent and an explicit hydrogen; this is not the ordinary tetrahedral sulfonamide connectivity one might assume from a casual reading. The leader has 25 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings. The [SH] text occurs in 160 of 870 child optimizer proposals, versus one Parent proposal for this task. Seed 2 instead reaches an N-methylated dicarbonyl nitrogen heterocycle linked through a fluorinated enone to a large conjugated nitrogen-containing ring; other output includes fused lactam/thiol chemistry. The Parent leading families included N-acyl triazolyl azetidines and hydrazino or nitroso-bearing nitrogen compounds. The output therefore changes its nitrogen/fluorine chemistry substantially, but the newer high sulfur family still lacks demonstrated ordinary chemical plausibility. Across optimizer rows the median is 26 heavy atoms and three rings, versus 24 and three in the Parent.
liabilities: Hydrogen-bearing, highly coordinated sulfur environments and variants with additional N–S/O–N connections need explicit chemical review before being treated as practical molecules. RDKit parsing does not establish their stability or preparation.

Seventy-two of the 870 emitted structures have a direct N/O/S–halogen bond under a bond-based count, compared with 26 Parent structures. The cited O–F-containing high example shows that such connectivity is not confined to the low tail.

The alternative high family includes conjugated enones and large conjugated nitrogen rings; variants acquire N–F or additional ring fusion. These are possible reactivity and geometry concerns, with no supplied experimental assessment.
missing_features: Stable, ordinary-valence alternatives that preserve the useful local aryl/alkyne/nitrogen/fluorine arrangement are not established for the leading sulfur family. It would be incorrect to diagnose a general absence of nitrogen, fluorine or carbonyl chemistry.
Core changes that preserve that compact functional-group arrangement remain inconsistent; some late multiplication or relocation of otherwise familiar motifs leads to extremely low scores.

Stereochemically specified saturated and bridged alternatives are absent elsewhere in the output. These observations do not identify an objective-preferred configuration or prove that one particular missing heterocycle is required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated aryl-alkyne structure with the unusual sulfur centre scores 0.5600222476080907. Its otherwise corresponding phenyl analogue without that aryl fluorine scores 0.5113964873062803, and shortening the sulfur-bound fluoroethyl group to fluoromethyl gives 0.4963704929462404 in the aryl-fluorinated family. A longer diyne relative scores 0.5252583563261087. Replacing the oxygen-linked fluoromethyl group by a direct O–F substituent still gives 0.4963704929462404, illustrating that this gradient does not certify normal reactivity. The separate dicarbonyl/enone family reaches 0.4853564671811107. In contrast, a large fluorinated polyaryl/alkyne assembly scores 0.0, a long polar guanidine/amide assembly scores 3.920867438776822e-82, and duplication of the late enone/heterocycle framework gives 2.250908533370224e-18. The pooled median is only 0.001751. Size, polar-group placement and exact connectivity are sharply consequential in these observations, but the high scores of atypical sulfur graphs do not reveal a missing conventional pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited leading aryl-alkyne molecule scores 0.5600222476080907 while carrying a hydrogen-bearing sulfur atom with oxo, carbon and two nitrogen bonds. Related O–F chemistry scores 0.4963704929462404, and a separate carbonyl/piperazine O–F analogue scores 0.21440741901011376. The full output also contains direct N/O/S–halogen bonds. Accepted molecular graphs and favorable scores therefore coexist with chemically questionable connectivity.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve ordinary functional-group valence and attachment chemistry when elaborating useful structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent functional-group replacements that retain useful surrounding aromatic and polar relationships while distinguishing ordinary amines, amides, oxo-sulfur groups and carbon-bound halogens from unusual heteroatom valence or heteroatom halogenation. Let accepted session feedback compare chemically coherent alternatives; do not treat valence parsing or score alone as evidence of stable chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal set contains 347 of 870 molecules above 50 heavy atoms, compared with 128 for its Parent, while its leading cited structure has only 23 heavy atoms. Other low tails include methane, OO and OF at 0.0, and large duplicated amine or conjugated-carbonyl structures score 0.03431111746034991 and 2.250908533370224e-18. Some larger molecules still occupy high tails, so a universal small-molecule rule is not supported.
transferable_gaps.gap: Growth and contraction do not reliably preserve an appropriate molecular scale or a coherent useful core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide core-preserving growth, contraction and linker alternatives that can vary size without removing the useful donor, acceptor, amine and aromatic relationships or repeatedly joining whole successful molecules. Determine useful scale from the current accepted observations rather than imposing a task identity or treating size alone as the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest gives stereocentre_rate 0.0. Read-only RDKit inspection finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 290, 215, 433, 511 and 298 optimizer rows in the supplied task order and no assigned centres. Cited pyrazoline-like rings, branched aminoalkyl groups and substituted N–N/carbonyl rings provide concrete examples; short closures and ring rearrangements also occur among high-scoring variants.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemistry and controlled ring geometry remain missing even when the output contains configurationally rich structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make specified configurational alternatives and chemically credible ring closure, expansion and contraction available while preserving useful surrounding connectivity. Separate changes in stereochemistry, saturation and ring geometry so their consequences can be learned from accepted feedback. The present absence of specification does not establish a benefit for any chosen configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The quoted upper tails repeatedly decorate a fused N-carbamoyl core, an aminopyridine/triazole family, an arylpiperazine/selenium family, a fused carbonyl/piperazine family and an unusual sulfur-bearing aryl-alkyne family. Different seeds produce different families, and nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts are 624, 719, 632, 702 and 515 across the child sets. Many of those distinct graphs are local ring changes or elaborate assemblies; those counts alone do not establish useful core diversity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of useful, chemically distinct cores is uneven within the leading neighborhoods despite a varied overall graph repertoire.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve access to more than one accepted core family and enable core replacements that retain spatial and electronic relationships among the locally useful groups. Compare core chemistry and functional-group arrangement rather than relying only on unique molecular identity, changed SMILES traversal or peripheral decoration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Selenium appears in 174 of 870 proposals in one child set and in none of its corresponding Parent set. The high child family has scores near the upper limit, but Parent amine/aromatic molecules without selenium already reach 0.9999986918258995. A shorter child linker architecture reaches 0.9999993561334308 near a more elaborate tertiary-amine example at 0.9999994775753148. These observations support an aryl/amine arrangement but do not identify selenium or extra complexity as necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: New unusual-element families lack matched conventional chemical alternatives that would distinguish useful geometry from element-specific exploitation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Keep access to chemically matched element, ring and linker alternatives around accepted arrangements, including conventional heteroatom or carbon analogues when representable. Use actual session feedback to determine what the structure needs, without inferring element necessity from a single enriched high-scoring family or tiny near-limit score differences.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent starts at the best supplied scored molecule and repeatedly samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits from that one current graph. It sanitizes and normalizes each edited molecular identity, rejects previously proposed molecules, and submits the first full batch admitted by short-term inverse-motif memory. Memory vetoes a neighbor only when both inverse signs match the same earlier selected transition. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even when its score worsens, while a separate archive keeps the best observation. Bounded inverse restrictions, four-step aging, overlap refresh and obstruction release remain part of that Parent, as does the repaired proposal-to-feedback identity join.
approach.novelty: Add one local sulfur-valence introduction gate. A generated neighbor may retain or remove a sulfur environment already present in its source, but it may not introduce or multiply a sulfur environment outside an explicit small envelope of ordinary valence patterns. This redirects eligible graph edits toward alternative neighbors before they reach the unchanged memory gate. It preserves thiol and sulfide valence, aromatic sulfur, terminal carbon-sulfur double bonds, and the usual neutral sulfur-oxide patterns. Earlier siblings changed memory matching and repaired identity bookkeeping; they did not constrain sulfur chemistry. The related corpus-support experiment in another walk admitted chemistry merely because it occurred locally in a corpus. This proposal instead tests a fixed, narrow sulfur rule without learning a vocabulary or changing preparation.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject an otherwise valid canonically novel graph neighbor before tabu testing exactly when it introduces or increases the multiplicity of a sulfur local-environment signature outside a fixed neutral sulfur-valence envelope relative to the same scored source graph, then continue the inherited graph-edit sampling loop from that unchanged source.

finding_summary.headline: The sulfur gate eliminated targeted violations, with higher sampling cost and uneven score gains.
finding_summary.insights:
The targeted sulfur channel was largely independent of the existing tabu veto: 760 of 766 rejected draws would otherwise have reached allocation. Ordinary sulfur alternatives remain abundant enough to fill every batch and retain the panel's average score, despite the extra sampling work. All selected initial sources were already clean under the envelope, so the experiment demonstrates prevention of new violations; it does not exercise recovery from an inherited violating source. Most rejected opportunities come from atom replacement, which accounts for 734 of the 766 rejections.

The small favorable mean score is accompanied by a substantial loss in one seed and lower mean scores on two tasks. It supports the stated mean non-inferiority direction on this panel without establishing a consistent improvement. The molecular assessment also shows where the chemical benefit stops: more ordinary sulfur and recognizable aromatic polyamines coexist with nitrogen/oxygen-halogen bonds, constrained unsaturation, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry. Sulfur valence is one separable source of implausible chemistry; whole-molecule stability, accessible ring geometry and stereochemistry remain unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
The gate rejected 766 of 5,307 otherwise valid novel neighbors across all fifteen task sessions. Of those rejections, 760 would have passed the unchanged tabu rule, and every rejection was followed by a different permitted neighbor from the same scored source. None of the 4,350 emitted molecules contains sulfur outside the declared envelope, compared with 2,398 of 4,350 Parent emissions. Sulfur remains in 2,821 emitted molecules, including thiols, sulfides, aromatic sulfur, thiones, sulfoxides and sulfones.

All three seeds complete all five 300-evaluation tasks and all 435 ten-member batches. The sampling cost rises from 5,285 to 6,234 raw attempts, or 12.15 to 14.33 attempts per batch. Emission yield falls from 82.31% to 69.78% of raw attempts. Recorded edits, normalized identities, accepted-score joins and downstream memory/winner rules pass the independent audit.

Mean macro final Top-1 rises from 0.520918 to 0.526783, a paired mean change of +0.005865. The seed changes are +0.015565, -0.061423 and +0.063454, and the macro population standard deviation rises from 0.004890 to 0.046774. Zaleplon and median_2 improve in every matched seed; decoration hopping declines in every seed, while DRD2 and sitagliptin have mixed outcomes. The gate therefore achieves its intended chemical and allocation changes with an uneven score response.
