molecular.headline: More conventional sulfur and amine skeletons coexist with N-halogen bonds, hypobromites and severely strained cages
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, compared with the supplied three-seed Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 trajectories. Ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout; aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9379 to 1.0, and charge and stereocentre token presence remain 0.0. These are string-presence counters, not atom fractions or measurements of ionization and stereochemical feasibility. The prominent high-scoring sulfur motifs now include thiols, sulfides, thiones, sulfoxides and aromatic sulfur, rather than the Parent's frequently multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur cages. Some aromatic amine leaders are entirely sulfur-free and have substantially more recognizable medicinal skeletons. This is a real difference in the observed chemistry, but the output still includes reactive N-Br/N-Cl/N-F and O-Br bonds, N-N/N-O networks, highly constrained small rings and dense carbon/nitrogen cages. Aromatic ring/carbonyl families, large decorated diones and polycyclic amines give moderate diversity across tasks and seeds; local families dominate each late trajectory. Overall synthetic plausibility remains poor because several of the leading complete structures are severely strained or reactive, despite more plausible subseries. No activation or causal attribution is inferred from these molecular observations.

per_task.generated_character: Moderately sized aromatic/fused-ring carbonyl compounds remain prominent. Seed 2 reaches a methoxy- and methyl-substituted indene linked to pyridine through a carbonyl-S-N unit carrying N-Br. Seed 1 contains more conventional indene aryl ketones with ethylthio, methylamino and methoxy substituents; other high examples carry hydrazine, bromomethoxy or sulfenamide groups. Seed 0 reaches an N-bromothioamide on an oxygen-containing unsaturated fused framework. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9977 and halogen presence is 0.8402. These replace the Parent's unusual-sulfur ketones or N-chloroamides with different sulfur chemistry, but several leaders still combine reactive functionalities. The aryl ketone subseries is comparatively plausible.
liabilities: Acyl-S-N-Br, N-bromothioamide and bromomethoxy groups introduce substantial reactivity despite ordinary sulfur valence.
N-N/N-O networks and constrained unsaturated ring closures remain chemically or geometrically questionable.
missing_features: Broader stable realizations of the compact aryl-carbonyl arrangement are underrepresented relative to N-halogen, sulfenamide and hydrazine substitutions.

Accessible alternatives to the late bridged N-O frameworks and explicit configurations for products that acquire stereocentres are absent from the shown high/final series; no unique target-specific group is established.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The carbonyl-S-N-Br compound reaches 0.4373696743346135 versus the Parent seed-2 maximum of 0.41003927643747895. A more conventional aryl ketone reaches 0.4156437178531234, and its chlorine/bromine aryl variants tie at that score, so reactive acyl-S-N-Br chemistry is not needed to approach this observed region. A ring-expanded N-containing ketone scores 0.02222493282960762, while a disrupted fused-ring thioamide scores 0.035101269092179636. Compact aromatic/carbonyl placement appears favorable relative to those expanded or disrupted structures. The final nitrogen/oxygen-rich bridged products lie below the earlier maximum.

per_task.generated_character: Large, heavily decorated nitrogen-rich diones dominate. The seed-2 best family joins the fused dione to a pyridine-like ring carrying a very small oxygen bridge, with amino-substituted linkers, brominated alkyl/alkene groups and an O-Br hypobromite. Seed 0 forms more extensively fused aromatic diones with ester/thioester and imine substituents; seed 1 reaches expanded nitrogen rings containing alkynes, imines, N-Br and halogenated side chains. Every proposal contains aromatic and ring-closure tokens, while cumulated-double-bond presence is 0.0851. Relative to the Parent's large sulfur-rich decorated cores, these products remain bulky and highly functionalized, with reactivity and ring-strain problems extending beyond sulfur valence.
liabilities: Hypobromite O-Br, N-Br, haloalkyl and imine functionality creates potential instability and reactive combinations.
Small aromatic-associated oxygen bridges, cyclic alkynes or cumulated unsaturation, and unspecified amino-linker configurations undermine whole-molecule synthetic plausibility.
missing_features: Compact, stable substituent sets around the recurring fused-dione arrangement are poorly represented among late molecules.
Accessible heteroaryl attachments without the small strained oxygen bridge, O-Br or N-halogen chemistry are missing from much of the high-scoring family.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.548381482770623; a modified low optimizer example scores 0.5286081645773063. The best seed-2 family reaches 0.5988528191359531, below its Parent seed-2 counterpart at 0.6092182584436399. Many alkyl, bromo/chloro and alkene variants share exactly 0.5988528191359531, as do final carbonyl/thione variants. Opening the fused dione into the final amino-containing cyclic carbonyl structure gives 0.5520804780439669. The recurring heterocyclic arrangement appears more consequential than several peripheral decorations; the plateau does not establish that the reactive groups are useful.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leaders are sulfur-free aromatic polyamines: chlorophenyl and pyridyl groups connect to an azetidine-containing polycyclic diamine framework, sometimes with aminomethyl or hydroxymethyl substituents. Related members insert an ether bridge or open part of the polycyclic framework. Seed 0 reaches more flexible aromatic tertiary-amine/sulfenamide chains, whereas seed 1 retains a sulfur heteroaromatic, amine and aryl family. Aromatic presence is 1.0 and halogen presence is 0.9954. Compared with the Parent's multiply bonded sulfur frameworks, the strongest current seed has more conventional C/N/O connectivity and recognizable medicinal architecture. Small fused rings and unspecified configurations still leave synthetic and conformational uncertainty; neutral SMILES do not establish actual protonation.
liabilities: Fused azetidine-containing frameworks have constrained geometry and unspecified ring-junction stereochemistry.
Multiple amines and aromatic groups leave ionization and physicochemical properties unresolved; other seeds still contain reactive N-S linkages or strained unsaturation.
missing_features: Accessible variants of the favorable aromatic/polyamine arrangement with less crowded small-ring fusion are underrepresented despite a high-scoring less connected analogue.
Explicit stereochemical and protonation alternatives are absent from the observed comparisons; a single required halogen or terminal polar group is not supported by the near-saturated series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 polyamine maximum is 0.999998887350651, compared with 0.9148143511682032 for the paired Parent. Early acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives remain low, including 0.007468397818197266. Many different aromatic substituents, ether insertion and a less connected ring analogue retain nearly saturated scores; the latter scores 0.9999895780003252. Opening an aromatic ring into an expanded unsaturated ring lowers the final example to 0.39449574864596665. The visible gradient supports aromatic/amine spacing while leaving substantial freedom in halogens and ring connectivity. The improvement is not uniform across seeds: the current seed-1 maximum is below its Parent counterpart.

per_task.generated_character: The highest seed-0 molecules combine ethoxy-substituted aromatic rings and a pendant alkylphenyl group with a constrained lactam/hydrazide and an oxygen-rich macrocyclic bridge. N-N and N-O connectivity is prominent. Other seeds explore related aryl lactam/ester frameworks, and the final seed-2 family adds a dense N-N-rich bridge system and N-Cl. Aromatic and ring-closure presence rates are 1.0, while halogen presence is 0.0977. Relative to the Parent's sulfur-rich bridges and brominated alternatives, these leaders mainly use C/N/O frameworks, but controlled ring closure, heteroatom compatibility and stereochemistry remain unresolved. The size is moderate to bulky, with recognizable aromatic/carbonyl fragments embedded in unusual complete structures.
liabilities: Hydrazide, N-O and acetal-like linkages complicate stability and synthetic compatibility in the macrocyclic framework.
Late dense nitrogen bridges and N-Cl combine unresolved ring geometry with reactive functionality.
missing_features: Accessible macrocyclic or fused alternatives preserving the aromatic/lactam arrangement without extensive N-N/N-O connectivity are underexplored.
Simpler stable linkers and defined configurations are absent from much of the late bridged output; the score differences do not reveal a uniquely missing target fragment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best aromatic/lactam macrocyclic member scores 0.22352659924261728 compared with the Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.2107445781802027. An opened dicarbonyl derivative scores 0.1263981386214515, and a polyene replacing aromatic structure scores 0.14644884303054695. The gradient therefore favors the retained aromatic/carbonyl arrangement in these series. Phenol and thiol substitutions tie at 0.21874182349972615, showing limited discrimination of that chemical change. The late N-chloro bridged family remains lower, including 0.19903147130554083; adding reactive nitrogen and more bridges is not consistently rewarded.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leaders remain highly compact polycyclic cages, now built from carbon/nitrogen frameworks with sulfoxide, thiol and a very small aromatic N/S ring. They contain multiple carbon-bound fluorines, an N-F cyclic carbonyl/amidine region and, in the best molecule, a severely constrained cyclic allene. Other high members replace the allene with densely fused small carbon rings. Seeds 0 and 1 also retain complex cages with sulfoxide or related oxygenated sulfur and thiol groups. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9379, higher than the broadly nonaromatic Parent cage families, but the aromatic portion is small relative to the total cage. Ordinary sulfur bonding has not made these complete structures synthetically plausible.
liabilities: A small-ring cyclic allene, very small aromatic N/S ring and densely fused cage junctions impose severe geometric and stability concerns.
N-F and thiol functionality remain reactive liabilities, and neither carbon-centre nor sulfoxide stereochemistry is specified.
missing_features: Stable accessible frameworks preserving the favorable carbonyl/nitrogen/fluorinated arrangement without the cyclic allene and densely fused small rings are not demonstrated.
Chemically conventional substitutes for the N-F motif and explicit stereochemistry at cage junctions and sulfoxide centres are absent from the shown high-scoring comparisons.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 maximum reaches 0.6534580802597463 versus its Parent maximum of 0.4484554129767839; the other paired seeds have lower maxima than their Parents. An early modified fused dione scores 7.590554525032884e-10. In a close high-scoring cage pair, replacing N-F by NH lowers 0.619441659867296 to 0.12291544159228127. Expanding the adjacent carbonyl-containing ring gives 0.12275001618495877. Thus local nitrogen substitution and ring geometry receive strong score discrimination, including a preference for a reactive N-F bond in this pair. These observations do not establish an accessible pharmacophore or reward for chemical stability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Current digest leaders contain acyl-S-N-Br, N-bromothioamide, O-Br hypobromite and N-F motifs. A matched N-F versus NH cage pair scores 0.619441659867296 and 0.12291544159228127, so the observed scalar feedback can favor a chemically reactive substitution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still emits reactive nitrogen-halogen and oxygen-halogen bonds within high-scoring molecular families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable nitrogen and oxygen bonding alternatives available while preserving local attachment geometry, and represent functional-group compatibility independently of the scalar objective. Ordinary sulfur valence alone does not address these remaining liabilities.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring outputs now include a small-ring cyclic allene, a very small aromatic N/S ring, strained oxygen bridges and dense fused carbon/nitrogen cages. Other high outputs contain recognizable azetidine-containing polyamines, so small rings are not uniformly implausible.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can exchange unusual sulfur chemistry for equally problematic carbon, nitrogen and oxygen ring geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Distinguish accessible small rings from severely constrained multiple bonds and incompatible fused-ring closures. Provide simpler fused, spiro or ring-opened alternatives that preserve useful substituent spacing rather than treating all valid graph closures as equally feasible.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre-token presence is 0.0 in every current digest despite substituted polycyclic diamines, fluorinated cage junctions and unsymmetrically substituted sulfoxides. The supplied high/final structures do not compare explicitly assigned stereoisomers.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator continues to omit stereochemical specification at saturated ring junctions and stereogenic sulfur centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support consistent configuration assignment and stereoisomer variation for eligible carbon and sulfur centres, and retain that identity through generation. Any scoring benefit must be measured because these trajectories do not establish stereochemical sensitivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A less connected aromatic polyamine analogue scores 0.9999895780003252 while more constrained relatives have nearly saturated scores. A decorated dione family shares 0.5988528191359531 across numerous side-chain and carbonyl/thione changes, and recognizable aryl ketones reach 0.4156437178531234 near more reactive alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable simpler analogues remain underexplored when a family already has broad tolerance to peripheral changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate compact linkers, fewer ring connections and stable substituent replacements around recurring aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements. This would expose accessible alternatives within the observed favorable regions without relying mainly on additional heteroatoms or complex ring closures.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

retained_mechanisms: Fixed stochastic atom and bond graph edits from one scored current molecule, with canonical novelty and graph validity checks
Unconditional highest-accepted-neighbor walk with lexicographic canonical tie selection
Signed occurrence differences of canonical rooted radius-one local motifs and bounded inverse-attribute installation from the selected transition
Same-transition conjunction of active positive and negative inverse restrictions, admitting partial and cross-transition-only matches
Four-completed-step tabu tenure, latest-provenance overlap refresh and documented global-oldest release after generation obstruction
Independent monotone best-observed archive without archive restarts
Passive first-valid-novel batch and same-state original-OR diagnostics carried through accepted-score and selected-transition provenance without additional oracle calls
Round-trip normalization of generated molecular identities before novelty filtering, pending-trace bookkeeping and emission
Pure source-relative outside-envelope sulfur-signature introduction gate on valid novel normalized graph neighbors before tabu matching

approach.method_basis: The Parent performs molecular search directly in fixed-width SELFIES token frames. It keeps one real score and the original construction frame for each canonical molecule, ranks observations into a small positive group and lower-scoring negatives, and selects a positive exemplar uniformly. A fresh random coordinate order fixes values from that exemplar until every retained negative frame is excluded, then continues until at most four coordinates remain free. Uniform token draws in the resulting region supply most proposals; a broad uniform component supplies the rest. Molecular validation and novelty filtering precede evaluation, and complete-batch feedback updates the ranked records. Its observed negative exclusions were correct, but the four-coordinate limit determined every final mask, leaving the molecular neighborhoods strongly dependent on each molecule's single retained serialization.
approach.novelty: Add verified equivalent serialization views to the labeled molecular records. Each molecule receives a small, bounded bank of alternative SELFIES frames obtained through graph-preserving atom reorderings and exact molecular identity checks. Each regional classifier selects one view per labeled molecule, so the same real observations can define different token neighborhoods without receiving extra weight. Original sampled frames remain immutable score receipts. This is the lineage's first Child: its only existing implementation always classifies and samples using the one retained original frame. The new causal claim is that changing an equivalent coordinate representation changes decoded regional proposals; a paired diagnostic using the original frames will measure that effect before considering whether scores improve.

nodes.hypothesis: For each regional RACOS classifier, uniformly select one identity-verified equivalent SELFIES serialization view per scored molecular record from a bounded task-local view bank, and apply the inherited negative-exclusion, uncertainty-shrinking and uniform-sampling rules to those selected views while preserving one observation weight and the immutable original sampled-frame score receipt per molecule.

finding_summary.headline: Equivalent views changed 782 evaluated proposals; the screening mean fell
finding_summary.insights:
Equivalent construction representatives can change the molecules reached by a local token sampler. The effect comes from different fixed token values: all 1,341 paired regions fixed the same 75 coordinate locations and left four free. Alternative negative views changed when exclusion finished in 652 regions, but never added a final restriction beyond the uncertainty limit. This narrows the demonstrated contribution to the selected exemplar representation under the observed masks. Eleven alternative-view pairs still decoded to the same molecule, so token differences alone would have overstated the effect.

More novel support did not establish better search. Only 36 of 792 accepted children from alternative exemplar views beat their source, compared with 42 of 517 from original views; these conditional groups have different molecule and task support and do not isolate a score effect. The alternatives for generated records also remove an average of 17.58 non-PAD tokens, so this experiment combines atom traversal with normalization of redundant construction tokens. Coverage is uneven: 325 generated records have no admitted alternative, including 137/290 in drd2_docking and 119/290 in sitagliptin_mpo. The paired shadows have no scores, leaving both the contribution to later optimization and reliability across seeds open.

The supplied molecular assessment still finds frequent radicals, unusual charges and reactive or strained connectivity among generated molecules, including high scorers. Exact identity verification protects the already scored bank entries; it does not make their sampled offspring chemically credible or preserve useful scaffold relationships. Useful, chemically ordinary molecular neighborhoods remain unresolved despite the demonstrated representation effect.
finding_summary.results:
The equivalent views produced a measurable molecular effect. Verified alternatives were available for 1,175 of 1,500 scored records, and an alternative exemplar was selected in 808 of 1,341 regional constructions. Holding the molecular observations and sampling randomness fixed, 797 paired proposals decoded to different molecules; 782 of those changes survived filtering and received real evaluator scores. All identity, one-observation, score-attachment and batch checks passed.

Regional novelty acceptance rose from 96.24% to 97.61%, and decoded overlaps across regions fell from 48 of 1,355 raw draws to 31 of 1,341. The fraction of accepted regional children beating their exemplar rose slightly, from 67/1,304 (5.14%) to 78/1,309 (5.96%). The five-task final Top-1 mean nevertheless fell from 0.315539 to 0.289335. Parent-to-current maxima were 0.345581 to 0.366339 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.579123 to 0.571504 for deco_hop, 0.120104 to 0.028849 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.168550 for median_2, and 0.365051 to 0.311434 for sitagliptin_mpo. Both runs completed all five tasks with 300 evaluations each. This is one screening seed.

molecular.headline: Frequent rings conceal radical-rich chemistry: recognizable aryl/carbonyl scaffolds coexist with highly charged polyenes and strained rings.
molecular.overall_character: The digest and all supplied current and Parent seed-0 trajectories were read. Each covered task contains 300 observations, including 290 optimizer proposals; no tasks lack trajectories. The output ranges from tiny fragments to medium and larger multiring frameworks. Ring_closure_rate spans 0.6966 to 0.8172, but aromatic_atom_rate spans 0.0207 to 0.6: ring construction is common while intact aromatic chemistry is very uneven. These digest rates measure the presence of SMILES text features in proposed molecules, not fractions of atoms or perceived ring counts. The recognizable families include haloaryl indole carboxamides, methoxy chromenone/pyridyl assemblies, and aryl ester/dicarbonyl frameworks. Other high-scoring families are almost entirely nonaromatic polyenes, cumulenes and unusual heteroatom rings. Charged_rate spans 0.6897 to 0.9448. Read-only RDKit reparsing of the supplied graphs confirms frequent radical centres, including in leading molecules and in some structures without formal charge. Low-coordinate boron, carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and silicon environments coexist with oxonium, unusual sulfur bonding, peroxide-like chains and strained unsaturation. Synthetic plausibility is poor overall; neutral carbonyl-rich examples and some conventional aromatic fragments provide a more credible subset. Formal graph diversity is substantial, but stronger proposals within a task repeatedly revisit related families, giving moderate useful structural diversity. Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0, establishing absent stereochemical specification rather than absence of potentially stereogenic atoms. Parent comparisons below describe observed chemistry and supplied scores; neither those comparisons nor local score associations identify an unseen target pharmacophore or establish a causal score contribution from a particular chemical feature.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized, branched, unsaturated frameworks with haloaryl carboxamides, alongside small fragments. Mean SMILES length is 42.9 and maximum length 84; ring_closure_rate is 0.8172, aromatic_atom_rate 0.5655 and halogen_rate 0.7552. Evaluation 30 retains a methoxyindole carboxamide linked to fluorophenyl, but carries a radical-bearing boron anion. Evaluation 268 instead combines a bromophenyl aminoacetamide with an unsaturated oxygen-containing bicyclic core and low-coordinate boron/nitrogen substituents. The intact amide and aromatic fragments are recognizable synthetic chemistry; the electronic states and reorganized unsaturated rings make the leading complete structures implausible ordinary synthetic targets. Charged_rate is 0.831.
liabilities: Low-coordinate boron anions and additional radical nitrogen/phosphorus centres. Evaluation 189 has compensating formal charges while retaining radical centres, so net neutrality does not establish credible electronic structure.
Extensively rearranged unsaturated rings, atypical sulfur substitution and unspecified stereochemistry make scaffold geometry and synthesis uncertain.
missing_features: Reliable coverage of chemically ordinary variants retaining the haloaryl-carbonyl/nitrogen architecture visible in the stronger molecules. The supplied neutral indole carboxamide shows a credible version, but the leading generated variants add radical-bearing atoms.

Controlled variation of intact heteroaromatic and amide arrangements beyond repeated ring expansion and heteroatom insertion. The equal scores of the aromatic and partly nonaromatic relatives prevent inferring a universal requirement for additional aromatic rings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial neutral methoxyindole carboxamide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145; the boron-anion indole at evaluation 30 scores 0.354481213984869, and its ring-expanded, partly nonaromatic relative at evaluation 174 has exactly the same score. The aminoacetamide/bromophenyl framework at evaluation 268 reaches 0.36633919598396925. Thus the visible upper tail preserves assembled aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl relationships, while strict aromaticity alone does not explain the score. The tiny epoxide at evaluation 298 scores 0.0; the final sulfur-containing ring-reorganized aminoacetamide at evaluation 300 scores 0.2966478915460209. Parent n-e8acbddfa050 reached 0.3455806835841063 with a nitrogen/thione-rich multiring framework carrying oxonium and low-coordinate charged atoms. The current upper tail shifts toward haloaryl carboxamides and boron-bearing unsaturated cores, while unusual electronic states persist.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules are medium-to-large aromatic assemblies containing methoxy-substituted chromenone-like carbonyl heterocycles, phenyl/pyridyl regions and often nitriles. Mean SMILES length is 46.9 and maximum length 86; ring_closure_rate is 0.7793 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.5828. Hydrazinium substituents recur. Evaluation 237 incorporates an extended unsaturated ring bridge, imidate-like connectivity and an O-N substituent. Evaluation 199 combines a reorganized lactone/oxonium ring system with a charged O-O-O chain. The aromatic and carbonyl components are recognizable, but the elaborate cyclizations and reactive decorations make the overall synthetic plausibility questionable to poor. Charged_rate is 0.8276.
liabilities: Peroxide-like O-O chains, multiply charged oxygen environments and the O-Br bond in the final small acyl hypobromite at evaluation 299.

Ring-contracted lactone connectivity, extended unsaturated bridges and recurrent N-N/N-O functionality require specific stability and synthetic justification. The leading evaluation 237 is closed-shell on reparsing, but that does not establish an accessible synthetic route.
missing_features: Broader stable decoration chemistry around the aromatic/polar frameworks. The current upper tail repeatedly uses hydrazinium, aminooxy or oxonium/oxygen-chain functionality, while the Parent contained a relatively strong neutral aryl-aminal example.

Coherent alternatives that retain useful aryl/carbonyl relationships without requiring highly rearranged lactone rings or long unsaturated cyclization bridges. Exact hidden decoration requirements cannot be inferred from these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy chromenone/biaryl nitrile at evaluation 8 scores 0.5418375031378128; the pyridyl-nitrile/hydrazinium derivative at evaluation 37 scores 0.5643691820162409. The oxonium/methylthio-containing evaluation 249 receives the same 0.5643691820162409, despite its additional oxonium centre and altered substituents. The ring-bridged evaluation 237 scores 0.5715043852298755 and the charged oxygen-chain relative at evaluation 199 scores 0.5684258279147134. Acetylene at evaluation 246 scores 0.5. The final extensively rearranged, nonaromatic polycycle at evaluation 300 scores 0.507630410654828. The observed preference is for assembled aromatic/polar architectures over tiny or strongly disrupted structures; the score does not show that reactive oxygen or hydrazine functionality is necessary. The Parent upper tail instead emphasized indole amidine/carboxamide and diaryl cyclic-aminal families: its maximum was 0.5791225581141548 and a neutral diaryl hydroxyaminal scored 0.5766980825479363. The current maximum is associated with a different, still chemically problematic aromatic family.

per_task.generated_character: The upper tail consists of relatively large nonaromatic polyenes/cumulenes, branched chains and large unsaturated rings. Mean SMILES length is 60.7 and maximum length 109. Ring_closure_rate is 0.6966, but aromatic_atom_rate is only 0.0207; charged_rate is 0.9448 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.6207. The best molecule, evaluation 277, is acyclic. Evaluation 293 closes a long heteroatom-bearing unsaturated chain into a large ring. Both contain repeated carbon cations, boron anions, low-coordinate phosphorus, unusual sulfur multiple bonds and oxonium environments. Reparsing confirms multiple radical centres in these leading graphs. They express extensive formal unsaturation and heteroatom diversity with very little conventional medicinal scaffold chemistry, making them implausible ordinary isolable compounds.
liabilities: Numerous radical centres and low-coordinate charged atoms, including repeated carbon cations, boron anions and atypical sulfur/phosphorus multiple bonds within individual molecules.

Long cumulated/conjugated sequences and highly unsaturated macrocyclic or bridged connectivity with unspecified geometry. A ring-closure digit here supplies little evidence for a stable, useful three-dimensional scaffold.
missing_features: Chemically credible closed-shell realizations of the larger carbon frameworks and polar functionality represented in the current upper tail. Its apparent size/architecture preference is realized through highly unusual electronic states.

Coverage of intact aryl-containing, constrained polar architectures is greatly reduced relative to the Parent upper tail. The low-scoring aromatic and tertiary-amine examples show that neither adding a generic aromatic ring nor adding an amine is an evidence-backed solution by itself.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The long acyclic evaluation 277 scores 0.028848761971118526 and the large-ring relative at evaluation 293 scores 0.02884865939301175. The similarly elaborate final evaluation 296 scores 0.02884463593273818. A much shorter boron/nitrogen/oxygen ionic fragment at evaluation 212 scores 0.0020518739328129186; the final short brominated oxonium ether at evaluation 295 scores 0.004062928989281451. Within this trajectory, fuller nonaromatic carbon/heteroatom frameworks generally occupy the upper tail, with little separation among the largest relatives. Simple aromatic presence is insufficient: the biphenyl nitrile/alkoxide at evaluation 16 scores 0.0013501216598358666, and the initial aromatic amide/hydroxamate with a saturated tertiary amine at evaluation 6 scores 0.0003786988088202195. The Parent maximum, 0.12010438063540518, came from a halogenated aryl-containing polycycle with its own unusual sulfur/nitrogen chemistry. The current maximum accompanies near-loss of aromatic frameworks and growth of nonaromatic chains/large rings; this comparison does not isolate why the scores differ.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules are medium-to-large aryl ethyl-ester/dicarbonyl frameworks with N-methyl carbonyl or urea-like regions, phenol/ether substituents and substantial ring rearrangement. Mean SMILES length is 48.7 and maximum length 84; ring_closure_rate is 0.8034 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.6. Evaluation 243 is a neutral aryl-ester macrocycle joining the carbonyl/nitrogen region through an N-O-methylene-O linkage. Evaluations 282 and 298 are also neutral and closed-shell, retaining aryl and dicarbonyl motifs in cross-conjugated or ring-expanded arrangements. These are more recognizable synthetic targets than much of the remaining output, although their cyclizations and reactive linkages remain demanding. Charged_rate is 0.6897; uncharged phosphorus-containing relatives also carry radicals on reparsing.
liabilities: N-O/acetal-like linkage in the leading macrocycle and extensive cross-conjugation or ring expansion in nearby neutral structures; chemical stability and synthetic accessibility are unestablished.

Phosphorus/silicon insertions, radicals and charged replacements elsewhere in the same families. Evaluation 53 lacks formal charge but contains a radical-bearing phosphorus environment, illustrating an electronic-state problem that charge counting alone misses.
missing_features: More controlled, stable variations of the aromatic/ester/carbonyl arrangement supported by the stronger molecules. Current high-scoring neutral examples exist, but often reach new topology through extended cyclization or N-O connectivity.

Broader development of distinct intact aromatic amide-rich families, exemplified by the relatively strong initial amide/hydroxamate, alongside the dominant ester/dicarbonyl family. The observations do not reveal an unseen reference structure.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl ester/fused dicarbonyl at evaluation 7 scores 0.1678386594791329. The generated macrocycle at evaluation 243 scores 0.16854996561581048; evaluations 282 and 298 score 0.16695175953014704 and 0.1651413292730383. Adding the sulfur-oxygen substituent in the related evaluation 271 gives 0.160745220268056. The late short brominated ether at evaluation 299 scores 0.020160580116942894, while the small imidate-like anion at evaluation 292 scores 0.0. The gradient supports retention of assembled aromatic/ester/carbonyl relationships over fragments; substantial rearrangements within that family remain close in score. The chemically distinct initial aromatic amide/hydroxamate at evaluation 6 also scores 0.1569767171139282. The Parent retained the same initial maximum of 0.1678386594791329, with its best generated annulated dicarbonyl relative at 0.16526725762745997. The current leading chemistry remains centered on the same ester/dicarbonyl family while exploring new neutral ring topologies.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger output comprises medium-sized, mostly nonaromatic fluorinated amino/polyene frameworks, unusual boron/phosphorus rings, and imine-containing polycycles with silicon or selenium. Mean SMILES length is 44.4 and maximum length 84; ring_closure_rate is 0.7828, aromatic_atom_rate 0.2138, charged_rate 0.9241 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.4483. Evaluation 298 links an amino-substituted unsaturated ring to a methoxy-substituted small cyclic alkyne bearing adjacent carbon anions, and adds a boron/sulfur/iodine appendage. Evaluation 210 combines fluorophosphorus and boron/oxygen ring chemistry with carbon anions; evaluation 223 is a long acyclic unsaturated nitrogen/oxygen/sulfur chain. These upper-tail structures contain radicals and unusual ionic states. The cyclic alkyne geometry and heteroatom connectivity make their synthetic plausibility especially poor.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make closed-shell polar structures and chemically ordinary ionization states routinely accessible through joint control of bond patterns, valence, radical state and protonation. transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading digest molecules include small cyclic alkynes, charged oxygen chains, reorganized lactone rings and long cumulene-rich loops. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent functional-group stability and feasible ring geometry even when a graph parses successfully.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide stable, ordinary substitution and ring-construction options that maintain complete functional groups and feasible unsaturation. transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring excerpts repeatedly retain assembled aryl/carboxamide or aryl/ester/dicarbonyl motifs, whereas low-score and final excerpts include tiny fragments or substantially disrupted variants. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator inconsistently preserves useful scaffold and linker relationships while exploring new molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support coherent substitution and attachment changes that preserve the ring edges and complete linker/functional-group patterns of useful observed structures. transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0. Stronger ring-containing examples are dominated by unsaturated, ring-expanded or unusually charged architectures. Ordinary saturated nitrogen rings occur in the supplied initial chemistry, but the leading generated structures often express nitrogen functionality through hydrazinium, imines, radical anions or heteroatom-rich unsaturated loops. This identifies a coverage gap; the visible scores do not establish a universal benefit from saturation, a basic amine or stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional saturated heterocycle and stereochemically specified structure coverage is weak among the stronger generated molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make feasible saturated and partly saturated heterocycles, controlled amine ionization and explicitly specified stereochemical alternatives available as general construction choices. nodes.method_name: RACOS: negative-exclusion sampling of de novo SELFIES regions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is RACOS, selected before locating the primary source. Its categorical form chooses a positively labeled exemplar, randomly fixes coordinates to that exemplar until negative examples are excluded, further restricts the number of free coordinates, and samples the resulting region; a broader uniform component preserves exploration. Each proposal can use a newly randomized classifier. These are the mechanisms described by Yu, Qian and Hu in [Derivative-Free Optimization via Classification](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/10289/10148). My molecular adaptation applies this process directly to bounded categorical SELFIES frames, with removable padding that permits changes in molecular length. Preparation extracts only a construction-token alphabet from the permitted unlabeled corpus. There is no trained molecular encoder or decoder. Initial labeled molecules become exemplars only after encoding and decoding reproduce their canonical identity. For generated molecules, retain the actual sampled frame, its decoded canonical molecule, and the score actually returned for that molecule. Rank the current objective's observed molecules into a high-score positive group and a lower-score negative group; use these labels to construct exclusion regions. Free token positions are newly sampled and decoded into complete molecules, checked, canonicalized, and deduplicated. Rebuild a region or use the broad generation component when a region cannot provide a fresh molecule. These are online constructions from token primitives, not retrieval or enumeration of complete molecules. After each announced batch receives real feedback, refresh the labeled sets and incumbent; all pending proposals use only previously observed scores. Each objective starts with clean task-specific state and follows the protocol's supplied batch and resource limits. The hypothesis is that explicitly excluding observed poor token configurations will concentrate new molecular proposals around combinations that improve the incumbent with few labels. Success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Region exclusion, validity, or classification accuracy alone cannot establish that hypothesis. Positional token restrictions may have weak structural meaning, and multiple frames can decode to the same molecule; exact representation checks address score provenance but do not establish useful search geometry.

approach.method_basis: Particle swarm optimization runs a population of points that each remember where they have been. A particle keeps a position, a velocity, and the best position it has personally found, and each step its velocity is pulled by inertia toward its own past direction, by a stochastic attraction to its personal best, and by another to the best position the whole swarm has seen. Applied to molecules, the positions live in the continuous latent space of a molecular autoencoder, and every position is turned into a real molecule by a frozen decoder before being scored.
approach.novelty: This root commits to velocities that persist across the entire objective rather than being redrawn each round, so a particle carries momentum through many feedback batches. It attaches accepted scores to the exact latent position that generated the molecule, rather than to a re-encoding of it, which is what keeps the personal and social memories geometrically honest when the decoder is many-to-one.

nodes.hypothesis: Move persistent particles through a frozen deterministic SELFIES VAE latent space using inertia plus independent stochastic attractions toward their own best observed position and the swarm best observed position, and attach accepted molecular scores to the exact generating positions before updating those task-local memories.

finding_summary.headline: Swarm dynamics reproduced across seeds as final scores fell
finding_summary.insights: The lower scores do not come from omitted inertia, unused personal memory, missing information transfer or score assignment to the wrong logged latent position. The initial identity gate prevented all supplied initial scores from becoming attractors in the new seeds; shared memory was then established from the first accepted batch and used normally thereafter. That separates safe score handling from the decoder's limited ability to recover the supplied molecules. Low token loss and abundant valid outputs coexist with weak exact reconstruction and large structural changes: emitted molecules average about 0.85 Morgan distance from both their decoded source and personal best. The molecular assessment is consistent with this coarse search behavior, finding many polyenes, irregular rings and reactive polar forms, with conventional aromatic/amine arrangements unevenly represented. The loss of the stronger aromatic/basic-amine family accompanies the largest score decline, but the data do not isolate its cause. These replicas vary both the prepared representation and the stochastic search, so they do not establish that encoder quality is the sole constraint or that any swarm component improves scores. Representation quality and motion scale remain separate questions for controlled follow-up. The execution finding is specific to the evaluated CUDA runtime: all runtime repeat-decodes matched, while independent CPU replay changed the decoded identity on 16 of 2,932 new motion attempts. Cross-backend decoder identity is therefore not established.
finding_summary.results: The two additional seeds reproduced the intended persistent motion, accepted-score memories and information transfer. All 2,932 motion equations and state transitions were verified, including 2,732 reuses of persistent velocity. Cognitive attraction was nonzero in all 1,896 eligible distinct-position opportunities, social attraction in all 2,801 eligible opportunities, and real shared memories influenced other particles 2,700 times. Accepted proposals established 200 personal bests and strictly improved them 658 times; every updated personal memory with a later opportunity was reused. All 2,900 proposals were accepted with no evaluator invalids or duplicates, and every generating position matched its runtime repeated decode. Mean final-best scores were 0.450789 in the original seed, 0.358719 in the first new seed and 0.288163 in the second. The three-seed mean is 0.365890 with a population standard deviation of 0.066585. Most of the variation comes from drd2_docking, whose final scores fell from 0.859171 to 0.476176 and 0.124923. The three-seed means for the other objectives are 0.345495 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.569962 for deco_hop, 0.174178 for median_2 and 0.253060 for sitagliptin_mpo. The decoder learned in each preparation: new-seed heldout reconstruction losses fell from 4.565228 to 0.629885 and from 4.534641 to 0.633075. Exact heldout molecular reconstruction remained only 6/480 and 7/480. None of the 100 initial encoding receipts in the new runs reconstructed its original identity, so all 200 particles correctly began without scored attractors.

molecular.headline: Polyene-rich molecules with irregular ring systems and reactive polar groups; conventional aromatic–amine arrangements are unevenly represented
molecular.overall_character: This report covers the supplied seed-1 and seed-2 trajectories, compared with seed 0 of the same Algorithm Node. All five tasks are represented, each by 600 evaluated records including 580 optimizer proposals. The output is structurally varied but dominated by alternating double bonds, enol ethers, aldehydes, conjugated carbonyls and irregular medium-sized or large ring closures. Phenyl, thiophene and occasional nitrogen heteroaromatic fragments are present, but many compounds combine them with nonaromatic polyenes or unusually connected rings rather than conventional medicinal scaffolds. Ring-closure indicator rates are 0.8897–0.9724, whereas aromatic-atom indicators are only 0.5517–0.8172. Rings are therefore abundant without being uniformly aromatic. Mean SMILES lengths range from 40.5 to 62.5, with a maximum of 147 on one task. These text lengths are not molecular weights. The cumulated-double-bond counter ranges from 0.0 to 0.05; it does not count the many ordinary alternating polyenes visible throughout the trajectories. The compounds contain useful amide, sulfone, amine and aromatic elements, but synthetic plausibility is questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because long conjugated linkers, aldehydes, unusual sulfur/nitrogen valence patterns and complicated closures recur even among favorable examples. Some smaller conventional-looking compounds occur, so this is not a claim that every structure is unmakeable. Every stereocentre indicator is 0.0, and the cited polyenes also leave alkene geometry unspecified. Graph validity and a favorable scalar score do not establish an isolable chemical form, stability or a defined three-dimensional structure.

per_task.generated_character: The high group consists of moderately sized but unusual conjugated ring systems: an S-imino diene ring attached to an aminated unsaturated carbon ring with carboxamide and thienyl enone groups, a fused unsaturated lactam/thioether system bearing a fluoroaniline, and hydrazone-containing or charged nitrogen structures. Aldehydes, amides, nitro groups, thioethers and enamine-like connections recur. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9552, aromatic_atom_rate 0.631 and mean SMILES length 40.5. Ring perception of the best structure gives a nonaromatic medium carbon ring rather than an ordinary phenyl or azaaryl core. Synthetic routes and stereochemical forms would be materially less straightforward than those of the initial indole carboxamide.
liabilities: The highest-scoring structure combines an unusual S-imino ring with an enone, while another high scorer carries O=[N+]=N. Their chemical forms and reactivity require separate assessment.

Aldehydes, thioesters, conjugated enamines and multiple unspecified double-bond geometries complicate stability and synthesis. Cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.05, in addition to the frequent alternating polyenes.
The worst proposals introduce substantial size, flexibility or tightly connected ring complexity without retaining favorable scores.
missing_features: Consistent assembly of compact, conventional aromatic and polar ring systems is missing from much of the output; ring closure is often achieved through extended unsaturated or irregular fused frameworks instead.

Stable and geometrically defined alternatives to the conjugated aldehyde/enamine and unusual S=N or O=[N+]=N motifs are insufficiently represented around otherwise favorable size and polar-group combinations.
No unique missing target motif follows from the chemically heterogeneous high group, and stereochemical sensitivity is untested.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The S-imino/polyene/carboxamide structure scores 0.3565472174010858 and the fluoroaniline/lactam/thioether structure scores 0.34302515021197216. The initial conventional indole carboxamide already scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 best at 0.37483330611175764 was also an unsaturated lactam bearing polar nitrogen functionality and an aromatic nitrile/carboxamide region, so the replication retains the same broad conjugated/polar character while changing connectivity. At the bottom, very large alkylated or ring-extended molecules score 1.1533920765551684e-30 and 8.812272454079934e-27; a long arylalkyl amine/polyene scores 3.8438521003485694e-25. The initial tiny alkyl bromide is also very low at 8.305895500294491e-10. The observable preference is a bounded size with aromatic/polar features, not unrestricted extension or truncation. The median is 0.042253, and late seed-2 oxygen/sulfur-rich polyenes remain modest, including 0.09723031993424279 and 0.03267406883416671. The high scores do not identify a uniquely required ring system or establish that the unusual functionalities are beneficial in isolation.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end is dominated by very elaborated polyaryl amides, ureas, nitroaryl groups and fluorinated phenyl rings, sometimes joined into large conjugated or cyclophane-like systems. The best structure encodes an unusually large conjugated nitrogen/carbonyl ring with fused aromatic portions and unsaturated side arms. Other high examples are long chains of phenyl rings connected to amides and nitrobenzophenone-like regions. Seed 2 includes additional irregular fused or bridged polar rings. Mean SMILES length is 62.5 and the maximum is 147; ring_closure_rate is 0.9655 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.7638. These are mostly large, synthetically demanding structures, with only a modest numerical separation from the initial screening-like molecules.
liabilities: Multiple nitroaryl groups and extensive conjugated or polyaryl surfaces introduce physicochemical and reactivity questions that the score does not answer.
A relatively high-scoring structure contains an acyl fluoride, which is chemically distinct from ordinary aryl fluorination.
Large irregular ring closures, unspecified polyene geometry, a late peroxide linkage and hydrogen-bearing sulfur functionality make many examples demanding synthetic or chemical-form targets.
missing_features: Compact, well-defined arrangements of aromatic nitrogen, donor/acceptor groups and linkers are unevenly represented; much of the output adds phenyl rings, polyenes and carbonyl groups instead.

Chemically comparable alternatives around the low-scoring nonaromatic sulfone systems are missing as an interpretable local series. The baseline shows that sulfone removal cannot be prescribed universally.
The high group does not reveal a unique missing decoration or geometry, and a small score difference from the initial molecules does not establish a need for its much greater structural complexity.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The large conjugated polycarbonyl/N-containing ring system scores 0.5620451020164658, the polyaryl amide/urea with nitro groups scores 0.5619777544131481, and the extended oligophenyl amide scores 0.5607123583378306. The initial fused-dione ester already scores 0.548381482770623, compared with a reported median of 0.520067. The visible gradient therefore tolerates extensive aromatic and polar-group elaboration without demonstrating that such complexity is necessary. The seed-0 best scored 0.5927058823529412 and combined a nitrogen-rich aromatic ring, a sulfone and aryl imine/amine links; the new high group shifts toward larger carbon-rich aromatic/amide assemblies. All six digest worst proposals contain carbon-bonded sulfones in largely nonaromatic unsaturated surroundings, with the worst at 0.25506553536376875. The higher-scoring baseline sulfone prevents attributing this contrast to sulfone presence alone. Late seed-2 sulfone/polyene structures continue near 0.26–0.28, while a different fused aminal/heteroaryl structure reaches 0.5551363900174116. These are unpaired chemical contrasts, not proof of a required substituent or a forbidden functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The new high-scoring molecules are chiefly chlorinated arylalkyl hydrocarbons with long alkyl or conjugated links. The best contains chlorinated phenyl groups and a chlorinated diene, with no nitrogen or oxygen. Other upper examples add a phenol, aldehyde, ether or an enamine-like amino arm; a partially unsaturated aryl-substituted nitrogen ring appears below them. This is a largely lipophilic, halogen-rich population rather than a dense family of conventional basic cyclic amines. Mean SMILES length is 55.5, halogen_rate 0.8948, ring_closure_rate 0.9276 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.6724. The arylalkyl chemistry can be recognizable, but long links and unusual heteroatom-rich late structures weaken general drug-likeness.
liabilities: The high nitrogen-free arylalkyl molecules combine extensive halogenation and hydrophobic surface with few polar groups, raising solubility and nonspecific-partitioning questions without establishing either outcome.
Conjugated aldehydes, enol ethers and halogenated unsaturation recur. Late proposals add very unusual sulfur or organophosphorus forms, including a difluorophosphoryl group, without favorable scores.
Long chains and large irregular closures increase conformational ambiguity; the score alone does not supply a binding geometry.
missing_features: The combined exposed aliphatic amine and bounded aromatic/spacer arrangement seen in the favorable baseline is poorly represented in the new high group, even though the generator can make amines.
The new examples do not provide a controlled comparison of linker length, amine availability and aromatic substitution; adding nitrogen indiscriminately would not follow from the shown scores.
Defined configurations and alkene geometries are absent in molecules whose flexible or substituted links can change their spatial arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The nitrogen-free chlorinated arylalkyl/diene scores 0.4761756997497859, and the more extended chlorinated arylalkyl structure scores 0.3966137972553488. An amino/phenol/aldehyde-containing relative scores 0.35740480261120694. The current high group therefore associates the visible signal with connected hydrophobic aromatic surfaces; it does not itself demonstrate a mandatory amine. The supplied seed-0 baseline is informative: its best at 0.8591709360377655 paired a free tertiary alkylamine with a brominated fused aromatic region, and another tertiary-amine-containing structure scored 0.7578688791540653. The new upper group largely lacks that combination. Current low examples include a small fluorinated enol-ether ester at 0.00010990702906285781, a conjugated aryl aldehyde at 0.00012492407267700092 and an amide-containing biphenyl at 0.00012620521493077546. Aromatic or halogen presence alone is insufficient. The median is 0.022728, and the final sulfonamide/polyene or oxygen-rich structures remain low. The baseline comparison supports exploring exposed amines in suitable aromatic surroundings, while remaining insufficient to claim a particular receptor interaction.

per_task.generated_character: The favorable seed-2 molecules are relatively compact combinations of aromatic rings and polar cyclic groups. The best joins benzodioxole through an amino link to a methoxy/methyl-substituted seven-membered N-containing carbonyl ring; the latter should not be called an ordinary six-membered pyridone. Other high examples include a diaryl sulfone with an oxygen-rich fused medium ring and a benzodioxole-containing cyclic hydrazone/lactam. Seed 1 more often emits enlarged fused carbonyl/imine systems with alkyl appendages. Mean SMILES length is 43.6, ring_closure_rate 0.9724 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.8172. The smaller upper examples have recognizable chemical components, but uncommon ring topology and more elaborate lower-scoring structures keep makeability uncertain.
liabilities: The unusual seven-membered aromatic carbonyl ring and cyclic hydrazone require attention to tautomeric form and geometry rather than treatment as routine six-membered heteroarenes.

Other proposals combine aldehydes, N–O connections, ester/acetal-rich medium rings and highly unsaturated small rings. These features create stability or synthetic questions even when ring and aromatic indicators are positive.
missing_features: Reliable access to compact, chemically conventional versions of the favorable aromatic/polar arrangements is limited; many alternatives instead become long polyenes or irregular medium-ring systems.
A unique missing reference-like structure cannot be inferred from the narrow score separation and chemically different upper examples.
Stereochemical and double-bond geometry specification is absent in the substituted saturated and hydrazone/polyene structures.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The benzodioxole/amino/aza-carbonyl-ring compound scores 0.18685638443799904, the diaryl sulfone scores 0.17882042440964765 and the cyclic hydrazone/lactam scores 0.17816898171823184. The initial fused-dione ester scores 0.1678386594791329. That initial molecule was also the seed-0 overall best; the highest seed-0 optimizer proposal was an unsaturated macrocyclic lactam at 0.14023138978580565. Thus the favorable new chemistry is somewhat more compact and organized around aromatic/polar ring combinations than the baseline generated high end. The lowest current examples are a small dibromoalkane at 0.014314958357846713 and acyclic unsaturated acid, aldehyde and enol-ether structures around 0.018–0.021. This supports aromatic ring architecture with appropriately arranged polar functionality over simple polyene fragments or heteroatom count alone. The median is 0.111326. The last proposals range from a small oxygen heterocycle at 0.0464643845937283 to a complex amide/lactam at 0.17194608615974535, so favorable chemistry is not tied to a single ring family or monotonically increasing size.

per_task.generated_character: The output favors moderately sized but highly unsaturated carbonyl/N/O-rich structures: an N-methoxy nitrogen-rich cyclic amide with a benzoyl group and an aldehyde arm, aryl amides bearing imidates and explicit alkoxides, sulfonamide/enamide chains and unsaturated lactam-containing rings. Many structures have few or no aromatic rings; aromatic_atom_rate is 0.5517 and ring_closure_rate 0.8897. Mean SMILES length is 40.7 and halogen_rate only 0.069. The chemistry is therefore substantially different from a uniformly fluorinated aromatic library. Ordinary amide or phenyl fragments are embedded in numerous unusual, potentially labile molecular forms.
liabilities: The best molecule contains an N–O connection, an N–N connection and a conjugated aldehyde; these introduce stability, oxidation and isomeric-form questions.
Explicit benzyl alkoxide or deprotonated oxygen species occur among favorable examples. Their protonation state and isolable form cannot be inferred from their score.

Repeated enol ethers, imidates, alpha-dicarbonyls and enamine-like connections make the population chemically reactive or tautomerically ambiguous. The large polyene and polyacetal extremes additionally impose size or flexibility burdens.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently reproduce the particular bounded connectivity that separates the favorable cyclic compound from its closely related open-chain form.
Chemically stable, well-specified alternatives to the alkoxide, N–O/N–N, imidate and conjugated-aldehyde arrangements are insufficiently demonstrated around the favorable polar skeletons.

The trajectories do not justify a claim that a specific fluorinated fragment or basic amine is missing from an obligatory target motif. The larger limitation is control of topology, polarity and chemical form.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-methoxy cyclic amide with an N–N connection, benzoyl group and conjugated aldehyde scores 0.2687964912603012. A closely related open-chain compound evaluated last scores 0.040358516578188335, providing a useful contrast in connectivity with largely overlapping functional groups. The aryl amide/imidate/benzyl-alkoxide structure scores 0.23418129517000225, and a nonaromatic unsaturated bicyclic amide with a sulfonamide arm scores 0.23098874100279387. Neither aromaticity nor fluorination is a universal high-end feature here. The seed-0 best at 0.259395205519374 was another carbonyl-rich unsaturated amide chain attached to a brominated unsaturated carbocycle. Both baseline and replication favor particular moderately sized polar/unsaturated arrangements, without establishing that the reactive functionality itself is required. At the bottom, a much larger fluorinated polyene scores 5.931767096585795e-76 and an oxygen-rich polyacetal macrocycle scores 1.8652722566013391e-41. Adding unsaturation, fluorine or oxygen alone does not help. The median is 0.000248, and most final carbonyl-rich structures also remain very low, so even abundant amides and aldehydes do not reliably reproduce the favorable connectivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring-closure indicators remain high at 0.8897–0.9724 while aromatic indicators range only from 0.5517 to 0.8172. The digest repeatedly shows nonaromatic polyene rings, long unsaturated chains and complicated closures. Several extended examples score near zero, whereas smaller aromatic/polar combinations score favorably. A cyclic nitrogen-rich compound scores 0.2687964912603012 and its closely related open-chain form 0.040358516578188335, showing that connectivity can matter beyond functional-group inventory.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator often substitutes long conjugated links and irregular large rings for bounded, chemically conventional scaffold architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable bounded ring sizes, controlled linker lengths and chemically conservative changes in ring connectivity around observed favorable structures. Preserve the ability to explore nonaromatic rings while distinguishing purposeful ring architecture from unchecked chain extension or closure complexity; let current task-local observations choose useful topology and size.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest high or late examples contain conjugated aldehydes, enol ethers, imidates, thioesters, an acyl fluoride, unusual S=N and O=[N+]=N functionality, N–O/N–N links and explicit alkoxides. These occur alongside useful amide, sulfone and aromatic features rather than only among the lowest-scoring molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Favorable polar-group combinations are not consistently supplied in stable, well-defined chemical forms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer conservative functional-group and oxidation-state alternatives within related skeletons and preserve explicit, chemically coherent hydrogen and charge states. Use local observations to test alternatives instead of assuming that a favorable scalar objective establishes stability or that all ionizable, sulfur-containing or carbonyl groups should be removed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied baseline includes a tertiary alkylamine attached to a halogenated fused aromatic region at 0.8591709360377655. The corresponding new high group is dominated by nitrogen-free chlorinated arylalkyl compounds, with a best of 0.4761756997497859. Amines are present elsewhere, and some favorable carbonyl-rich molecules do not need an exposed amine, so simple amine absence or universal amine addition would misread the output.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably combine exposed aliphatic amines with bounded aromatic and linker arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled placement of unacylated aliphatic nitrogens, together with variations in aromatic attachment and spacer length, while retaining other favorable scaffold features. Let current task-local feedback determine when exposed basicity is useful rather than prescribing it for every objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 across 580 optimizer proposals. The cited structures include substituted saturated ring junctions, branched side chains, hydrazones and many polyenes whose SMILES do not specify the relevant configuration or alkene geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Geometrically complex saturated and unsaturated structures are emitted without configuration specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make configurationally defined variants accessible and preserve their identities through generation and canonicalization. Assess them only through the current task observations; the files establish missing specification, not which stereoisomer is preferable or whether a particular score is stereosensitive.

nodes.method_name: Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in Molecule Swarm Optimization: each particle keeps its latent position, velocity and best observed position, and moves through inertia plus independent stochastic attractions toward its personal best and the swarm's best. [Winter et al., Methods 2.2-2.4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6836962/) describe this molecular use of particle swarm optimization. For our adaptation, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder, and start each objective with clean swarm memories. Encodings of supplied molecules provide starting geometry; their scores initialize attractors only when decoding preserves canonical molecular identity. Otherwise establish scored attractors from actual generated evaluations, never from mislabeled reconstructions. Generate fresh latent positions through particle motion and decode new complete molecules. Locally retry stochastic motion for invalid or duplicate outcomes until the announced batch is filled. Match accepted feedback to the exact generating position before updating personal and shared bests; each batch uses only resolved memories. The corpus supplies a generator, never a molecule library for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that persistent individual trajectories explore alternatives while shared successful locations redirect them quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. This uses the provided scalar objective directly, without additional desirability terms. Useful latent geometry and rapid transfer of discoveries between particles remain empirical prerequisites. The published model and evaluation scale do not establish those prerequisites under the permitted preparation and scarce feedback.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecules from score-ranked accepted parents using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It trains a Tanimoto fingerprint Gaussian process on all accepted observations and chooses a batch from each new offspring pool through correlated posterior function draws. Its atom-replacement move picks any source atom, then applies the inherited aromaticity and valence rules to choose a different element. That move can remove a carbonyl from an otherwise promising amide or carbonyl-containing ring.
approach.novelty: Preserve existing carbonyl groups during atom replacement by choosing the replacement site only among atoms outside C=O pairs. The remaining atom and element substitutions use the Parent's rules, allowing local variants around an intact carbonyl framework. This differs from the completed halogen-site experiment and earlier changes to parent memory or partner choice: it changes the support of one substitution operator, with intact C=O retention as the measurable intermediate effect.

nodes.hypothesis: Restrict atom-replacement targets to atoms outside existing carbonyl C=O pairs, preserving both carbonyl atoms and their double bond in that operator.

finding_summary.headline: Carbonyls survived replacement, but scores fell and neighboring functional groups still changed
finding_summary.insights: The intervention closes the intended destructive replacement channel, but that channel is not sufficient to explain useful graph evolution. Existing carbonyl atoms and their double bond can survive while adjacent amide-like or ester-like connections change, and subsequent operators still remove some carbonyls. Indeed, thirty-six protected replacements introduced an acyl-halide connection by changing an unprotected neighboring atom, and five of those paths reached evaluation. The sole all-protected case correctly retried through another operator rather than substituting a protected endpoint. The Parent also had five source-beating carbonyl-loss emissions, so motif removal was not uniformly harmful. The negative score result therefore narrows the useful question to which complete functional relationships deserve preservation, rather than carbonyl retention alone. The supplied chemistry reinforces that limit: useful aryl amine and indole-carbonyl families coexist with strained aromatic bridges, oversized repeated assemblies and reactive halogen or peroxide connections, with no specified stereochemistry. In particular, the large seed-0 DRD2 decline accompanies bulkier hydroperoxide-containing chemistry; the experiment does not isolate one structural cause of that decline. The inherited representation issue also reached one evaluated pure-crossover product, outside the replacement channel. Neither unchosen sites nor unselected pool molecules have counterfactual scores, so the observed subgroups cannot establish that allowing a particular omitted replacement would have improved the endpoint.
finding_summary.results: All 12,104 successful replacements on carbonyl-bearing sources preserved every original C=O pair. The protected substitutions reached 11,191 pool descendants and 718 actual evaluated descendants. Among products made by a single replacement, carbonyl loss fell from 751 of 7,016 Parent pool products and sixty of 589 Parent emissions to zero of 7,100 pool products and zero of 526 emissions. This did not preserve the whole functional group: 93 evaluated descendants contain replacements that changed an original carbonyl’s neighboring atom class, including 41 that lost an adjacent nitrogen. Across the full emitted stream, acyl-halide-bearing molecules increased from seventeen to 272. All fifteen task/seed runs completed with 4,350 valid novel submitted offspring and no evaluator invalid or duplicate attempts. Mean final score fell from 0.544374 to 0.509621, a paired change of -0.034753. The seed changes were -0.089860, -0.027023 and +0.012624. The mean DRD2 change was -0.146641, while median_2 improved by 0.009198.
