molecular.headline: Conventional amide and cyclic-amine families coexist with polyfluorinated amidoximes, polynitro aromatics and incomplete stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All five tasks have complete supplied trajectories for three seeds, with 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. All 4,350 optimizer-proposal SMILES parse with RDKit. The dominant chemistry is ring-rich and recognizable: aryl/heteroaryl amides, pyrazole carboxamides, sulfonamides, cyclic amines, hydrazone or azine connections, and heteroaromatic carbonyl systems. Median proposal heavy-atom counts are 23, 26, 26, 23 and 24 in fixed task order; median ring count is three throughout. Digest aromatic-token rates are 0.9437-0.9920 and ring-closure rates 0.9747-0.9966. The main limitations are therefore not absent rings or aromatic atoms. There are 460-762 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds per task, but leading molecules concentrate in several local chemical families. Most connectivity is synthetically plausible, with specific qualification for repeated nitro substitution, amidoxime/hydrazone geometry, occasional isocyanides and chloroalkyl appendages. In the most nitro-rich session, the digest charged rate of 0.2586 includes nitro and other internally charge-separated groups: 216 proposals contain nitro groups, but only five have nonzero net formal charge. Relative to the parent, familiar carbonyl and cyclic-amine chemistry persists, while different positional arrangements and nitrogen-linker families dominate individual high-score sets. No proposal contains assigned stereocentres; 184, 62, 414, 231 and 308 proposals contain an unassigned centre in task order. These structural observations do not establish synthesis, physical properties, stability or experimental activity.

per_task.generated_character: The two highest molecules are compact alpha-aryl, alpha-pyridyl acetamides with an N-pyridyl amide substituent. They have three aromatic six-membered rings, 23 or 24 heavy atoms and an unassigned central stereocentre. Another family is an N-aryl pyrazole carboxamide, while much of the remaining leading digest consists of azine-linked thiazolidinone-like carbonyl rings carrying two haloaryl regions. Those latter examples contain a C=N-N=C connection whose configuration is not specified. The parent led with substituted indole carboxamides; the current highest family rearranges its aromatic and carbonyl groups around a stereogenic acyclic carbon instead. N-N=C proposals number 101 versus 34 in the parent, consistent with the greater visibility of nitrogen-linked imine chemistry in the current output.
liabilities: C=N-N=C and related imine connections introduce E/Z and tautomeric questions not resolved by the displayed scores.
Several equal-score haloaryl variants increase mass without demonstrating a benefit in the visible gradient.
Four proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and bulky multiply linked structures dominate the very low-score tail despite familiar individual functional groups.
missing_features: The highest acetamides do not specify their stereogenic central carbon, so the useful three-ring/polar arrangement has not been proposed as distinct configurations.

The leading region has limited chemically distinct alternatives beyond acetamide, pyrazole and azine-linked analogue families; repeated halogen substitutions do not address the missing precise placement of polar groups.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methylphenyl/pyridyl acetamide scores 0.454082 and the methoxyphenyl counterpart 0.453163. In the latter framework, replacing the alpha-pyridyl ring with phenyl gives 0.375059 in the terminal digest, supporting the value of that ring-nitrogen placement within this local arrangement. The pyrazole carboxamide reaches 0.436818. Numerous halo-substitution variants of the azine/thiazolidinone family all score 0.413359, so their extra chlorine or fluorine changes do not establish a useful gradient. By contrast, very large peptide-like, polycyclic or extended aromatic assemblies are as low as approximately 2.93e-67, while a simple arylsulfonamide terminal molecule is about 3.66e-08. The useful association is organized moderate-size aromatic/carbonyl chemistry, not either maximal size or an isolated polar group.

per_task.generated_character: The highest structure is a compact hydroxy aza-fused aromatic sulfonamide bearing a difluoroanilino group: 24 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and molecular mass 353.310. Other leaders include polyfluorinated aryl amidines, amidoximes and aminoheteroaryl systems. One high example is an isocyanide-bearing multi-heteroaryl molecule, and another has four nitro groups across an aromatic ether assembly. The whole proposal set has median 26 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and a very low median sp3-carbon fraction of about 0.0833. There are 216 nitro-containing proposals and 102 O-N=C matches, the latter reflecting abundant oxime/amidoxime chemistry. Parent leaders included aromatic acylhydrazones and fluorinated heteroaryl systems; current N-N=C proposals fall from 181 to eight while the displayed imine chemistry shifts toward amidines and amidoximes. These motifs are synthetically recognizable, but repeated nitro and fluorine decoration narrows their apparent medicinal-chemistry quality.
liabilities: Polynitro aromatic systems and the isocyanide example introduce reactivity or stability questions that differ from ordinary amides and sulfonamides; valid graph representations do not resolve them.
The charged-string rate should not be interpreted as a population of ionic molecules: only five proposals have nonzero net formal charge, while 216 contain nitro groups.
Strong aromatic bias and extensive aryl fluorination provide little saturated shape in many leaders, and seven proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
missing_features: The leading output lacks broad stable alternatives that reproduce the useful polar/aromatic arrangement without relying so heavily on dense fluorination, amidoxime variants or repeated nitro substitution.
Amidine and amidoxime C=N configurations are unspecified, and their tautomeric or ionization behavior is not established by the supplied scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact difluoroanilino sulfonamide scores 0.612372, a more heavily fluorinated aryl amidine 0.606725 and an aminoheteroaryl compound 0.606682. These show that maximal fluorination or aromatic expansion is not necessary for the highest displayed score. Within a specific amidoxime pair, a more fluorinated aryl region scores 0.602841 versus 0.571754 for its less fluorinated terminal counterpart, supporting a local substituent effect without a universal fluorine rule. The polynitro aromatic ether scores 0.598691 and the isocyanide-bearing example 0.604700, so these liabilities are tolerated. Low-score benzyl, alkyl or cyclic sulfones lie near 0.262-0.302 despite sulfur, oxygen and aromatic rings; their different attachment context matters.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule joins an amino-oxazole-like aromatic ring to a substituted cyclohexane, an ethyl linker and an arylpiperazine. It has 27 heavy atoms, four rings, two aromatic rings and molecular mass 372.488, with unspecified stereochemistry in the substituted saturated ring. Most other leaders are arylpiperazines or seven-membered diazepanes linked to diarylmethyl or aryl/cyclohexyl regions, often bearing bromine or multiple chlorines. These are recognizable basic-amine medicinal-chemistry families. Parent leaders also had arylpiperazine and fused-amine architectures, including indole-linked examples; the current leading neighborhood emphasizes saturated cyclohexyl and diarylalkyl arms. Full proposals have median 26 heavy atoms and three rings, but their median score is only 0.027500: the near-ceiling structures do not describe the typical score or all of the generated chemistry.
liabilities: Diarylmethyl arms, long linkers and multiple bromine or chlorine substituents raise mass and conformational freedom without demonstrating a general need in the highest structure.
Several leaders approach or exceed molecular mass 500, while the highest displayed molecule is 372.488.
Eleven proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms and the largest has 88, so otherwise familiar amine chemistry can expand into much less economical whole molecules.
missing_features: The output already reaches useful cyclic-amine arrangements, but those arrangements are inadequately represented across a population whose median score remains 0.027500.

Relative configuration on the substituted cyclohexane and configuration at diaryl/aryl-cyclohexyl centres are unspecified; 414 proposals contain an unassigned stereocentre and no proposal assigns one.
No additional required pharmacophoric group can be inferred from the near-ceiling examples; precise alternative arrangements are better supported than prescribed extra substituents.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminoheteroaryl/cyclohexyl piperazine scores 0.999994 and a diarylalkyl diazepane 0.999984. Haloaryl piperazine analogues lie around 0.99, indicating that a basic ring nitrogen positioned between aromatic and saturated hydrophobic regions is productive across several topologies. The top molecule does not require the extensive heavy-halogen decoration of many nearby leaders. Low examples are rich in amide, sulfonamide, nitro or hydrazone functionality, approximately 3.80e-05 to 6.08e-05, with different nitrogen electronics and spatial arrangements. This supports contextual amine presentation rather than nitrogen or ring counts alone. The comparison describes supplied molecular scores and does not establish receptor activity or a universal ring-amine requirement.

per_task.generated_character: Leading molecules include arylsulfonylpiperazines, methylenedioxybenzyl piperazines and fused lactam/indole structures. The highest example is a piperazine bearing an ethoxy/methoxy arylsulfonyl group and a bis-amide side chain, with 33 heavy atoms, three rings and molecular mass 479.530. A much simpler methylphenylsulfonyl N-methylpiperazine has only 17 heavy atoms and two rings. A methylenedioxybenzyl N-methylpiperazine also has 17 heavy atoms. These are plausible conventional chemotypes. The parent already had a simple N-methyl arylsulfonylpiperazine and fused carbonyl alternatives among its leaders, so the principal chemistry is shared while the attachment patterns vary. Full proposals have median 23 heavy atoms and three rings, with 736 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds.
liabilities: Acylated and sulfonylated piperazine nitrogens are electronically different from free tertiary amines; the leading family cannot be summarized as simply adding more basic centres.
Large bis-amide or fused-ring appendages increase synthetic and physical-property burdens while remaining close in score to compact examples.
Five proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and exceptionally long alkyl chains appear at the low end of the observed distribution.
missing_features: The leading repertoire needs more precise alternatives in aromatic/piperazine attachment and polar-linker placement; larger elaborations provide little visible separation from simple structures.
Configuration remains unspecified in chiral fused carbonyl alternatives and in 231 proposals overall, although the simplest piperazines are achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The larger bis-amide/sulfonylpiperazine scores 0.208126, the simple arylsulfonyl N-methylpiperazine 0.207671 and the methylenedioxybenzyl N-methylpiperazine 0.204569. Their close scores show that the added aromatic ring, amides and size of the largest example are not clearly necessary. These structures associate organized aromatic, cyclic-nitrogen and polar-linker regions with the higher visible scores, but not a unique ionization pattern: the highest piperazine has both nitrogens sulfonylated or acylated, unlike the basic N-methyl alternatives. Small polar species or simple cycloalkyl amines score approximately 0.008-0.029, and very long-chain molecules remain near 0.018-0.020. Adding polarity, basic nitrogen or size alone therefore does not reproduce the useful arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is a tert-butyl-substituted nitrogen-rich heteroaromatic carbonyl ring attached to a benzamide with a 2-chloroethyl substituent: 23 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings. Other leaders include a benzimidazole/pyrazole-like heteroaryl system bearing an ethyl methylsulfone side chain, a trimethoxyaryl pyridyl acylhydrazone, compact aminoheteroaromatics and nitroaryl thiosemicarbazone-like structures. These are mostly recognizable synthetic families, with specific concerns for the chloroethyl arm, imine geometry and sulfur/nitrogen-chain chemistry. Parent leaders also included fused nitrogen/carbonyl structures and compact polar amides, but the current digest supplies different combinations and sparse moderate-score examples. Full proposals have median 24 heavy atoms and three rings, with 762 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds. The worst displayed molecules include oversized peptide-like, polyfunctional or heavily chlorinated multiaryl assemblies.
liabilities: The primary chloroethyl arm is a possible electrophilic side-chain liability, while nitroaryl and thiosemicarbazone-like examples introduce separate reactivity or stability questions.
Large peptide-like and heavily elaborated aromatic structures can contain many familiar polar groups while giving exactly zero score; eight proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
Terminal sulfur/disulfide or highly substituted fused structures add chemistry whose practical stability and physical properties are not established by the trajectories.
missing_features: More precise and broader coverage of compact polar heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangements is missing even though several viable-looking families are already produced.
Stable alternatives to the chloroethyl and thiosemicarbazone-like features are not demonstrated as matched high-score analogues; the visible data do not establish those liabilities as required.
Hydrazone C=N geometry is unspecified, and no proposal assigns stereocentres despite 308 containing an unassigned centre; many of the displayed leaders themselves are achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The benzamide/heteroaromatic-carbonyl molecule scores 0.268815, the sulfone-substituted heteroaryl molecule 0.233604 and the trimethoxyaryl acylhydrazone 0.229727. Compact aminoheteroaromatic and sulfur-containing alternatives reach roughly 0.18-0.23. Those examples suggest a preference for particular compact polar arrangements without establishing any one mandatory group; the highest chloroethyl substituent is not shown in a matched pair proving its necessity. The large peptide-like and multiaryl molecules are zero or vanishing. The digest median is rounded to 0.0: the full 900-row median is 1.766839397052908e-07 and seven rows are exactly zero. Thus the higher-score chemistry occupies a sparse part of a predominantly very-low-score population, not a population of literal zeros.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A methoxyphenyl/pyridyl acetamide scores 0.453163 while its displayed phenyl-for-pyridyl counterpart scores 0.375059. In another set, conventional cyclic-amine leaders reach near-ceiling scores while typical output has a median of 0.027500 and low examples place nitrogen in amides, sulfonamides or hydrazones. A further leading set includes both a piperazine with acylated/sulfonylated nitrogens and basic N-methylpiperazines at nearly equal scores, showing that useful nitrogen chemistry depends on the surrounding arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently reproduce the precise placement and electronic context of useful polar groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support meaningful alternatives in ring-nitrogen position, amide orientation and linker attachment while preserving the useful structural relationships suggested by feedback. Treat free amines, amide nitrogens, sulfonamide nitrogens, amidines and hydrazones as distinct chemical environments rather than interchangeable nitrogen content.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Per-session nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts range from 460 to 762, yet digest leaders repeat acetamide, azine/thiazolidinone, fluorinated amidoxime or cyclic-amine families. Several haloaryl azine variants have the same score of 0.413359. One structurally diverse session has 762 scaffolds but a full-trajectory median score near 1.77e-07. Meanwhile, 33- and 17-heavy-atom piperazine structures in another session score 0.208126 and 0.207671, illustrating that added size is not necessarily useful coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad scaffold counts do not provide sufficiently broad coverage of productive, economical chemical families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically distinct core and linker alternatives that preserve an observed useful arrangement, alongside controlled local variation. Measure chemical breadth through access to productive families and alternatives, rather than more unique graphs, repetitive halogen changes or larger appendages alone.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No assigned stereocentres occur in 4,350 optimizer proposals. The five sessions contain 184, 62, 414, 231 and 308 proposals with unassigned centres. Higher-score examples include alpha-aryl/heteroaryl acetamides, substituted cyclohexyl cyclic amines, diarylalkyl centres and fused lactams. Amidoxime, hydrazone and azine leaders also omit explicit C=N configuration; one session contains 102 O-N=C matches.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereogenic centres and configurationally variable nitrogen double bonds unspecified.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable chemically consistent, explicitly configured alternatives when a proposed structure has stereocentres or relevant imine geometry, while retaining achiral chemistry. The supplied observations do not identify a preferred unobserved stereoisomer or tautomer, so those possibilities must remain empirically distinguishable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One session contains 216 nitro-bearing proposals and displays a four-nitro aromatic ether at 0.598691, while its highest structure is a smaller difluoroanilino sulfonamide at 0.612372. An isocyanide and dense fluorinated amidoximes also appear among leaders. Elsewhere, the highest compact benzamide carries a primary chloroethyl arm without a matched example proving that arm necessary. Across sessions, four, seven, eleven, five and eight proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and long-chain or peptide-like structures recur among very low or zero scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator needs stable and less burdensome alternatives to repeated reactive-group decoration and excessive molecular growth.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Retain access to conventional stable linkers and substituents that realize useful polar arrangements with controlled mass and appendage size. Distinguish potentially reactive nitro-rich, isocyanide, imine-chain and haloalkyl motifs from ordinary aromatic substitution, and avoid treating tolerated chemical burden as evidence that more of it is required.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: CMA-ES samples candidate points from a multivariate Gaussian, ranks the ones that come back, and moves the distribution itself rather than any individual point. The mean shifts toward a weighted average of the better samples, the covariance matrix adapts so the Gaussian stretches along directions that have been paying off, and a separate cumulative path controls the overall step size. Applied to molecules, the sampled points are latent vectors and each one is turned into a molecule by a frozen autoencoder decoder before scoring.
approach.novelty: This root commits to a 24-dimensional latent with full covariance adaptation rather than a diagonal approximation, so the Gaussian can learn correlated directions in the latent space. It attaches every observed score to the exact latent sample that generated the molecule, uses descending score rank with logarithmic recombination weights, and carries cumulative evolution paths for both covariance and step size across all fourteen generations of an objective.

nodes.hypothesis: Sample de novo molecules through a frozen deterministic SELFIES VAE decoder from an adaptive multivariate Gaussian, attach observed scores to the exact generating latent samples, and update the Gaussian mean, full covariance, and global step size using descending score ranks, weighted recombination, and cumulative evolution paths.

finding_summary.headline: Full covariance adaptation ran exactly and finished eleventh at 0.303, undone by one objective
finding_summary.insights: The optimizer is correct and its budget is the problem. Fourteen generations of twenty scored offspring is a very short run for an algorithm that spends its early generations learning a covariance, so the distribution barely finishes adapting before the budget ends. Its collapse on drd2_docking is informative in a different way: that objective rewards a compact basic amine, and this node's proposals there average eighty characters, nearly double every other objective on the same node. The Gaussian drifted into a region of latent space that decodes to large lipophilic molecules and covariance adaptation then reinforced that direction. A smaller population with more generations is the obvious change. One seed only.
finding_summary.results: The macro mean of 0.303 places this eleventh of thirteen. The result is bimodal: 0.611 on deco_hop, which is the third best in the round, and 0.443 on zaleplon_mpo, against 0.064 on drd2_docking, which is the second worst any root recorded there. median_2 reached 0.208 and sitagliptin_mpo 0.187. Every mechanism check was exact. All 70 generations used full 24 by 24 covariance matrices with reconstructed rank-one and rank-mu terms, the recomputed learning constants matched, the cumulative path and step-size control were independently reproduced through eigendecomposition of each covariance, and every one of the accepted offspring joined its exact generating latent and score.

molecular.headline: Latent drift into large lipophilic molecules, with aromatic content collapsing on the objectives it loses
molecular.overall_character: The population varies more by objective than any other root, which is what covariance adaptation in a latent space would be expected to produce. Where it does well, aromatic content reaches 86 to 95 percent with molecules around forty to fifty-nine characters. Where it fails, aromatic content drops to 36 and 49 percent and molecules balloon to eighty characters of fluorinated ethers and alkyl chains. Ring closure stays high throughout at 87 to 99 percent, so the decoder is producing closed structures; what changes is whether those rings are aromatic and whether the molecule stays a reasonable size.

nodes.method_name: CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the optimizer in CMA-ES: sample a multivariate Gaussian, rank evaluated samples, move its mean by weighted recombination, and adapt covariance and step size using selected displacements and cumulative evolution paths. [Hansen, Sections 1-4](https://arxiv.org/html/1604.00772v2) describes this mechanism. For the molecular transfer, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus and freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder. Each objective starts with fresh Gaussian and path state. Encodings of high-scoring supplied molecules may initialize geometric search locations, but their scores must not be assigned to nonidentical reconstructions. Generate latent samples, decode them into new molecules, and attach accepted oracle feedback to the exact latent sample that produced each submitted structure. Assemble scored generations while respecting the evaluator-announced batching, then update the Gaussian from descending observed-score ranks. Reject invalid or duplicate structures locally and continue de novo decoding. The corpus trains a generator and never supplies a ranked molecular library. The hypothesis is that learning correlated latent displacements directly from successful generations can uncover improving combinations without first estimating an objective surrogate, increasing the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Useful decoder support and covariance adaptation within scarce feedback are empirical prerequisites; continuous-domain performance is not evidence that decoded molecular landscapes will behave similarly.

approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates a learned molecule sampler with ordinary graph breeding. An autoregressive SMILES model is first trained on unlabeled molecules and kept as a frozen prior. Each objective gets an adaptable copy that generates one batch, followed by two batches made through graph crossover and atom or bond edits. Accepted neural samples refresh a scored population of up to sixty-four molecules, and a fresh neural sample is forced to participate in breeding at each handoff. Accepted graph descendants then train the adaptable sampler through score-ranked replay, trajectory balance with a learned normalizer, and regularization toward the frozen prior. This reciprocal loop ran repeatedly, but each valid novel graph descendant was sent directly for evaluation, and most scored below its best generating parent.
approach.novelty: Add posterior-sampling selection to the genetic phase. A Gaussian process learned from this objective's accepted scores uses molecular fingerprints to draw plausible score functions over a fresh pool of offspring from the existing graph operators. Each available evaluation slot takes the best remaining offspring under a new sampled function. The first forced neural-parent offspring at each handoff stays as in the Parent, so the reciprocal exchange remains intact. This lineage has only tested direct submission so far; the new ingredient is selection among genetic offspring before they receive real scores. A related graph-only experiment improved final best scores without improving its parent-beating rate, so the hypothesis here concerns discovering useful upper-tail outcomes within the reciprocal loop, with descendant efficiency measured separately.

nodes.hypothesis: Use a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process to choose genetic-phase evaluations by posterior-function maximization over fresh graph offspring pools, retaining the Parent's mandatory first fresh-policy offspring at each graph-cycle handoff.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection and reciprocal feedback reproduce across seeds; offspring efficiency remains weak
finding_summary.insights: Replication rules out missing selector execution or a broken reciprocal handoff as explanations for the weak offspring yield: both mechanisms remain active across all three seeds. It also weakens the original suggestion of improved average child-minus-parent score, which held on the screening seed but not on the two additional seeds. The selector consistently changes which offspring are evaluated, but this does not establish that uncertainty itself improves final scores. The original direct-submission Parent has only one available seed, so the earlier paired score gain of 0.005848 remains a single-seed comparison; the new results establish repeatable execution and describe score variability without establishing a paired multi-seed improvement. Prediction error in the new runs is lower than an archive-mean baseline on four of five objectives, yet nominal 95% latent intervals cover only 80.4% of selected accepted scores overall and 41.9% on sitagliptin_mpo, where prediction MSE is also worse than that baseline. These are informative but uncalibrated predictions on the selected molecules. The molecular assessment shows that ring systems and useful basic-amine chemistry are already available, while leading families still mix conventional scaffolds with reactive substitutions, complicated connectivity and unspecified stereochemistry. That narrows the remaining questions toward reliable discrimination among chemically credible alternatives and broader useful scaffold coverage. Matched Parent replicas and a same-pool mean-only or direct-order comparison are still needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency and uncertainty's contribution.
finding_summary.results: Both additional seeds reproduced the intended selection and feedback behavior. Every one of their 1,800 selected offspring maximized its reconstructed correlated posterior draw, and uncertainty changed 1,671 choices (92.8%) relative to choosing the highest posterior mean. All 190 fits used earlier accepted scores only, all 1,710 eligible fixed-molecule predictions changed after feedback, and all 100 protected neural-to-graph handoffs were preserved. There were 90 later reciprocal cycles and 4,480 nonzero graph-bearing policy updates. The two new mean final-best scores were 0.528301 and 0.517608, compared with 0.516098 in the original run of the same algorithm. Across all three seeds, mean final-best score is 0.520669 with a population standard deviation of 0.005432. The three-seed objective means are 0.458300 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.615427 for deco_hop, 0.999997 for drd2_docking, 0.204624 for median_2 and 0.324997 for sitagliptin_mpo. Only 246 of 1,900 graph descendants in the new runs beat their best generating parent (12.95%), and their mean child-minus-parent score was -0.110567. Across all three runs those quantities are 386 of 2,850 (13.54%) and -0.099708. These are below the original direct-submission Parent's single-seed parent-beating rate of 18.21%; that historical comparison is not a paired three-seed efficiency estimate.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and cyclic-amine chemistry, with useful scaffolds mixed with reactive substitutions and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The supplied seed-1 and seed-2 trajectories each cover every listed objective. Each task digest contains 600 evaluated molecules, including 580 optimizer proposals. These are predominantly connected, branched, ring-bearing organic structures: the taskwise ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.9793 to 0.9948 and aromatic_atom_rate from 0.9362 to 0.9828. Those are SMILES-text presence rates, not fractions of atoms or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths range from 46.0 to 69.7. The repertoire includes biaryl pyrazoles, indole carboxamides, quinoline ureas, azoles and acylhydrazones, aryl-substituted saturated amines, carbonyl-rich fused heterocycles, and triazolyl azetidines. Ring chemistry and basic amine centres are demonstrably available. The individual high-score families are more concentrated than the variety of the complete proposal sets. Conventional medicinal-chemistry building blocks coexist with oxygen- and nitrogen-halogen bonds, hydrazine/nitroso functionality, unusual short ring closures, and oversized concatenated structures. Consequently, synthetic plausibility is questionable overall and drug-likeness is mixed rather than uniformly poor. No proposed set contains explicit stereocentre annotations: every digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0, even though several depicted saturated cores can have configurational alternatives. The charge-marker rate must not be read as a basic-amine rate; neutral amine SMILES can describe protonatable centres, and nitro groups also produce charge markers. For this replication ticket, the supplied parent_trajectories and focus.parent identify seed 0 of n-cc2d839e347b itself. Comparisons below describe that prior run, not an intervention between different algorithms. Apparent score preferences are associations in the supplied molecular observations; absent chemistry is not evidence that an unobserved replacement would improve the score.

per_task.generated_character: Most proposals are aromatic, moderately sized molecules carrying amides, ureas, methoxy or hydroxy groups and frequent halogen substituents. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9793, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9569 and halogen_rate 0.7966. The seed-1 leader is an N-methyl acetanilide bearing a biaryl-linked pyrazole and a phenol. Seed 2 instead favours methoxyquinoline linked through a urea to isoindoline. Earlier proposals include substituted indole carboxamides related to the initial molecule scoring 0.3051048083696145. These recognizable cores are plausibly accessible, although many neighbouring substitutions are less convincing. Low-scoring material includes tiny fluorinated heteroatom fragments and large, heavily decorated polyaryl structures. Compared with the prior seed-0 high tail of modified indole carboxamides, including unusual amide-nitrogen and cumulated-side-chain chemistry at 0.4219568943587627, the new runs supply more conventional alternative leading cores.
liabilities: The high tail includes an aryl hypochlorite and an aryl sulfur-chlorine group, which introduce reactive bonds despite favourable recorded scores.
A chloromethyl substituent occurs in a leading indole derivative. Large conjugated or multiply decorated late products add synthetic complexity without preserving the favourable score range.
The leading aromatic series carries substantial aromatic surface and limited saturated shape variation; this is a structural description, not a measured solubility or exposure result.
missing_features: Broader stable variants preserving the useful phenol, amide and heteroaryl arrangement are poorly represented relative to peripheral halogen and heteroatom substitutions in the leading families.

Controlled changes of core and linker geometry that retain the compact high-score arrangement remain incompletely explored. The observations establish distinct useful core families, but do not identify a uniquely required missing scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenolic biaryl-pyrazole acetanilide scores 0.5256780516063334; its otherwise corresponding unsubstituted aryl analogue scores 0.4865761385111112. The oxygen-chlorinated analogue scores 0.49263201457052164, so the observed best local substitution is an ordinary hydroxyl group. The related sulfur-chlorine structure scores 0.4686060677105447. Seed 2 reaches 0.427264458706691 with the fluoroquinoline urea, and its final hydroxyquinoline urea scores 0.4219568943587627. At the other extreme, the tiny nitrogen-fluorine fragment scores 0.0, while the large methoxy-rich sulfonamide/polyamine conjugate scores 6.660632986075464e-46. The visible preference is for a coherent aromatic core with a limited polar-group arrangement and controlled size; neither halogen addition nor continued growth is uniformly rewarded.

per_task.generated_character: The high-score molecules are conjugated, nitrogen-rich heteroaromatics rather than small aliphatic structures. Seed 2 produces a quinoline-oxadiazole assembly joined by a formamidine-like linkage to a multiply fluorinated aromatic ring; seed 1 produces substituted quinoline acylhydrazones terminating in nitro-containing diazines. Other upper examples contain fused nitrogen/oxygen heterocycles. The digest records aromatic_atom_rate 0.9828, ring_closure_rate 0.9897, mean_smiles_length 69.7 and max_smiles_length 173, consistent with extensive ring chemistry and a sizeable elaborated tail. Its charged_rate 0.3121 includes charge-separated functional groups such as nitro, and does not demonstrate a population of protonated amines. Individual azoles, aryl amides and hydrazones are recognizable synthetic motifs, but extended nitrogen linkages and reactive substitutions make the ensemble questionable. The prior seed-0 leader instead used a conjugated oxygen heterocycle with oxygen- and sulfur-containing heteroaryl appendages and scored 0.6295439524124257.
liabilities: Acylhydrazones and formamidine-like connections introduce tautomeric or configurational alternatives without corresponding geometric specification in the cited structures.
An oxygen-fluorine bond appears in both a leading quinoline derivative and a late enlarged analogue. This is different chemistry from ordinary carbon-bound fluorine.

Nitro-containing heteroaromatics, densely conjugated nitrogen-rich assemblies, and further concatenation warrant chemical-stability and synthetic scrutiny; the recorded score does not establish either property.
missing_features: Stable, geometrically specified alternatives to the imine, hydrazone and extended nitrogen linkages are not established among the supplied leaders. Short polar linkage geometry appears useful, but these observations do not identify a required replacement chemistry.

The high tail has limited evidence for useful saturated shape variation. The equal score of the aromatic and ring-expanded leading pair prevents claiming that additional aromaticity itself is a missing requirement.

The more ordinarily makeable aryl sulfone-linked amide scores 0.26999666722212967, and the sulfonylhydrazone scores 0.2969569015725102; synthetic familiarity alone therefore does not explain this gradient. A long nitrogen-rich conjugate scores 0.3298125254720826. Late extended analogues reach 0.597892888498683 and 0.5811424248155854, below the leading compact connected heteroaryl arrangements. per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules combine halogenated aromatic surfaces with saturated nitrogen rings and accessible aliphatic amines. Seed 2 favours arylpiperidines connected through aminoalkyl chains to another aromatic group or to a benzodioxane-like ring system. Seed 1 includes a diaryl ether bearing linked piperidine and pyrrolidine rings. These are medium-sized, recognizable medicinal-chemistry architectures, although some variants acquire imines or unusual bridged ring closures. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9948, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9793 and halogen_rate 0.7897. Its low charged_rate of 0.0121 does not mean basic centres are scarce: the neutral SMILES explicitly contain secondary and tertiary amines. The prior seed-0 leader was a more compact fused aza-polycyclic structure with an N-propyl substituent and an aryl fluoride, scoring 0.9999968262975905. The new high tail is often more extended while retaining the same broad amine-plus-aromatic character.

Some high-scoring variants contain extra short closures across an aromatic ring or unusually bridged oxygen-containing ring systems; a chemically valid graph does not establish an accessible, unstrained structure.
Late sulfur-nitrogen substitutions and imine additions can alter the electronic character of otherwise useful amines. Relevant saturated centres are not stereochemically specified.

Systematically controlled linker geometry and configurationally specified saturated-ring variants are not demonstrated. Their absence limits the chemical interpretation of shape changes, but the trajectories do not establish that adding them would raise this score.

per_task.generated_character: The upper tail consists largely of bulky, densely functionalized ring systems: substituted aromatic groups carry piperazine units alongside fused or rearranged nitrogen heterocycles with carbonyl and ether functionality. Seed 1 often sulfonylates a piperazine nitrogen and adds cyclopropyl or cyclopropenyl groups; seed 2 includes N-methylpiperazine-containing relatives of the initial diaryl fused dicarbonyl heterocycle. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9828, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9552, mean_smiles_length 64.1 and max_smiles_length 163. transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited high tails contain an aryl hypochlorite scoring 0.49263201457052164, an aryl sulfur-chlorine derivative scoring 0.4686060677105447, and an N-fluorohydrazino azetidine scoring 0.3532645847815139. Other cited examples include oxygen-fluorine bonds and nitroso-bearing nitrogen chains. Conventional phenol, amide and primary amine alternatives also occur. These examples show that reactive connectivity survives even among favourable accepted observations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve chemically credible functional-group connectivity when modifying useful molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable functional-group replacements available while retaining the surrounding aryl, amine and carbonyl relationships. Distinguish carbon-bound halogen changes from halogenating oxygen, nitrogen or sulfur, and compare chemically coherent alternatives through the current session's accepted feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited low tails include methane and hydrazine at 0.0, tiny fluorinated heteroatom fragments at 0.0, and oversized polyaryl or polyfunctional conjugates with extremely small scores. Conversely, some relatively large piperazine/carbonyl structures occupy a high tail, while a simpler ethylsulfonylpiperazine/aza-lactam structure scores 0.19835388147218586 near more elaborate relatives. The evidence supports context-dependent size and connectivity requirements.
transferable_gaps.gap: Control of molecular size and connectivity is uneven: useful cores are sometimes fragmented away or expanded into overly elaborate assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide growth, contraction and linker changes that preserve a coherent molecular core and useful local functional-group relationships. Explore size around accepted structures without relying on either repeated fragmentation or concatenation, and let feedback determine useful complexity for the current session.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Cited triazolyl azetidines, bridged nitrogen/oxygen cores, substituted saturated amine rings and carbonyl-rich ring junctions can have configurational alternatives. Some leading structures also contain unusually short closures across aromatic frameworks or contracted ring systems. Abundant ring-closure markers therefore establish ring presence, not well-defined or accessible geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks explicit stereochemical specification and provides inconsistent geometric control over new ring closures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit configurational alternatives and chemically credible ring closure, expansion and contraction moves around useful molecular arrangements. Treat changes of saturation, junction geometry and linker shape as distinct chemical possibilities for feedback to assess. The present observations establish missing representation, not a demonstrated score benefit from any particular configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied leaders repeatedly revisit related biaryl-pyrazole or quinoline-urea cores, imine/acylhydrazone-linked heteroaromatics, aryl saturated-amine architectures, piperazine-bearing carbonyl polycycles, and N-acyl azetidines. Different seeds reach visibly different core families, showing that the generator can change scaffold, but much of each leading neighbourhood consists of decoration, local ring edits or further assembly of those families.
transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of chemically distinct useful cores remains uneven within runs, despite abundant unique molecular identities and an overall varied repertoire.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to multiple accepted scaffold families and enable core replacements that preserve useful spatial relationships among donors, acceptors, amines and aromatic groups. Assess diversity in the chemistry of the cores and their functional-group arrangement rather than treating a new molecular string or peripheral substituent as sufficient coverage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Accessible saturated amines in aryl/linker arrangements accompany scores such as 0.9999986918258995, while a nitro-containing aromatic molecule that also has a primary amine scores 8.914135292267243e-05. In another local family, the N-fluorohydrazino azetidine scores 0.3532645847815139, but a structure carrying that type of substituent on the triazole while retaining an aminomethyl group scores 0.0009072140941170833. These are whole-molecule observations, but they directly contradict a simple more-nitrogen or more-fluorine interpretation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group placement is not reliably conserved when exploring favourable amine and heteroaryl chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and vary functional-group attachment context, spacing and electronic environment deliberately. Make changes to a free amine, an amide nitrogen, a ring nitrogen and an imine distinct chemical operations so accepted feedback can reveal useful local arrangements without repeatedly losing them during unrelated growth.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent prior from the supplied unlabeled SMILES, always conditioning each next-token prediction on the intact preceding tokens. Its fixed holdout chooses the prior checkpoint. Each objective then starts with a fresh policy and a frozen reference prior. The best current observations train together with a uniform sample from a memory of the thirty-two strongest earlier accepted elites, preserving their original strings and accepted rewards. Bounded prior-likelihood-plus-reward updates adapt the policy, which samples complete new molecules with chemical and duplicate checks. The prior has not been trained to recover after a small amount of context information is missing.
approach.novelty: During each unlabeled training sequence, hide exactly one randomly selected content-token embedding and still predict the original unmodified targets with the existing equal-token loss. The rest of the sequence remains visible. This asks the recurrent state to use surrounding context instead of depending entirely on one local input. Clean strings and the original clean holdout still determine checkpoint selection, and online learning and generation use ordinary intact inputs. Earlier siblings changed bracket units, equivalent string views or branch loss allocation; this Child tests robustness to one missing internal context vector without changing those mechanisms. A successful robustness result still has to translate into useful valid new molecules.

nodes.hypothesis: Train the unlabeled recurrent prior to predict the unchanged original SMILES targets after zeroing exactly one uniformly selected eligible content-token input embedding per sequence, while keeping the Parent uniform token loss, clean fixed-holdout checkpoint selection and all online computations unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Missing-context prediction improved sharply, but validity and final molecular scores declined
finding_summary.insights: The missing-vector probe measures a capability the prior successfully learned; the absolute erased-context loss improvement is much larger than the small clean-context loss degradation. Its failure to improve raw molecular validity separates this capability from tolerance of the mistakes that matter during ordinary generation. The probe leaves all later teacher-forced tokens correct and never measures recovery from an incorrectly sampled token or molecular graph. It therefore supplies no evidence that the main online error source has been addressed. Lower duplicate concentration broadened the sampled output slightly, but did not preserve the chemical arrangements needed for the strongest objectives. The molecular assessment found mostly conventional medicinal chemistry, together with extreme polar and lipophilic tails; for sitagliptin, the stronger parental polar-ring/carbonyl families were not recovered. This connects the score loss to a change in chemical coverage without identifying a single causal functional group. The evidence supports missing-context robustness as a retained capability, with a clean-language-modeling tradeoff and no demonstrated optimization gain under the tested panel.
finding_summary.results: The preparation mechanism executed on all three seeds: one eligible content embedding was erased in each of 7,613,952 training-sequence exposures per prior, with the original target strings preserved. Independent replay exactly reproduced all three training-target and erasure-mask receipts. On the entire fixed 4,096-row holdout for each seed, mean erased-downstream negative log likelihood fell from the Parent's 1.00417 to 0.53006; every seed improved. The corresponding erasure penalty fell from 0.53933 to 0.05658. This was a real improvement in prediction with missing context, although clean full-sequence NLL worsened from 0.56458 to 0.57213. Clean likelihood still selected checkpoints, and online computation used intact inputs with a frozen prior. Downstream generation did not gain validity: raw RDKit-valid draws fell from 90.43% to 89.27%. Duplicate draws fell from 30.11% to 27.51%, so the raw canonical-novel fraction rose from 60.31% to 61.76%; all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and unique. The final three-seed macro mean fell from 0.50755 to 0.49844, a paired change of -0.00911. Seed changes were -0.01795, +0.00012 and -0.00950. The preparation mechanism executed on all three seeds: one eligible content embedding was erased in each of 7,613,952 training-sequence exposures per prior, with the original target strings preserved. Independent replay exactly reproduced all three training-target and erasure-mask receipts. On the entire fixed 4,096-row holdout for each seed, mean erased-downstream negative log likelihood fell from the Parent's 1.00417 to 0.53006; every seed improved. The corresponding erasure penalty fell from 0.53933 to 0.05658. This was a real improvement in prediction with missing context, although clean full-sequence NLL worsened from 0.56458 to 0.57213. Clean likelihood still selected checkpoints, and online computation used intact inputs with a frozen prior. Downstream generation did not gain validity: raw RDKit-valid draws fell from 90.43% to 89.27%. Duplicate draws fell from 30.11% to 27.51%, so the raw canonical-novel fraction rose from 60.31% to 61.76%; all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and unique. The final three-seed macro mean fell from 0.50755 to 0.49844, a paired change of -0.00911. Seed changes were -0.01795, +0.00012 and -0.00950. Mean zaleplon score rose by 0.03533, while sitagliptin fell by 0.08046 and lost score in every seed. The intended +0.002 macro improvement was not achieved.

The missing-vector probe measures a capability the prior successfully learned; the absolute erased-context loss improvement is much larger than the small clean-context loss degradation. Its failure to improve raw molecular validity separates this capability from tolerance of the mistakes that matter during ordinary generation. The probe leaves all later teacher-forced tokens correct and never measures recovery from an incorrectly sampled token or molecular graph. It therefore supplies no evidence that the main online error source has been addressed. Lower duplicate concentration broadened the sampled output slightly, but did not preserve the chemical arrangements needed for the strongest objectives. The molecular assessment found mostly conventional medicinal chemistry, together with extreme polar and lipophilic tails; for sitagliptin, the stronger parental polar-ring/carbonyl families were not recovered. This connects the score loss to a change in chemical coverage without identifying a single causal functional group. The evidence supports missing-context robustness as a retained capability, with a clean-language-modeling tradeoff and no demonstrated optimization gain under the tested panel.

molecular.headline: Mostly conventional aromatic amides, amines and sulfonamides, with extreme polar or lipophilic tails and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and parent trajectories were read. Each current task contains 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is broadly diverse and mainly resembles ordinary medicinal chemistry: aryl amides and ureas, heteroaromatic amino compounds, indanol/tetralin-like alcohols, piperazines, sulfonamides, cyclic carbonyl compounds and ether-linked heterocycles. Most leading structures have plausible synthetic entry points and conventional bonding. Ring-closure rates range from 0.9793 to 0.9977 and aromatic-token rates from 0.946 to 0.992. Mean SMILES lengths range from 40.4 to 50.5, while the low tails include much larger peptides, polyamines, sugars, macrocycles and long hydrocarbon chains. Charged-token rates range from 0.0368 to 0.1299 and include ordinary nitro, azide and ammonium representations as well as occasional unusual electronic states; these rates are not a measure of solution ionization. All stereocentre-token rates are 0.0, as in the parent strings, leaving substituted saturated-ring alcohols and other stereogenic products undefined. The chemistry is generally plausible and moderately drug-like, but chemical plausibility alone does not explain the score variation, and individual reactive or geometrically difficult alternatives remain.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are moderate-sized aromatic amides or diaryl ureas, with methoxy phenyl or pyridyl groups, another aryl ring and a pyridyl or pyrimidyl carbonyl partner. Connections vary between methylene, direct biaryl and diarylamino arrangements. The molecules have recognizable amide/urea donors and acceptors, mostly ordinary aromatic substitution and little stereochemical complexity. They are generally synthetically plausible. The lowest examples are substantially larger peptide-like structures, highly hydroxylated or phosphorylated compounds, a long-ring polyamine and a very small cyanide species. Final molecules range from appropriate aromatic amides to much simpler hydrocarbons or heteroarenes that lose the polar-linker arrangement.
liabilities: Multiple aromatic rings with flexible methylene or amino links can increase conformational freedom even when the individual bonds are ordinary.
Peptide-like and highly hydroxylated proposals introduce substantial size or polarity outside the leading families.
Small charged fragments and isolated unusual electronic-state variants occur in the wider trajectories despite the conventional leading chemistry.
missing_features: Low peptide-like, polyol and macrocyclic products lack the compact aromatic and carbonyl-linker organization of the leading molecules.
The simpler low final heteroarenes lack the amide/urea arrangement retained by the stronger examples; aromatic content alone is insufficient.

The current displayed leaders do not cover the substituted indole-carboxamide arrangement of the stronger parent seed-0 molecule. That is a coverage difference rather than proof that an indole is universally required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Several different methoxy diarylmethyl heteroaryl amides and a methoxypyridyl/diaryl urea all score 0.48839749189747395. Related diarylamino and alternative pyridyl amides score 0.4767312946227961. These ties support a relatively compact aromatic/polar-linker balance without identifying one uniquely required ring nitrogen position or linkage. An aromatic tertiary amide in the final set scores 0.4155143263564241, whereas a naphthalene-pyridine without the amide arrangement scores 0.0019315588620192265. The large peptide-like low example scores 1.2479689558218067e-56. Parent seed 0 reached 0.5280588545286916 with a substituted indole carboxamide, while current seed 0 reaches 0.48839749189747395 with diarylmethyl amides. Current seed 1 and seed 2 reach 0.48839749189747395 and 0.4540824430539665 versus parental 0.4067656765249372 and 0.3900700429110833. The new leading chemistry is conventional, but the comparisons do not isolate a single missing pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecules are aromatic nitrogen heterocycles bearing arylamino groups, alkoxy substitution, nitrile or trifluoromethyl groups and, in the leader, a nitroanilide carboxamide. Other strong families include amino-linked fused diones, ordinary aryl sulfonamides and acylhydrazones. These are generally moderate to bulky, planar or partly planar medicinal-chemistry structures with recognizable synthetic connections. The low examples include a large ester/amide/methylsulfone assembly, an indole ether-acetamide/benzothiazole combination and a sulfone-substituted indole. Small acyclic or fluorocarbon fragments sit close to the low baseline. The output has abundant aromatic and heteroatom content but its placement matters.
liabilities: Several leading compounds carry extensive aromatic and fluorinated substitution with little saturated shape diversity.
Nitroaryl, acylhydrazone and thioether variants have distinct chemical liabilities that are not resolved by their similar scores.
A low charged nitrogen/oxygen fragment has an unusual electronic-state representation, so charge tokens should not be interpreted as uniformly ordinary ionization chemistry.
missing_features: The small low-baseline fragments lack the connected aromatic and polar-linker organization of the stronger products.

The low but synthetically plausible multiaryl structures show that merely including heterocycles, an amide or oxidized sulfur does not preserve the useful arrangement. Matched attachment-position and ring-nitrogen variants remain incompletely explored in the displayed leaders.
Less aromatic, more saturated shape variants retaining the useful polar fragments are limited among the strongest examples; their potential score benefit is not established by this set.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The nitroanilide/aza-aromatic leader scores 0.6111751890298603. Replacing that carboxanilide appendage by methoxy in the same broader scaffold family gives 0.6076219961668878; a nitrile relative scores 0.6056754360035471. Amino-linked diones with ethylthio, methoxy or propargyloxy substitution all score 0.6014089846464902, so those peripheral groups are not uniquely distinguished. An aryl sulfonamide reaches 0.5999223218699244, whereas a differently arranged sulfone-indole scores 0.31752369822101023 and an indole/benzothiazole amide scores 0.3004981574996588. This is evidence for particular heteroaromatic/linker arrangements, not a general sulfur penalty or reward. Current per-seed maxima are 0.6111751890298603, 0.5908091850309445 and 0.5784746092483299, compared with parental 0.5913471190523991, 0.61192894944948 and 0.5758665324320438. per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are conventional aryl- or pyridyl-piperazines connected through ether/alkyl or aminoalkyl chains to indanol- or tetralin-like frameworks. Alcohol, methoxy, amino and aryl halogen substituents vary around the fused ring. The products combine available aliphatic amines with aromatic surface and a polar alcohol or ether. Seed 2 also produces flexible biaryl compounds with an expanded diaza ring and a nitrile-bearing phenoxyethyl connection. These are recognizable synthetic families. Low examples are amide, ester, sulfonamide or hydrazone-dominated compounds lacking the same organized aliphatic-amine framework, although one low structure does contain a primary amine.
liabilities: Flexible alkyl chains and several potentially basic centres introduce conformational and ionization ambiguity.
Unspecified alcohol and substituted-ring stereochemistry prevents the leading structures from describing single defined stereoisomers.
Other seeds include an organic azide among stronger products, so the conventional main piperazine family does not imply uniform stability across the full output.
missing_features: The low amide/sulfonamide series lacks the accessible aliphatic amine placement and hydrophobic-ring spacing of the stronger piperazine families.
The low primary-amine-containing urea shows that a basic centre without the useful overall arrangement is insufficient; matched linker geometry and ring-size comparisons are still needed.
The leading alcohol-bearing fused rings have potential stereogenic centres but no specified configurations. No stereochemical preference can be read from the supplied unlabelled molecules.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluoroindanol/propoxy/pyridylpiperazine molecule scores 0.999998460810131; its nonfluorinated indanol relative scores 0.9999948760798478. Several aminoalkyl/tetralin-like alternatives also approach 1.0, and matched aryl fluorine/chlorine substitutions have identical recorded values of 0.9999949345268564 or 0.9999929302907594. These nearly equal values support the general aryl/aliphatic-amine arrangement but do not establish a unique halogen or fused-ring size requirement. The lowest amide-rich example scores 3.243749221679736e-05, while a primary-amine-containing but differently connected urea scores 6.812931663695377e-05; amine presence alone is not enough. Parent seed 1 already had an indole/alkyl/arylpiperazine leader at 0.9999999999666845. per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules include an N-methylpiperazine sulfonamide attached to a fused benzoxazolinone-like cyclic carbamate, and a benzodioxole-sulfonyl piperazine bearing a benzodioxole acetamide side chain. Other stronger examples are a benzodioxole-substituted fused aromatic lactam, imidazole-like compounds, aromatic amides and sulfonamides. These have conventional amine, carbonyl, ether and oxidized sulfur functionality and are mostly synthetically plausible. Low products include flexible acyclic polyamines, small sulfur-containing acids, a saturated cage amide and a small carbonyl-containing oxygen/sulfur ring. The final molecules span complex sulfonamide assemblies and simpler structures lacking the same aromatic/polar arrangement.
liabilities: Large sulfonamide/amide combinations can add aromatic bulk and polarity while scoring below a simpler leader.
Some saturated or fused alternatives have undefined stereochemical relationships, although the principal piperazine leaders are achiral.
Small fragments and highly flexible charged or polyamine products can lose the aromatic organization retained by the stronger structures.
missing_features: The low flexible polyamines and small sulfur-containing acids lack the integrated aromatic/carbonyl or sulfonyl/amine arrangement found in the stronger molecules.
The displayed leaders incompletely sample matched aromatic partners and linker placements around the sulfonyl-piperazine arrangement; larger or more polar appendages are not automatically beneficial.

The trajectories do not identify one uniquely missing group beyond these observed associations. The remaining chemistry gap concerns compatible connectivity and shape rather than adding piperazine or sulfur indiscriminately.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact piperazine/fused cyclic-carbamate sulfonamide scores 0.2189839359276689, while the larger benzodioxole/sulfonyl-piperazine/acetamide combination scores 0.2160027395643138. A benzodioxole-linked aromatic lactam reaches 0.19966749769191652. Thus higher scores can occur with several carbonyl- and aromatic-containing arrangements, with a particularly clear sulfonyl-piperazine family. A flexible acyclic polyamine/polyether scores 0.0, a small sulfur-ring acid scores 0.026148818018424533, and a more complex saturated cage amide scores 0.04076048393103888. The final methoxyaryl piperazine amide reaches only 0.1411862416005035, showing that piperazine alone is not sufficient. The parent seed-2 N-methyl phenylsulfonyl piperazine scored 0.20718664161756667, versus 0.2189839359276689 for the current fused-carbamate aryl partner. Current seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.19966749769191652 and 0.2160027395643138 versus parental 0.20090425134085538 and 0.21944544104637362.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is a diarylethyl-substituted aminoguanidine hydrazone, combining aromatic hydrophobic groups with a strongly polar imino/nitrogen-rich head. Other stronger products are quite different: a pyrrolidine linked to a small sulfonylated diaza ring with an oxime-like group, an ester/amide-substituted aromatic pyridone, an oxalamide with a bridged saturated amine, and ether-linked triazole/imidazole-like heterocycles. Most fragments are familiar, but hydrazone configuration, small-ring strain and ionization remain unresolved. The lowest products are very long lipids or polyamines, highly hydroxylated sugar/nucleoside-like compounds and other bulky flexible molecules. There is no dominant shared high-scoring ring family.
liabilities: The aminoguanidine hydrazone combines a potentially strongly basic head with an unassigned imine configuration and an N-N connection.
The sulfonylated diaza/oxime alternative contains a strained small nitrogen ring, while other candidates introduce bridged saturated rings without stereochemical definition.
Extreme hydrocarbon chains, long polyamine chains and sugar-rich structures dominate some low-score examples, despite being chemically very different from each other.
missing_features: The lowest long-chain, polymer-like and highly hydroxylated products lack the moderate scale and localized polar/aromatic organization of the better examples.

The supplied leaders are too chemically disparate to establish a single unseen functional group as the answer. Matched series preserving a useful polar-linker arrangement while varying size, geometry and ionization-relevant groups are missing from the displayed evidence.
The stronger parental carbonyl and polar-ring arrangements are not represented among the current leaders as closely matched alternatives.
Hydrazone or oxime geometry and possible saturated-ring stereochemistry are not specified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminoguanidine hydrazone scores 0.2320107079772056; the sulfonylated small diaza-ring/oxime compound scores 0.23124825514969893, and the aromatic ester/amide/pyridone scores 0.22293874669174316. A methoxyaryl/heterocycle ether reaches 0.1871471057147747, while a related ethoxyaryl ketone reaches 0.15125101854430076; additional peripheral changes mean this is not a single-bond comparison. These observations support moderate size and particular localized polar/aromatic arrangements, but do not identify a universal carbonyl, basic amine, fluorine or heterocycle requirement. Long-chain lipid and polyamine examples score 0.0, and a sugar-rich structure scores 9.167234704499243e-127. The digest reports a median of 0.0. Current per-seed maxima are 0.2320107079772056, 0.23124825514969893 and 0.1871471057147747, versus parental 0.2932061327730367, 0.28770317918999355 and 0.3108657757276207. The current chemistry is plausible in many cases but does not recover the stronger parental polar-ring/carbonyl families.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Low examples include long lipids, long polyamine chains, highly hydroxylated sugars, peptide-like molecules and small polar fragments. Better molecules instead combine moderate aromatic frameworks with localized amide, urea, sulfonyl, amine or ether functionality. Both very hydrophobic and very polar extremes can have recorded scores of 0.0.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve a useful molecular scale or balance of aromatic and polar functionality.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemical variations that preserve a promising size and functional-group arrangement while changing scaffold or linker geometry. Avoid making local variation depend on large chain growth, excessive polar repetition or deletion of most of the useful framework.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A low primary-amine-containing urea scores 6.812931663695377e-05 despite the success of several piperazine/aryl-amine families. An ordinary aryl sulfonamide reaches 0.5999223218699244 while a differently arranged sulfone-indole scores 0.31752369822101023. A final piperazine amide scores 0.1411862416005035 versus 0.2189839359276689 for a compact sulfonyl-piperazine/aromatic-carbonyl combination.
transferable_gaps.gap: Matched spatial arrangements are incompletely represented even when the useful functional groups are already available.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate coherent matched series varying attachment position, linker length, ring nitrogen placement and saturation while retaining the rest of the framework. Do not substitute simple counts of amines, rings or sulfur groups for the chemical arrangement supported by feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The strongest alcohol-bearing indanol/tetralin-like products have possible stereogenic centres, and other displayed molecules contain substituted pyrrolidines, bridged rings, hydrazones or oxime-like groups. Many aromatic amide and piperazine leaders are achiral, so the missing definition is structure-dependent.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic alcohol and saturated-ring products, and configurationally variable imines, remain undefined.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Specify feasible absolute and relative configurations, and imine or oxime geometry where relevant, and preserve them during structural changes. Compare matched configurations without treating stereochemical labels as universally necessary or automatically beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several different aromatic amide and urea arrangements share 0.48839749189747395. Ethylthio, methoxy and propargyloxy relatives share 0.6014089846464902, while multiple aryl fluorine/chlorine pairs have identical near-maximum scores. These observations do not demonstrate a unique need for the more elaborate appendages.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically simple alternatives are not consistently distinguished from extra functionality whose local score contribution is unclear.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include matched simplifications that reduce flexible chains, excess substitution or reactive functionality while retaining the useful core arrangement. Use observed feedback to determine which simpler structures preserve the desired chemistry.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent samples local molecular graph edits from one scored current state, normalizes identities, rejects duplicates and sends the first full tabu-admissible batch for evaluation. It then walks to the best accepted neighbor, including worsening moves, while retaining an independent best archive. Bond changes alter bond order; deletions remove atoms or leaves. Neither directly relocates an intact side group along an aromatic ring. The Parent already includes the repaired identity join and its established inverse-motif memory.
approach.novelty: Add one intact-substituent relocation along an existing aromatic ring edge. Detach an acyclic pendant group from an aromatic carbon and reconnect the same group to an adjacent aromatic carbon bearing a hydrogen. This changes substitution position while retaining the whole group, the ring framework and molecular formula. The move becomes an extra choice when the existing bond-change operator selects that attachment bond. Earlier branch deletion discarded groups; nitrogen exchange moved ring elements. This experiment instead reconnects an existing side group and incorporates neither earlier extension.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing change_bond neighborhood with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to its adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, directly exposing substitution-position isomers while preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula.

finding_summary.headline: Ten intact-group position changes were evaluated, but none carried the improved panel score
finding_summary.insights: Direct positional accessibility is established: none of the ten scored products is reachable by a single original bond-order change, and each changes local motifs and measured score. Intact-group retention therefore avoids the necessary atom loss of branch deletion, but it does not reliably make a stronger neighbor. All four evaluated larger-branch relocations lose to their sources, including the methoxy and carboxyl shifts. The distinction between a successful panel and useful new molecules matters here: since no relocation is selected, the panel gain cannot be credited to descendants carrying a moved group. The expanded menu also changes proposal choices and batch competition among the original operators. The evidence supports a working positional channel and one local thiol-position gain, while leaving a reproducible score benefit from retaining a new position unresolved. The stronger sulfur-free aryl-amine series identified by the molecular assessment is an original-operator outcome and still contains strained nitrogen rings; other populations retain unusual sulfur and reactive heteroatom bonds. Conserving the existing group and ring has not established better stability or synthetic accessibility.
finding_summary.results: Ten fresh positional isomers reached evaluation from thirteen sampled branch relocations, with all atoms, the complete branch, molecular formula and aromatic ring framework retained. Six moved one-heavy-atom groups and four moved larger groups. One thiol position change improved its source score; the other nine lost. None won its batch, updated the best archive or produced a later walk descendant. The three-seed macro mean nevertheless rose from 0.520918 to 0.525257, a paired gain of 0.004339 that exceeds the 0.002 target. One seed improved and two declined; the largest endpoint gain was in one DRD2 seed, while median_2 and sitagliptin endpoints were unchanged throughout.
