molecular.headline: Ring-rich inherited scaffolds acquire unusual reactive appendages; conventional amides and amines coexist with azo, N-F and thiocarbonyl chemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All supplied trajectories were read, covering every task in the brief. Each contains 300 molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals, on seed 0. There is no Parent or Parent trajectory, so the comparison is with the supplied initial molecules and the observed within-task score gradient. Scores quoted below are rounded recorded values, not new evaluations. The output contains substantial ring chemistry: ring_closure_rate is 1.0 throughout. The recurrent frameworks are indoles, diaryl fused dione heterocycles, quinoline/phenoxy/piperidine assemblies, biphenyl/arylsulfonyl/pyrrolidine assemblies, and oxygen-rich polyacetals. These are recognizable in the initial molecules; much of the subsequent variety changes their substituents while retaining their ring frameworks. Aromatic_atom_rate, which measures the fraction of proposal strings containing aromatic atoms rather than the fraction of atoms that are aromatic, is 0.9586, 0.9897, 0.9966, 1.0 and 0.331 in the fixed task order. The last trajectory develops a predominantly nonaromatic polyacetal series. Thus structural diversity is moderate across the supplied outputs, but the chemically favored series within a task are narrower than the 300 unique identities suggest. Synthetic plausibility is mixed. Familiar amides, ethers, esters, alkylated amines and heterocycles remain available, while many proposals combine N-F, repeated N-O or N-N linkages, sulfur-halogen bonds, unstabilized thiocarbonyls or cumulated double bonds. The recognizable cores do not make these appendages ordinary medicinal chemistry. Every proposal set has charged_rate and stereocentre_rate of 0.0: explicit ions and assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry are absent from the submitted strings, although ionizable atoms and potential stereocentres are present. No synthesis, stability, affinity or protonation-state measurement was supplied.

per_task.generated_character: The better molecules are medium-sized, aromatic indole derivatives carrying a fluorophenyl group through a carboxamide or an aminomethyl linker. Methoxy/other ether substituents and the indole NH are recurrent. Evaluation 153 is a comparatively conventional dimethoxyindole carboxamide with an N-methyl-N-fluorophenyl amide; its amide nitrogen is not an ordinary basic amine. Other upper-score examples add N-fluoroaminomethyl ethers, N-ethynyl groups or vinylamine motifs. Lower-score families include elaborate saturated polyacetals and bulkier diaryl fused diones. The optimizer strings have mean length 48.6, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9586 and halogen_rate 0.9483. The best conventional amide looks synthetically plausible in outline; many surrounding analogues are substantially less convincing.
liabilities: N-F-bearing amines, sulfur-fluoride/chloride appendages and heteroatom-substituted alkynes raise stability and route-planning concerns. The aryl C-F bond in the best molecule should not be conflated with these heteroatom-halogen bonds.
Cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.1345. Several high-score analogues retain unsaturated or N-F-bearing appendages even though the observed maximum needs neither.
missing_features: The later output does not consistently retain the favorable combination of a small N-alkyl carboxamide and uncomplicated aryl ethers: final analogues frequently replace it with N-F, ethynyl-ether or sulfur-halogen chemistry. The clean combination exists at the maximum, so this is a coverage gap rather than complete inability to make it.

Alternative ring-nitrogen placements and reorganized ring frameworks are not represented among the cited high-score molecules. Their benefit cannot be established from this trajectory, which does not identify a unique missing target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole secondary amide at evaluation 9 scores 0.305105, whereas the dimethoxy N-methyl amide at 153 scores 0.395373. This supports a local preference for that combined substitution change, without separating the effects of losing a methoxy group, its position and amide methylation. The N-F-containing analogue at 160 is nearly equal at 0.394920, so the score tolerates unusual chemistry rather than demonstrating its necessity. The oxygen-rich polycycle at 13 scores 0.0000369102 and the larger fused-dione compound at 95 scores 0.0000487084. Final ethynyl-ether/sulfur-fluoride indoles at 299 and 300 both score 0.0153241. The observed favorable feature is the particular compact indole/aryl/linker combination, not aromaticity or halogenation alone.

per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by fairly large diaryl fused dione heterocycles with N-methylated ring nitrogens. Their aromatic substituents acquire primary or alkylated amino groups, methylthio groups, fluorinated aminoalkyl branches and azo/diazene substituents. The maximum at 284 combines a fused dione core with densely substituted phenyl rings, dimethylamino functionality, an alpha-fluoroamine branch and repeated azo functionality. A distinct high-score example at 169 instead has amino/methylamino groups, a phenol and an aldehyde, without azo or fluorinated appendages. Indole carboxamides also recur late. Mean SMILES length is 65.4, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9897 and halogen_rate is 0.6621. Familiar cores are present, but the densely decorated azo/aminal-rich periphery often makes the complete molecules questionable synthetic targets.
liabilities: Aryl/alkyl azo groups and terminal diazenes introduce unassigned geometric isomerism and potential redox or decomposition liabilities; repeated N-N units and highly substituted aminal/hemiaminal-like branches are especially unconventional.
Aldehydes, amino-substituted aromatics and methylthio groups still need chemical scrutiny in the simpler series; a high scalar score is not evidence of stability or an executable synthesis.
Fluorinated aminoalkyl branches can introduce stereocentres, but no tetrahedral configuration is specified in these proposal strings.
missing_features: Relatively simple amino/phenol/carbonyl combinations are underrepresented among the heavily decorated upper-score examples, despite evaluation 169 demonstrating a competitive conventional alternative. What is missing is sustained exploration of that chemistry without repeatedly coupling it to azo chains or mixed heteroatom-rich branches.

The cited upper-score set supplies little evidence of alternative cyclic linkers or new ring heteroatom arrangements. Their contribution to this objective remains untested rather than known to be beneficial.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dione at 7 scores 0.548381; its extensively decorated relatives at 284 and 286 score 0.583606 and 0.582950. Amino, thioether and azo substitutions on those aromatic surfaces accompany the higher values. However, the amino/phenol/aldehyde analogue at 169 scores 0.575221 without azo groups, showing that they are not required for the upper observed range. The saturated polyacetal at 47 scores 0.506214, while the quinoline/piperidine analogue with an N-O-rich chain at 24 scores 0.530764. The late indole amide at 297 reaches 0.574024 with a methylthio/azo/amino decoration. These comparisons support locally useful aromatic polar substitution on more than one core; they do not establish that indiscriminately adding heteroatoms improves the objective.

per_task.generated_character: Most proposals are large, heavily decorated biphenyl compounds joined to an arylsulfonyl pyrrolidine through amide, amine, enamine or aminothiol-containing linkers. The recurring pyrrolidine nitrogen is sulfonylated; it should not be described as an unmasked basic cyclic amine. Extra aniline or aliphatic amino groups appear on the periphery. The best molecule at 273 has a dimethylamino-substituted dichlorophenyl sulfonamide, a difluorobiphenyl group and a chlorinated enamine linker. Evaluation 218 instead supplies an accessible dimethylaminomethyl branch. Mean SMILES length is 84.2, the longest mean in the digest; aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9966 and halogen_rate is 0.9862. The underlying sulfonamide/aryl chemistry is recognizable, but many proposed complete structures are encumbered by polyhalogenated appendages and reactive linkers.
liabilities: Chlorinated enamines, sulfenamide/aminothiol motifs and extensively brominated or chlorinated branches complicate stability and synthesis. Fluoroalkyl cumulenes occur late; cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.1414.

Large aromatic surfaces and heavy halogen decoration coexist with several flexible bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. These are liabilities for a tractable series even when the recorded scalar increases.
Neutral input notation must not be mistaken for proof that the molecules are nonionizable, and a docking-task scalar must not be equated with measured receptor affinity.
missing_features: The dominant series does not provide a conventional, independently varied basic cyclic nitrogen: its ring nitrogen remains sulfonylated while additional amines are appended elsewhere. The useful peripheral amine examples motivate a gap in independent control of nitrogen placement and electronic state, not a claim that any cyclic amine would help.

Defined stereoisomers of the substituted pyrrolidine and benzylic/linker centres are absent. Explicitly charged representations are also absent from the submitted strings; whether the evaluation prepared protonated forms internally is not shown.

Chemically ordinary alternatives to the chlorinated enamine and aminothiol linkers, retaining comparable attachment geometry, are missing from the cited upper-score series. Their score effect would require observation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial arylsulfonyl/pyrrolidine amide bearing a carboxylic acid at 10 scores 0.0190412. The amine/enamine-bearing analogues at 218 and 273 reach 0.187076 and 0.189601, respectively. Several changes occur together, so the trajectory does not isolate an amine, acid-removal or linker effect. A particularly informative pair is 272 versus 273: relocating fluorines on the distal phenyl ring changes 0.124071 to 0.189601 without changing the main framework or elemental composition. This makes substituent placement an observed distinction beyond simply adding nitrogen or halogens. The quinoline/phenoxy/piperidine compound at 275 scores only 0.00334580 despite a tertiary cyclic amine. Final polyhalogenated/cumulene-containing analogues such as 300 score 0.0677295. The evidence favors particular spatially organized combinations; it supplies no binding pose or interaction assignment.

per_task.generated_character: This trajectory contains the most conventional upper-score chemistry in the supplied set. Better molecules include alkyl-substituted quinolines connected through a methylene ether and phenyl amide to N-alkyl piperidines, alongside diaryl fused diones bearing esters, ethers and alkyl substituents. Evaluation 237 combines a propyl/methyl quinoline, an aryl ether, an amide, an N-methyl piperidine and an aldehyde. Evaluation 102 is an ethyl-substituted diaryl fused dione with an ethyl ester. Elsewhere the trajectory still proposes N-O and N-S chains and branched alkyl growth. These are medium-to-large molecules with mean SMILES length 65.9; aromatic_atom_rate is 1.0, halogen_rate 0.5586 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.0. The main high-score motifs are plausible medicinal-chemistry starting points in outline, with route and stereochemical details unresolved.
liabilities: The highest quinoline example retains an aldehyde, introducing an electrophilic and potentially metabolically sensitive group; its score does not establish acceptable stability.
Long alkyl branches enlarge flexible hydrophobic regions. Early N-O/N-S-rich variants are chemically less ordinary than the upper-score ester/amide series.
Substituted saturated rings and branched chains contain potential stereochemical distinctions that are unspecified in every optimizer string.
missing_features: Many later molecules do not preserve the modest alkyl substitution and simple polar-group balance seen in the better examples; long or branched alkyl additions and further N-alkylation often accompany lower scores. The gap is reliable exploration around chemically economical combinations already demonstrated by the output.

Alternative ring arrangements and defined piperidine/substituent stereochemistry are not represented in the cited upper-score set. The observed modest score differences do not identify a specific absent target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dione at 7 scores 0.167839. Loss of its phenolic OH together with ethyl substitution on an aromatic ring gives 0.175839 at 102 and 0.174613 at 103. The quinoline/piperidine initial molecule at 6 scores 0.156977; the propyl-substituted aldehyde analogue at 237 scores 0.175888. Conventional alkyl/ether/carbonyl patterns therefore characterize the upper observed values. Alkyl extension is not monotonically favorable: the otherwise closely related pentyl quinoline at 282 scores 0.166260, below the propyl compound at 237. N-O-rich derivatives at 18-20 score 0.110506, and the modified flavone at 14 scores 0.112923. The useful distinction is a particular balance and placement of hydrocarbon substituents and conventional polar groups, not unlimited growth or heteroatom-chain elaboration.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecules are nonaromatic oxygen-rich polyacetals resembling heavily protected carbohydrate frameworks, decorated with terminal thioaldehydes, other thiocarbonyl groups, aldehydes and chlorinated carbon branches. Evaluation 243 retains the elaborate polyacetal framework while adding repeated terminal thiocarbonyls, an aldehyde and a trichloromethyl substituent. Its near-equal-score relative at 242 redistributes the appendages around the same kind of framework. Other proposals explore hydrazones, N-O chains, sulfur/nitrogen chains and thioketene or longer cumulene appendages; aromatic starting families persist at lower values. Mean SMILES length is 57.6, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.331, halogen_rate 0.5345 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1931. The polyacetal skeleton is recognizable chemistry, but the multiply reactive sulfur-rich products look poor as isolable medicinal compounds without substantial stabilization and synthesis evidence.
liabilities: Repeated terminal thioaldehydes, thioketenes and adjacent thiocarbonyl motifs present substantial chemical-reactivity and isolation concerns. These differ materially from ordinary stable thioamides or sulfones.
The crowded polyacetal framework and multiple oxygen-bearing stereocentres would demand controlled synthesis; no stereochemical assignments or synthetic route are supplied.
Hydrazone/N-O-rich side chains and long cumulated unsaturation recur even among very low-scoring analogues. Rich ring content here does not imply conventional drug-like chemistry.
missing_features: The upper-score series lacks chemically stable alternatives that preserve its favorable balance of ring oxygen, sulfur-containing substituents and chlorinated branches without exposed terminal thioaldehydes or cumulated bonds. Whether a stable replacement preserves the score is unknown.

Conventional basic amines and aromatic nitrogen acceptors are absent from the highest polyacetals, while the earlier aromatic/amine-containing molecules are generally poorer. Their absence can be described, but this trajectory does not support prescribing their addition as this objective's answer.
The stereochemical configurations needed to specify these highly substituted polyacetals are absent from the proposal strings. There is no evidence here of a stereochemically resolved series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial polyacetal at 4 scores 0.0000254690; the extensively sulfur/chlorine-decorated polyacetals at 242 and 243 each score approximately 0.0881235. In contrast, the same broad polyacetal family with hydrazone and O-N appendages at 56 scores 1.23960e-32, and the nitrogen/sulfur-decorated biphenyl amide at 130 scores 1.06523e-33. This supports a narrow favorable combination on the oxygen-rich scaffold, not a general reward for sulfur, heteroatoms or chlorination. The final trichloromethyl/thioketene-containing polyacetal at 296 falls to 1.03025e-09 despite retaining many ostensibly favorable ingredients; the final thiocarbonyl/aldehyde variant at 300 scores 0.00937443. The nearly equal scores for 242 and 243 show tolerance of those particular positional alternatives. No reference molecule or component scores were shown, so the large gradient cannot be assigned to a specific desired pharmacophore or physicochemical term.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Its output repeatedly combines N-F bonds, N-O/N-N chains, sulfur-halogen groups, terminal thioaldehydes and cumulated bonds with otherwise familiar ring frameworks. Cumulated-double-bond rates reach 0.1345, 0.1414 and 0.1931 in the affected proposal sets. A conventional dimethoxy N-methyl indole amide has recorded score 0.395373, while a closely related N-F-bearing analogue scores 0.394920; unusual appendages are therefore not required to reach that observed neighborhood. Conventional amino/phenol/carbonyl and ester/amide examples also coexist with reactive variants.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably keep new substituents within chemically stable functional-group environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add task-independent sensitivity to local bond environments and functional-group compatibility so ordinary amines, ethers, amides and appropriately stabilized sulfur groups remain available without automatically turning into heteroatom chains or reactive endpoints. Preserve structurally comparable stable alternatives and let accepted scalar feedback determine their usefulness.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring_closure_rate is 1.0 for every proposal set, but the repeated indole, fused dione, quinoline/piperidine, arylsulfonyl/pyrrolidine and polyacetal frameworks are recognizable in the supplied initial molecules. The cited maxima remain variations on those frameworks. Across the trajectories, much of the visible novelty lies in pendant chains, exocyclic functionality and substitution positions rather than new cyclic connectivity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring abundance does not translate into demonstrated exploration of substantially different ring frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator seeking broader chemical coverage would need a way to vary cyclic connectivity, ring heteroatom placement and the connections between ring units, while retaining chemically plausible scaffolds as alternatives. This is a chemical capability gap, not evidence that any particular unseen ring system will improve the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The dominant sulfonylated pyrrolidine series keeps a deactivated ring nitrogen while introducing separate aniline or aliphatic amine centres. Upper-score analogues mix those changes with chlorinated enamine or aminothiol linkers. Relocating distal phenyl fluorines on an otherwise matching framework changes the recorded score from 0.124071 to 0.189601. Conversely, a tertiary cyclic amine on another scaffold has a low recorded score, so nitrogen presence alone does not explain the observed chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output offers limited independent control of functional-group position, basicity and linkage geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support matched changes in attachment position, nitrogen bonding environment and linker type so the search can vary accessible basic centres and molecular geometry independently of adding reactive appendages. Distinguish amines, anilines, amides and sulfonamides as different chemical environments using only the observed scalar feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre_rate and charged_rate are both 0.0 in every proposal set. Nevertheless, the submitted molecules include substituted piperidines and pyrrolidines, benzylic amino centres, fluorinated aminoalkyl branches and complex polyacetals. Several structures contain ionizable amines or acids. These counters establish absent input annotations, not absent molecular stereochemistry or neutral behavior in solution; evaluation-side preparation was not supplied.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not express stereochemically resolved or explicitly charged candidate alternatives in these outputs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where the candidate contract supports them, provide chemically justified stereoisomer and ionization-state alternatives and track their identities explicitly. Base the choices on generic chemical rules and accepted observations, without assuming that added stereochemical or charge annotation is itself rewarded.

nodes.method_name: Inverse-QSAR: mixed-integer de novo molecular construction
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in inverse-QSAR through coupled linear regression and mixed-integer graph construction. [Zhu et al., Sections 1, 3 and 4](https://www.imrpress.com/journal/FBL/27/6/10.31083/j.fbl2706188) encode both a molecular descriptor function and a learned predictor in a program that constructs a graph satisfying structural specifications. Our benchmark adaptation fits a regularized linear score model only to the current objective's accepted observations, using atom-type, degree and typed-bond counts that can be represented exactly by integer constraints. For each proposal, take a scored molecule, choose a bounded editable peripheral region and retain its connected surrounding context. Represent replacement atom identities, bond orders and attachment choices as discrete variables, with connectivity, valence and descriptor-consistency constraints. Maximize the fitted scalar prediction over these variables instead of solving the paper's fixed target-interval problem. A feasible integer assignment supplies the new molecular graph directly. Validate the actual graph and recompute its descriptors before submission; exclude repeated assignments and retry construction when canonical identity is duplicate or invalid. Vary contexts and editable regions as feedback accumulates, and continue construction until the announced batch is filled. Use bounded subproblems and feasible solver incumbents rather than requiring a proof of global optimality for every proposal. The root needs no generative checkpoint or external labels. It constructs atom and bond combinations, without a corpus molecule pool, stored-fragment retrieval or the paper's subsequent isomer-enumeration stage. Each objective starts with clean scored and fitted state. The hypothesis is that jointly enforcing realizable structure while optimizing a task-local prediction concentrates evaluations on improving molecules and raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Exact descriptor realization cannot compensate for an inaccurate predictor; both predictive usefulness and sufficient construction throughput remain unproven.

Exact whole-molecule atom, heavy-degree and typed-bond count equations including retained context and attachment-degree changes
Positive observed-score rank preference over eligible accepted source contexts with alternative sources retained

approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates direct neural molecular proposals with two graph refinement phases. It learns from a full archive of real accepted scores and exact molecular token trajectories sampled by score rank. Joint trajectory-balance updates adapt the policy and a learned normalizer, while policy-to-prior categorical KL keeps a reference to frozen corpus-trained weights. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior allocates graph-offspring evaluations and protects the initial fresh-policy handoff. The frozen prior was selected along unchanged unlabeled training by valid, connected, unique generation yield, with original holdout loss breaking ties. In its current update, both trajectory-specific score mismatch and the common normalizer mismatch contribute to policy credit.
approach.novelty: Center the trajectory-balance policy credit within each actual replay minibatch and assign the common mismatch to the existing normalizer alone. Each trajectory still receives relative credit from its exact accepted score and likelihood, and every pairwise difference in those coefficients is retained. Unlike the earlier scaffold mixture or reversed KL penalty, this changes neither which records are learned from nor the reference distribution. It tests whether separating shared normalization error from relative policy learning makes accepted-score adaptation more useful; it does not assume that zero mean credit or lower loss guarantees better molecules.

nodes.hypothesis: Center accepted trajectory-balance policy coefficients within each replay minibatch while routing the detached common residual exclusively to the learned normalizer, preserving score-ranked replay and the original categorical prior penalty.

finding_summary.headline: Centering activated, but common error grew and useful neural emission fell
finding_summary.insights:
The common policy-credit component was not merely an expendable normalization error in this setting. Removing it left the scalar objective unchanged at a given state, yet shifted much more unresolved error onto the normalizer and weakened later transfer of graph feedback into neural proposals. This happened while graph-origin replay share increased from 73.54% to 75.43%, so dilution of graph records is not the explanation. Greater emitted scaffold variety and the disappearance of duplicate raw draws also failed to compensate for lower valid yield and policy-origin scores.

The early-versus-late reversal narrows the problem to continuing accepted-score adaptation rather than a different prepared prior: the checkpoint identities and preparation were unchanged. Preserving the direct normalizer derivative was insufficient to preserve its trajectory, because the policy state and shared clipping changed. The improved sitagliptin endpoint must also be read alongside the molecular assessment, which found prominent peroxide-linked, stereochemically undefined structures; broader graph coverage does not establish better chemical quality. Mechanism execution is confirmed, while the registered search-advantage condition is unsupported. The remaining question is how to control common and relative learning jointly without discarding the useful molecular transfer observed in the parent.
finding_summary.results:
All 7,200 replay updates used the intended centered policy credit. Independent differentiation verified that the common term had no policy gradient and that the normalizer retained its original direct derivative. The change reversed 99,068 of 230,400 policy-credit signs while preserving pairwise differences and the scalar loss value within numerical precision. Nevertheless, the common mismatch became much larger in the resulting histories: its mean squared contribution was 44.130, compared with 4.418 in the parent, accounting for 62.59% rather than 14.95% of trajectory-balance loss.

Raw valid novel yield fell from 7,991/12,000 draws (66.59%) to 6,861/12,280 (55.87%). The first adapted policy batches improved in validity, but later yield fell from 64.00% to 51.82%. Mean accepted policy-origin score fell from 0.204941 to 0.172874, and later emitted molecules matching previously trained graph scaffolds fell from 53 to 15. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.550198 to 0.542654, a decrease of 0.007543; paired changes were -0.009239, -0.029845 and +0.016454. All fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations.

molecular.headline: Recognizable amide and piperazine chemistry is mixed with acid chlorides, N-O-O chains and stereochemically undefined polycycles
molecular.overall_character: The supplied panel is complete: each of five tasks has 900 evaluated molecules across three seeds, including 870 optimizer proposals. All 4,350 optimizer-proposal SMILES parse with RDKit. Rings and aromatic atoms are plentiful: digest ring-closure rates are 0.9851-0.9931 and aromatic-token rates 0.9402-0.9828. In fixed task order, proposal median heavy-atom counts are 25, 37, 25, 30 and 26, and median ring counts are three, five, three, four and four. Conventional aryl propionamides, aminoheteroaryls, cyclic tertiary amines, arylsulfonylpiperazines and aromatic dicarbonyl systems coexist with O-fluoro groups, O-acyl hydroxylamines, acid chlorides, bridged sulfur/nitrogen ring systems and unusual N-O-O-C substituents. These liabilities occur in leading families: one task contains 139 acid-halide proposals; another contains 211 proposals with O-O single bonds, including 201 with N-O-O chains, and its highest structure has seven RDKit-perceived unassigned stereocentres. No proposal assigns a stereocentre, while counts containing an unassigned centre are 492, 198, 389, 350 and 538. Each task has 553-679 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, but leading molecules repeat close families rather than establish broad accessible synthetic diversity. The parent already generated elaborate ring systems and unusual bonds; current acid-halide and peroxide-rich families make those limitations prominent. Overall drug-likeness is weak because major leading families carry reactive or physically burdensome features, despite conventional amide and piperazine subsets. The trajectories do not establish synthesis or stable experimental compounds.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is an alpha-aryl propionamide whose amide nitrogen carries a methylene-linked N-arylpyrrole; the attached aryl group is a fluoropyridine. It has 25 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and an unassigned alpha-carbon stereocentre. Related leaders use pyrazoles, an O-acyl hydroxylamine connection instead of the amide, or ring-contracted unsaturated nitrogen heterocycles. The ordinary amides are recognizable medicinal chemistry; aryl O-F, acyl-O-N and four-membered unsaturated nitrogen-ring variants need separate qualification. Parent leaders included indole-amide and fused heterocyclic structures, whereas this digest concentrates around a three-ring propionamide/heteroarylmethyl architecture.
liabilities: An O-acyl hydroxylamine is an acyl-O-N connection, chemically distinct from an ordinary amide or hydroxamic acid; the score does not establish its stability.
Sixteen proposals contain O-halogen bonds and 23 N-halogen bonds, although the highest displayed molecule requires neither.
Eleven proposals have at most three heavy atoms and 18 exceed 50, so fragmentation and overgrowth coexist with the leading ring-rich chemistry.
missing_features: The leading alpha-aryl acyl family does not specify its central stereocentre, leaving the proposed configurations undefined.
Broad stable alternatives retaining the useful amide/heteroaromatic relationship are less visible than O-F, N-O and small-ring variants.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The conventional amide scores 0.445826 and its displayed aryl O-F counterpart 0.445454, showing tolerance rather than a demonstrated need for O-fluorination. In another local pair, an O-acyl hydroxylamine scores 0.442718 and the direct amide 0.432360; that extra oxygen changes bond chemistry, not just polarity. A related three-ring amide remains at 0.417399, whereas truncated two-ring amide or heteroaryl structures score 0.007181 and 0.004449. Very large assemblies and tiny halogen or hydrazine species reach zero. The visible association is a particular moderate-size ring/linker/carbonyl arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family is a three-ring aminoheteroaryl assembly with methoxy, dimethylamino, bromo or fluoro substituents and a vinyl-ether-containing N-substituent. Its top member has 34 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and molecular mass 534.390. A second leading family has arylsulfonamide/anilino frameworks bearing two acid chlorides, often with methylenedioxy and sulfur/nitrogen fused rings. These are recognizable reactive intermediates rather than demonstrated stable final medicinal compounds. Some variants add aromatic bridges or unusual sulfur double-bond arrangements. Full proposals have median 37 heavy atoms, five rings and molecular mass 573.860; 201 exceed 50 heavy atoms. Acid-halide proposals increase from 15 in the parent to 139 here.
liabilities: There are 139 acid-halide proposals, and several leaders contain two acid chlorides, providing reactive acylating sites rather than demonstrated persistent drug-like substituents.
Thirty-three proposals contain O-halogen bonds and 41 have O-O single bonds, distinct concerns from ordinary aryl halogenation.
The proposal range reaches 111 heavy atoms and molecular mass 2035.098, limiting the practical meaning of graph validity.
missing_features: Stable functional-group alternatives retaining the useful polar/aromatic arrangement are not demonstrated across the high-score acid-chloride neighborhood.
The output lacks consistently economical whole-molecule coverage around the aminoheteroaryl family, often extending into larger repeated or fused structures.
Synthetic access and stable geometry are unestablished for the aromatic bridges and unusual sulfur-bond variants.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminoheteroaryl leader scores 0.615282, a close analogue 0.614174 and a methoxy-for-bromo variant 0.613310, so bromine is not required for a nearby score. The bis-acid-chloride sulfonamide scores 0.613582; ring-bridged or sulfur-bond variants remain near 0.61. Those values tolerate reactive groups without establishing chemical persistence. Replacing methoxy with O-F in a local aminoheteroaryl pair gives 0.609781 versus 0.614174, providing no benefit from O-F. Low sulfone-rich or heavily elaborated structures lie around 0.285-0.299 despite many rings and heteroatoms.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule combines a nine-membered tertiary-amine ring with indole and phenol regions, an ethyl substituent and a fluoromethylamino arm. It has 32 heavy atoms, four rings and two unassigned stereocentres. The fluoromethylamino arm is N-CH2-F, not a direct N-F bond. Eight-membered analogues, bridged amines, dimethylaminoethyl aromatic frameworks and aldehyde-bearing arylpiperidines also lead. These include familiar medicinal motifs, but medium or bridged rings raise synthetic and conformational questions. Parent leaders likewise combined cyclic amines with aromatic, indole or phenolic regions; the current digest emphasizes medium-size rings and unusual junctions. Full proposals have median 25 heavy atoms and three rings.
liabilities: Eight- and nine-membered rings and multiple bridges impose conformational and synthetic questions that the graphs do not resolve.
Some leaders contain aldehydes, and 32 proposals have direct N-halogen bonds; the highest N-CH2-F structure must not be confused with those direct N-F species.
Sixteen proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, with a maximum of 95, showing excessive elaboration around otherwise useful amine chemistry.
missing_features: Leading medium-ring and bridged amines lack explicit relative configurations and established conformations; 389 proposals contain unassigned stereocentres.
No additional mandatory group follows from near-ceiling scores; economical stable alternatives preserving the observed amine/aromatic relationships are the supported need.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The nine-membered amine scores 0.999991, an eight-membered analogue 0.997059, a less elaborate dimethylaminoethyl aromatic structure 0.993803 and an aldehyde-bearing arylpiperidine 0.993765. Their shared feature is accessible amine functionality positioned with aromatic regions; the nine-membered ring and fluoromethylamino arm are not universal requirements. Low acylhydrazone, carbamate, thiosemicarbazone and amide examples lie near 4.11e-05 to 1.11e-04 despite nitrogen and rings. A terminal direct N-F cyclic amine scores 0.247498 while other terminal amines remain above 0.91, but those are different structures and do not isolate an N-F substituent effect.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest family is conventional arylsulfonylpiperazine chemistry with the second piperazine nitrogen attached to a substituted quinoline-like or diazaaromatic fused ring. The highest has 29 heavy atoms, four rings, three aromatic rings and molecular mass 409.555. Methyl, fluoromethyl, chlorine, hydroxyl and amino substitutions supply close alternatives. Another leader is a fused aromatic dicarbonyl nitrogen heterocycle attached to an ethoxy-substituted N/O ring system. These leaders are more chemically straightforward than many terminal structures. The parent also produced sulfonamide and fused cyclic-carbonyl architectures. Current proposals have median 30 heavy atoms and four rings versus parent medians of 32 and four, with 666 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds.
liabilities: Sulfonylated and aryl-attached piperazine nitrogens are electronically different from interchangeable free aliphatic amines.
Terminal proposals include O-O-containing rings, dense sulfur/nitrogen fusion and duplicated carbonyl frameworks without established stability or synthetic access.
Sixty-eight proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, substantially larger than the leading conventional piperazines.
missing_features: Useful sulfonylpiperazine and dicarbonyl arrangements have limited distinct alternatives beyond local substitutions with identical or nearly identical scores.
The wider output lacks consistent ring-fusion and configurational control: 350 proposals have unassigned centres, although the highest piperazine family is achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The arylsulfonylpiperazine scores 0.232655, the alternative dicarbonyl compound 0.231883 and the fluoromethyl variant 0.231824. Several amino, hydroxyl, fluoro or aryl-halogen variants share 0.225523, giving little evidence that more peripheral decoration resolves the remaining gap. Small ethane, ether, carbonate or guanidine-like species score approximately 0.012-0.029 and lack the combined aromatic/polar-ring architecture. Terminal examples repeating carbonyl heterocycles or adding complex rings remain around 0.139-0.203. More ring closure or heteroatoms alone therefore does not explain the useful arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family combines a five-membered lactone or cyclic carbamate with a multiply fluorinated fused sulfur/nitrogen system and a fluorinated cyclopropyl group. Most displayed members also carry an unusual N-O-O-C connection. The highest has 29 heavy atoms, five rings, only one aromatic ring and seven RDKit-perceived unassigned stereocentres. This is detailed connectivity without configurational specification, and the N-O-O chain combines N-O and peroxide bonds. Another high family contains an N-fluoro sulfur-containing fused system; terminal molecules show nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl cores linked to unsaturated sulfur rings bearing carbon allenes. Parent leaders also included unusual fluorinated heterocycles, but current O-O proposals rise from 48 to 211, including 201 with N-O-O chains. These structures need strong chemical qualification as stable compounds.
liabilities: N-O-O chains occur in 201 proposals and any O-O single bond in 211; these are chemically different from ordinary ethers or amino substituents.
Twenty-five proposals contain N-halogen bonds and 29 carbon allenes; 19 place an allene in a perceived ring of at most seven atoms, leaving local reactivity and ring geometry unresolved.
Several cited lactone/carbamate leaders have five to seven unassigned centres, so saturated complexity does not establish a coherent specified stereoisomer.
missing_features: Stable alternatives preserving the useful carbonyl, fluorinated-ring and nitrogen arrangement without N-O-O chains or other unusual bonds are not demonstrated across the leading neighborhood.
The highest structure has seven unassigned centres, and 538 proposals contain unassigned centres with none assigning any; defined three-dimensional molecules are missing.
Stable geometry and synthetic access are unestablished for fused sulfur/nitrogen cores, fluorinated small rings and cyclic-allene alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The lactone/N-O-O structure scores 0.519276 and a ring-connectivity analogue 0.501405. In a close cyclic-carbamate pair, the N-O-O version scores 0.492253 and its shorter N-O counterpart 0.463156. That numerically favors peroxide insertion in this pair without establishing stability. A different N-fluoro fused structure scores 0.475223. Several terminal carbon-allene sulfur-ring compounds reach approximately 0.302-0.403. Very polar glycosylated, multiply hydroxylated or oversized structures are as low as 1.13e-128. The full median is 0.0028918204 and there are no exact-zero rows, so this is a wide score distribution rather than a zero-score population.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One set contains 139 acid halides and leaders with two acid chlorides near score 0.613. Another has 211 O-O proposals, 201 with N-O-O chains; a cyclic-carbamate pair scores 0.492253 with N-O-O versus 0.463156 with N-O. Elsewhere, ordinary amide and aryl O-F variants score 0.445826 and 0.445454, showing that the reactive bond is not numerically needed in that pair. All structures pass RDKit parsing, which does not establish chemical persistence.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish stable functional-group alternatives from reactive connections tolerated by scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide stable bonds and functional groups that preserve useful observed arrangements. Distinguish amides from O-acyl hydroxylamines, ethers from peroxide or N-O-O chains, aryl halogens from O-halogen bonds, and stable carbonyl groups from acid halides independently of objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No assigned stereocentres occur in 4,350 optimizer proposals. The five sessions contain 492, 198, 389, 350 and 538 proposals with unassigned centres. The highest peroxide-bearing lactone has seven RDKit-perceived unassigned centres, and leading propionamides and medium-ring amines also omit configuration. Several strong piperazines are achiral, so the issue is conditional.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator adds stereogenic complexity without defining the configurations of its proposed molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit chemically consistent configurations and relevant bond geometries when the structure permits them, while retaining achiral alternatives. Complex connectivity must not substitute for specified three-dimensional molecules, and the data do not prescribe an unobserved preferred stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The five sessions contain 18, 201, 16, 68 and eleven proposals above 50 heavy atoms; the largest has 111 heavy atoms and molecular mass 2035.098. High-score aminoheteroaryls also include simpler three-ring structures, and conventional four-ring sulfonylpiperazines score above more elaborate terminal carbonyl assemblies. Other proposals contract aromatic heterocycles into small unsaturated rings or create medium and bridged amine rings without defining geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent control of molecular growth and ring elaboration around useful chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain economical alternatives with controlled linker length, topology, appendage count and mass while preserving useful polar relationships. Overgrowth and indiscriminate ring contraction can both lose valuable chemistry; the missing capability is contextual control of accessible whole molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each task has 553-679 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, yet leaders cluster around propionamides, aminoheteroaryls, bis-acid-chloride sulfonamides, medium-ring amines, sulfonylpiperazines or fluorinated peroxide-bearing polycycles. Several piperazine amino, hydroxyl, fluoro and aryl-halogen variants share 0.225523. In an aminoheteroaryl family, bromo and methoxy alternatives remain near 0.614 while O-F substitution is lower than its methoxy counterpart.
transferable_gaps.gap: Substantial graph diversity still produces narrow leading families and repetitive peripheral-substitution alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden meaningful core and linker alternatives preserving useful functionality, beyond repeated halogen swaps and ring closures. Functional-group position, electronic environment and stable geometry need representation alongside scaffold identity, with their usefulness determined by observed feedback.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent makes local graph edits from one scored current molecule, sanitizes and normalizes each identity, rejects duplicates and directly evaluates the first full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening score and separately retains its best observation. Ring closure samples hydrogen-bearing attachment pairs within the existing graph-distance range and adds a bond; it can connect sites across already extensive ring frameworks. Same-transition bidirectional tabu matching, the repaired identity join and the established memory lifecycle remain in place.
approach.novelty: Add one topology gate specifically to new ring closures. A proposed closure may form a cycle whose chosen existing shortest path contains no old ring atom, one old ring atom, or two adjacent old ring atoms joined by an existing ring bond. These cases retain access to separate, spiro-like and single-edge fused additions while excluding more extensive overlap under this narrow rule. All edit sampling stays unchanged; an otherwise valid fresh rejected closure is replaced by continued sampling from the same source. This differs from the earlier sulfur filter, branch-removal menu and configuration assignment, and incorporates none of them.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject an otherwise valid canonically novel close_ring neighbor before tabu testing unless its source shortest path overlaps the existing ring graph in zero atoms, one atom, or exactly one existing ring edge, thereby redirecting new-cycle proposals away from extended or separated ring overlap while retaining the Parent's edit sampling and accepted-score walk.

finding_summary.headline: Targeted ring closures disappear, while the mean score falls by 0.003396
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment establishes that a narrow source-path rule can strongly control ring-junction growth without disabling all closures or disturbing identity, memory and feedback. Most evaluated rings remain, and the admitted closure repertoire still produces improvements. The score cost is nevertheless real on this panel: the parent had 37 source-improving and 19 selected closures in the now-excluded class. Those historical observations explain why score retention required a test, but they do not provide scores for the newly rejected structures or identify which missing transition caused a later loss.

The chemical assessment shows what the topology restriction leaves unresolved. Less elaborate ring cages still contain unusual sulfur coordination, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds and unspecified configurations. The permitted classes do not establish accessible three-dimensional geometry or synthetic plausibility, and the rule neither removes complexity already present in a source nor constrains other edit types. The campaign now has evidence that extensive ring overlap can be suppressed selectively, alongside evidence that this degree of suppression did not retain the registered mean-score margin. Ring topology and local chemical bonding remain separate limitations.
finding_summary.results:
The gate rejected 275 valid, fresh ring-closure attempts. Independent reconstruction of the current tabu table shows that 257 of these would otherwise have been admitted; each was replaced by a different neighbor from the same scored source before feedback. Emitted closures with extended or separated overlap fell from 241 to zero. Ring growth remained active through 40 permitted closures: six paths outside existing rings, three with a single old ring atom and 31 sharing one old ring edge. Nine permitted closures beat their source score and seven improved the best archive.

The overall molecules also lost much of the targeted complexity. Among 4,350 emitted neighbors, the number with a pair of RDKit-perceived rings sharing at least three atoms fell from 1,867 to 10, while mean ring-atom participation changed only from 62.89% to 61.70%. This preserved substantial ring content while removing most extensive ring overlap. All batches completed, requiring 12.83 attempts per ten submitted molecules versus 12.15 for the parent. The complete three-seed mean fell from 0.520918 to 0.517522, a paired change of -0.003396 that exceeds the allowed 0.002 loss. Seed changes were +0.004044, -0.024305 and +0.010073. DRD2 improved on average; the other four task means declined.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl and amine frameworks retain reactive halogens, unusual sulfur bonding and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied current and parent trajectory was read. Each task has 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The current output remains entirely ring-bearing by the digest's string counter, with aromatic-token rates from 0.9103 to 1.0 and mean SMILES lengths from 46.6 to 73.2. Molecules range from compact fused heterocycles to bulky aryl amines and expanded carbonyl-containing heterocycles. The leading structures generally have fewer elaborate cage connections than several parent families, but that does not make their bonding uniformly conventional. Ordinary thioethers, sulfoxides, amides and amines coexist with substituted S-H centres, multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional substituents, N-halogen groups, O-F groups and reactive sulfur-halogen connections. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. Neutral SMILES do not establish neutral solution species for the amines, and the many potentially stereogenic ring and sulfur centres remain unspecified. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and families, with the displayed leaders often concentrated in one closely related series. Synthetic plausibility and drug-likeness are limited primarily by unusual local bonding and reactive functionality, rather than by a lack of rings or heteroatoms.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules are compact fused furan/unsaturated sulfur-ring systems bearing an aryl amide or pyridyl ketone. Alkyl, aminomethyl, imine and chlorinated amino substituents decorate the larger ring; the main ring sulfur itself is an ordinary divalent sulfide. The best molecule contains both an amino-chloromethyl substituent and an N-chloro amide. A close-scoring pyridyl-ketone relative has methylamino and imine groups without an N-halogen bond. Seed 1 retains a comparatively straightforward ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. The low examples disrupt the attached aromatic ring, expand or open a heterocycle, or replace the compact carbonyl-containing connection with a more flexible heteroatom chain.
liabilities: N-chloro amides, N-chloro amines and amino-chloromethyl groups introduce reactive bonds beyond ordinary aryl chlorination.
Some alternatives contain labile imines, free thiols, sulfur-halogen groups or cumulated unsaturation.
Partly saturated fused rings and multiple unsaturated connections are not accompanied by defined stereochemistry or alkene geometry.
missing_features: The lowest ring-expanded and chain-like derivatives lack the intact aromatic carbonyl organization present in the stronger structures.

The high-scoring set lacks a systematic series that preserves the fused aromatic carbonyl framework while replacing reactive N-chloro and amino-chloromethyl groups with stable alternatives; a chlorine-free relative already shows that such chemistry can score closely.
Ring substituents with possible stereogenic relationships remain unassigned, and no configuration preference can be inferred from these strings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused furan/sulfur-ring N-chloro amide scores 0.41700086027236194; a pyridyl-ketone relative with methylamino and imine substituents but no N-halogen group scores 0.4137456434408254. The ordinary indole carboxanilide reaches 0.39905049777278273. Thus the observed high-scoring family does not require every reactive chlorine substituent. A compact aryl-amide example scores 0.3957609793331631, while replacing its attached aromatic nitrogen-containing ring by an expanded unsaturated ring gives 0.01654726774958358. A pyridyl ketone at 0.40650757542526167 becomes 0.3305825215461728 when its carbonyl connection is replaced by a sulfoxide. The gradient favors retention of a compact aromatic carbonyl arrangement more clearly than sulfur enrichment. Current seed 2 reaches 0.41700086027236194 versus parental 0.41003927643747895 with a related but differently fused framework; seed 1 retains the same best indole amide, while seed 0 reaches 0.3504977161693128 versus 0.3966634883331815.

per_task.generated_character: The highest-scoring family is a bulky substituted phenyl group connected through an amino/exocyclic unsaturated arrangement to a nitrogen-containing carbonyl/imino ring. It carries branched conjugated carbon chains, fluoromethyl or difluoromethyl substituents, direct N-chlorination and an ester or imidate side chain ending in an aldehyde. Some side chains include an oxygen-linked alkyne, and some close relatives replace part of the carbon chain with additionally substituted, multiply bonded sulfur. The final seed-2 family instead contains an expanded nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl ring, imine and nitrile side chains, alkyl groups, methoxy groups and a bromoalkyl substituent. Early low examples retain more compact ester/phenol/dicarbonyl frameworks with disrupted ring connections. The assembled leading molecules have recognizable fragments but a high density of reactive or unusually conjugated connections.
liabilities: Direct N-Cl bonds, aldehydes and oxygen-linked alkynes introduce reactive functionality; the imidate alternative adds another hydrolysis-sensitive connection.
Extensive conjugated unsaturation and branching create configurational ambiguity and synthetic complexity.
Multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur and bromoalkyl groups appear in alternatives even where their local score advantage is not demonstrated.
missing_features: The low ring-altered compounds do not retain the same decorated aromatic and exocyclic heterocycle organization as the higher-scoring family.

Matched chemically simpler versions retaining that organization are underrepresented among the displayed leaders. Equal scores across several appendage changes do not demonstrate that the reactive or flexible embellishments are needed.
Imine and alkene geometry, and the configurations of branched side chains, are unspecified throughout the proposal set.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading imidate/alkyne/aldehyde derivative scores 0.6005008990495762, compared with 0.5976915588930607 for its carbonyl ester relative. Multiple variants share exactly 0.5976915588930607 despite changes in side-chain branching, alkene substitution, aminoalkyl substitution, aldehyde versus ketone termination, or introduction of an unusual sulfur-containing carbon-chain replacement. This supports the broader decorated aryl/heterocycle arrangement more strongly than those individual embellishments. Early ring-altered examples score 0.526081691583997 and 0.5266950153555399, while the initial aromatic dione scores 0.548381482770623. Relative to the parent, current seed 1 reaches 0.6005008990495762 versus 0.5906482326855353 with a different unsaturated decorated family. Current seed 0 and seed 2 reach 0.5925137762645043 and 0.5862876583994872 versus parental 0.6161710037174721 and 0.6092182584436399. The chemistry changes are mixed rather than a uniform preference for added complexity.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are bulky aryl-rich amines built around a saturated diaza ring with N-propyl and N-methyl substituents. A phenyl-pyridyl group and a chlorophenyl group provide aromatic surface, while a small saturated sulfur ring and an S-S connection link the latter to the amine framework. The small-ring S-H atom also carries an external sulfur substituent, giving an unusual neutral sulfur coordination state rather than an ordinary thietane. The diaza ring includes an aminal-like carbon connection. Other seeds produce amidine/amine-rich aryl compounds or more unsaturated sulfur rings. The low examples are carboxylic acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives with much less freely basic aliphatic nitrogen. Familiar aryl and amine fragments are present, but the assembled sulfur-containing structures remain chemically questionable.
liabilities: The saturated S-H ring atom is additionally substituted, and the adjacent S-S connection adds chemical lability and synthetic uncertainty.
Aminal-like carbon connections, multiple basic nitrogen centres and extensive hydrophobic substitution occur together without a defined ionization state.
Alternative families add S-Cl, bromoalkyl, imine and unusually unsaturated sulfur functionality.
missing_features: The low acid/amide/sulfonamide molecules lack the accessible aliphatic amine organization found in the stronger aryl-rich products.
The displayed leaders lack a matched conventional-valence sulfur or carbon-linker series that preserves the useful saturated amine and aromatic arrangement.
The substituted diaza and sulfur rings have possible stereogenic relationships but no explicit assignments; the observed scores do not identify a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-propyl diaza-ring molecule scores 0.9720943226453176. The corresponding N-ethyl relative scores 0.9310539197784231, while aromatic methyl, hydroxy or fluoro variants remain high but below the unmodified leader. This associates the observed scores with the aryl-rich saturated-amine arrangement and linker/substituent geometry. The early acid/amide/sulfonamide compounds score 0.007468397818197266 to 0.011875520467584314, so simply retaining nitrogen and aromatic rings is insufficient. Current seed 1 reaches 0.9720943226453176 versus the parent's 0.868020189804352, changing from a more fused unsaturated sulfur-containing framework to this diaza-ring family. Current seed 0 and seed 2 reach 0.8580723809662946 and 0.8946236316069243 versus parental 0.8856242185485628 and 0.9148143511682032. These cross-family observations do not establish a need for the unusual sulfur coordination.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family is a bulky expanded polyheterocycle with aromatic or pyridyl substituents, carbonyl groups, ether/ester-like connections, a cyclic sulfur-oxygen connection and an aryl alkyl sulfoxide. Nitrogen substituents include an N-S-H group or its N-S-Br relative. The main sulfoxide itself has a conventional bonding pattern. Other seeds contain cyclic imine/hydrazine/carbonyl frameworks or brominated aromatic compounds with acyl bromide and O-Br groups. Low-scoring examples open the carbonyl-containing ring, interrupt aromatic organization or introduce extended unsaturated chains. The products preserve much more ring and heteroatom content than simple fragments, but their large mixed N/O/S rings and reactive sulfur substituents make synthesis and stability uncertain.
liabilities: N-S-H, N-S-Br and cyclic S-O connections add reactive or labile chemistry within already complex rings.
Other seed families contain acyl bromide, O-Br and unusual substituted S-H groups.
Expanded mixed heteroatom rings increase conformational and synthetic complexity without a clear score benefit for several local extensions.
missing_features: The low ring-opened or extensively rearranged molecules fail to preserve the constrained aromatic/carbonyl organization of the stronger frameworks.

A matched series retaining that organization with ordinary stable ring connections and without terminal sulfur-halogen groups is incomplete. The N-S-H relative already scores above its N-S-Br partner, although N-S-H itself is not a general stability solution.
Possible sulfoxide and ring-centre stereochemistry is absent, and the large heterocyclic rings have no demonstrated preferred conformation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryl-sulfoxide/polyheterocycle with N-S-H scores 0.20285512197228367, compared with 0.19999114123092163 for its N-S-Br relative. Extending a nearby ring connection in the brominated relative gives 0.20173664619648224. Extending the sulfoxide alkyl chain or adding a methylene before the pyridyl group gives 0.19905436822494996. These small differences support retention of the overall aryl/carbonyl/ring arrangement more clearly than a need for terminal sulfur bromination or further chain growth. Earlier ring-opened dicarbonyl derivatives score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515. Parent seed 2 reaches 0.20185639717998205 with a different expanded N/O/carbonyl framework, close to the current value. Current seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.20020116392756776 and 0.18904611422707487 versus parental 0.2107445781802027 and 0.19092251395438758. The remaining shortfall cannot be assigned to a single absent functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules contain compact nitrogen/carbonyl or imino heterocycles decorated with fluorinated carbon sites and unusually unsaturated sulfur rings. The best family includes a carbonyl/imino aza ring, an alkyl-fluorinated connection, a thiocarbonyl fluoride group and an O-F substituent attached through sulfur. Several sulfur centres are multiply bonded while carrying additional substituents, and others retain S-H within small rings. A second strong family has an NH-rich heteroaromatic dione with fluorinated small sulfur rings and a chlorinated side chain. These are less extensively caged than some parent leaders but remain synthetically questionable. Low molecules can already be sulfur-rich and ring-bearing, demonstrating that those features alone do not explain the score.
liabilities: O-F and thiocarbonyl fluoride groups are reactive functionality, not interchangeable with ordinary stable aryl or alkyl fluorination.
Small unsaturated sulfur rings contain unusual S-H and multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur centres.
Cumulated unsaturation has a string-level rate of 0.0828, and the wider trajectories include highly constrained sulfur-containing unsaturated rings; valid text does not establish feasible geometry.
missing_features: Low-scoring rearrangements fail to retain the compact heterocyclic carbonyl/imino and fluorinated-substituent arrangement present in the stronger families.

The displayed leaders lack a matched chemically stable series preserving that arrangement while replacing O-F, thiocarbonyl fluoride and unusually coordinated sulfur. The observed scores do not establish that these reactive bonds are required.
Potential stereogenic fluorinated carbon sites and ring junctions have no explicit configuration, and unsaturated small-ring geometries remain unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading fluorinated carbonyl/imino structure scores 0.6093265714673088; shortening its N-linked fluorinated side chain gives 0.5988225297176035. A related structure with carbon in place of an additional sulfur ring atom scores 0.5838393854264313 versus 0.5803523965017872 for the sulfur-containing partner, so sulfur enrichment is not consistently rewarded. In the second family, the heteroaromatic dione scores 0.533982380907913; a more saturated and reorganized carbonyl-ring variant scores 0.12049296847930738, while enlarging its small sulfur ring gives 0.41309444888784197. The observations favor particular polar-ring and fluorinated-substituent arrangements, not fluorine or sulfur counts alone. Current seed 0 and seed 2 reach 0.6093265714673088 and 0.533982380907913 versus parental 0.48118636011729826 and 0.4484554129767839 with denser sulfur cages. Current seed 1 reaches 0.35677909167534066 versus parental 0.5903526424693334, retaining highly unusual sulfur and unsaturation chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited leaders contain N-Cl, O-F, thiocarbonyl fluoride, N-S-Br and unusually substituted S-H atoms. Yet a chlorine-free aromatic carbonyl relative scores 0.4137456434408254, a conventional indole carboxanilide reaches 0.39905049777278273, and replacing terminal sulfur bromination by hydrogen changes a paired score from 0.19999114123092163 to 0.20285512197228367.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful aryl, amine and carbonyl arrangements remain coupled to reactive halogen and sulfur chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Supply stable matched alternatives that retain useful fragment placement. Distinguish ordinary thioethers, thiols, sulfoxides and sulfones from unusual sulfur coordination, and distinguish conventional carbon-bound halogens from reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Displayed low molecules often open a carbonyl ring, expand an attached aromatic ring or reorganize a compact aza-carbonyl framework. Such changes can produce scores of 0.01654726774958358 or 0.12049296847930738 even when much of the surrounding heteroatom and ring content remains.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve promising aromatic and polar-group organization when changing ring connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate matched changes in ring size, linker placement and heteroatom position that preserve useful local arrangements while exploring ordinary, geometrically feasible ring systems. Chemical diversity should include coherent alternatives to both ring opening and unusual sulfur-rich constructions.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Multiple decorated heterocycles share 0.5976915588930607 across chain branching, alkene substitution, terminal carbonyl changes and introduction of unusual sulfur. A carbon-containing ring relative scores 0.5838393854264313 versus 0.5803523965017872 for an additionally sulfur-substituted counterpart. Added complexity is therefore not consistently associated with higher scores in the supplied molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically simpler relatives remain incomplete where several appendage changes have indistinguishable scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include simplifications that reduce reactive bonds, excessive branching or flexible appendages while preserving the principal ring and functional-group arrangement. Let the existing score observations determine which chemically simpler structures retain useful behavior.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The cited products contain substituted diaza rings, fluorinated carbon sites, sulfoxides, expanded mixed heteroatom rings and small unsaturated sulfur rings. Some families also show cumulated unsaturation, so chemically meaningful configuration extends beyond a single tetrahedral label.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic and highly unsaturated ring systems are emitted without explicit stereochemical identities or demonstrated geometric feasibility.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent feasible absolute and relative configurations and alkene geometry where applicable, preserve them through structural changes, and offer ordinary ring alternatives when a proposed topology demands severe geometric distortion. Do not infer synthetic accessibility from successful SMILES parsing alone.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

Unconditional highest-accepted-neighbor walk with lexicographic canonical tie selection
Signed occurrence differences of canonical rooted radius-one local motifs and bounded inverse-attribute installation from the selected transition
Same-transition conjunction of active positive and negative inverse restrictions, admitting partial and cross-transition-only matches

approach.method_basis: The Parent is a genetic algorithm that breeds molecular graphs from a population of up to sixty-four scored molecules. It draws parents from three high-ranking score bands, makes connected-fragment crossovers and local atom or bond edits, and sends each valid, novel offspring directly for evaluation. Accepted scores immediately update a greedy survivor population, so useful offspring can become parents of the next batch. This feedback loop worked, but most evaluated offspring scored below their generating parents.
approach.novelty: Add posterior-sampling selection before offspring reach the oracle. The same graph operators first generate a fresh pool; a fingerprint Gaussian process learned only from this task's accepted scores draws plausible score functions, and each batch position takes a different sampled function's best available offspring. This concentrates evaluations on promising generated structures while allowing uncertainty to change the choices. The lineage has only its root so far: no sibling has tested learned offspring selection, and the supplied mechanism-cluster history is empty. The new mechanism changes which generated offspring are evaluated; its training archive and diagnostics support that single selection mechanism.

nodes.hypothesis: Select oracle-bound offspring by maximizing independent joint posterior function draws from a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process over a fresh pool generated by the Parent's unchanged graph evolution operators.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection reproduces across seeds, but offspring yield stays below the historical parent-beating rate
finding_summary.insights: The experiment now separates reliable selector execution from the hoped-for improvement in offspring yield. The new runs' posterior means contain useful predictive information on the selected molecules: pooled prediction MSE is 0.017182 versus 0.036613 for the same-fit archive mean, with average within-batch rank correlation 0.412. Yet this information and widespread uncertainty-driven choice do not produce a higher parent-beating fraction. The remaining question is how to turn predictive information into more productive evaluations relative to already strong parents. Prediction quality is also uneven: on sitagliptin_mpo it is worse than the archive-mean predictor in two of three seeds, and that objective has the largest final-score variation. The chemistry assessment shows ample aromatic amides, cyclic amines and carbonyl-containing rings, alongside reactive substitutions and destructive edits; access to recognizable molecular families is established, while reliable discrimination among useful, chemically credible alternatives remains open. The unused pool members have no scores, so these runs cannot identify which rejected alternatives would have been better. Matched Parent replicas and same-pool comparisons with mean-only and generation-order selection are needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency, and uncertainty's contribution.
finding_summary.results: The two additional runs reproduce posterior selection and feedback. All 2,900 selected offspring maximize their reconstructed correlated function draws, uncertainty changes 2,693 choices (92.86%) compared with choosing the highest posterior mean, and all 2,800 eligible predictions on the same molecules change after accepted feedback. All 290 fits use only earlier accepted observations. Mean final-best score across the five objectives is 0.558863 in the first additional run and 0.526723 in the second, compared with 0.547535 in the original run of this selector. Across all three seeds, mean score is 0.544374 with population standard deviation 0.013310. The intended offspring-efficiency improvement does not appear: only 371 of 2,900 new offspring beat their best generating parent (12.79%), and their mean child-minus-parent score is -0.100465. The original direct-submission Parent's single-seed references are 13.86% and -0.084154. Across all three selector runs, 565 of 4,350 offspring beat their best parent (12.99%). The original paired screening-score gain of 0.055880 remains a one-seed comparison because matched additional runs of the direct-submission Parent are unavailable.
